title: fix: Ctrl+ chords now trigger shortcuts on Windows/Linux (#245)
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
# Fix #245 — Ctrl+ shortcuts on Windows/Linux

## Issue summary

FilmCraft's `Ctrl+` keyboard chords, when sent through the control channel (or MCP), did not
trigger their bound shortcuts on Windows/Linux. Only `Cmd+` chords worked. A synthetic `Ctrl+Z`
sent as `{"method":"ui.key","params":{"key":"Ctrl+Z"}}` produced no undo, while the equivalent
`Cmd+Z` did.

## Root cause

Both `parse_shortcut()` in `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs` and the `modifiers()` helper in
`crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs` set only `ctrl = true` when parsing/emitting a `Ctrl` chord on
non-macOS platforms. They did not also set `command = true`. On Windows/Linux, egui-winit maps a
physical Ctrl key press to **both** `ctrl` and `command` modifiers, so shortcuts are stored and
matched as `Cmd+…`. Because the synthetic events built from the control channel only set `ctrl`,
they failed to match bindings stored with `command`, and the shortcuts did nothing.

## Files changed

1. `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs` — `parse_shortcut()` now sets `command = true` alongside
   `ctrl = true` when not on macOS.
2. `crates/ui-egui/src/control.rs` — the `modifiers()` helper now sets `command = true` when
   `ctrl` is true on non-macOS.

## The fix

On non-macOS, `command = true` is now set together with `ctrl = true`, matching what egui-winit
does for physical Ctrl key presses on Windows/Linux. Synthetic key events produced from the
control channel therefore carry the same modifier bits as real key presses, and bindings stored
as `Cmd+…` now match `Ctrl+…` chords.

## Test procedure

A Python script (`tests/manual/test_245_ctrl_shortcuts.py`) connects to the running FilmCraft
instance over the JSON-lines control channel on `127.0.0.1:9876` and, in order:

1. Opens the demo project (`file.openDemoProject`).
2. Captures a screenshot of the initial state.
3. Makes an undoable edit (`sequence.addEdit`).

author: mjohnson7cd
body:
# Fix #244 — project.delete accepts explicit items without UI selection

## Issue summary

`project.delete` required a UI selection to work. Calling it programmatically through the control
channel (or MCP) with an explicit `items` array — but with nothing selected in the Project panel —
failed with "select an item in the Project panel", even though the caller had told the command exactly
which items to delete.

## Root cause

The command's guard was `has_project_selection` instead of `always`. The guard is what decides whether
the command is allowed to run in the current UI state; `has_project_selection` means "only run when the
user has selected something in the Project panel", so any programmatic call that supplied its own
`items` (and therefore had no need for a selection) was blocked outright.

## Files changed

`crates/engine/src/commands.rs` — `project.delete`:

1. Guard changed from `has_project_selection` to `always`, so the command runs regardless of UI state.
2. Added an early error check: when `items` is empty *and* there is no selection, it returns a helpful
   error instead of silently doing nothing.

## The fix

The guard is now `always`, so the command runs whether or not anything is selected in the Project
panel. It reads the explicit `items` parameter (falling back to the current selection only when no
`items` are passed), and if the resulting list is empty it returns:

```
no items to delete: pass `items` or select something in the Project panel
```

This matches the AGENTS.md "never crash" rule: an unusable request yields an actionable error, never a
panic or a silent no-op.

title: fix: filmcraft-cli exits quietly on broken pipe (#285)
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Fix: filmcraft-cli exits quietly on broken pipe (#285)

### Issue
`filmcraft-cli` panicked with "failed printing to stdout: Broken pipe (os error 32)" (exit 101) when its stdout was closed early, e.g. `filmcraft-cli commands | head`.

### Root Cause
Rust's default `println!` panics on `BrokenPipe` errors. The CLI used `println!` everywhere, so any reader that stopped early (like `head`) crashed the program.

### Fix
Replaced all `println!`/`print!` calls with `outln!`/`out!` macros that handle broken pipes gracefully:

- **First failed write sets a flag** (`STDOUT_GONE`); later output is dropped silently
- **The program keeps running** — remaining script lines, `--save`, `--save-as` all execute
- **A closed pipe is not an error** — exit status comes from the actual work (0 on success, 1 on command failure)
- **Any other stdout write error** is reported to stderr and makes the exit status 1

This means `filmcraft-cli commands | head -1` no longer crashes, and `filmcraft-cli --demo --save-as p.fcproj run - | head -c 1` still writes the project file.

### Approach
Based on the review feedback from @Oldrich333 (https://github.com/Oldrich333/filmcraft/commit/4f2b9a5163efeb3ae046827e7b5f86535f354abb), which improved on the earlier exit-on-BrokenPipe approach by keeping the work alive instead of bailing early.

### Files Changed
- `apps/filmcraft-cli/src/main.rs` — `outln!`/`out!` macros, `STDOUT_GONE`/`STDOUT_ERROR` flags, `stdout_failed()` handler
- `apps/filmcraft-cli/tests/cli.rs` — two new tests: `closed_stdout_ends_quietly`, `closed_stdout_still_runs_the_script_and_saves`
- `ROADMAP.md` — changelog entry
- `docs/agents.md` — CLI documentation update

### Test Results
- `cargo fmt --check` ✅
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings` ✅
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-cli` → **9 passed** (including 2 new tests)

### Compliance
- No `unwrap()`, `expect()`, `panic!`, or `unsafe` in production code
- No Adobe assets
- No GPL code

title: export: free the frame pool when an export ends
author: dcarnelutti
body:
Follow-up to #184, as suggested in its review: trim the process-wide float pool after an export so it doesn't hold up to 320 MiB idle.

## Summary

- `filmcraft_frame::pool::trim()` frees every idle buffer of the pool.
- `Pipeline` (the per-export picture pipeline) calls it in `Drop`. That is one place for every way an export ends: done, failed, cancelled, or dropped half way by a host that steps it (the web build steps exports with `Session::pump_jobs`), for `export` and for `Exporter`. Previews, proxies and AAF/OMF mixdowns go through the same pipeline, so they give their images back too.
- A job still rendering when another one ends allocates a few images again: the pool is only a cache. I considered counting live pipelines and trimming only at zero; what that avoids is a few allocations, so I left the state out.

I trimmed the plane shelves as well, not only the float images: an export fills them too (it decodes a lot), and `perf.stats` reports the three shelves together as `decode.planePoolMB`, which now reads 0 after an export. If you would rather keep decoder planes warm across exports, leaving them out is one line in `trim()`.

## Measured (Apple M1)

A synthetic 3 s 1080p24 matte exported as PNG frames three times in one process; `footprint` of the process:

| | right after | 2 s | 5 s | 10 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| without the trim (pool holds 332 MB idle) | 892 MB | 797 MB | 575 MB | **575 MB** |
| with the trim | 892 MB | 726 MB | 472 MB | **258 MB** |

So the trim takes back the 317 MB the pool was holding. It is not instant: macOS returns freed pages over a few seconds.

## Tests

- `crates/frame/tests/pool_trim.rs`: a buffer on each of the three shelves, all freed; nothing is handed out again from a trimmed shelf; the pool keeps working afterwards; trimming twice is fine.
- `crates/export/tests/pool_trim.rs`: after an image sequence, a finished video, a cancelled video, an export that could not start (no encoder) and a stepped `Exporter` dropped hal…

title: platform: ask for the hardware HEVC encoder in the background at startup
author: dcarnelutti
body:
Follow-up to #186, as suggested in its review: warm `hevc_available()` in the background in `register()` so the first format-list draw doesn't create a VideoToolbox session on the UI thread.

## Summary

`Format::Hevc` is available only where a hardware HEVC session can be created, and `hardware_encode::hevc_available` finds out by creating a small one on the first question (a `OnceLock`). That question comes from the first draw of Export mode's format list, on the UI thread. Timed in fresh processes on an Apple M1, that first call takes 88–100 ms (seven of eight runs) and 222 ms (the first run, colder), so the app stalls for about that long the first time Export is opened.

- `register()` now calls `hardware_encode::warm_hevc_probe()`, which asks the question on a thread of its own, once however many times `register()` is called.
- Whoever asks while it runs waits for the same answer, no longer than asking first. If the thread cannot start, or the probe panics (caught), the first caller asks, as before.
- `hardware_encode::hevc_probed()` says whether the answer exists yet (diagnostics and the test).

The cost is the same 0.1 s of work, moved to a background thread at startup on macOS.

## Tests

`crates/platform/tests/hevc_probe.rs`: registers, never calls `hevc_available`, and waits for `hevc_probed()`; asking again and registering again change nothing. Without the call in `register()` it fails after its 60 s wait ("register() did not start the probe"). title: Program monitor: the picture follows a value that is dragged
author: justjohn12345
body:
> **Measured on macOS only, with synthetic drags.** The numbers below come from the release app on one Mac (wgpu path, demo project), driven through the control channel at one pointer step per refresh. Not run on Windows or Linux. `cargo xtask wasm` was not run (no wasm32 target on this machine).

## What was wrong

Dragging a value in Effect Controls or Properties (Scale, for example) did not update the Program monitor while the mouse moved. The picture stayed as it was before the drag and jumped to the new value when the mouse rested, which reads as about half a second of latency. Premiere follows the mouse.

Two separate causes:

1. **No stand-in across revisions.** Every step of a drag is a new project revision. The monitor asks for the frame at that revision, which cannot be ready on the same refresh, and the stand-in lookup (`nearest_plan` / `nearest`) only looks at earlier frames of the *same* revision. So the frame from the refresh before, which is ready by then, was never looked up. A backward or fast scrub has the same gap (nothing cached before the frame due).
2. **Slow frames were thrown away.** A paused monitor's request cancels the job already running for that view. That is right for scrubbing, but for the same frame at a newer revision it meant that when a frame takes longer than a refresh (CPU effects), each one was cancelled by the next step. The job ran to the end anyway and its result was dropped.

## What it does now

- The monitor remembers the frames it asked for on its latest paused refreshes (64, about a second). When neither the frame due nor a cached frame just before it is ready, it shows the newest remembered frame that is. Lookup order is: frame due, nearest cached frame before it (as before), newest remembered frame, the picture already on screen (as before).
- A job running for the same frame at an older revision is left to finish. A request for a *different* frame of the view still cancels it, so scrubbing behaves as before.

## What was wrong

`essentialSound.autoMatch` metered every clip as the stereo pair `render::audio::clip_signal` plays. A mono source (or a single picked channel from Modify ▸ Audio Channels / Breakout to Mono) is copied onto both sides, so the meter saw dual mono and read 3.01 LU louder than the file. The match gain was then 3 dB too small, and `measuredLufs` disagreed with ffmpeg's `ebur128` by exactly the 3 LU the issue measured.

## The change

- `crates/render/src/audio.rs`: new `clip_is_mono(item, sources)`, true when the clip's left and right source channels are the same one (`source_pair`), `None` when it has no audio source.

author: WavJaby
body:
YUV range normalization currently uses the texture decoding scale as the quantization count. For 8-bit full-range frames this gives span 254 / chroma center 127.5 instead of 255 / 128; limited-range 10/12/16-bit offsets and spans are also scaled incorrectly.

- New regressions fail on base `5231852` and pass after the fix. Eight uniform cases + 24 native GPU fixtures cover 8/10/12/16-bit full/limited ranges: neutral RGB channels equal, CPU/GPU max error <=1 byte code, prepared/inline uploads byte-identical.

title: fix: frame stepping broken for non-standard frame rates (#301)
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Fix: Frame stepping broken for non-standard frame rates (#301)

### Issue
Frame stepping (Step Forward / Step Back) is inconsistent or completely broken when a sequence uses a non-standard frame rate like 37.516 fps. Step Forward sometimes moves backward, stalls at frame 0, or skips frames. The Demo Project works fine because it uses 23.976 fps (a standard rate).

### Root Cause
FilmCraft represents time as integer ticks at 254,016,000,000 ticks/second. All 11 standard broadcast frame rates (23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 48, 50, 59.94, 60, 119.88, 120) divide evenly into this tick rate, so their frame durations are exact integers.

Non-standard rates like 37.516 fps (9379/250) do **not** divide evenly: the frame duration is `6,770,871,094.999…` ticks — not an integer. `tick_of()` used floor division (`div_euclid`), truncating to `6,770,871,094` and losing ~1 tick per frame. This breaks the round-trip: `frame_at(tick_of(1))` returns `0` instead of `1`.

The stepping code does:
```rust
let f = rate.frame_at(s.playhead()) + n;    // current frame ± 1
s.set_playhead(rate.tick_of(f.max(0)));      // convert back to ticks
// set_playhead also calls rate.snap() → tick_of(frame_at(tick))
```

With the truncation, each step loses a tick, so:
- **Step Forward from frame 0**: `frame_at(0)=0 → +1=1 → tick_of(1) → snap → frame_at(tick_of(1))=0` → stuck at 0 forever
- **Step Backward from frame 5**: `frame_at(tick_of(5))=4` (already lost one!) `→ -1=3 → tick_of(3) → snap → frame 2` → jumps backward by 3

This affects **any** non-standard frame rate where `TICKS_PER_SECOND × den` is not divisible by `num` — approximately 119,460 rates between 1–120 fps at 0.001 resolution.

### Fix
Changed `tick_of()` and `frame_duration()` from floor division to **rounded division** (round to nearest). This ensures `frame_at(tick_of(f)) == f` for all non-negative frame indices, even when the frame duration has a fractional remainder.

Move and float panels

You can now drag panels anywhere in the workspace, like in Premiere Pro.

Moving panels

Drag a panel’s tab onto another panel’s tab strip or middle to join it as a tab.
Drop it on a panel’s side to split the space and place it next to it.
Tools and Audio Meters have no tab, so drag the three dots at their top.

Floating panels

title: Playback: Linux audio over the PulseAudio native protocol, pure Rust (#106)
author: Chace-Berry
body:
## Problem

On PipeWire systems (most current distros, including RHEL 10 from #106), desktop playback has no working sound:

- cpal's ALSA backend runs through the pipewire-alsa bridge. The output stream gets exactly one callback, then dies with `alsa::poll() returned POLLERR` and `snd_pcm_recover underrun occurred`, and never recovers. Since #155 the playhead keeps running on the wall clock, so the result is video playing with silent audio while the loudness meters still move (the mix is fine, the device is gone).
- ALSA device enumeration only sees ALSA hardware PCMs, so PipeWire-only sinks (Bluetooth headsets, virtual sinks) never appear in Settings > Audio Hardware.

Should fix #106; the `snd_pcm_recover` spam there is this same path.

## Fix

A native PipeWire output backend for Linux, `apps/filmcraft/src/pipewire_audio.rs`:

- `PipeWireOut` implements `AudioOut` with a `pw_stream` (F32 interleaved, stereo, FL/FR). PipeWire resamples, so the requested sample rate (or the document rate when forced) is always granted. The I/O Buffer Size preference is passed as `node.latency`. Played frames drive the playback clock as before; stream errors set the failed flag so the wall clock takes over, same contract as `CpalOut`.
- Settings > Audio Hardware lists PipeWire `Audio/Sink` / `Audio/Source` nodes by description, so Bluetooth and virtual sinks show up. An empty Default Output follows the system default sink, including device hot-swaps.
- `SystemOut` selects the backend: PipeWire when its socket is reachable and Device Class is empty or "PipeWire"; picking "ALSA" (or any cpal host) keeps the old path. Other platforms are untouched.

One implementation note worth flagging for review: the process callback fills only `buffer.requested()` frames per cycle. Filling the whole mapped buffer (as the pipewire-rs tone example does) drains the mixer's 200 ms lead in one callback and every subsequent cycle underruns, which sounds like stuttering.

Three small changes for an app that embeds FilmCraft's egui UI inside its own window or page. One commit each.

1. **`filmcraft_web::set_context`** (`apps/filmcraft-web/src/lib.rs`). `post` and `repaint` wake the egui context that `start` stores in a private thread-local. title: HW5: Linux VA-API hardware decoding for H.264 and HEVC (Main / Main 10)
author: JordyUSA
body:
## Summary

Linux hardware video decoding through VA-API, for **H.264** and **HEVC (Main, Main 10)** (#30).

VA-API decoding is stateless: the application parses the stream and keeps the decoded picture buffer, and the GPU decodes one picture's slice data at a time. This PR does that host side with **FilmCraft's own decoders' code**: the H.264 and HEVC parameter-set / slice-header parsers, POC computation and DPBs (`filmcraft_h264::dpb` and `filmcraft_hevc::dpb` are now generic over what a picture is). The hardware and software decoders therefore make the same reference-marking, reference-list and output-order decisions, and the pictures are **bit-exact** with the software decoders in the parity tests.

- `libva.so.2` / `libva-drm.so.2` are loaded at run time (`libloading`, already in the lockfile). No libva headers are needed to build, and a system without libva, a render node or a driver decodes in software as before.
- FFI is limited to `vaapi::va` (`#[allow(unsafe_code)]`, `// SAFETY:` on every block). `vaapi::ffi` is transcribed from libva's MIT-licensed `va.h` / `va_dec_hevc.h`, with generated ABI tests (sizes, offsets, constants, bit-field positions) as for NVENC. The front ends and `VaDecoder` are safe code.
- `HybridDecoder` keeps the transparent software fallback. Anything the hardware path doesn't take is declined up front or handed to software mid-stream: interlaced or 10-bit H.264, 4:2:2/4:4:4, HEVC range extensions, FMO / SP / SI, missing HEVC references, driver errors.
- H.264 frame_num gaps (every open-GOP seek) get the software decoder's stand-in frames (`vaPutImage`), so the decoder stays in hardware.
- ADR 0001 addendum, platform README, architecture, performance and roadmap are updated.

title: #236: audio in MKV and OBS-remuxed MP4 plays without crackling
author: IppSec
body:
Fixes #236.

## Cause

An AAC access unit decodes to 1024 samples, which is 21.33 ms at 48 kHz. Matroska stores timestamps in whole milliseconds, so frames are stamped at 0, 1008, 2064, 3072… samples instead of 0, 1024, 2048, 3072. OBS's remux to MP4 carries that rounding into the sample durations (1008, 1008, 1056…).

The MKV and MP4 readers put each decoded packet at its own timestamp. That overwrote the end of one packet and left a hole of silence after another (the read buffer starts zeroed), giving a click every few packets. The result was crackling throughout preview and export, while VLC and ffmpeg play the same file cleanly.

On a 10 s 440 Hz tone muxed the way OBS does it, the old readers produced about 850 clicks and 154 runs of inserted silence. ffmpeg's decode has none. The AAC decoder itself was fine: with the fix, every sample matches ffmpeg's decode to within 1e-4.

## Fix

- **`audio::contiguous_starts`:** for codecs whose packets all decode to the same length (AAC, MPEG audio, AC-3), each packet starts where the previous one ended. It resynchronises to the timestamp only when the two disagree by more than half a packet (a real gap or overlap in the recording). This is the rule the MPEG-TS/PS reader already uses (`mpeg.rs`).
- **MKV:** AAC, MP3/MP2 and AC-3 use it. Laced frames without a duration, which repeat the block's timestamp, follow on too. The existing Opus start logic (`opus_starts`) now goes through the same helper.
- **MP4:** AAC, MP3 and AC-3 use it. Audio packet starts are now kept in samples instead of track timescale units, and the Opus pre-roll is in samples to match.
- **`audio::fixed_packet_samples`:** packet length per codec. AAC gives 1024, or 2048 when `PacketDecoder::aac` upsamples an HE-AAC core. MPEG audio and AC-3 come from the first packet's header.

## Tests

- **`codecs/src/audio_timing_tests.rs`** (no ffmpeg needed): our own AAC encoder's output is muxed into MKV with millisecond timestamps (plain and Xiph-laced, at 48 an…

title: #341: CLI export message names the file written, not the requested path
author: JordyUSA

title: Fix #179: leave OpenGL out of the Windows wgpu instance (Vulkan | DX12 by default)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Closes #179

Same fix as storytold/designcraft#168, applied to FilmCraft.

## Problem

On Windows, FilmCraft can exit right after launch: the process shows in Task Manager for a moment and no window appears (#179). eframe's default wgpu instance enables `PRIMARY | GL`, and creating the OpenGL backend can crash inside AMD's OpenGL driver (`atio6axx.dll`) before adapter selection or any Rust error handling runs. In storytold/designcraft#167 the same symptom went away with `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12`.

## Change

- New `apps/filmcraft/src/graphics.rs`: when no `WGPU_BACKEND` is set, the Windows wgpu instance enables only DirectX 12 before it is created, so OpenGL is never initialized as a fallback. Picking an adapter afterwards would be too late.
- `main.rs` applies it on Windows only. An explicit `WGPU_BACKEND` is still honoured, and the process environment is not changed.
- macOS, Linux and web (`filmcraft-web` keeps its WebGL setup) are unchanged.
- README: a short Windows troubleshooting note on the default and the `WGPU_BACKEND` override.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p filmcraft graphics`: 2 passed. `windows_default_initializes_only_dx12` asserts that eframe's default includes GL and that the configured instance is DX12 only. `explicit_backend_override_is_preserved` covers overrides.
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. `rustfmt --check` on the changed files: clean.
- Limitation: this was built and tested on Linux. The Windows-only call site was not compiled for Windows here, and the AMD driver crash was not reproduced. The DX12 workaround comes from the designcraft report.

## Possibly related

- #268: Windows 10 portable flashes a loading cursor, then nothing.
- #310: v4 installer "briefly flashes then nothing" on Windows 10. The reporter says `WGPU_BACKEND=dx12` did not help, so that one may have a different cause.

title: Export: stage timings in perf.stats, and render the next batch while encoding
author: SaymonMaster14
body:
Two commits, independent of #328 / #360. Progress on #30, and it lowers the 4K export peak (related to #55).

title: GPU.EFFECT_SOURCE: preserve exact texel centers for effect inputs
author: sanyamsingh001
body:
Odd-sized GPU effect inputs can acquire small alpha values when interpolated vertex coordinates sample nominal pixel centers. Inverting alpha then turns those rounding errors into visible color differences. author: SaymonMaster14

Re-runs the #55 workflow on 0.4.0 as the issue audit asked, finds why the caps from #41 still let memory grow, and bounds it. Progress on #55. Does not close it: the 42-source report was on macOS, this is Windows.

## Reproduction (synthetic, shareable)

The issue has no synthetic reproduction, so I made one:
- **Media:** 42 distinct 4K25 H.264 clips of 20 s (ffmpeg testsrc2 / mandelbrot variants, AAC), back to back on V1, every 5th one also stacked on V2 for 10 s, plus 2 WAVs on A2 / A3.
- **Driving:** the desktop app (`filmcraft --control`), Program Monitor at Full, Hardware decoding Auto (Media Foundation).
- **Phases:** import → place → playhead to the middle of each clip in turn → 200 random seeks → 5 × 50 scrub seeks 100 ms apart → 8 × 10 s of playback → back to the first 5 clips → 30 s idle.
- **Sampling:** every 500 ms, private bytes, working set, system available RAM, GPU memory (`nvidia-smi`) and `perf.stats`.
- **Safety:** a watchdog kills the app at 13 GiB private or when the system runs low.

**v0.4.0 on Windows** (RTX 5060 8 GB, 16 GB RAM):

| phase | private peak | `decode.liveDecoders` | `decode.cacheMB` (budget 1074) | GPU memory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| place | 3.2 GB | 0 | 0 | 4.8 GB |
| playhead to each clip | 5.1 GB | **42** (cap 4) | 1991 | **6.5 GB** |
| random seeks | **6.6 GB** | 11 | **3907** | 3.0 GB |
| scrub | 5.2 GB | 11 | 3882 | 2.7 GB |

- **Bursts escape both caps.** Anything that touches many clips within 3 s keeps every one of them, with a decoder (a Media Foundation session holds VRAM) and up to `max(384 MiB, 64 frames)` of frames, about 800 MB per 4K clip. Examples: the playhead hopping from clip to clip, random seeks, scrubbing.

title: Thumbnails decode with small decoders that are not kept (#55)
author: SaymonMaster14
body:
**Stacked on #381.** Review only the last commit until #381 merges; I'll rebase then. Progress on #55.

## Problem

Right after importing many 4K clips, the Project panel and the timeline ask every clip for a thumbnail (`App::thumbnail`, priority 50; the Media Browser asks at 40). The burst behaves like this:
- **Six decodes at once.** Up to six frame workers decode the thumbnails in parallel.
- **Full-size decoders.** Each decode makes a frame-threaded software H.264 decoder: `h264::default_threads()` = 16 and 18 pictures in flight on this 28-thread machine, about **0.5 GB per 4K decoder**.
- **The decoders stay.** Every cache asked within the last 500 ms counts as in use (#381), and a thumbnail burst completes within that window.

The result is a jump in private bytes at import. With hardware decoding **Off**, 42 4K clips took the process past **6 GB** while importing; the watchdog killed every run of both v0.4.0 and #381.

The import itself is cheap (`filmcraft-cli import` of the same 44 files peaks at about 75 MB): this is the UI's thumbnail burst. With hardware decoding Auto the same burst opens Media Foundation sessions instead, which hold VRAM (see #381).

## Fix

- **Background hint.** `filmcraft_media::cancel::with_background(on, f)` is a thread-local hint, restored by a guard so a caught panic does not leave a worker marked.
- **Which jobs are background.** The frame server runs **item** jobs at priority ≥ 40 (`BACKGROUND_PRIO`: Project panel, timeline, Media Browser thumbnails) under it. Sequence frames never are, whatever their priority: the scopes ask for the program frame at 40 while playing.
- **Small decoders.** H.264 decoders made under the hint use **2 threads** (`VideoDecoder::thread_limited`), kept across `reset()`. No L0 change: `filmcraft_h264::Decoder::with_threads` already exists. Parallelism comes from the workers decoding different files instead of 16 threads on one.
- **Not kept.** `gop.rs` releases the decoders of caches that only backgro…

title: #262: file dialogs list extensions in any capitalisation on Linux
author: txiki739
body:
Fixes #262.

On Linux, file dialogs hid camera files with an upper-case extension (`CLIP.MP4`). rfd passes each filter extension to the XDG portal / GTK / Zenity as a `*.ext` glob, and those globs match case-sensitively.

This is an alternative to #286, which adds the all-lower and all-upper spellings to the three media Open dialogs. This PR also covers:

- **mixed case**, e.g. `clip.Mp4` or `Edit.FcProj`. Some cameras, phones and copy tools produce these. #286's spellings still hide them;
- **project dialogs**: Open Project and Save Project use the same filter, so an `EDIT.FCPROJ` copied from another system is visible too;
- **save dialogs** (`pick_save`, `pick_save_as`), with the literal extension kept first so the default suffix of a saved file is unchanged.

## How it works

- `apps/filmcraft/src/file_filters.rs::extensions` keeps the extensions as given, then on non-Windows/macOS targets appends one bracket pattern per extension with letters: `mp4` → `[mM][pP]4`, `m2ts` → `[mM]2[tT][sS]`. The portal's [FileChooser docs](https://flatpak.github.io/xdg-desktop-portal/docs/doc-org.freedesktop.portal.FileChooser.html) note that patterns are case-sensitive and suggest exactly this form; GTK's filter globs accept it too. Extensions without letters (`*`, digits) are left alone.
- Every filtered dialog in `main.rs` goes through it: import, Link Media/relink, Open file (presets etc.), Open Project, Save Project and Save As. Windows and macOS dialogs already ignore case and receive the plain list unchanged.
- `apps/filmcraft/README.md` (new) documents the helper.

## Tests

In `file_filters.rs`, matching the patterns the way the portal does (`*.{ext}` globs via the `glob` dev-dependency, MIT/Apache-2.0):

title: #340: FCP7 XML clip source span always matches its record span
author: txiki739
body:
Fixes #340.

`write_clip` rounded `start`, `end`, `in` and `out` to frames independently. For a clip placed by seconds in a 23.976 sequence (start 0, source in 20 s, 3 s long) that gave `start 0 / end 72` but `in 480 / out 551`: a 71-frame source span for a 72-frame record span, so Premiere and other xmeml readers take a different source range than FilmCraft plays.

## Fix

At normal speed, and on a freeze frame, the source span *is* the record span. `out` is now `in + (end - start)`, with `in`, `start` and `end` each rounded to the nearest frame as before. This is the "round the source range together with the record range" option from the issue; placement stays exact in the project, where `Tick` is the source of truth. Clips with a speed change keep their independently rounded `out`; their spans differ by design. The master `duration` is raised to `out` if rounding pushed `out` past it. `pproTicksIn` / `pproTicksOut` still carry the exact ticks, and the "sub-frame clip positions were rounded to frames" warning is unchanged.

## Tests

`sub_frame_clips_keep_equal_source_and_record_spans` (`crates/interchange/tests/fcp7.rs`): the issue's case, then 125 combinations of start, source in and duration in tenths of a second at 23.976. It asserts `out - in == end - start` for each. Before the fix it fails on the issue's case with `[(0, 72, 480, 551)]`.

Run on Linux (Kali, i5-4310U):

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                         ✅
cargo clippy -p filmcraft-interchange --all-targets -- -D warnings ✅
cargo test -p filmcraft-interchange                                ✅ (all, incl. golden and round-trip tests)
cargo test -p filmcraft-engine --lib -- fcp7 xml interchange       ✅ 7 passed
cargo xtask layers                                                 ✅
```

title: #379: preset export and import go through the host, so the web build no longer traps
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #379.

**What the user saw:** in the browser build, `presets.export` hit an uncaught Wasm `unreachable` trap. No file downloaded, and later commands (such as `file.exportFrame`) never settled until the page was reloaded.

**Cause:** `presets::export` wrote the file with `filmcraft_format::atomic_write` directly. That function calls `std::process::id()` and real filesystem APIs, and both trap on wasm32. `presets::import` read the file with `std::fs::read`, which has the same problem. Every other exporter writes through `s.services`.

**What changed:** export now calls `s.services.write_file` and import calls `s.services.read_file`. On the desktop, `FsServices::write_file` still uses `atomic_write`, so native behaviour does not change. On the web, the host's `write_file` offers the file as a download, and `read_file` reads the file the user picked. The user library file (`effect-presets.json`) still uses `std::fs`. It only exists when `start_autosave` sets a data dir, and only native frontends call that.

**Tests:** `presets_tests::export_and_import_go_through_host_services` runs the commands with an in-memory `Services` (no real filesystem). It exports to `/exports/owned-preset.prfpset`, the path from the report, and checks the bytes arrived through the host. A second session imports the file from there, and importing a missing path still returns an error. Before the fix, the export goes to the real disk and fails, so the test fails.

title: #318: a reversed clip shows exactly its source range
author: txiki739
body:
Fixes #318.

A trimmed clip (source frames 10–29) played in reverse showed 30 down to 11: one frame past its source range, and never its In.

## Cause

`TrackItem::moving_source_time_at` maps a reversed clip's timeline time to the instant just before its mirrored source position (`source_out - rel - 1 tick`). That is right for a reader that picks the frame at or before the time. The MP4 reader converts the request to the track timescale rounding to the *nearest* unit first (deliberately, `mp4.rs`: coarse timescales round sample times), and one tick below a frame boundary rounds up onto the boundary, so it decodes the next frame.

## Fix

`video_source_time` (`crates/render/src/lib.rs`) snaps a reversed clip's video request down to the start of the media frame that contains it, on the source's own frame grid. It is clamped to `[source In, the unsnapped time]`, and every reader then shows that frame. It is used by both places that ask a media source for a clip's picture: `media_frame` (CPU) and the plan path (`plan.rs`). Nothing else changes:

- `source_time_at` itself is unchanged. Audio and nested sequences use it as a continuous time, where the one-tick offset is right.
- Forward clips, frame holds and sources without a frame rate keep their request as is.
- Frame Blending (`interpolation_blend`) already measures from the frame at or before the time, which is now the base frame requested too.

## Tests

`a_reversed_clip_shows_exactly_its_source_range` (`crates/render/src/tests.rs`) uses a source that picks frames the way the MP4 reader does: nearest unit at 12288 units/s, then the frame at or before. It records which frames it is asked for. For the issue's clip (source 10–29, 20 frames), through both `render_sequence` and the plan path:

- forward control at timeline frames 0, 7, 19 → 10, 17, 29;
- reversed → 29, 22, 10 (before the fix: 30, …, the issue's result);
- reversed, every timeline frame 0–19 → exactly 29 down to 10.

title: Import every audio track of MP4/MOV files
author: rangamitch
body:
﻿## Summary

A file with several audio tracks (for example a game track and a microphone track) imported only its first track. This PR makes MP4/MOV imports keep every audio track.

- **Codec (`crates/codecs/src/mp4.rs`)**: each playable audio track (up to 8) is opened as its own stream. The channels of all streams are joined in file order. Single-track files take the same path as before.
- **Media (`crates/media/src/lib.rs`)**: new `MediaSource::audio_streams()`, defaulting to the single stream. `info().audio.channels` is now the total across streams, so Modify ▸ Audio Channels sees the right count.
- **Engine (`crates/engine/src/commands.rs`)**: on import, a multi-stream file gets one audio clip per stream through the existing channel map. Placing it adds audio tracks when the sequence lacks them, instead of silently dropping the extra clips.

## Testing

- New tests: a two-AAC-track MP4 plays each tone on its own channel pair (codec); the channel map and one-clip-per-stream placement (engine, `multi_audio_tests.rs`).
- Manual check on a 7-track Medal.tv MP4: all 7 streams decode, and placing it gives 7 linked audio clips on A1–A7.
- `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo xtask layers` pass for the changed crates.
- The engine suite has 10 failures that also fail on `main` (export paths, AAF, relink), so they are not from this change.
- `cargo xtask wasm` was not run (wasm32 target not installed locally).

## Limits

- MP4/MOV only. MKV, WebM and MXF still expose their first audio track.
- Projects imported before this change keep only their first track until re-imported or remapped with Modify ▸ Audio Channels.
- Each clip decodes every stream of the file. A later change could decode only the streams a clip uses.

title: #259: the edge you press is the edge you trim
author: ItzBloxy
body:
Fixes #259. Also covers the trimming bullet of #329 ("make trimming … behave intuitively").

## What was wrong

- **A press was decided after the pointer had moved.** The Timeline hit-tested a press only when egui reported a drag, after the pointer had moved 6 pt. Pressing a clip edge and dragging inward (to shorten the clip) had already left the 7 px edge zone by then, so the clip was selected and moved instead of trimmed. A moved clip lagged the pointer by the same distance.
- **At a cut, the left clip always won.** The left clip's Out edge claimed both sides, so the right clip's In edge could not be grabbed with the Selection tool. The cursor showed a trim cursor there anyway.
- **Caption blocks had the same press problem.** Their 5 px edge zone was decided after the drag threshold.

## What it does now

- **One shared hit-test.** `panels::timeline_hit::grab_at` works out what a press grabs: the edge and the trim it starts, or the body, transition, empty track or ruler. It is used by the cursor, the press and `ui.timeline.hit`, so what the pointer shows is what a press does.
- **The press is decided where the button went down.** It is stored on that frame (`TlState.pressed`), so it also works for clicks; egui no longer knows the press point when it reports a click.
- **The side of the cut picks the clip.** Inside a clip beats outside it, so just right of a cut you trim the right clip's In edge. A narrow gap splits at its middle, exact ties go to the later clip, and zero-width clips (zoomed far out) have no edges. The zone sizes are unchanged: 7 px, or a third of a narrow clip.
- **Drags measure from the press.** Trims, rolls, rate stretches and remixes move by how far the pointer moved since the press instead of jumping to the pointer, and a moved clip stays under the point it was grabbed by.
- **Hover bracket.** Hovering an edge draws the edit-point bracket at half strength on the edge a press would grab: red for ripple, yellow otherwise, and both sides of the c…

title: Linux: VA-API hardware decoding (H.264, HEVC, VP9, AV1) and H.264 / H.265 export encoding
author: mutombopr
body:
Adds **hardware video decoding and export encoding on Linux through VA-API**, the Linux counterpart of VideoToolbox (macOS) and Media Foundation / NVENC (Windows), as discussed in #30.

**Decoding** (Settings ▸ Playback ▸ Hardware decoding, as on the other systems)
- H.264 (8-bit), HEVC Main and Main 10, VP9 profiles 0 and 2, AV1 Main (8- and 10-bit), 4:2:0.
- VA-API is stateless, so the codec crates gain an accelerator hook (`accel` modules in `filmcraft-h264`, `filmcraft-hevc`, `filmcraft-vp9`, `filmcraft-av1`): the software decoder's own parsing, reference handling and output order run, and only the reconstruction goes to the GPU. Both paths therefore agree picture for picture.
- Pictures are **bit-exact** with the software decoders on every fixture (H.264 High, HEVC Main / Main 10, VP9 p0 / p2, AV1 from libaom 8/10-bit and SVT-AV1 10-bit), over the whole stream, after every reseek and after resets. Damaged samples never crash. Anything the GPU does not take (field-coded H.264, AV1 film grain, scalable AV1, inter-frame size changes, missing references, driver errors) falls back to software in `HybridDecoder`.

| 4K, Radeon RX 7900, Mesa 26.2 | CPU ms per frame, software → VA-API | fps |
|---|---|---|
| H.264 | 136.7 → 3.2 | 97 → 107 |
| HEVC | 118.3 → 2.8 | 87 → 148 |
| HEVC Main 10 | 113.2 → 4.1 | 88 → 126 |
| VP9 | 61.1 → 2.9 | 50 → 118 |
| AV1 | 64.0 → 3.0 | 41 → 138 |

**Export encoding**
- **H.264** (Export ▸ Hardware encoding, off by default as on the other systems): IDR + P, CBR / VBR in the driver, our SPS / PPS in `avcC`. 191 1080p frames 4.9 → 3.1 s, 296 → 62 CPU ms/frame; 52.1 dB from the software export of the same frames.

title: AV1 export format, encoded with VA-API on Linux
author: mutombopr
body:
**Depends on #408** (Linux VA-API): this branch contains it. Only the last commit, `HW6: AV1 export format, encoded with VA-API on Linux`, is new here.

Adds an **AV1 export format** (MP4 `av01` + `av1C`, AAC audio). Like H.265, it has no software encoder: it is offered only where a hardware encoder registers one (format probe), with H.265's bitrate controls and one pass. This PR provides the VA-API encoder; other backends can register theirs the same way.

**Export**
- `Format::Av1` (names `av1`, `av01`); MPEG-4 only, so a QuickTime multiplexer setting left over from H.264 does not apply (`Format::is_mp4_video`, `Format::is_mp4_with`); size estimate and summary; the Export panel shows it with the hardware-only controls.
- `filmcraft-isobmff`: `SampleEntry::av1`.

**VA-API encoder** (`crates/platform/src/vaapi/av1enc.rs`): Main (8-bit SDR 4:2:0), key + inter frames with one reference, the GPU's tool set (64×64 superblocks, TX_MODE_SELECT; no warped motion, compound modes, filter intra, superres or restoration).
- The driver needs a packed sequence header and a packed frame header per frame. It writes its own sequence header, which goes into `av1C` only after a check against everything our frame headers assume (anything else is an error, never a broken file). Its rate control patches base_q_idx, loop filter and CDEF into our frame header at the bit offsets we give.
- 1280×720 and 640×352 exports at worst 50.8 / 49.3 dB from the software H.264 export of the same frames; ffprobe reads `av1`, `av01`; ffmpeg decodes them without errors.

**Limitation (Mesa radeonsi, RX 7900)**: the driver codes a width that is not a multiple of 64 rounded up, and a height that is not a multiple of 16 two rows taller (1080 → 1082). title: #323: AAF files open in readers that load the meta-dictionary
author: txiki739
body:
Fixes #323.

pyaaf2 refused every AAF FilmCraft writes: `AAFPropertyError: cannot find index stream: ClassDefinitions-3 index`.

## Cause

The Root's MetaDictionary was written as an object with no properties. An AAF meta-dictionary has two strong-reference sets, ClassDefinitions (0x0003) and TypeDefinitions (0x0004), keyed by the definitions' AUIDs (0x0005). Readers that load the meta-dictionary to merge it with their built-in model, like pyaaf2, expect both sets and their index streams.

## Fix

- The MetaDictionary now has both sets, empty. They only carry extensions to the baseline object model, and everything FilmCraft writes is baseline, so there is nothing to put in them; readers use their own baseline definitions.
- An empty strong-reference set now writes the right key size in its index (16 bytes for AUID keys, 32 for MobIDs) instead of 0, which used to be taken from the first entry.
- The sets get readable storage names (`ClassDefinitions-3`, `TypeDefinitions-4`).

## Tests

- `the_meta_dictionary_has_its_class_and_type_definition_sets` (`crates/interchange/src/aaf/tests.rs`), for 4096- and 512-byte sectors: the `MetaDictionary-1` storage has both index streams with 0 entries, key pid 0x0005 and 16-byte keys, and our reader reads both sets back. It fails on `main` (no `ClassDefinitions-3 index` stream).
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-interchange` passes in full, including the AAF/OMF round trips through our own reader.
- Checked locally with pyaaf2 1.7.1 as an external oracle (not added to CI). On `main`, a demo-project AAF exported with `filmcraft-cli … exec file.exportAaf` fails with the issue's error. With the fix, both sector sizes open, the composition enumerates (timecode, video and audio slots), and every SourceClip reads back its start and length and resolves to its MasterMob (`a.mov`), through transitions and an OperationGroup.

title: GPU export rendering (on by default) and Vignette, Video Limiter, Lumetri Color on the GPU compositor
author: mutombopr
body:
GPU export rendering and more standard effects on the GPU compositor, the "GPU export" step of #30. Independent of #408 / #409.

**GPU export rendering** (Export ▸ GPU Rendering, now **Auto by default**)
- `export` gets a frame-renderer registration hook (like `register_encoder`): `Pipeline::frame` asks the registered renderer first and falls back to the CPU reference renderer (`render_sequence`) for anything it cannot draw, frame by frame.
- The renderer is `filmcraft-gpu`'s off-screen compositor (`plan_frame` + `GpuCompositor`). It reads back the **linear float accumulator**, not the sRGB display texture, so overlays, HDR and the video limiter behave as on the CPU. The desktop app and `filmcraft-cli` register it.
- Export workers share a pool of up to four renderers on one wgpu device, and each frame is one submission with a reused staging buffer. With a single mutex-guarded renderer the workers queued and GPU export was ~20 % slower than the CPU.

| 191 frames → H.264 + AAC, Linux, Ryzen 7 9700X + RX 7900 | Off: s / CPU ms per frame | **Auto**: s / CPU ms per frame |
|---|---|---|
| one 1080p clip | 5.96, 6.08 / 292 | 6.07, 6.36 / 281 |
| 1080p, 3 layers + effects (new bench scene `h264_fx`) | 13.00, 12.67 / 737 | **5.63, 5.00 / 238** |
| the same scene at 4K | 38.74, 39.34 / 2955 | **11.99 / 775** |

Every Auto row rendered all its frames on the GPU, with no fallbacks. With layers and effects the GPU is 2.4× (1080p) to 3.2× (4K) faster; on a plain clip, which is bound by decoding and encoding, it takes the same time.

**Trade-off to note**: the GPU matches the CPU within the compositor's parity tolerance, not bit for bit, so with Auto an export's bytes can depend on the machine's GPU. Off keeps exports byte-reproducible; the determinism tests register no GPU renderer and are unaffected. If you would rather keep Off as the default, it is the last commit (`GPU3d`) alone.

title: fix: prevent duplicate file imports (#356)
author: mjohnson7cd

## Summary
Importing a file that's already in the project from the UI no longer adds a second project item. Detection is path-only: both paths are compared after `std::fs::canonicalize`, so `dir/./a.mov`, `dir/sub/../a.mov` and a path through a symlinked folder all match the existing item.

The check is opt-in (`"skipDuplicates": true` on `file.import`). The Import dialog, files dropped from the OS, and paste pass it. Scripts, agents, the CLI/automation server and internal imports (graphics, Media Browser, export frame) don't, so they can still import a file twice on purpose and pay no extra cost.

## Changes
- `crates/engine/src/commands.rs`: `find_duplicate_item()` compares canonical paths. It only canonicalizes existing items whose file name matches, so large projects don't stat every file. Skipped files go in a `duplicates: [{path, item}]` list, separate from `errors`, and the user sees a toast: "N file(s) already in the project". title: Issue #552: MP4 and Matroska colour from the bitstream when the container has none
author: LloydNicholson
body:
Fixes #552.

ffmpeg writes MP4 without a `colr` box unless asked to (`-movflags +write_colr`). The MP4 importer only read `colr` (or `vpcC` / `apvC`), so such files fell back to BT.709 limited range:

- An HEVC PQ file was detected as `rec709`, `hdr: false`. The same stream with `colr` gives `rec2100-pq`, `hdr: true`.
- A full-range H.264 file (`yuvj420p`) was detected as limited range.
- BT.601 SD was given BT.709 primaries.

Decoded pictures were already right, because the decoders read the VUI. What was wrong was `media.colorInfo`, HDR detection and the Interpret Footage defaults. Matroska files without a `Colour` element had the same gap.

### What changes
- New `codecs::stream_color` reads the colour a codec configuration carries in its bitstream, using the decoders' own parsers: the SPS VUI in `avcC` / `hvcC`, and the `color_config` of the AV1 sequence header in `av1C`. A truncated or corrupt parameter set gives no colour.
- Precedence is field by field: `colr` (nclx / nclc) or the Matroska `Colour` element first, then `vpcC` / `apvC` / the bitstream, then the existing size defaults (BT.601 matrix for SD, BT.709 otherwise). Unspecified (2) code points fall through to the next source.
- `nclc` has no range flag, so the bitstream's range now applies. An ICC `colr` no longer hides the bitstream's code points.

### Before / after (`media.colorInfo`, synthetic ffmpeg files)
| File | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| HEVC PQ MP4, no `colr` | rec709, hdr false | rec2100-pq, hdr true |
| H.264 `yuvj420p` MP4 | range Limited | range Full |
| H.264 720×480 smpte170m MP4 | primaries Bt709 | primaries Bt601_525 |
| HEVC PQ MKV, no `Colour` | rec709, hdr false | rec2100-pq, hdr true |
| HEVC PQ MP4 with `colr` | rec2100-pq | unchanged |

### Tests
- `stream_color_tests.rs` builds `avcC` / `hvcC` / `av1C` bit by bit. It covers PQ, full range, BT.601 (NTSC / PAL), an unspecified VUI keeping the defaults, `colr` winning (including partly unspecified, nclc and ICC), AV1, and Ma…

title: Hybrid decoder: a rejected replayed sample no longer discards the replay's pictures (#447)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #447.

When the hardware decoder fails, `HybridDecoder::fall_back` replays the logged samples through the software decoder. Before this change, one sample rejected by the software decoder stopped the replay with `?`. The pictures already decoded were lost, and the remaining samples were not fed.

Now the replay loop is a small `replay` helper:

- A sample the software decoder rejects is skipped, as a caller does after a decode error. The replay continues with the remaining samples.
- Pictures decoded before and after the rejected sample are kept and returned the normal way (merged with the pictures the hardware decoder had not yet returned). A warning is logged with the first error.
- `fall_back` returns the error only if the replay recovered no pictures. This is the same result as before for that case.
- A cancellation (`CodecError::Cancelled`) still stops the replay and is returned as `Err(Cancelled)`, so a cancelled job is not reported as decoded.

No other code path changes.

Tests: three unit tests in `crates/platform/src/hybrid.rs` use a mock decoder:

- one sample rejected: the pictures from the other samples are kept, and the error is reported;
- no errors: all pictures, and no error;
- a cancellation: the replay stops and reports `Cancelled`.

title: perf(windows): integrate resident frames with fallible CPU access
author: WavJaby
body:
Windows GPU frame pipeline: follow-up to #152

Follow-up to [#152](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/152), integrated with main and hardened at the shared frame boundary. Windows Media Foundation D3D11 surfaces reach the DX12 compositor without a CPU round trip when import is supported. Original author commits remain in the branch history. GPU-import fallback, crop bounds, surface ownership/cache eviction and explicit backend overrides are preserved.

Integration retains shared GPU transitions ([#308](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/308)), YUV normalization ([#319](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/319)), Web YUV planes ([#375](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/375)), Windows backend selection ([#365](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/365)), export render-ahead ([#370](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/370)) and still-frame export ([#353](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/353), integrated by [#425](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/425)).

GPU readback failure previously produced gray pixels as a successful frame. CPU conversions now return `Result`; render/effects, preview, export and analysis propagate that failure. Preview keeps pending/cancelled requests distinct from terminal errors; failed frames cannot enter successful caches or encoder input. Push inputs restore the parent accumulator before returning an error, and export render-ahead preserves per-thread pending handling. Source/Program still export fails before overwriting output or importing it.

The failure contract is shared by desktop and Web; the measured no-copy speedup is Windows-only. WebCodecs resident-frame integration is a follow-up, not included here. Decoder policy, Web threads and GPU export remain unchanged; [#421](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/421) is separate work. Existing shared YUV reconstruction and color guarantees are retained. Background: [#30](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/issue…

title: MCP render_frame: max_side 0 means no limit (#459)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #459.

`render_frame` with `"max_side": 0` failed in headless mode with "render scale 0 must be finite and positive": the render scale was computed as `max / longest_side`, which is 0 for `max_side: 0`. `png_rgba` already treats 0 as "no limit", so the render step now does the same.

- New pure helper `render_scale(max_side, w, h)` in `crates/automation/src/server.rs`: returns 1.0 for `max_side == 0`, otherwise the previous fit-and-never-upscale formula (with a guard against a zero-sized sequence).
- The headless branch of `render_frame` uses it. The Bridge branch passes `max` to the screenshot path, which ends in `png_rgba` and already handles 0, so it is unchanged.
- Unit test `render_scale_zero_means_no_limit`: 0 gives 1.0 (fails before the fix, which gave 0.0), 960 on 1920x1080 gives 0.5, 960 on 640x360 gives 1.0.

title: FCP7 XML: keep the source channel of split mono audio tracks (#463)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #463.

A stereo file split onto two mono tracks (A1 = channel 1, A2 = channel 2) came back from `file.exportFcp7Xml` with both clips on source channel 1, because every audio clip item was written with `<sourcetrack><trackindex>1</trackindex></sourcetrack>` and the FCP7 importer never read `sourcetrack`.

- **Export:** `trackindex` is now the clip's first `source_channels` entry + 1 (1-based). Clips without a channel pick still write 1, as before.
- **Import:** for audio clip items, `sourcetrack/trackindex` above 1 sets `source_channels = [trackindex - 1]`. Index 1 (and a missing, zero or invalid value) keeps the default empty mapping, because index 1 is also what an ordinary stereo clip carries, so existing imports play the same as before. Video clip items are not touched.

Known limit: a clip picked to channel 1 only (`source_channels = [0]`) still exports as `trackindex` 1 and comes back with the default mapping on re-import into Filmcraft. Premiere reads the exported file correctly (A1 = 1, A2 = 2).

Tests (`crates/interchange/tests/fcp7.rs`):
- `split_mono_tracks_keep_their_source_channel`: two audio clips on channels 0 and 1 survive export, import and a second export with `trackindex` 2 intact.
- `audio_sourcetrack_trackindex_2_imports_as_source_channel_1`: a hand-written clip item with `trackindex` 2 imports as `source_channels == [1]`.

Both fail without the change.

title: #474: VA-API decoders share one display (no 0.3 s open / 70 ms close per decoder on NVIDIA)
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Fixes #474.

## What was wrong

Every VA-API decoder opened its own display and terminated it when dropped. With NVIDIA's driver that means a CUDA context each: 190–310 ms to open and 59–72 ms to close, plus about 104 MB of video memory per display. That cost lands on the thread that creates or drops the decoder: a frame worker at every clip change (dropped frames), and the UI thread when media is removed (a ~0.6 s freeze when deleting five played clips). Measurements are in #474.

## What it does now

`crates/platform/src/vaapi/va.rs`, about 70 lines, no new `unsafe` blocks:

- **One shared display.** `Session::new` takes the process's shared display instead of opening one. The startup probe's display becomes that shared display instead of being terminated, so the first decoder no longer pays the open either. It stays open for the life of the process, like the libva libraries already do. Sessions still make and destroy only their own configuration, context, surfaces and image.
- **`unsafe impl Sync for Display`**, justified by libva's *Multithreading Guide* in `va.h`. libva's functions are thread-safe and drivers must be too; several threads may use one display as long as each VA object is used by one thread at a time. Every `Session` owns its context, surfaces and image, used only through that session, and the display itself is only read (`api`, `dpy`, `vendor`). `Session` stays `Send` and not `Sync`, as before.
- **Recovery.** If creating a session on the shared display fails (say the shared display stopped working after a GPU reset), it is tried once on a new display, which is shared from then on if it works. Sessions still on the old display keep it until they end, and it is terminated when the last one lets go. A stream the driver doesn't take fails on both, at the cost of one extra display opening.
- `va::displays_opened()`: a counter, for diagnostics and the test.

Behaviour on Intel / Mesa is unchanged apart from not re-initialising a display per decoder, w…

assertion `left == right` failed:

title: M-HW: NVENC takes the export's RGBA and converts it on the GPU (#30)
author: MasakatsuFunaki
body:
Progress on #30.

## What this changes

This only changes hardware (NVENC) exports: H.265, and H.264 with Export ▸ Hardware encoding on. Software exports are unchanged.

Before NVENC can compress a frame, the frame has to be converted from RGB to YUV (BT.709, limited range, 4:2:0). FilmCraft did that on the CPU, on the encode thread. That conversion competed with the render of the next frames for the same thread pool, so in a real export it ran at roughly single-thread speed: about 13 ms per 1080p frame, against 1.5 ms when it runs alone. NVENC sat idle waiting for it.

Now FilmCraft sends NVENC the RGBA frame directly (an `NV_ENC_BUFFER_FORMAT_ABGR` input buffer), and the GPU converts it. NVENC follows the VUI matrix the session already declares (BT.709), so the colours come out exactly the same as the CPU conversion. If a driver refuses RGB input, the encoder falls back to the old CPU conversion into NV12 automatically. HEVC Main 10 (HDR) is unchanged: it still takes its 10-bit planes from the CPU.

## How much faster

Same 60 s of a real 1080p30 project (H.264 screen recordings, four cuts), exported as H.265 inside the app, old build vs new build, both driven over the control channel:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Time | 18.7 s | 15.0 s |
| Speed | 96 fps | 120 fps |
| CPU used | 230 core-s | 205 core-s |
| `perf.stats` convert | 11 330 ms | 0 ms |
| `perf.stats` encode | 12 673 ms | 4 803 ms |

That's about 25% faster in the app. Headless (`filmcraft-cli`) the same slice went from 30.3 s to 16.8 s (59 → 107 fps), because there the encode thread was the whole bottleneck (`waitMs` ≈ 0).

After this change the render is the limit (`waitMs` went up from 0.45 s to 1.5 s): NVENC now waits for frames instead of for the conversion. Moving the render itself to the GPU is the bigger next step for #30 and is not part of this PR.

## Colours

- **Solid colours:** red, green, blue, white, black and grey encoded through the RGBA input and decoded with FilmCraft's own …

title: #288: MP4 / MOV pictures are cropped as the file says (H.264 / HEVC cropping, clean aperture)
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Fixes #288.

## What was wrong

The MP4 source took the picture size from the sample entry (`stsd`) and only swapped it for the display rotation. Two crops were lost:

1. **The codec's own cropping**: the H.264 SPS frame cropping and the HEVC conformance window. The decoder already returned the cropped picture, but the reported size (and with it the sequence made from the clip, which then letterboxed or scaled the picture) was the sample entry's. That is the coded size when a file was written that way (ffmpeg's `h264_metadata` with crop does this, for example).
2. **The clean aperture (`clap`)**, which QuickTime / iPhone files use for the stabilisation margin. It was parsed into `VideoParams::clean_aperture` but never used, so pictures kept the margin. That's the iPhone case in #288: 1920×1440 coded, a 1744×1308 clean aperture, and a −90° display matrix should give **1308×1744**, as ffmpeg, QuickTime and Photos show. FilmCraft gave 1440×1920.

## What it does now

- `crates/codecs/src/mp4.rs`: for H.264 and HEVC the size comes from the stream's parameter sets (`NalStreamInfo::crop`, what the decoder returns). The clean aperture is then a rectangle inside that picture: its size, centred and moved by its offsets, rounded to whole samples (`clean_aperture`). That size is what the source reports, before the existing swap for a quarter-turn rotation. A clean aperture that makes no sense (a zero denominator, an empty size, a size larger than the picture, a rectangle outside it) is ignored, so the whole picture is shown as before.
- `crates/codecs/src/gop.rs`: `GopCache::with_crop` cuts every decoded frame to that rectangle **before** the display rotation (crop in coded space, then rotate, as #288 points out). Hardware and software decoders both pass through here.
- `crates/frame/src/lib.rs`: `VideoFrame::cropped(Region)` for every pixel format (RGBA8 / F32, 8- and 16-bit Y'CbCr, with alpha). The region is clipped to the frame. On subsampled Y'CbCr, an odd corner moves one…

title: Premiere FX & Projects
author: cirocueto2013-wq
body:
## Summary

Adds **Premiere FX & Projects**, a clean-room native data-file importer integrated with FilmCraft's existing File Import, Media Browser and Effects / Presets workflows.

- Import PremiereData v3 `.prproj` object graphs (plain XML, UTF-16 or gzip): project bins, media references, sequences, track flags, exact clip/source ticks, links, nests, selected stock effects and timeline transitions.
- Import `.prfpset` trees into the persistent preset library, including folders, supported parameters/keyframes, Scale / Anchor to In / Anchor to Out timing, frame-relative geometry and Cross Dissolve transition presets.
- Use existing streaming media readers for relinking, preserve project-import/preset-application undo/redo, roll back failed library persistence and expose fidelity reports through commands and the UI. Presets read through host services, including filesystem-free web hosts.
- Bound document size, decompression, object expansion, nesting, keyframes and imported timing; reject malformed/cyclic inputs and unsafe retiming before mutating the document.

## Scope and fidelity

title: interchange: fix file:// URLs for Windows verbatim paths (FCP7 XML media offline in Premiere)
author: digitaldecaycreations-lgtm
body:
## Problem

On Windows, FCP7 XML exports write media paths like:

```xml
<pathurl>file://%3F/C:/Users/me/media/clipA.mp4</pathurl>
```

Imported media paths reach `path_to_file_url` in Windows verbatim form (`\\?\C:\...`, the form `std::fs::canonicalize` returns). After the backslash-to-slash replacement this becomes `//?/C:/...`. That matches the UNC branch, so `?` ends up as the URL host. Premiere Pro then can't resolve the files and opens the sequence with all media offline.

## Fix

Before building the URL, `path_to_file_url` now strips the verbatim prefix:
- `\\?\C:\x` → `C:/x` → `file://localhost/C:/x`
- `\\?\UNC\server\share\x` → `//server/share/x` → `file://server/share/x`

Ordinary paths are unchanged. There are two new assertions next to the existing `path_to_file_url` tests.

## Verification (Windows 11)

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-interchange --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test -p filmcraft-interchange` all pass.
- End to end: `filmcraft-cli` imported three MP4s, placed them, made a razor cut, and ran `file.exportFcp7Xml`. Before the fix, every `pathurl` was `file://%3F/C:/...`; after it, each is `file://localhost/C:/...`. The XML opens in **Premiere Pro 2026** with all media online, and the cut, linked audio and timing are intact.

title: #430, #224: select, edit, delete and resize transitions
author: swillunderscore
body:
Fixes #430 and #224. An applied transition could not be selected, edited, deleted or resized: clicking it did nothing, and Effect Controls stayed on "(no clip selected)".

It now follows Adobe's published behaviour (Align transitions, Change transition duration, Change transition settings):

- **Click** a transition to select it. It's outlined, and Shift adds or removes. It opens in **Effect Controls**: Duration (timecode), Alignment (Center at Cut, Start at Cut, End at Cut, plus Custom Start once it's dragged off-centre), Reverse, its own settings, and Reset.
- **Delete** removes it and leaves its clips.
- **Drag an end** to trim that end. **Drag the middle** to slide it over the cut, which makes it Custom Start.
- **Double-click** it for **Set Transition Duration**.

Every change is one undo step, including a whole drag or a value drag in Effect Controls.

### Choices where Adobe's pages are silent

I state these so you can say if you'd prefer otherwise:

- **Delete removes a selected transition.** The pages don't cover deleting transitions. This is how Delete works for clips and in every editor.
- **Dragging a transition's end trims that end only.** The other end stays, so a centred transition becomes Custom Start. Adobe's page shows the Trim-In / Trim-Out icon there. The "depends on the alignment" rule is written for the Duration value, so it applies to typed durations: Effect Controls' Duration and Set Transition Duration. I'm not certain how Premiere itself behaves when a centred transition's end is dragged, so if you know, I'll match it.
- **A transition can extend at most over the clips it joins**, from the outgoing clip's start to the incoming clip's end. Premiere limits it by handles, but FilmCraft doesn't check handles when applying a transition, so I didn't start here.

title: Project files: each sequence reopens with its playhead where it was left
author: liangforstudy
body:
## What and why

A project file already stores each sequence's zoom, scroll and track heights in its `view`, and the engine already keeps one playhead per sequence while a project is open (switching sequences returns each to where it was). But the playheads were not saved: after saving and reopening, every sequence started at zero.

This adds `playheads` (sequence id → `Tick`) to `ProjectView`, written beside the tabs and views and restored with them when **Restore open sequences when opening projects** is on.

- **Older files** have no `playheads` and open exactly as before (every playhead at zero). `skip_serializing_if` keeps it out of files where nothing moved, and older builds ignore the field.
- **Values from a file are not trusted:** ids that are not sequences are dropped, playheads are clamped to `0..=ProjectView::MAX_PLAYHEAD` (10,000,000 s, the same bound as a view's scroll) and snapped to a frame of their sequence, the way `set_playhead` does.
- A restored playhead is not an edit and does not mark the project dirty.
- `docs/project-files.md` mentions the new field.

## How it was tested

- New `each_sequence_reopens_with_its_playhead_where_it_was_left`: two sequences with different playheads survive save → reopen, an untouched sequence stays at zero, the preference off restores nothing, and a file with `playheads` removed opens with every playhead at zero. **It fails without the fix** (playhead comes back as `Tick(0)`).
- `a_damaged_view_in_a_project_file_is_cleaned_up_or_ignored` gains hostile playheads: negative, `i64::MAX`, off-frame, a non-sequence item and an unknown id.
- `the_view_of_a_deleted_sequence_is_forgotten` checks a deleted sequence's playhead is not written.
- The `filmcraft-format` view round trip now carries a playhead.
- End to end with `filmcraft-cli`: playhead set to 7 s, saved, reopened, comes back at 6.965 s (the frame boundary at 23.976).

title: fix(mcp): media_import schema mirrors file.import (#499)
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary
Fixes #499 — the MCP `media_import` tool now exposes the correct schema that mirrors the underlying `file.import` engine command.

## Problem
The `media_import` tool advertised "Import media files by absolute path" but its schema was `{"text": string}`. Agents had no way to know `text` was a file path, couldn't pass multiple files in one call, and couldn't set `bin` or `imageSequence` options.

## Solution
Created `MediaImportParams` struct with:
- `paths: Vec<String>` (required) — array of absolute paths
- `bin: Option<u64>` (optional) — bin ID to import into  
- `image_sequence: Option<bool>` (optional) — import numbered stills as a sequence

The tool now properly forwards all parameters to `file.import`.

## Files Changed
- `crates/automation/src/server.rs`: Added `MediaImportParams` struct, updated `media_import` tool implementation

## Testing
✅ `cargo fmt --check` — passed  
✅ `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — passed  
✅ `cargo test -p filmcraft-automation` — all 15 tests passed  

The fix is a schema correction that exposes existing `file.import` functionality. Existing engine tests verify `file.import` behavior with paths, bin, and imageSequence parameters.

## Known Limitations
None — this strictly expands capability without breaking changes.

title: ui: add an eyedropper to colour parameters (Ultra Key, Color Key...)
author: Guilhermeb-Ferrarezi
body:
﻿Closes #311

Adds an eyedropper to colour parameters in Effect Controls, so the Ultra Key key colour, Color Key's colour, mattes and every other `ParamKind::Color` can be picked from the footage instead of typed or eyeballed.

## How it works
- A pipette button sits next to each colour swatch. Click it to arm it, then click a pixel in the Program monitor; the parameter is filled with that colour. Esc (or clicking the pipette again) disarms it. The cursor is a crosshair while armed.
- The colour is the average of the 5x5 pixels around the click, so a noisy green screen gives its true green rather than one speckle.
- The colour is read from a render of the sequence at the playhead **with the armed effect switched off** (on a throw-away copy of the project, under its own frame-cache revision). Otherwise an Ultra Key that is already applied would have keyed the green out of the Program picture and there would be nothing left to pick.
- The value goes through `effects.setParam` (one undo step), stored the same way the colour picker beside it stores it (linear `Rgba`). Masks' colour parameters work too.
- The pipette is a new code-drawn icon (`Icon::Eyedropper`, original work, no assets), it registers an automation id (`effectControls.<effect>.<param>.eyedropper`), and the armed state is transient UI state (`UiState::eyedropper`, `serde(skip)`).
- Spanish catalog entries added for the two new strings.

I could not build locally (Windows Smart App Control blocks `cargo.exe` on my machine), so I ran the checks in GitHub Actions on my fork (Ubuntu, `ubuntu-latest`):

title: effects.setParam: choices by name, a `keyframe` option, and the keyframe count in the result
author: maccagnit
body:
Three small changes to `effects.setParam`, found while cutting a 47 s montage through the MCP server (about 1,600 commands, FilmCraft 0.4.0 on Windows). All three are about an agent not being able to tell what happened.

**1. A choice takes its option name as well as its index.**
`{"effect": "opacity", "param": "blend", "value": "Screen"}` now works, matched without case, as transition parameters (`sequence.setTransition`) and `graphics.set` already do. Before, only the index was accepted (`"value has the wrong type"`), so an agent had to count positions in the `options` array of `effects.list {"detail": true}`. A name that is not an option is an error that lists the options. Indexes behave exactly as before.

**2. `"keyframe": true` writes a keyframe and animates the parameter.**
`effects.setParam` with a `time` only writes a keyframe when the parameter is already animated; otherwise it sets the static value and the time is not used. That is the Effect Controls behaviour and it stays the default, but over MCP it is easy to send a series of `{value, time}` calls and get the last value everywhere with every call reporting success (it happened to me: a 75 to 100 scale ramp became a constant 100). With `"keyframe": true` the call is the stopwatch and the value in one step, the same option `clipMixer.set` has. A parameter that cannot be animated (a choice) refuses it.

**3. The result is `{"keyframes": n}` instead of `null`.**
`0` means the value is static, so the caller can see that its `time` did not produce a keyframe. Nothing in the repository reads the old `null` (the UI callers ignore the result).

The parameter doc string says all of this, so it shows up in `command_list`.

## Not changed

- A numeric choice index is still not range-checked (as before); I left that alone because some option lists are per-effect conventions (track choices) and I did not want to change what existing callers can store.
- `effects.setKeyframe` values: choices are not animatable, so n…

title: Linux: NVDEC hardware decoding for H.264 and HEVC
author: SilentYeti
body:
## What this does

Adds a second hardware decoder backend on Linux that talks to NVIDIA's proprietary driver directly, in `crates/platform/src/nvdec`.

- Codecs: H.264 8-bit and HEVC 8-bit and 10-bit, 4:2:0, progressive.
- `libnvcuvid.so.1` and `libcuda.so.1` are loaded at run time. Without them nothing is registered and startup is unchanged.
- The factory is registered in front of VA-API. What NVDEC declines still reaches VA-API, then the software decoders.
- Mid-stream failures fall back to software through the existing `HybridDecoder`.

## Why

NVIDIA's driver has no VA-API of its own. Today hardware decoding on NVIDIA only works if the separate `libva-nvidia-driver` package is installed. This backend removes that dependency.

On a machine that already has `libva-nvidia-driver`, the speed gain is small, because that driver also uses NVDEC underneath.

## How it works

- NVIDIA's parser takes Annex B access units, so there is no host-side DPB. The decoder is created in the parser's sequence callback.
- Pictures are read back as NV12 or P016 through the CUDA driver into the existing `biplanar::to_frame` path.
- The CUDA context is the one `nvenc::device` already retains. It gains push/pop current and copy-to-host.
- Callbacks never unwind into C. They record the first error and return 0.
- A seek recreates the parser and keeps the decoder.
- After a start at a CRA picture, its RASL pictures are not fed. Otherwise the parser shows the CRA picture with the wrong timestamp.

## Other changes

- `tests/setting.rs` expected the Media Foundation backend name on Linux and failed on any Linux machine with a hardware decoder. It now checks against the backend `register()` reports.
- The Hardware decoding tooltip mentions NVDEC. The Spanish row in `es.tsv` is updated to match.
- README, platform README and ADR 0001 describe the new backend.

## Testing

Tested on an RTX 3080, driver 615.71.09, Linux x86-64.

- `tests/nvdec.rs`: bit-exact with the software decoders over whole…

author: ahmedhosnypro
body:
Linux opens its window undecorated: the 38 pt header is the one and only top bar, as in Premiere — the app icon leads the bar where the OS bar carried it, and the minimize / maximize-restore / close caption buttons sit flush in the top-right corner.

Fixes #433 (the second option there: an in-app title bar, as PhotoCraft does on Linux).

## Same implementation as PhotoCraft

This is the same implementation as the PhotoCraft app's title bar (`photocraft/crates/ui-egui/src/titlebar.rs`), written for FilmCraft's header: the same 10 pt caption glyphs (minimize bar, maximize square, restore two-square, close X), the same 46 pt caption targets, the same hover fills (close red `caption_close`, new theme token), the same edge/corner resize zones and the same "close = the window manager's close" behavior.

## The change

- **Undecorated window** (`apps/filmcraft/src/main.rs`): Linux-only; macOS keeps its native traffic lights, Windows its OS title bar. `FILMCRAFT_DECORATIONS=1` restores the OS title bar as an escape hatch and disables the in-header buttons.
- **App icon at the start of the bar** (`brand::paint_mark`): the 128 px FilmCraft tile, 20 pt, where PhotoCraft shows its mark.
- **Caption buttons** (`header.rs`): flush right, full bar height, 46 pt cells; tooltips Minimize / Maximize (Restore when maximized) / Close, translated (Spanish added); automation ids `header.window.*` and `header.brandMark` for agents.
- **Edge resize** (`lib.rs::edge_resize`): invisible zones along the window edges/corners begin an OS resize; disabled while maximized or full screen.
- The rest of the bar keeps its window duties: dragging it moves the window, double-click maximizes.

## Follow-up fixes included (from the branch work review)

1. **Resize zones no longer steal caption clicks** — `edge_resize` takes the header height; the North zone is gone and the East/NW/NE zones start below the header, so the caption strip and the header's drag area own their input. New test `caption_clicks_w…
