title: #480: exports no longer stop for good when a clip's decoding uses rayon (rotated iPhone HEVC clips)
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Fixes #480.

## What was wrong

Reproduced with the three public iPhone files from the issue (sha256 checked) on current `main`, Linux, 16 threads: the 3-clip export stopped making frames in 5 of 16 runs, and in 7 of 14 more runs later. The process stayed alive at 0 % CPU with the output file no longer growing.

A thread dump at the stall (`gdb`, export run under it) shows it is not the HEVC decoder's frame threads (they are idle) but a deadlock in the frame cache (`GopCache`) on the global rayon pool:

- 15 export frame jobs (`Pipeline::frame` on rayon) wait in `GopCache::frame_late` for the cache's lock.
- The lock holder is in `GopCache::store` → `VideoFrame::rotated` → `rotate_plane`, which splits the rotation over rayon (`par_chunks_mut`). It waits in `join` for a piece another worker took.
- That worker, while waiting inside the piece, picked up another frame job asking the same cache for a frame, and blocks on the lock. The piece the holder waits for is under it on that worker's stack.

Each waits for the other, for good. The iPhone clips trigger it because their display rotation (-90°) is applied to every decoded frame under the cache's lock. The same can happen with anything else that uses rayon under that lock: cropping (`clap`), and decoders that split pictures over rayon (ProRes, DNx, APV, MPEG-2, VP9). The existing guard (`DecodingGuard` → `private_frame`) only covers a nested request on the *same* thread.

## The fix

`crates/codecs/src/gop.rs`:

- A cache's decoding, run with its lock held (decoder calls, crop, rotation), now runs through `isolated`, on a separate rayon pool (`decode-N` threads). Pieces of that work are then only ever picked up by threads that never wait for a cache's lock.
- A caller that is itself a rayon worker would still run other jobs of its own pool while waiting for the decode pool, and some of those could need a cache lock while it holds one. It waits on a plain scoped thread instead, which does no rayon work. Callers that ar…

title: #461: interchange import links media through the streaming reader
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #461.

## Problem
`file.import` of an interchange document (FCP7 XML, OTIO, EDL, AAF…) merges the cut, then links each media file it names. That step read every file whole into memory (`services.read_file` + `MediaPool::open_bytes` in `crates/engine/src/interchange.rs`). With multi-GB 4K MP4s on an external SSD, that is where the 97 s / 66 s went, and the bytes stayed resident afterwards. A direct import of the same files opens them through the host's random-access reader and reads only the container index, hence under 1 s.

## Fix
Link through `MediaPool::open_file`, as `import_streamed` (direct import) already does: the reader reads the container index now and samples on demand. A missing file still ends up in `offlineMedia`, and hosts without a reader (`Services::reader` returns `None`) still read the file whole, as before.

title: #333: Fade In and Fade Out presets add up on one clip
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #333.

## Problem
`presets.apply` replaced an intrinsic effect (Opacity) wholesale (`put_effects` in `crates/engine/src/presets.rs`). Fade In and Fade Out both keyframe Opacity, so whichever was applied second wiped the other's keyframes.

## Fix
When a preset lands on an intrinsic effect, the clip's existing keyframes for a parameter are kept if they lie outside the time span the preset animates for that parameter; the preset's keyframes are added and the list re-sorted. Re-applying the same preset still replaces its own ramp, and static (non-animated) preset values behave exactly as before.

- Existing presets tests (intrinsic replace, built-ins, retime modes) still pass.

title: M5: Accelerate Apple Silicon media and GPU effect pipelines
author: notnotshuts
body:
Video playback and GPU export currently copy decoded frames through CPU planes, repeat point-effect passes, and recompute mask geometry. This change reduces those costs and bounds caches on low-memory Apple Silicon machines.

### Changes

- Retain eligible VideoToolbox 8/10-bit surfaces and import their planes into Metal, with lazy exact CPU materialization and fallback for unsupported layouts/devices.
- Fuse point effects; compile bounded shader variants in the background; cache exact mask coverage; use shared-memory prefix-scan blur for measured radii 8–32.
- Extend live GPU SDR grading/keying and mask handling while preserving CPU fallbacks and effect ordering.
- Apply RAM/pressure-aware frame, pool and GPU source-cache budgets; feed eligible SDR hardware exports through Metal-to-NV12 surfaces directly into VideoToolbox.
- Document Apple Silicon build settings, architecture, reproducible benchmarks and limitations.

### Measurements

On A18 Pro / 8 GiB RAM, with hot modules built at opt-level 3, 4K path medians improve by 1.96× (8-bit native frame preparation/draw), 4.48× (10-bit), 1.37× (specialised already-fused effect chain), 2.60× (unchanged cached mask), and 3.75× (radius-32 six-pass blur). These measure separate warmed paths, exclude compressed decoding/UI/readback, and are not whole-editor FPS. Full methodology is in `docs/performance.md`.

### Validation

- 409 targeted unit/integration tests passed, including actual VideoToolbox/Metal checks, GPU/CPU parity, lazy materialization and surface lifetime, native export and fallback coverage.

author: vangel76

## Problem
"In Effect Controls, every option (Scale, Position, etc.) should have a ⟳ icon. Crucially, pressing it should NOT delete keyframes."

I checked it in a headless wgpu screenshot: it doesn't overlap values, combo boxes or the keyframe navigator.

title: #457: Settings > Appearance > UI Scale
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #457.

## Problem
FilmCraft has no UI scale preference. The interface always follows the scale the desktop reports (150% on the reporter's Mint XFCE / X11 setup), and the only way to change it is Ctrl+- / Ctrl++, which is lost on restart. PhotoCraft has a UI scale setting; FilmCraft didn't.

## Fix
- `crates/engine`: new preference `appearance.uiScale` in Settings ▸ Appearance, a choice of Auto (default) or 75 / 100 / 125 / 150 / 175 / 200 / 250 / 300 %. It goes through the existing schema, so `prefs.set` rejects any other value and a bad value in a settings file falls back to Auto. `AppearancePrefs::ui_scale_factor()` resolves it.
- `crates/ui-egui`: `apply_ui_scale` (run from `apply_prefs`) sets egui's zoom so that a point is that many physical pixels, whatever the system reports (100% = one pixel per point). It only acts when the setting or the system scale changes, so Ctrl+- / Ctrl++ still zoom for the session, and moving the window to a monitor with another scale keeps the chosen size. Switching back to Auto gives the system's scale back.

## Tests
- `panels::settings::tests::ui_scale_overrides_the_system_scale_and_auto_restores_it`: with a native scale of 1.5, Auto leaves the zoom at 1.0, 100% sets it to 1/1.5, a later Ctrl+- zoom is not undone on the next frame, an unlisted value (`130`) is rejected, and Auto restores 1.0. It fails without the fix.

title: platform: look up kVTCompressionPropertyKey_ConstantBitRate at run time
author: abdelkabirouadoukou
body:
Fixes the app aborting at launch on macOS 12 (Monterey) with dyld: Symbol not found: _kVTCompressionPropertyKey_ConstantBitRate.

That key only exists from macOS 13, but it was linked directly, so dyld refused to start the app on macOS 11 and 12 even though the encoder already had an average-bitrate fallback. The key is now looked up at run time with dlsym: macOS 13+ behaves as before, and older versions take the existing fallback.

title: Pass Hard Limiter look-ahead into the DSP limiter
author: vbasky
body:
Closes #542.

Hard Limiter stored Look-Ahead Time but never passed it to the DSP limiter, so 0 ms and 30 ms mixed the same clip. The limiter now sizes its look-ahead from that parameter (0–30 ms) and pre-rolls for the chosen window.

The DSP delay line is allocated for the 30 ms maximum so changing look-ahead between blocks stays within the existing buffer except for the moving-average ring.

Tested: `cargo test -p filmcraft-audio-dsp limiter_lookahead` and `cargo test -p filmcraft-render audio_fx_limiter`.

title: Apply Ultra Key Setting as a parameter preset
author: vbasky
body:
Closes #458.

Ultra Key Setting (Default / Relaxed / Aggressive) only scaled two internal multipliers, so the matte stayed at Default. Switching Setting now writes a Premiere-like parameter set (transparency, shadow, tolerance, pedestal, choke, soften, contrast, desaturate, and related matte values). Custom leaves the current values. The renderer uses the same table so older instances that stored Aggressive without rewritten params still key that way.

Tested: `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine ultra_key_setting` and `cargo test -p filmcraft-render keyers_known`.

title: Add file.import replace mode for empty-project round-trips
author: vbasky
body:
Closes #592.

`file.import` still merges into the current project by default. `file.import {replace: true}` starts from `file.newProject` with the same name, then imports, so a headless import→export round-trip contains only the imported timeline.

Documented in `docs/architecture.md`. Merge-by-default is unchanged.

Tested: `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine import_replace_starts`.

title: Treat media extensions as case-insensitive on import
author: vbasky
body:
Closes #593.

Camera files such as `CLIP.MOV` were easy to miss on Linux because some matching assumed lowercase suffixes. Import, the media browser, and image-sequence sibling numbering now treat extensions as case-insensitive. Native picker filters already covered mixed case.

Transform listed a shutter angle but had no override, so that angle was never used for motion blur. The effect now has **Use Effect Shutter Angle**. When it is on and the angle is greater than zero, the CPU path samples the animated transform across that shutter.

title: #342: ProRes 4444 and 4444 XQ export, with alpha
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #342.

## Problem
`filmcraft-prores` already encodes ProRes 4444 / 4444 XQ (optionally with alpha), but export only knew the four 422 flavours: `prores_profile` mapped anything else to HQ, and the ProRes export encoder always built a 4:2:2 frame without alpha. So there was no way to export 4444, and graphics lost their transparency.

## Fix
- `proresProfile` accepts `4444` and `4444xq` (`prores_profile()` in `crates/export/src/lib.rs`).
- For these profiles the ProRes export encoder converts each frame to 10-bit 4:4:4 (new `to_yuv444_10`, BT.709 for SDR, the signal's matrix for HDR). With **Include Alpha Channel** it also codes the straight alpha of the picture. A new `ExportSettings::supports_alpha()` / `keeps_alpha()` decides this, and the pipeline uses it so these frames are no longer flattened over black.
- Export Settings: the ProRes Profile combo offers Apple ProRes 4444 and 4444 XQ, and the Alpha checkbox is shown for them.
- New presets: Apple ProRes 4444, Apple ProRes 4444 with Alpha, Apple ProRes 4444 XQ.
- The summary text names the profile. MXF OP1a ProRes writes coding label 5/6, and the descriptor keeps the 12-bit 4:4:4 depth `PictureDesc::new` sets, instead of always forcing 10.

## Tests
- `filmcraft-export` `tests::prores_4444_export_roundtrip`: 4444 and 4444 XQ exports decode as `ProRes 4444` / `ProRes 4444 XQ` 4:4:4 frames with the right colour. A half-transparent matte keeps alpha ≈128 with Include Alpha Channel and is opaque without it. This test fails on main, where the export comes out as 422 HQ.
- `filmcraft-engine` `export_tests::every_builtin_preset_exports_and_ffprobe_confirms` now covers the new presets: ffprobe profile `4444` / `XQ`, a `yuva444…` pix_fmt only for the alpha preset, and bitrate within the nominal bound. title: #239: Position keyframes get the value and velocity graphs
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #239.

## Problem
Effect Controls only offered the graph twirl-down (value and velocity graphs) for scalar (`Float`) parameters. Position is a point parameter (`Vec2`), so you could keyframe Position but never open its graphs, while Scale's graphs worked.

## Fix
`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/effect_controls.rs`:
- New `graphable()` check (Float or Vec2) is used both for the twirl-down in `param_row` and for drawing the graph rows.
- `graph_rows` handles a point as two curves: X (accent colour) and Y (green), with a small X/Y legend. Each keyframe gets a draggable dot on each curve. Dragging one sends `effects.setKeyframe` with `[x, y]` and changes only that coordinate.
- The Bezier influence handles sit on the X curve only, because both coordinates share one influence.
- The velocity graph shows the speed along the path, `|d(x,y)/dt|`. For scalars it shows the signed derivative, as before.
- NaN "auto" coordinates are skipped instead of drawn. The value range falls back to a sane default if nothing is finite. Velocity is computed with `windows(2)` instead of index arithmetic.
- Scalar graphs keep their current automation ids. Point keyframes register `effectControls.<param>.graph.keyframe.<t>.x` / `.y`.

## Tests
- New `position_graph_drags_one_coordinate_of_a_point_keyframe`: draws the real graph for Motion ▸ Position with two keyframes and drags the X keyframe up. It checks that X rises, Y and the other keyframe stay the same, it is one undo step, and the `.y` automation id is registered. Before this fix no keyframe dot was painted for a Vec2 parameter, so the test failed.
- The existing scalar graph drag test was adjusted to take the parameter id as an argument and still passes.

title: fix(monitor): make Button Editor customize transport controls

existing serde default behavior.

Existing saved UI configurations can load without requiring

title: feat(timeline): rename video and audio tracks from their headers
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

FilmCraft already supports renaming video and audio tracks through
its command interface, but the Timeline does not expose a
corresponding rename control.

Users cannot conveniently assign descriptive names such as
"Dialogue", "Music", or "B-roll" while editing.

## Root cause

The engine's `timeline.setTrack` command already accepts a `name`
parameter and records the change in edit history.

However, the Timeline track headers only display the track name.
They do not provide an interaction for changing it.

## Changes

- Add a Rename context menu to Timeline track headers.
- Open the menu by right-clicking the track-name area.
- Provide an editable text field with Apply and Cancel controls.
- Reject empty or whitespace-only track names.
- Commit valid changes through the existing `timeline.setTrack`
  engine command.
- Preserve the existing undo/redo and project persistence behavior.
- Add automation IDs for the rename field and Apply action.
- Add a headless UI regression test covering rename and undo.

## Implementation

The change reuses FilmCraft's existing track settings command.

It does not introduce a separate rename mechanism, modify the
project file format, or change track identity.

Video and audio tracks use the same interaction.

## Validation

- Reviewed the existing Timeline header implementation.

title: #680: Shift+Delete ripple deletes with the Timeline focused
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes point 1 of #680 (Part of #680).

## Problem
With the Timeline focused, Shift+Delete removed the selected clip like plain Delete and left a gap. `handle_shortcuts` tried every binding of the focused panel before the application-wide ones, and egui's `consume_key` ignores extra Shift and Alt. So the Timeline's own `Delete` → Clear binding (added for #243) matched the Shift+Delete press before the app-wide `Shift+Delete` → Ripple Delete got a turn.

## Fix
Candidate bindings from both scopes are now sorted by how many modifiers they name, most first. The sort is stable, so a panel shortcut still wins over an application shortcut on the same chord. The modifier count moved into `menus::specificity`, which `menus::bindings` already used for its own sort.

Point 2 of #680 (Alt+click on one side of a linked clip, then Delete, removes both) is a separate cause and is not touched here.

title: #279: WAV opens in place and reads only the samples asked for
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #279.

## Problem
WAV had no streaming reader, so `open_reader` fell back to reading the whole file into memory (`read_range` over the full length), and `WavSource` held those bytes for as long as the clip stayed open. A 90-minute WAV cost about its own size in memory, and `file.import` blocked until the whole file had been read.

## Fix
- `WavSource` now reads through a `SharedReader`. `WavSource::open` walks the chunk headers (`fmt `, `data`, `bext`, `iXML`) without touching the samples. The walk is capped at 65 536 chunks, and the iXML read at 1 MiB.
- `audio()` reads only the frame range the request needs, in blocks of 4096 output frames. If an extreme resampling ratio would make one block span more than 4 MiB of the file, it reads just the two frames each output sample needs instead. Indexing uses `get` and checked/saturating math.
- `open_reader` / `open_reader_within` open WAV this way after the registered reader openers and before the whole-file fallback. This means the Media Browser's 64 MiB probe limit no longer refuses large WAVs.
- `WavSource::parse(name, bytes)` still works on in-memory bytes (it wraps them in a `MemReader`), so `open_bytes` callers behave as before.
- Read errors (including the web reader's `WouldBlock`/pending) are passed on as `MediaError::Io` instead of turning into silence, so pending reads are retried as they are for MP4.

`file.import` itself still runs on the UI thread (the issue's second, independent direction). For WAV, opening now costs only a few header reads.

## Tests
- `reader::tests::wav_opens_in_place_and_reads_only_requested_samples` (new): opens a 20 s stereo WAV with a whole-file limit of one sniffing head. It checks that opening reads no more than the head plus the chunk headers, that 480 frames from the middle read exactly the 481 frames they need with the right sample values, and that a request past the end reads nothing. This test fails without the fix: the WAV is refused as too large to read whole.

author: vangel76

title: #67: media files share a bounded pool of open descriptors
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #67.

## Problem
`FileReader` (`crates/media/src/reader.rs`) owned its `std::fs::File` for as long as the reader lived, so every open media source pinned one file descriptor. A project with hundreds of sources hits the soft descriptor limit (256 by default on macOS, 1024 on Linux). After that, opening fails with `MediaError::Io` and the remaining media show as failed or offline.

## Fix
I went with the LRU option from the issue, so no `setrlimit` and no FFI:
- `FileReader` now stores its path and opened length. It borrows the file from a shared pool that keeps at most `MAX_OPEN_FILES` (128) files open.
- Past the cap, the pool closes the least recently read file. That reader reopens its file by path on its next read.
- If another thread is still reading from a file when it is evicted, the file stays open until that read finishes (`Arc<File>`).
- A reopened file that is now shorter than when it was first opened (replaced or truncated) is refused with an error instead of being read as the old file. A longer one (still being written) is read up to the opened length, as before.
- Dropping a reader closes its file. The public API (`FileReader::open`, `ByteReader`) is unchanged.

## Tests
- New test `reader::tests::more_file_readers_than_the_pool_holds_stay_readable`: opens 5 readers on a pool capped at 2 and reads them in turns. It checks that every read returns the right file's bytes, that the pool never holds more than 2 open files, that a file truncated after its reader was evicted is refused, and that dropping the readers empties the pool.
- The existing `file_reader_reads_ranges_in_place` still passes.

## Gates
Run locally:
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-media --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-media`
- `cargo xtask layers`

title: #614: Head, Head and Tail and Continuous video thumbnails in the Timeline
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #614.

## Problem
A video clip in the Timeline only ever showed one thumbnail, the frame at `source_in`, at its head. **Show Video Thumbnails** was a plain on/off switch (`show_thumbnails: bool`), so at high zoom the rest of a wide clip stayed a flat colour.

## Fix
- **Modes**: the Timeline wrench menu keeps **Show Video Thumbnails** and adds **Head** (the default, as before), **Head and Tail** and **Continuous** as radio items under it. They are disabled while thumbnails are off. Automation ids: `timeline.settings.showThumbnails` and `timeline.settings.thumbnails.<head|headAndTail|continuous>`.
- **Continuous**: aspect-correct tiles across the clip, on a grid anchored at the clip's head. When you scroll, tiles already on screen keep their frames and only new tiles are requested. Only tiles inside the panel's clip rect are listed, with at most 256 per clip. Each tile shows the source time under its left edge, mapped through `source_time_at` (speed, reverse, frame holds) and the multicam angle, the same path the head thumbnail uses. The last partial tile is cut off by the clip rect. Frames go through the existing `FilmcraftApp::thumbnail` path: frame cache, background priority 50, small thumbnail decoders.
- **Head and Tail**: the head tile plus the clip's last frame at the right edge. Clips too narrow for two tiles (or for one tile in Continuous) show only their head.
- **Persistence**: `TimelineView::thumbnail_mode` is a new `#[serde(default)]` field (default Head). The `show_thumbnails` bool stays as the Off switch, so existing settings keep working with no migration. `ui.set {timeline: {thumbnails: "off"|"head"|"headAndTail"|"continuous"}}` sets the mode and rejects unknown names. Documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`.
- The new strings go through `tl!`, with es / zh-cn / ja catalog entries.
- Small hardening while in there: the multicam lookup uses `video_tracks.get(ti)` instead of indexing, and a zero or non-finite media aspect draws no thumbnail.

title: #313: J/K/L shuttle the Source monitor both ways at up to 8x

title: #411: importing a folder keeps its structure as bins
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes point 3 of #411 (Part of #411).

## Problem
Importing a folder from the Media Browser (`mediaBrowser.import`, also used by File ▸ Import from Media Browser and by dragging a folder out of the browser) took only the folder's first-level files and dropped them flat into the target bin. Sub-folders were skipped and no bins were created, so the folder hierarchy was lost.

## Fix
`crates/engine/src/media_browser.rs`:
- A folder becomes a bin named after it (inside `bin`, else the root) holding its files. Each sub-folder that contains media becomes a bin inside that one, recursively, as Premiere's Media Browser does. Folders without media get no bin.
- The walk is bounded (depth 32, at most 4096 folders) so symlinked folder loops can't run away.
- Each folder's files go through `file.import` with that folder's bin, so Ingest settings, captions and the rest behave as before. The merged result keeps `items` and `errors` and adds the new `bins`.
- Plain file imports and Import as Image Sequence behave as before.

Points 1 (deleting bins) and 2 (multi-selection) of #411 are covered by the open PRs #622 and #607.

## Tests
`media_browser_tests::importing_a_folder_mirrors_its_sub_folders_as_bins` imports a nested folder tree from the fake filesystem. It checks the bin tree (`Shoot > Day 1 > Cam A`), which files land in which bin, and that an empty sub-folder gets no bin. The test fails without the fix. The existing folder-import assertion still passes.

title: fix(captions): reject overflowing TTML times and round extreme clocks safely
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Importing malformed TTML subtitle files can produce incorrect
caption timestamps.

The TTML parser calculates time expressions using i128 arithmetic
but converts the result to i64 without checking whether the value
fits.

For example, an expression such as `999999999999999s` can wrap
into an unrelated timestamp instead of being rejected.

The shared caption-clock formatter also performs an addition
that can overflow for extreme input-derived timestamps.

## Root cause

- TTML time expressions are converted using unchecked `as i64`
  casts.
- Clock expressions do not consistently validate minute, second,
  frame, and subframe boundaries.
- Caption timestamp formatting performs rounding arithmetic
  within the i64 range.

## Changes

- Use checked i64 conversions for calculated TTML timestamps.
- Reject oversized time expressions rather than wrapping them.
- Validate minute and second boundaries.
- Validate frame numbers against the nominal frame rate.
- Validate subframe numbers against the configured subframe rate.
- Use i128 arithmetic when rounding caption timestamps for output.
- Preserve valid TTML timing behavior.

## Regression Coverage

Added tests for:

- Oversized hours, minutes, seconds, milliseconds, frames,
  and tick expressions.
- Invalid clock-time components.
- Out-of-range frame and subframe indices.
- Valid subframe expressions.
- Malformed TTML cues alongside valid cues.
- Caption-clock formatting at extreme i64 values.

## Validation

- Reviewed affected parsing and formatting paths.
- Added focused regression tests.
- Committed changes to an isolated branch based on upstream main.
- Verified the branch was pushed successfully.

Rust tests, formatting checks, and upstream CI have not been
executed for this commit.

## Compatibility

No project-format changes, new dependencies, or codec changes.

Valid subtitle timestamps retain their existing representation.
Invalid or unrepresentable timestamps are rejected instead of
silently produc…

title: fix(captions): preserve literal angle brackets in EBU STL export
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Exporting EBU STL subtitles can silently remove ordinary caption
text containing angle brackets.

For example:

    2 < 3 > 1

The STL encoder interprets `< 3 >` as markup and discards it,
causing the exported subtitle to lose part of its original text.

This also affects expressions such as:

    x < y > z

The resulting subtitle no longer matches the editor's caption.

## Root cause

`encode_text` in `crates/captions/src/stl.rs` treats every sequence
beginning with `<` and ending with `>` as markup.

It discards unrecognized sequences without distinguishing actual
markup from ordinary text.

Consequently, literal comparison expressions can lose content
during export.

## Changes

- Distinguish plausible markup tags from literal angle-bracket text.
- Preserve comparison expressions containing whitespace or numeric
  content between angle brackets.
- Continue translating recognized italic and underline tags into
  their corresponding EBU STL control bytes.
- Preserve the existing handling of whitespace-tolerant styling tags.
- Keep the change localized to STL text encoding.

## Regression Coverage

Added a regression test that:

1. Creates a subtitle containing literal comparison expressions.
2. Exports the subtitle to EBU STL.
3. Imports the generated STL data.
4. Checks that the original caption text is preserved.
5. Checks that recognized italic styling continues to generate
   the appropriate control bytes.

## Validation

- Reviewed the existing STL encoding and decoding paths.
- Added a focused round-trip regression test.
- Verified the implementation commits and changed files on the fork.
- Rust tests and formatting checks have not been executed.
- Upstream CI has not been run.

## Compatibility

No changes to the STL file structure, project format, dependencies,
or public APIs.

The change preserves additional literal subtitle content while
retaining existing recognized styling behavior.

- While the field has focus it shows what you type, even when that isn't a colour yet.
- Each valid colour is saved as you type it, so the swatch and the preview follow along.
- Clicking away shows the last valid colour again, so a half-typed value never sticks.

- `panels/settings.rs`: `color_field` keeps the typed text in egui's temporary memory while the field has focus and saves each valid `#rrggbb` as it comes. It is the only typed hex field in the app; the other colour fields (label colours, the menu dialogs) are swatches only.

title: Captions: delete caption tracks from the timeline and Delete Tracks dialog
author: impostazioni
body:
`captions.deleteTrack` exists in the engine, but it has no menu path and nothing in the UI calls it, and `Sequence ▸ Delete Tracks…` only handles video and audio. - Captions on deleted tracks are dropped from `caption_selection`.
- All deletions in one call are a single undo step.

**Dialog** (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/dialogs.rs`, `state.rs`): Delete Tracks gets a Caption Tracks section ("Delete Caption Tracks" with All Empty Tracks or `C1`…`Cn`).

title: fix(cli): honor global version queries and space-separated GPU options
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Two documented CLI argument forms were not handled correctly:

## Root cause

Version detection ran before normal argument parsing, and `--gpu-rendering` was missing from the parser's list of value-taking options.

## Changes

- Recognize `--version` after preceding global options.
- Preserve the existing `-V` alias and help behavior.
- Parse `--gpu-rendering auto|off` as a valued option, including space-separated syntax.
- Add argument-parser regression tests.

title: fix(tts-text): preserve amounts and numeric units in narration
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

The narration text normalizer could change the meaning of supported numeric input:

1. Short hyphen-separated sequences such as `5-10-15` dropped an interior number.
2. Decimal and whitespace-separated percentages such as `20.5%` and `50 %` lost the word "percent".
3. Currency amounts such as `$1.5` were interpreted as one dollar and five cents instead of one dollar and fifty cents.

These errors occur before phonemization and can change the information represented by the narration script.

## Root cause

- The short digit-group parser emitted only the first and final values for certain multi-group inputs.
- Percentage parsing handled an immediately attached `%` after integers but did not account for decimal numbers or whitespace.
- Money parsing interpreted a one-digit fractional component directly as minor currency units.

## Changes

- Preserve every number in short hyphen-separated numeric sequences.
- Retain existing two-number range readings and phone-like digit-by-digit normalization.
- Recognize percentage signs after decimal numbers and optional whitespace.
- Interpret single-digit monetary fractions according to their decimal place value.
- Add focused regression tests for US and British English, including grouped numbers, percentage variants, currency amounts, and existing phone-number behavior.

## Validation

- Regression tests added but not executed in this environment.
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-tts-text`, formatting, linting, and CI remain pending.
- Neural speech synthesis and audio playback were not tested.
- The pushed branch and its source diff were verified against upstream.

## Issues

Fixes #716
Fixes #717
Fixes #718

title: fix(edl): retain named audio crossfades when importing EDL
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Importing an EDL with a named audio dissolve could replace the intended transition with Constant Power.

This affected supported names including Constant Gain and Exponential Fade, including EDL files exported by FilmCraft itself.

The import report could also incorrectly claim that a supported audio transition was unsupported and imported as Cross Dissolve.

## Root cause

EDL import resolved named transitions using video-effect definitions before determining the destination track kind.

When the transition was subsequently placed on an audio track, the importer replaced the incompatible video effect with Constant Power.

## Changes

- Resolve EDL transitions using the destination track kind.
- Maintain separate cached transition definitions for video and audio channels.
- Preserve named Constant Gain, Exponential Fade, and Constant Power audio transitions.
- Keep Constant Power as the default for unnamed audio dissolves.
- Preserve warnings and fallback behavior for unsupported transition names.
- Add synthetic EDL regression cases covering named audio transitions, unknown effects, unnamed dissolves, and named video transitions.
- Verify transition timing, alignment, and clip endpoints in the added tests.

## Validation

title: #711: named audio dissolves keep their effect on EDL import
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #711.

## Problem
The EDL importer resolved an event's `* EFFECT NAME:` once, as a video transition (`transition_effect(name, false, …)`), and then swapped any non-audio result for Constant Power on audio tracks. Because of that, `CONSTANT GAIN` and `EXPONENTIAL FADE` were imported as Constant Power with the warning "transition … is not supported; imported as Cross Dissolve". This also happened when re-importing an EDL that FilmCraft had exported itself. `CONSTANT POWER` kept its effect but got the same false warning.

## Fix
- `crates/interchange/src/common.rs`: moved the alias table out into `transition_alias`, and added `audio_transition_named`, which looks a name up as an audio transition (alias, id or display name) without writing to the report.
- `crates/interchange/src/edl.rs`: audio channels of a dissolve use the named audio transition when there is one. The name is only resolved as a video transition, which is where the warnings come from, when the event has a video channel or the name is not an audio transition. Unknown names behave as before (warning, Constant Power on audio). On an A/V event, the video track gets Cross Dissolve and the audio track gets the named audio transition.

## Tests
`named_audio_dissolves_keep_their_effect` in `crates/interchange/tests/edl.rs` covers:
- Constant Gain, Exponential Fade and Constant Power on an `A` event: each keeps its effect, with no "not supported" warning.
- An unknown name: still warns and falls back to Constant Power.
- A `B` (A/V) event named Constant Gain: Cross Dissolve on video, Constant Gain on audio.

This test fails on `main` (`constant_power` != `constant_gain`).

title: #714: an MP4 without an edit list starts at its first picture
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #714.

## Problem
An MP4 video track with no edit list (x264 output written with `-use_editlist 0`, or a fragmented MP4) kept its raw first PTS as its origin. That PTS is the B-frame composition delay, two frames in the report. So media time zero repeated the first picture for the length of the delay. The clip lasts the media duration (correct, 0.48 s), which meant the last two pictures never appeared in a sequence made from it: `[0, 0, 0, 1, …, 9]` instead of `[0, 1, …, 11]`.

## Fix
`crates/codecs/src/mp4.rs`: after opening, if the video track has no edit list and its first picture starts after zero, every track moves back by the earliest start among the video and audio tracks. ffmpeg does the same with an input's start time.
- Video-only files (the reported case, regular and fragmented) start at their first picture and show every picture once.
- A file whose audio starts at zero is not shifted, so A/V sync stays as it was.
- Tracks with an edit list (empty-edit delays, B-frame skips) are never rebased. The issue's `-itsoffset 0.2` control is unchanged.

## Tests
- `mp4::tests::unedited_composition_delay_starts_at_the_first_picture`: a four-picture ProRes MOV with a constant composition offset and no `elst` must show one picture per frame, in order, over four frames. It fails without the fix (`[10, 10, 10, 69]`).
- Also checked by hand against ffmpeg-generated fixtures (not committed). Video-only no-edit MP4: all 12 pictures, in order, over 12 frames. A/V no-edit MP4 with audio at 0: unchanged. Explicit 0.2 s empty-edit control: unchanged.

## Gates

- `cargo test -p filmcraft-codecs` (lib and integration tests, all green)

title: #721: 5.1 AAC imports decode in WAV/SMPTE channel order
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #721.

## Problem
Our AAC decoder (`filmcraft-aac`) outputs channels in AAC element order — C, L, R, Ls, Rs, LFE for channel configuration 6 — and `PacketDecoder` in `filmcraft-codecs` passed that through unchanged. Everything downstream (mixer, 5.1 panner, loudness, WAV/MP4 export) uses WAV/SMPTE order L, R, C, LFE, Ls, Rs (`audio-dsp/src/channels.rs`). So a 5.1 AAC import put centre in L, L in R, R in C, the surrounds one slot early and LFE in Rs, which matches the 500/300/400/700/800/60 Hz export in the report. The export path already reorders for the AAC encoder; the decode path did not.

## Fix
`PacketDecoder` now reorders our AAC decoder's output into WAV/SMPTE order for channel configurations 3–6 (`aac_to_wav_order`), the same way the AC-3 decoder and Opus mapping family 1 already do. Configurations 1, 2, 7 and PCE layouts keep the decoded order. The Opus reorder now uses the same bounds-checked helper (`get_mut` instead of indexing; a decode whose channel count doesn't match the order is left as it is).

## Tests
- `audio::surround_order_tests::aac_51_decodes_in_wav_order`: encodes six distinct tones with our AAC encoder (fed in AAC order, as the exporter feeds it), decodes them through `PacketDecoder::aac` and checks that each output channel carries its own WAV-order tone. Fails without the fix.
- `audio::surround_order_tests::reorder_leaves_mismatched_channel_counts_alone`.

## Gates

- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-codecs -p filmcraft-audio-dsp --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-codecs` (all pass)

title: #710: --version works after global options
author: vangel76
body:

## Problem
`filmcraft-cli --demo --version`, `--compact --version` and `--data-dir <dir> --version` printed `missing subcommand` and exited 2, although the docs say options may go anywhere. `cli()` only recognised `--version` / `-V` as the very first argument (`std::env::args().nth(1)`); after a global option the parser took `--version` as a flag and no subcommand was left.

This still happens before the hardware decoders and GPU renderer are registered, so a version query stays cheap. `--help` is still checked first, so `--help` anywhere keeps printing the reference (one side effect: `--version --help` now prints help, matching the desktop app's `parse_args`).

title: graphics: shape handles change the shape's Size, Shift keeps the ratio
author: ReReddo
body:
Dragging a handle of a rectangle, ellipse or polygon in the Program monitor changed the layer's Scale, and a corner scaled width and height alike. So a shape couldn't be made wider or taller from a corner; you had to find an edge handle or type a Size in Properties.

In Premiere the handles change the shape itself (its Path) and leave the layer's Transform alone: the anchor point stays where it is while the shape gets wider or taller, even when the shape shrinks away from it, and a corner moves freely. Now FilmCraft does the same:

- **The handles change the shape's Size**, the equivalent of Premiere's Path. Scale is untouched.
- **The dragged side or corner follows the pointer** and the opposite one stays put.
- **The anchor point stays on its spot of the picture**, and Position doesn't change.
- **A corner moves freely; Shift keeps the proportions.**
- **A path** (drawn with the Pen) has no Size, so it still stretches as before, with the same Shift rule on its corners.

**Changes**

- `panels/graphics.rs`:
  - New `HandleDrag::Size`: the box the drag leaves, turned into `size` and `anchor` for `graphics.set`. The box scales with Size about the layer's origin, so the origin moves and the anchor point is renumbered by the same amount, which keeps it and the side that wasn't dragged in place. This works for polygons too, whose box isn't centred on the origin.
  - Shift on a corner: the side that moved further sets the scale of both.
  - The paragraph-text box and the shape box share the side-dragging code (`drag_sides`).
  - Paths keep `HandleScale`; its corners now move freely too, and Shift keeps their ratio.
- `docs/graphics.md`: the Selection tool row describes the new handles.

**Testing**

- `crates/ui-egui/tests/graphics_handles_ui.rs`:
  - New `shape_handles_change_its_size_and_shift_keeps_the_ratio`: a corner dragged sideways makes the shape wider only, with Scale at 100, the opposite corner, the anchor point and Position in place; with Shift, both sides gro…

title: HW5: AV1 sequence headers compare by picture format, so SVT-AV1 files stay on hardware
author: mutombopr
body:
Split out of #408, as suggested there: the AV1 `FrameStreamInfo::parameters_changed` fix on its own.

**Problem**: `parameters_changed` compared each in-band AV1 sequence header with `av1C`'s byte for byte. SVT-AV1 writes a provisional sequence header in `av1C` whose coding tool flags (CDEF, loop restoration, warped motion…) differ from the in-band one. The headers never matched, so every SVT-AV1 MP4 was handed to the software decoder from its first frame, on every hardware backend that uses `HybridDecoder`.

**Fix**: compare sequence headers by what the picture format depends on: profile, maximum frame size and colour configuration (bit depth, chroma format, colour description). A header that does not parse still counts as a change, so anything unexpected still falls back to software as before. VP9 is unchanged.

**Test**: `hw_frame::tests::av1_sequence_headers_compare_by_picture_format`, with an `av1C` / in-band header pair taken from an SVT-AV1 720p 10-bit file. It fails on `main` ("only coding tool flags differ") and passes here.

**Gates**: fmt; clippy `-D warnings` on `filmcraft-codecs` and `filmcraft-platform`; `filmcraft-codecs` unit tests (87 pass). The change is confined to `crates/codecs/src/hw_frame.rs`.

title: #712: keyboard Slide keeps linked picture and sound aligned at a neighbour limit
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #712.

## Problem
`timeline.slideLeft`, `timeline.slideRight`, `timeline.slideLeft5` and `timeline.slideRight5` (`slide_selection` in `crates/engine/src/keyboard.rs`) slid every member of the expanded selection by the raw requested delta. When a neighbour limited only one linked partner, for example a three-frame sound-only follower, each partner was clamped on its own, so picture and sound ended up with different starts (5 vs 2 frames in the issue's fixture). `timeline.slide` already clamped to one common delta.

## Fix
- New `edit::slide_items(seq, clips, delta, ctx)` in `crates/edit`. It works out the delta allowed by the most restrictive item (on clones), slides every item by that common delta, and returns it. If any item's limit points the other way, nothing moves.
- `slide_selection` (keyboard) and `timeline.slide` (commands.rs) both use it. For `timeline.slide` this replaces the same clamp loop that was written inline.

## Tests
- `keyboard_tests::keyboard_slide_keeps_linked_partners_aligned_at_a_neighbour_limit` rebuilds the issue's fixture: an Offline File pair at frame 0 with source In 20 and 60 frames long, plus a three-frame A1 follower. `timeline.slideRight5` now moves both partners to frame 2, and the follower ends up at frame 62 with duration 1 and source In 2. A further `timeline.slideRight` moves neither partner. Without the fix this test fails: the picture start is frame 5 instead of 2.
- The existing `slide_moves_linked_audio_with_the_video` and keyboard slide coverage still pass.

So markers placed on the Timeline could not be removed from it.

- A press on a marker's pentagon on the ruler puts the playhead exactly on the marker (selects it), whatever the snapping settings.
- Right-clicking a marker selects it the same way and opens a marker menu: Clear Selected Marker, Clear Markers (existing commands and translated labels; automation ids `timeline.markerMenu.<command>`).
- The pentagon's rect is now one helper (`timeline_hit::marker_rect`) shared by drawing / the `timeline.marker.<id>` automation rect and the hit test (`timeline_hit::marker_at`).

title: #715: a Matroska remux that keeps its timestamps starts at its first picture
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #715.

## Problem
`MkvSource` used the raw Segment timestamps as media time, and the absolute `Info/Duration` endpoint as the clip length. A remux that keeps its source's first PTS (`ffmpeg -copyts`, 1.48 s in the report) repeated its opening picture until 1.48 s, and turned 2 s of media into a 3.48 s clip (87 frames instead of 50). A/V files shifted the same way doubled in length.

## Fix
`crates/codecs/src/mkv.rs`, in `MkvSource::open_reader`:
- Media time zero is the earliest start among the playable tracks. An audio track starts where its first packet did before the demuxer took `CodecDelay` off (that delay only hides Opus priming), and never before zero.
- Every track moves back by that origin, so a delay between picture and sound survives. The low-level demuxer's timestamps are not changed.
- The duration is the Segment end minus the origin, never less than the main track's samples. Files that already start at zero keep the same duration as before.
- Small cleanups on the way: the `CodecDelay` tick rounding is now a helper that `opus_starts` uses too, and `to_tick` passes the timebase to `Tick::from_rational` instead of multiplying first, so it can't overflow. The video bitrate now uses the corrected duration.

This works the same way as the MP4 fix in #732 (#714), but neither PR depends on the other.

## Tests
- `mkv::origin_tests::timestamp_preserving_remux_starts_at_the_first_picture`: an MJPEG + PCM Matroska file whose pictures start at 1.48 s, with sound 0.2 s later. The clip must last 10 frames, show each picture once and in order, and start the sound at 0.2 s. It fails without the fix (duration 1.88 s instead of 0.4 s).
- Also checked by hand with the issue's ffmpeg fixtures (not committed) through `filmcraft-cli` probe/render/export. `shifted.mkv` now lasts 2.00 s, like `zero.mkv` and `content.ts`. Its frame fingerprints at 0, 0.04, 0.48, 1, 1.48 and 1.96 s match the zero-origin control, and the render at 2.00 s is black. The `av-shifted.mkv` WAV…

title: Project panel: dragging one of several selected items places them all, back to back, in one undo step
author: aw4e
body:
## What

Dragging one of several selected Project panel items onto the Timeline places all of them, back to back, as one undo step.

- The first item lands at the drop point and each next one where the previous one ends. Insert mode (Cmd/Ctrl) works the same way.
- Dropping on an empty Timeline creates the sequence from the first item and places the rest after it, also as one undo step.
- The drag ghost reads "N items" when the selection is dragged.
- Dragging an item that is not in the selection still places only that item.
- Files dropped from the OS (#517) use the same command, so they are one undo step too.

## How

The placement is an engine command, so agents and the CLI can use it.

- `timeline.place` takes `items: [...]` as well as `item`. They are placed back to back, from `time`. If one fails, none is placed. `sourceIn` and `duration` name one item's range, so they need `item`. A list is capped at 10,000 items.
- `file.newSequence` takes `fromItems: [...]` the same way.
- New `Session::edit_group` runs several edits as one undo step and rolls back the project, the editor state and the history if any of them fails.
- The Timeline (drop from the Project panel, empty Timeline, OS file drop) calls these commands and reports errors in the status line.
- `chain_starts` and its tests are removed: the engine now lays the clips end to end.

This replaces the earlier #581, which also had the panel re-docking and the folder drop. Re-docking is covered by #331, and the folder drop will come as its own PR with an engine command.

On Windows after merging main: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --release -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `assets` and `wasm` pass, and every engine and UI test passes. `cargo test --workspace --release --no-fail-fast` has 4 failing targets in crates this PR does not touch: `filmcraft-hevc` (conformance), `filmcraft-matroska` (oracle), `filmcraft-platform` (media_foundation) and `xtask` (macOS entitl…

title: #719: positive Roundness rounds the Lumetri vignette
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #719.

## Problem
The Lumetri vignette scaled its horizontal coordinate by `1 + vround * 0.0` and applied aspect correction only when Roundness was negative. As a result, every value from 0 to +100 rendered the same picture. This affected the CPU `lumetri` path, the CPU `FxOp::Lumetri` and the GPU parameter packing in `crates/gpu/src/fx.rs`. Negative values also moved the vignette towards a circle, which is the direction positive values should take.

## Fix
A new helper, `filmcraft_render::gpufx::lumetri_vignette_aspect`, scales the horizontal coordinate by `aspect^roundness`:
- 0 keeps the ellipse that follows the frame (unchanged).
- Positive values make the vignette more circular; +100 is a true circle.
- Negative values widen the oval.

Non-finite or out-of-range values fall back safely: a bad aspect or a NaN roundness gives 1, and roundness is clamped to ±1. The CPU path, the CPU op and the GPU uniform all call this one helper, so they stay in parity. The WGSL shader already takes the precomputed factor, so it needed no change.

## Tests
- New: `lumetri_vignette_roundness_shapes_the_vignette` (`crates/render/src/effects.rs`) renders a grey 80×40 frame:
  - 0 follows the frame.
  - +100 darkens points 16 px right of and 16 px below the centre equally.
  - +50 falls between 0 and +100.
  - −100 darkens the side edge less than 0.
  - The CPU path and the GPU op agree within 1e-6.

  The test fails on main ("positive roundness changes the vignette").
- The existing CPU/GPU-op parity test still passes.

## Gates
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-render -p filmcraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-render`, `cargo test -p filmcraft-gpu`
- `cargo xtask layers`
- `cargo check -p filmcraft-render -p filmcraft-gpu --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`

title: macOS: open a double-clicked .fcproj from Finder
author: impostazioni
body:
Fixes #736.

Double-clicking a `.fcproj` in Finder (or Open With ▸ FilmCraft) showed "FilmCraft cannot open files of this type". There were two gaps.

**1. The bundle didn't claim the type** (`packaging/macos/Info.plist.in`). It exported the `ai.storyteller.filmcraft.project` UTI but had no `CFBundleDocumentTypes`. This PR adds one entry: role `Editor`, rank `Owner`, `LSItemContentTypes` = the exported UTI.

**2. Nothing received the document.** Launch Services passes documents as an open-documents Apple Event, not argv, and winit 0.30 doesn't surface it. With only (1), AppKit's default handler still shows the same error.

- `filmcraft_platform::open_documents` (safe, all platforms):
  - a process-wide queue of paths (capped) plus a waker;
  - `install()` / `set_waker()` / `take()`.
  - On other systems `install()` is a no-op: their file associations pass the file as an argument.
- `open_documents_macos` (FFI, macOS):
  - An NSObject subclass (`define_class!`) registered with `NSAppleEventManager` for `kAEOpenDocuments`.
  - AppKit installs its own handler while the app finishes launching, and `applicationWillFinishLaunching:` belongs to winit's delegate. So the handler is also re-installed from an `NSApplicationWillFinishLaunchingNotification` observer, posted at the same point.
  - It reads the direct object (a list of file references, or a single one), keeps the file URLs (at most 1024 per event), queues the paths and calls the waker.
  - Both callbacks run under `catch_unwind`.
- App (`apps/filmcraft`, `ui-egui`):
  - `main` calls `install()` before `run_native`, so the document that launches the app isn't missed; the paths wait in the queue until the first frame.
  - The creator sets the waker to `request_repaint`.
  - New `HostHooks::opened_files` is polled each frame next to the native-menu inbox. Paths are treated like command-line files: the first `.fcproj` goes through `file.open` (the same as File ▸ Open), and other files go through `file.import`. A failu…

title: #620: Project Notes panel, saved in the project
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #620.

## Problem
A project had nowhere to keep free text: to-do lists, instructions for whoever opens the project next, frame numbers, parameters.

- **Model:** `Project::notes`, plain text, saved in the project file (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "String::is_empty")]`). title: #456: a bin can be dragged into another bin and back out
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes point 2 of #456 (Part of #456).

## Problem
A bin stayed wherever it was created. `project.moveToBin` only moved project items, and bin rows and cards in the Project panel could not be dragged. The only way to nest bins was to create them inside each other.

## Fix
- **Engine / project model:** `project.moveToBin` also takes bin ids in `items`, the same way `project.delete` does. A bin moves with everything in it (`Project::move_to_bin`). It skips the root, and it skips any move that would put a bin inside itself or inside one of its own sub-bins. The command's param hint is now `{"items":[id|binId]?,"bin":binId|null}`.
- **Project panel:** bin rows (List view) and bin cards (Icon view) can be dragged now (new `DragPayload::Bin`; the drag ghost shows the bin's name). Dropping a bin on another bin nests it there. A target that would contain itself gets no highlight. Dropping a bin on empty space moves it into the bin the view shows, so it can come back out to the top level (or into the bin open in a tab).

## Tests

title: #483: media dropped past the last track goes on a new track
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #483.

## Problem
In Premiere Pro, dropping media in the empty space above the top video track (or below the last audio track) creates a track for it. In FilmCraft the drop did nothing. The Timeline accepted a project-item drop only over an existing track row (`row_at` returns nothing for the empty space), and `timeline.place` could only target tracks that already exist.

## Fix
- **Engine** (`crates/engine/src/sequence_tools.rs`, `commands.rs`): `timeline.place` now accepts `"new"` as `track` and/or `audioTrack`. For each stream the item carries (and the call enables), it adds a track after the last one of that kind, then places the clip there. The new tracks and the clip are one undo step. If the placement fails, the new tracks are removed again. Agents and the control channel can use this too, and the params doc string is updated.
- **UI** (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs`): a new `new_track_at` helper finds the empty space above the top video track or below the last audio track. It never matches over a track, the caption tracks, the divider or the Mix row. The drop ghost appears there, where the new track will go. On release the clip goes on a new video track (drop above) or a new audio track (drop below). The other stream goes on the track with the same number, or on a new track when that one doesn't exist.

## Tests
- `sequence_tools_tests::place_on_new_tracks_adds_them_in_one_undo_step` covers three cases: new video and audio tracks with the clips on them in one undo step; a new video track only, with the sound on A1; a placement that fails after the tracks were added, which leaves the sequence and the history unchanged. This test panics on main, where `"new"` is rejected as an unknown track.

title: #227: transitions travel with the clips they sit on when moved
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes the point "any transition placed gets removed when the clip gets moved" of #227 (Part of #227), which is also point 8 of #374 (Part of #374).

## Problem
Moving a clip in the Timeline (drag, `timeline.move`, nudge) made the transitions at its edges disappear. `edit::move_items` deletes the moved clips before placing them again, and that deletion drops every transition that refers to them (`remove_orphan_transitions`), so a fade at a clip's edge, or the cut between two clips that were moved together, never came back.

## Fix
`crates/edit/src/lib.rs`: before the move, `carried_transitions` collects the transitions whose clips all move onto one track by one offset (a fade from or to nothing at a moved clip's edge, or a cut whose two clips move together). Once the clips have landed (overwrite or insert move), they go back on the destination track, shifted by that offset. A crossfade whose partner stays behind is still dropped, as before. Transitions on locked tracks are left alone.

## Tests
`crates/edit/src/tests.rs` `transitions_travel_with_moved_clips` (fails on `main`): a fade-in follows its clip to another track; a crossfade and fade-out follow two clips moved together in an insert move; moving one side of a crossfade drops it while the moved clip's own fade stays.

title: #374: a clip's fades follow its edges on a regular trim
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes point 9 of #374 (Part of #374).

## Problem

A transition on one edge of a clip (a fade in from nothing or a fade out to nothing) stayed where it was when the clip's edge was dragged with the Selection tool. `edit::trim` only moved transitions with the cut in Ripple mode (`transitions_follow_cuts`). A regular trim moved the clip's edge and left its transition behind, away from the edge.

## Fix

`crates/edit/src/lib.rs`: after a regular trim, `fades_follow_edges` puts the trimmed clip's one-sided transitions back on its edges. A fade in starts where the clip starts and a fade out ends where it ends. If the clip becomes shorter than a fade, the fade is shortened to the clip's length. Transitions between two clips are not changed, because a regular trim does not move their cut. Linked partners go through the same `edit::trim` call, so audio fades follow as well.

## Tests

`fades_follow_a_regular_trim` in `crates/edit/src/tests.rs` trims both edges of a clip that has a fade in and a fade out, then trims it shorter than its fades. The test fails on `main` (both fades stay at their old positions) and passes with the fix.

title: #228: Export Frame reports a frame still loading instead of saving it blank
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #228.

## Problem
`file.exportFrame` rendered the Source/Program frame and wrote it without checking `filmcraft_media::pending`. On the web, WebCodecs decodes asynchronously and Blob reads can defer: the source marks the request pending and fails it, the render leaves that clip out, and the command still "succeeded" with a blank/transparent still. This matches both reports in the issue: the "frame 0" result is an all-dark ID image, and the follow-up shows fully transparent PNGs.

## Fix
`export_frame` (`crates/engine/src/keyboard.rs`) clears the pending flag before rendering and checks it afterwards. If a read was deferred, it returns `the frame is still loading; export it again in a moment` and writes nothing. A later call exports the real frame, which is the "report that the frame is not ready" outcome the issue asks for. Native hosts never set the flag, so nothing changes there. Clearing the flag first means a deferred read left over from an earlier request can't fail this export.

## Tests
In `crates/engine/src/frame_export_tests.rs`:
- `a_frame_still_loading_is_reported_not_saved_blank`: a source that marks pending (like `WcSource` while it decodes) makes both Program and Source exports fail and write no file. Once the real source is back, the same exports succeed. This test fails without the fix.
- `an_earlier_deferred_read_does_not_fail_the_export`: a stale pending flag doesn't block an export and is cleared afterwards.

## Gates
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine --lib frame_export` and `--lib keyboard`

title: #266: quitting with unsaved changes asks to save first
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes the second point of #266 (Part of #266): quitting with unsaved changes doesn't ask to save, so every relaunch offers a recovery. The reboot during recovery itself is not addressed here.

## Problem
Quit, Cmd+Q or the window's close button exited immediately, even with unsaved changes. The changes were left to the recovery journal, so the next launch always asked to recover them. `docs/project-files.md` already noted there was no "Save changes?" prompt on quit yet.

## Fix
- `FilmcraftApp::logic` checks for a close request. When the session has unsaved changes, it sends `ViewportCommand::CancelClose` and opens the existing Save Project prompt ("Save changes to “X” before closing?", **Cancel / Don't Save / Save**), as Premiere does. The automation ids are `quit.save`, `quit.dontSave` and `quit.cancel`. The title and message reuse existing strings, so no new i18n rows.
- **Save** saves the project, then closes the window. On a never-saved project it opens the Save dialog, here and in Close Project; before this change the button was disabled there. If that dialog is cancelled, you are back at the prompt.
- **Don't Save** discards the changes by force-closing the project, which also removes their recovery snapshot, so the next launch doesn't offer them again. Then the window closes.
- The control channel's `app.quit` still quits without asking, so scripts don't hang on the prompt. Its unsaved changes stay in the recovery journal, as before.
- Updated `docs/project-files.md` and `docs/control-protocol.md`.

## Tests
Two new tests in `crates/ui-egui/tests/clip_dialogs_ui.rs`. Both put a close request into the harness input (`ViewportEvent::Close`):
- `quitting_with_unsaved_changes_asks_to_save`: the close is cancelled and the prompt appears. Cancel keeps the app and the changes, and the next close asks again. Don't Save discards the changes, and the next close goes through.

title: GPU export: a frame planned as one CPU image skips the renderer pool (Auto was slower than Off)
author: maccagnit
body:
Follow-up to #421: one of the two points of [my comment there](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/421#issuecomment-6093828002), which was about the branch as it was before the merge. I measured it again on main (98ba9ac) and it is still there, so here it is as a PR. GPU rendering is Off by default now, so this only concerns an export that turns it on.

## The problem

With `gpuRendering: auto`, a timeline with an adjustment layer exports slower than with Off.

`plan_frame` hands a frame back as `FramePlan::Image(render_sequence(..))` when it cannot be layered: an adjustment layer or a complex transition at that time, an HDR / wide-gamut sequence. `ExportRenderer::render` calls `plan_frame` inside `RendererPool::with`, so such a frame is still rendered by the CPU renderer, but only as many at a time as there are pooled renderers (`clamp(2, 4)`) instead of one per export thread. It is then counted as a GPU frame.

## The change

`Pipeline::frame` asks the planner first and renders such a frame with `render_sequence` directly, without taking a renderer from the pool.

- `filmcraft_render::plan::is_cpu_frame(project, seq, t)` says whether `plan_frame` would return `FramePlan::Image`. Both go through the same private test (`whole_frame_on_cpu`), so they cannot drift apart.
- The frame counts as a fallback in `gpu_render_stats()`.
- The picture does not change: it was the CPU image before and it is now.

## Measurements

Windows 11 Pro, Ryzen 7 9800X3D (16 threads), RTX 5070 Ti, Rust 1.99. A 47 s 1080p60 montage: 2560x1440 AV1 sources, 52 clips with speed changes and Motion keyframes, 7 transitions (Whip, Glitch, Cross Zoom, VHS Damage), text and overlays in Screen / Add, the grade as Lumetri on adjustment-layer clips over the whole timeline. `export.queue.add` of a 10 s range (600 frames) to H.264 with NVENC over MCP, CLI built with `cargo build --release -p filmcraft -p filmcraft-cli`, two alternating rounds. Seconds:

| 600 frames | Off | Auto, main 98ba9ac | …

title: GPU export: a CLI built on its own exports on the CPU instead of failing
author: maccagnit
body:
Follow-up to #421: one of the two points of [my comment there](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pull/421#issuecomment-6093828002). I checked it again on main (98ba9ac) and it still happens. GPU rendering is Off by default now, so only an export that turns it on is affected.

## The problem

`filmcraft-gpu` depends on wgpu with `default-features = false, features = ["wgsl"]`. A build that includes the app gets the backends through eframe (`egui-wgpu/default` → `wgpu/default`), and the packaging scripts build the app and the CLI together, so released binaries are fine. A CLI built on its own is not: `cargo run --release -p filmcraft-cli -- mcp`, as the README and `docs/contributing.md` show, has no backend, and `wgpu::Instance::default()` panics:

```
thread 'tokio-rt-worker' panicked at wgpu-30.0.1\src\api\instance.rs:65:13:
No wgpu backend feature that is implemented for the target platform was enabled. See `wgpu::Instance::enabled_backend_features()` for more information.
```

An export with `gpuRendering: auto` then ends as `internal error (see the crash log); the job was stopped`, with no file. The panic is in the renderer's constructor, before the pool exists, so the pool's guard does not see it.

## The change

`ExportRenderer::new` returns `None` when `wgpu::Instance::enabled_backend_features()` is empty, like a host without an adapter. The `None` is kept in the same `OnceLock`, so it is checked once per process.

## Measured

Windows 11 Pro, Ryzen 7 9800X3D, RTX 5070 Ti. CLI from `cargo build --release -p filmcraft-cli`, a 10 s range (600 frames) of a 1080p60 montage to H.264 (NVENC) over MCP:

| | main 98ba9ac | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `gpuRendering: auto` | fails with the panic above | 37.1 s |
| `gpuRendering: off` | 37.5 s | not affected |

The export of this branch decodes to the same video as the Off one (MD5 of the decoded frames).

## Not changed

title: #626: undecodable video shows the MEDIA UNREADABLE slate, not black
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes the "silent black" point of #626 (Part of #626). The High 10 / 4:2:2 decoding itself is #629; this PR covers what the issue's notes ask for separately and what #629 lists under "Not included": formats that still can't be decoded show a visible "media unreadable" slate instead of black frames.

## Problem
A file can open fine and still have a picture FilmCraft can't decode: H.264 High 10 / 4:2:2 / 4:4:4, interlaced (field / MBAFF) H.264, or a codec with no decoder in TS / MXF / MP4. That file rendered **black, with no error anywhere**, while its sound played. The H.264 and HEVC wrappers in `filmcraft-codecs` turned the decoders' `Error::Unsupported` into a generic `CodecError::Decode`. The renderer drops any frame that fails, so nothing told the user why the picture was missing.

## Fix
- `crates/codecs/src/video.rs`: `h264_error` / `hevc_error` map the decoders' `Unsupported` errors to `CodecError::Unsupported` (`MediaError::Unsupported`, for example `H.264: chroma_format_idc 2 (only 4:2:0 is implemented)`). Every other error stays a decode error.
- `crates/engine/src/media_pool.rs`: every file source the pool opens (through `resolve` and `insert_file`) is wrapped in a private `UnsupportedAsSlate`. A frame whose decode fails as *unsupported* renders the existing **MEDIA UNREADABLE** slate, and the item gets an `Unreadable` offline status carrying the decoder's reason. Files that fail to open already get the same treatment, so the Project panel shows "Unreadable" and `media.status` reports `unreadable`. Frames that decode are untouched, damaged frames (`Decode` errors) are untouched, and the sound plays as before. Relinking the item clears the status.

## Tests
- `media_pool::tests::undecodable_frames_show_the_unreadable_slate` (runs everywhere, no ffmpeg needed) uses a source whose frames decode, fail as damaged, or fail as unsupported. It checks:
  - only the unsupported frames become the slate;
  - the item becomes Unreadable with the decoder's reason;
  - t…

author: vangel76
body:
Fixes the opened-clip switcher part of "Managing opened Source clips" in #313 (Part of #313). The timeline double-click part of that point is not included.

## Problem
The Source monitor only kept the one clip it showed (`EditorState::source_item`). Opening another clip forgot the previous one, so there was no list of recently opened clips to switch back to. title: web: opt-in threaded build, rayon on Web Workers (`cargo xtask web --threads`)
author: PassepartoutFR
body:
## What

An opt-in threaded web build. `cargo xtask web --threads` builds `filmcraft-web` with wasm atomics and starts a rayon pool of Web Workers at load time, so the parallel loops that already exist inside each frame job (generators, compositing, effects) use every core instead of running inline on the UI thread. The default build is unchanged.

On the demo project (Program monitor at 1/2, 8 s of playback through the overlapping clips and cross-dissolves, headless Chromium 149 on WebGPU, 16 logical cores):

| `--threads` build | rayon threads | frames shown | frames dropped |
|---|---|---|---|
| `?nothreads` (rayon inline, as in the default build) | 1 | 102 | 98 |
| `?threads=3` | 3 | 135 | 60 |
| `?threads=7` | 7 | 182 | 12 |
| default pool size | 8 | 193 | 1 |

Counts come from `perf.stats` (`playback.shown` / `playback.dropped`) over the same window. The default pool size was run twice (193 / 1, then 189 / 5). On 0.5.0, `?nothreads` matched the default build (84 / 117 against 84 / 120).

## How

- `apps/filmcraft-web`: a new `threads` feature, off by default, pulling `rayon` and `wasm-bindgen-rayon` 1.3 (`no-bundler`; Apache-2.0, and its `wasm_sync`, MIT OR Apache-2.0). That build exports `initThreadPool`; `filmcraft.info()` gains `rayonThreads`, and `threads` now says whether a pool runs.
- `web/index.html`: calls `initThreadPool` between `init()` and `start()` when the build exports it and the page is cross-origin isolated. `?threads=N` sets the pool size (default: logical cores - 1, at most 8), `?nothreads` skips it.
- `cargo xtask web --threads`: a nightly toolchain (`FILMCRAFT_WEB_TOOLCHAIN`, default `nightly`), `-Z build-std=std,panic_abort`, `+atomics,+bulk-memory,+mutable-globals`, an imported shared memory (4 GiB max) and the TLS exports wasm-bindgen needs, its own target directory (`target/wasm-threads`) so the regular build stays cached, and `wasm-opt --enable-threads`.

title: #313: double-clicking a Timeline clip opens it in the Source monitor
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes the timeline double-click part of "Managing opened Source clips" in #313 (Part of #313). Independent of #763 (Source clip history / Close), which left this part out; the two touch different code and merge cleanly in either order.

## Problem
The Timeline only handled double-clicks on transitions (Set Transition Duration) and nested sequence clips (open in their own tab). Double-clicking an ordinary clip did nothing, where Premiere opens it in the Source monitor.

Because it is a command parameter, the CLI, control channel and MCP can do the same.

title: codecs: an open GOP's leading pictures decode from the GOP before, not as black frames
author: alex-brazh
body:
## What was wrong

Video with open GOPs (every iPhone HEVC clip; x265 with `open-gop`) sometimes showed 1–3 black frames after a trim or a move on the timeline, at the start of a clip or in the middle. With a track below, that track showed through instead. Exports had them too.

In an open GOP, each CRA after the first is followed in decoding order by RASL pictures that display before it and are predicted from the GOP before. iPhone video has a CRA every 24 frames, so 3 frames in every 24 are RASL.

`GopCache` started a decoding run at `sync_before(i)`, the sync sample at or before the wanted sample in decoding order. For a RASL picture that is the CRA after it, and the decoders (software and VideoToolbox) rightly leave a run's leading RASL pictures out. So the frame was never produced, the request failed with "frame not produced", and the renderer left the clip's layer out. This happens wherever decoding starts fresh on one of those frames: a clip trimmed to start on one, the parked playhead after an edit, scrubbing, and parallel export. Straight playback decodes through them, which is why it only happened sometimes.

The MPEG and MXF readers already step back for leading pictures in their own `sync_before`. MP4/MOV and Matroska didn't.

This is a different cause from #626 / #762: there the format has no decoder; here the decoder works, but the run started at the wrong place.

## The fix

All in `crates/codecs/src/gop.rs`:

- `decode_start`: when the wanted sample displays before its sync sample, the run starts at the sync sample before that one (repeated if needed). Both `frame_late_locked` and `decode_to` use it.
- A running decoder that started after that point isn't continued for the wanted picture, because it has already left it out (`st.start <= key`). This also covers a run left behind by a cancelled scrub.

In closed-GOP streams every sample displays at or after its sync sample, so `decode_start` returns `sync_before(i)` as before.

title: text: the CJK system-font search no longer keeps every probed font file in memory (#769)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #769.

`cjk::system_font()` checked each non-italic system face with `Face::has_char`, which goes through `Face::bytes` and keeps the whole font file in the face's `OnceLock` for the life of the process. When the preferred families are not found (PingFang on macOS lives outside the scanned folders), every system face was read and kept: about 3.2 GB on the reporter's Mac.

- New `Face::covers_text(&str)`: if the face's file is not loaded yet, it reads the file into a temporary buffer, checks the charmap and drops the buffer. Faces that are already loaded (bundled, shared, or cached) use `has_char` as before.
- `cjk::system_font()` uses it, so only the chosen face's bytes stay in memory (copied once into egui's `FontData`, as before).
- `i18n::system_japanese_font()` has the same search loop (run when the interface is switched to Japanese without craft-fonts), so it uses `covers_text` too. Its doc comment already says only the chosen face's file is read; now that is true.

Face selection is unchanged: same samples, same preferred-family order, same weight tie-break.

Test: `fonts::tests::covers_text_does_not_keep_file_bytes` writes Inter to a temp file, builds a file-backed `Face`, checks `covers_text` gives the right answer (Latin + Cyrillic yes, Hebrew no), and that the face's byte cache is still empty afterwards. Loading through `data()` still fills it.

Not changed: sharing one buffer between the faces of a `.ttc`, deferring the search, and locating PingFang through Core Text. The issue lists these as alternatives; with this change only one face is kept, so they are not needed for the memory figure.

title: Timeline: draw each audio track's own waveform, not track 1's (#770)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #770.

**Cause:** timeline waveform peaks were computed with `MediaSource::audio`, which always reads audio stream 0, and cached per `ItemId` only. Every clip cut from a multi-stream file (e.g. an MKV with 4 audio tracks) therefore drew stream 0's waveform, whatever its `audio_stream` was, even though playback already uses the right stream.

**Fix:**
- The peak cache (`peaks`, `peaks_pending`, `peak_max`) is now keyed by `(ItemId, audio stream index)`.
- `draw_waveform` asks for the clip's own `it.audio_stream`; peaks are read with `MediaSource::audio_stream`, which the MKV and MP4 sources already implement (and which falls back to `audio` for stream 0 on single-stream sources).
- The peak loop moved into a small `source_peaks(src, stream, dur)` helper so it can be tested without a UI.
- Nested sequences (their mix) and the source monitor waveform keep using key/stream 0, as before.
- **Clip ▸ Generate Audio Waveform** (`clip.generateAudioWaveform`), which drops cached peaks so they are rebuilt, now drops every stream's entry for that item.

**Test:** `each_audio_stream_gets_its_own_waveform_peaks` uses a fake source whose stream 0 and stream 1 hold different constant levels, and checks that stream 1's peaks are its own and that a missing stream yields no peaks. With the old stream-0-only read it fails on the stream 1 assertion. Existing tests that read the peak cache (`nest_rendering_ui`, `scripted`) were updated for the new key.

body:
## What this does

H.265 export through NVENC was limited to Windows. This enables it on 64-bit Linux with NVIDIA's driver: Main 8-bit SDR and Main 10 HDR (PQ and HLG). It uses the CUDA device the H.264 NVENC encoder already uses on Linux, so there is no new FFI.

## Changes

- `nvenc/export.rs`: the HEVC factory is no longer Windows only.
- `lib.rs`: NVENC registration (format probe, HDR probe, warm HEVC probe, encoder factory) moved into one `register_nvenc()` used by Windows and Linux.
- On Linux it runs after the VA-API and NVDEC probes. Run beside the VA-API probe, the background HEVC probe's first `cuInit` can deadlock with libva-nvidia-driver, which calls `cuInit` from its library constructor under the loader lock. I hit this as a hang at 100% CPU in the export tests.
- The six `nvenc_hevc*.rs` tests and `nvenc_rgba_input.rs` now also build and run on Linux.
- Docs updated where they said H.265 NVENC export was Windows only.

## Testing

RTX 3080, driver 615.71.09, Linux, rebased on current main.

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets`: pass.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 2,754 passed, 0 failed.
- All NVENC HEVC tests pass on the GPU (22 tests, including the real export job to MP4 and QuickTime and the HDR PQ and HLG exports checked with ffprobe).
- `nvenc_rgba_input.rs`: 3 passed on Linux.
- `filmcraft-cli --demo export out.mp4 --format hevc`: ffprobe reads hevc, Main, hvc1, yuv420p, 1920x1080, 72 frames. `ffmpeg -xerror` decodes it clean.

Not run: `cargo xtask wasm` (no wasm target on my machine). Not tested on Windows, where the only change is the move into `register_nvenc()`.
