title: fix(tts-text): preserve magnitude, fractions and leading zeros in narration
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Several supported numeric forms produce incorrect narration text in both English modes:

- `120th` becomes "twentieth" instead of "one hundred twentieth".
- `7/100` and `100/7` are read with "slash" instead of fraction wording.
- `07%` and `07.5` lose their leading zero.

These incorrect readings also affect downstream phonemization.

## Root cause

Three normalization paths discard meaningful numeric information:

1. Exact-tens ordinal conversion drops preceding magnitude words.
2. Fraction parsing limits each operand to two digits.
3. Percent and decimal continuations convert integer values before preserving leading-zero notation.

## Changes

- Preserve magnitude words when forming exact-tens ordinals.
- Support fraction operands up to the existing cardinal digit limit.
- Preserve digit-by-digit readings for leading-zero percentages and decimals.
- Maintain date parsing precedence and invalid-denominator behavior.
- Add regression tests covering both English modes and previously correct cases.

## Validation

- Reviewed the implementation and committed diff against current upstream.
- Added three focused regression tests.
- Tests not executed because Rust/Cargo was unavailable.
- Workspace checks and CI remain pending.

## Issues

Fixes #897
Fixes #898
Fixes #899

title: fix(playback): rest Program marked playback on the Out frame
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Program playback commands "Play In to Out" and "Play from Playhead to Out Point" finish with the playhead one frame beyond the marked Out point.

Although Out is the final included frame, playback leaves the playhead outside the selected range.

## Root cause

Playback correctly uses the boundary immediately after Out as its exclusive stopping position.

However, that exclusive boundary is also assigned to the playhead when playback stops.

## Changes

- Track the inclusive resting position separately from the exclusive playback stopping boundary.
- Restore the playhead to the marked Out frame when Program range playback completes.
- Apply the behavior to both affected Program playback commands.
- Clear the resting position when playback stops.
- Preserve ordinary sequence-end playback and extended preroll/postroll behavior.
- Add a headless UI regression test covering both affected commands and preservation cases.

## Validation

- Reviewed the affected playback paths and committed diff.
- Added regression coverage using the existing UI test harness.
- Test execution remains pending because Rust/Cargo was unavailable.
- GUI smoke testing and CI have not been run.

## Issue

Fixes #904

title: fix(render): update Noise grain on every frame using exact timestamps
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

Noise and Noise (Legacy) can repeat the same random field across consecutive sequence frames.

At 60 fps, neighboring frames may receive identical noise. At 120 fps, several consecutive frames can share the same pattern.

Floating-point rounding can also produce occasional repeats at 30 fps.

## Root cause

Noise generation derives its temporal seed using:

`(cx.seconds * 30.0) as u64`

This quantizes animation to approximately 30 updates per second regardless of the sequence frame rate.

## Changes

- Derive the temporal noise seed from the exact effect timestamp instead of a fixed 30 Hz conversion.
- Share the seed calculation between the Noise implementation paths.
- Preserve deterministic output when rendering the same timestamp repeatedly.
- Add regression tests for Noise and Noise (Legacy).
- Cover consecutive frames at 24, 30, 60 and 120 fps.
- Include the previously observed 30 fps rounding case and an Amount-zero control.

## Validation

- Reviewed both Noise implementation paths and the committed diff.
- Added focused regression coverage.
- Tests not executed because Rust/Cargo was unavailable.
- Render validation and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #906

title: fix(export): estimate TIFF sequence size using the actual channel count
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Problem

The TIFF Sequence export summary estimates four bytes per pixel regardless of whether Include Alpha Channel is enabled.

Consequently, RGB TIFF exports receive an estimate approximately 33% larger than their pixel data requires.

Enabling alpha also fails to change the estimate even though the output gains another channel.

## Root cause

The export size estimator assumes that TIFF sequences always contain four channels.

Unlike TGA and EXR estimates, the TIFF estimate does not consult the effective alpha setting.

## Changes

- Estimate RGB TIFF output using three bytes per pixel.
- Estimate RGBA TIFF output using four bytes per pixel.
- Preserve the existing BMP channel-count behavior.
- Add regression coverage for TIFF summaries with alpha enabled and disabled.
- Add an export test comparing estimates with generated TIFF file sizes.
- Include BMP and TGA controls to guard against unrelated changes.

## Validation

- Reviewed the estimate calculation and committed diff.
- Added regression coverage for size estimates and generated output.
- Tests not executed because Rust/Cargo was unavailable.
- Export integration tests and CI remain pending.

## Issue

Fixes #908

title: Dropping a folder on the window imports it as a bin of its media
author: aw4e
body:
## What

Dropping a folder on the window imports it as a bin of the same name holding its media. Subfolders become sub-bins. Files are imported in alphabetical order; hidden entries (leading `.`) and files that are not media are skipped. Dropped plain files still import into the shown bin.

This is the second PR split out of #581. #746 has merged, and this PR is rebased on it: it uses `Session::edit_group` from there.

## How

The import is an engine command, so agents and the CLI can use it, and it goes through `services` (it works headless; where a host cannot list a directory, a folder path is treated as a file and the error is reported).

- `file.import` takes `bins: true`. Each folder among `paths` becomes a bin under `bin` holding its media; plain files among the paths import as before. The result adds `bins` (the new bin ids) and keeps `items` and `errors`.
- The walk uses `Services::list_entries`, not `std::fs::read_dir`. Depth (16 levels) and entries read (20,000 over the whole import) are capped and the cap is reported in `errors`, not ignored. Unreadable folders are reported too.
- One undo step for the whole import (`Session::edit_group`); if nothing could be imported the command fails and changes nothing.
- `replace: true` starts the new project before the folders are imported, not after.
- The window drop (`handle_drops`) now sends its paths with `bins: true` and shows the first error in the status line. The folder walk that was in the UI is gone.

## Testing

After the rebase onto current main, on Windows: `cargo fmt --check` passes, as do the engine `folder_import` (7) and `place_items` (7) tests and the `folder_drop_ui` (2), `timeline_drop_ui` (11) and `project_panel_ui` (23) tests. Before the rebase the clippy, `cargo xtask layers`, `assets` and `wasm` gates passed too; I have not rerun them since. title: fix(ui): add Korean font fallback for UI text
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes storytold/artcraft#2093 - Korean text cannot be typed or pasted in text fields on Windows 11. Appears as missing-glyph boxes instead of rendering.

## Root Cause

**Font issue, not IME:** Korean (Hangul) text was reaching the UI but had no font to render it. egui 0.36.2 ships no Hangul glyphs, and FilmCraft's interface font list only includes Japanese/Chinese fallbacks. On Windows, those fonts (Microsoft YaHei) lack Hangul coverage. Korean Windows often doesn't have Chinese fonts installed, leaving no fallback at all.

Copy-paste failing too confirms this is a rendering problem, not input method handling.

## Solution

Added Korean font fallback to UI font families. The code now searches for an installed Korean font (Malgun Gothic on Windows, Apple SD Gothic Neo on macOS, Noto Sans CJK KR, Source Han Sans K, or NanumGothic on Linux) and adds it as the last fallback.

Font is loaded from system, not shipped with the app.

## Implementation

**Changed:** `crates/ui-egui/src/cjk.rs`, `crates/ui-egui/src/theme.rs` (+~30 lines)
- Generalized `chinese_font()` to take sample text and font names as args
- New `korean_font()` finds installed Korean font
- Added to all interface font families in theme setup
- New test: `korean_text_renders_with_an_installed_korean_font`

## Test Results

✓ `cargo fmt`  
✓ `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` (filmcraft-ui-egui)  
✓ All tests pass in filmcraft-ui-egui

**Note:** Test passes on macOS (has Arial Unicode MS with Hangul), only proves fix on Windows/Linux with Korean fonts installed.

## Rollout

**Other affected apps:** effectcraft, designcraft, wordcraft, pdfcraft, craft-launcher all need the same pattern applied. This PR fixes FilmCraft only.

## Trade-offs

- Adds ~4-5 MB memory at startup when Korean font is installed
- No Korean font installed = no change from current behavior

title: #922: eight-channel AAC reports and returns eight channels
author: JordyUSA
body:
Fixes #922.

## Cause
`crates/codecs/src/mp4.rs` used the AudioSpecificConfig's `channelConfiguration` as the channel count. It is an index into ISO/IEC 14496-3 Table 1.19 (amended by Amd 4), so:
- **configuration 7** (7.1) reported **7** channels, and `audio()` sized its buffers from that, dropping the eighth decoded channel;
- **configuration 12** (7.1 back, which ffmpeg 9 writes for ordinary 7.1) reported **12** channels and failed to decode, so the file imported silent.

## Fix
- `AacConfig::channels()` (isobmff) maps the full table: 1–6 → n, 7 / 12 / 14 → 8, 11 → 7, 13 → 24, reserved → 0. The MP4 reader uses it, falling back to the sample entry's count for a PCE (configuration 0) as before.
- The AAC decoder now accepts **11** (6.1: SCE CPE CPE SCE LFE) and **12** (7.1 back: SCE CPE CPE CPE LFE). 13 (22.2) and 14 (7.1 with front heights) still report their channel count but aren't decoded.
- Configurations 11 and 12 are reordered to the WAV/SMPTE order already used for 3–6 (L R C LFE …). This is also ffmpeg's decode order.

## Tests
- `crates/codecs/tests/aac_channels_oracle.rs`: ffmpeg encodes 7.1 / 5.1 / 6.1 tones, with a different frequency on each channel.
  - **Configuration 7:** reports and returns 8 channels, all of them audible. Before the fix it returned 7 / 7.
  - **Configuration 12:** the same access units rewrapped under a configuration-12 header, because ffmpeg 8 writes 7.1 as 7. It reports 8 channels and matches ffmpeg's decode channel by channel, with a maximum difference of 0.0011 at a peak of about 0.13 (a swapped channel would differ by about 0.26).
  - **5.1 (configuration 6) and 6.1 (PCE) controls:** unchanged at 6 and 7 channels.
- Unit tests for the configuration → channel table (isobmff) and the new decoder layouts (aac).

`cargo fmt`, clippy (`-D warnings`) and tests pass for aac, isobmff and codecs, as do `xtask layers` and `xtask wasm`. The one failing codecs test, `eac3_oracle` (Matroska, 22 samples off), fails the same way on `main`;…

title: #923: reordered Matroska video without DefaultDuration keeps its frame rate
author: JordyUSA
body:
Fixes #923.

## Cause
When a Matroska video track has no `DefaultDuration`, `crates/codecs/src/mkv.rs` took the frame rate from the median gap between **neighbouring blocks in file order**. Blocks are stored in decode order, so with B-frames neighbours are two or more frames apart in presentation time (0, 80, 40 ms…). The median step came out as 80 ms, and a 25 fps clip reported **25/2**. That wrong rate then reached source frame positions and Sequence From Clip.

## Fix
Sort the first 241 presentation timestamps, then take the median step between them. Files with `DefaultDuration`, and files without reordering, give the same result as before.

## Test
`matroska_reordered_video_without_default_duration_keeps_its_rate` (`crates/codecs/src/tests.rs`): ffmpeg/x264 writes 25 fps clips with 0, 1 and 2 B-frames. Each is opened as written and again with `DefaultDuration` overwritten by an EBML Void of the same length, as in the issue's reproduction.
- **Before the fix:** the 1- and 2-B-frame files without `DefaultDuration` report 25/2.
- **After the fix:** all six report 25/1 with a duration of 1 s.

`cargo fmt`, clippy (`-D warnings`) and the codecs tests pass. The one failing codecs test, `eac3_oracle` (Matroska audio, 22 samples off), fails the same way on `main`; #790 / #792 cover it.

title: #924: decoded H.264 / HEVC frames keep the signalled colour primaries
author: JordyUSA
body:
Fixes #924.

## Cause
`vui_color` (`crates/codecs/src/video.rs`) builds a decoded H.264 / HEVC frame's `ColorInfo` from the VUI's matrix, transfer and range, but it never took the **primaries**, so every frame reported BT.709. Stream info already read the primaries (#446). A file whose BT.2020 primaries are signalled only in the bitstream (ffmpeg writes no `colr` box unless asked) therefore said BT.2020 in its info but BT.709 on its frames. The renderer, which uses the frame's colour, resolved such a frame to **Rec709** instead of Rec2020.

## Fix
`vui_color` now takes `colour_primaries` and maps it with the existing `primaries_from_code`, keeping BT.709 when the primaries are unspecified or unknown. All four callers pass it: the software H.264 and HEVC decoders, and the hardware-decode setup for both codecs in `hw.rs`.

## Test
`crates/codecs/tests/frame_color_oracle.rs` covers one-frame MP4s from ffmpeg with no `colr` box, which the test checks with our own parser:

| case | stream = frame | colour space |
|---|---|---|
| H.264, BT.2020 primaries / 709 transfer + matrix | ✓ | Rec2020 |
| HEVC, same | ✓ | Rec2020 |
| H.264, BT.709 (control) | ✓ | Rec709 |
| HEVC 10-bit, BT.2020 + PQ + BT.2020 NCL | ✓ | Rec2100Pq |

Before the fix, the first case fails with frame primaries `Bt709`.

`cargo fmt` and clippy (`-D warnings`) pass for codecs and platform, as do the codecs, render (182) and engine (542) tests. The one failing codecs test, `eac3_oracle` (Matroska audio), fails the same way on `main`; #790 / #792 cover it.

title: #977: MP3 export with a clean-room Layer III encoder
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G13 (docs/gaps.md).
Fixes #977.

## Problem
Premiere's **MP3** export format had no FilmCraft equivalent: MP3 could only be read. The audio-only exports were Waveform Audio, AIFF and AAC Audio.

## Fix
- **New L0 crate `filmcraft-mp3enc`**: a clean-room MPEG-1/2 Audio Layer III encoder written from ISO/IEC 11172-3 and 13818-3. No LAME, shine, FFmpeg or libmp3lame code was read; ffmpeg is only a test oracle. It depends only on `filmcraft-bitstream` and `thiserror`, and builds for wasm32.
  - CBR 32–320 kbit/s at 32 / 44.1 / 48 kHz (MPEG-1), and 8–160 kbit/s at 16 / 22.05 / 24 kHz (MPEG-2 LSF). Padding slots keep 44.1 kHz streams at the exact rate.
  - Mono, stereo, or joint stereo with mid/side chosen per frame.
  - The Annex C polyphase analysis filter (`C[i] = D[i]/32`, using the window table from our #819 branch), the normal-window MDCT and alias reduction. Long blocks only.
  - A simple psychoacoustic model: band energies spread to neighbouring bands, floored by the threshold in quiet, plus a low-pass that depends on the bit rate.
  - Inner and outer quantization loops with scalefactors and `scalefac_scale`. When every band is under its threshold and the reservoir has room, the global gain is made coarser to save bits.
  - An exhaustive choice of region split and Huffman table, plus the bit reservoir (bounded by the decoder's 7680-bit buffer and 511 / 255 bytes).
- **Export**: a new `mp3` format ("MP3") writes the sequence mix as a plain `.mp3` stream. `ExportSettings::mp3_stream` snaps the settings to what MP3 can carry: sample rate up to the nearest supported one (48 kHz above that), 5.1 folded to stereo, and the nearest Layer III bit rate. It is wired into `Format::is_audio_only`, the summary and size estimate, `file.exportMedia`, CLI extension guessing (`.mp3`), an "MP3 48 kHz 320 kbps" Audio Only preset, and the Export UI (MP3 bit rate choice). Strings added for es/fr/ja/zh-cn.

title: #980: VP9 decode loop-filters a frame as a superblock-row wavefront
author: vangel76
body:
Part of G16 (docs/gaps.md). Fixes #980.

## Problem

The VP9 decoder ran the post stage of each frame (band assembly, loop filter, publication) on one thread. Later frames wait per band for their references, so the serial loop filter (about 30 % of the decode profile) set the pace of every inter frame. With 16 threads the tile columns spent most of their time waiting for the previous frame's bands. A 1080p30 stream decoded only ~1.8x faster with 16 threads than with one.

## Fix

- The specification filters superblocks in raster order (8.8.1). Superblock (r, c) changes samples of (r, c-1), through its left vertical edges, and of (r-1, c), because its top horizontal edges reach 7 rows up. The last superblock before it that touches the bottom rows of (r-1, c) is (r-1, c+1). So rows can run as a **wavefront**, each row two superblocks behind the row above, and still give the spec's result.
- The post thread and helper jobs on the decoder's existing rayon pool each take the next row. No new dependency.
- **No lock is held while a superblock is filtered.** Each row filters its own band. Once a superblock column of its bottom 8 rows is final, the row shares a copy of it. The row below copies that into its scratch rows, and when it finishes it writes them back into band r-1, which is then final and published. Bands are still published in order as soon as they are final, so frame threading keeps overlapping frames. The output picture is still filled band by band.
- **Deadlock-free on the shared pool:** a row is only taken by a thread that is running it, so any wait for the row above is a wait on a thread that is making progress. Helpers never call back into rayon. The post thread works on rows too, so the frame finishes even if every pool worker is busy with tile decoding.
- **Never crash:** helpers run under `catch_unwind`. A failed row stops the wavefront, and the existing `PublishGuard` publishes placeholder bands so that waiting frames cannot hang. Copies use `get` / `g…

title: Reject non-finite numbers and empty LUT input ranges in .cube import (#998)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #998.

`Lut::parse_cube` accepted `LUT_1D_INPUT_RANGE 0 0` (and reversed ranges such as `1 0`). Applying the LUT then divides by a zero or negative width, so every output channel came out NaN. Numeric parsing also let `NaN`/`inf` into domains and table rows.

Changes in `crates/color/src/lut.rs`:

- `floats` rejects non-finite values (`not a finite number: "NaN"`). Every numeric field in `.cube` (`DOMAIN_MIN`/`DOMAIN_MAX`, both input-range keywords, table rows) and the `.3dl` mesh and rows go through it, so they are all covered.
- `LUT_1D_INPUT_RANGE` / `LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE` now need max > min. The error reads like the existing `DOMAIN_MAX must exceed DOMAIN_MIN` check: `LUT_1D_INPUT_RANGE maximum must exceed its minimum`. Valid ranges that are not 0..1 (e.g. `-0.5 2`) still parse.

`lut.import` uses this parser, so a bad file now fails the import with this error and never reaches the project library.

Test: `cube_sizes_up_to_65_and_errors` gets one loop over both keywords. It checks that zero-width, reversed, NaN and infinite ranges are rejected, and that `-0.5 2` is still accepted. It also checks NaN in a table row and `inf` in `DOMAIN_MAX`. On main it fails with `accepted LUT_1D_INPUT_RANGE 0 0`.

title: Count VideoToolbox sessions, frames and declined requests in perf.stats (#981)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #981.

`perf.stats` `export.hardware` reads the counters in `filmcraft_export` (`note_hw_encode_session`, `note_hw_encode_frame`, `note_hw_encode_declined`). The NVENC encoder calls them, but the VideoToolbox encoder on macOS never did, so a hardware H.264 / HEVC export on macOS left `frames`, `sessions` and `declined` at 0.

This change wires the VideoToolbox path the same way `platform::nvenc::export` does:

- `videotoolbox_encoder_factory` counts a session when `VtEncoder::new` succeeds, and a declined request when `config_for` or `VtEncoder::new` refuses (both places that already log "hardware ... encoding declined"). A request the factory does not act on (H.264 with Hardware encoding off, other formats) is not counted, as in NVENC.
- `HardwareEncoder::encode` counts a frame after each picture VideoToolbox encodes successfully, as `NvencEncoder::encode` does.

Only macOS code changes; NVENC already counts.

Test: `hardware_encoder_counters_follow_the_export` in `crates/platform/tests/hardware_encode.rs` (macOS). An odd picture size must increase `declined` (this does not need a hardware encoder, so it always runs on macOS and fails without the fix). Where a hardware encoder exists, creating one must increase `sessions`, and encoding 3 pictures must add at least 3 to `frames`. The counters are process-wide, so the test checks only increases.

title: Keep the voice-over start point when recording past the end of the timeline (#960)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #960.

Recording a voice-over on the empty timeline after the last clip did not work, for two reasons:

1. The microphone button puts the playhead on the capture start (record point minus pre-roll) and calls `play()`. Because that point is past the end of the sequence, the "At playback end, return to beginning when restarting playback" preference moved the playhead to 0, so the take started at the beginning of the sequence. `play()` now skips the return to the beginning while a voice-over take is recording.
2. Even from the right place, `advance_playback` stopped playback as soon as it passed the end of the sequence, and stopping ends the take, so nothing was recorded in the empty space. While a take is recording, non-looping playback now keeps going past the end until the take is stopped. Looping, Out + post-roll (`stop_at`) and normal playback are unchanged.

Docs: `docs/architecture.md` (voice-over section) and `docs/testing.md` describe the new behaviour.

Tests:
- `voiceover_playback_tests::a_voice_over_take_records_into_the_empty_timeline_past_the_end` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs`) starts a take 60 s past the end through the microphone-button entry point (`panels::voiceover::toggle`) and moves playback on by one second. It checks that the playhead stays on the record point, then that playback and the recording go on past the end. Without the fix the playhead jumps to 0, and the playback clock then stops the take at the end.
- `recording_past_the_end_of_the_timeline_starts_there_not_at_the_beginning` (`crates/ui-egui/tests/voiceover_ui.rs`) clicks the A2 microphone with the playhead far past the end and checks that playback runs from there.

title: #965: HDR and wide-gamut media play on the GPU path
author: JordyUSA
body:
Fixes #965.

## Cause
On a Rec. 709 sequence, any clip that needs colour management (PQ, HLG, BT.2020, P3) left the GPU playback path (`plan.rs`: `needs_management` → CPU). Each frame was then converted to a float image on the CPU: decode table, HLG OOTF, BT.2020 → 709 matrix, BT.2390 tone mapping and desaturation. It was then resampled to the output on the CPU too. For 4K portrait 10-bit HEVC, which is the reporter's media, that costs 2–5× the 33 ms frame budget at 30 fps. That fits the reporter's finding that converting the source to SDR fixes playback.

## Measured
`plan_frame` per frame for a 2160×3840 30 fps clip on a 1080×1920 30 fps sequence, release build, 16 threads. The clips were made with ffmpeg/x265 to match the issue: Main 10, BT.2020 NCL, HLG / PQ with HDR10 metadata, plus SDR controls.

| clip | Motion | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| SDR 8-bit | 100% | 18 ms | 15 ms |
| SDR 10-bit | 100% / 50% | 18 / 19 ms | 16 / 18 ms |
| **HLG 10-bit** | 100% / 50% (fit) | **98 / 48 ms** | **15 / 16 ms** |
| **PQ 10-bit** | 100% / 50% (fit) | **72 / 48 ms** | **17 / 19 ms** |

Decoding was never the bottleneck: `bench-decode` gives about 52 fps for all three 10-bit clips.

## Fix
The compositor's shader now runs the input transform itself, the same way the CPU does:
- `filmcraft_color::InputTransform::gpu_params()` gives its stages as numbers: the curve, the HLG OOTF weights and scale, the gamut matrix, the tone-mapping peaks and the desaturation weights. It returns `None` for log curves and camera-gamut compression, which stay on the CPU.
- `PlanLayer::input: Option<Arc<InputTransform>>`: `colorman::gpu_input` sets it for Y'CbCr layers on a plain (Rec. 709, no wide gamut) pipeline, with the PQ peak taken from the file's mastering metadata as before. The planner keeps these layers on the GPU path, both plain and with GPU effects such as Lumetri.
- `execute_cpu` (the CPU reference for the GPU plan) applies the same `InputTransform` through the same table and …

title: ci: refactor workflows to use storytold/craft-common-actions
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
### Summary
Refactors repetitive CI/CD workflows across FilmCraft to call centralized reusable workflows and composite actions hosted in the organization repository [`storytold/craft-common-actions`](https://github.com/storytold/craft-common-actions).

### Design Decisions
- **Hosted in Organization Repository**: Workflows live under `storytold/craft-common-actions` (no personal fork/repository).
- **Intentionally Tracks `@main` (Not SHA Pinned)**: Callers deliberately track `@main` with an inline explanation comment so that org-wide CI improvements, security fixes, and build optimizations propagate across all 13+ craftapps automatically without requiring individual PR churn in every repository.
- **Explicit Secrets**: Only the exact required signing secrets are passed explicitly (`secrets: inherit` is avoided).
- **Node 24 Runtimes**: All composite and third-party actions inside `storytold/craft-common-actions` are updated to Node 24 (and pinned internally to immutable commit SHAs), eliminating Node 20 deprecation warnings.
- **Strict Verification**: Build utilities like `nfpm`, `actionlint`, and `trunk` are verified against SHA256 checksums.
- Preserves 100% of existing packaging, release matrix, and linting semantics for FilmCraft.

title: #1039: faster HEVC motion compensation and deblocking, bit-exact (−10…28% cycles per frame)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #1039. This narrows the gap to ffmpeg but doesn't close it, so the issue stays open.

## Problem

The software HEVC decoder is 2.7–4× slower per core than ffmpeg on 1080p Main. Scrubbing a long-GOP clip pays that on every seek; it was found while measuring storytold/effectcraft#329. Motion compensation was about half of the profile:

- The default weighted-prediction stores clipped in 32-bit lanes, which SSE2 emulates in about 4 instructions per clip.
- Each line of a reference window was copied by a separate libc `memmove` call.
- Full-sample uni-prediction went through a window copy, a shift and a clipped store, only to return the reference sample.
- Deblocking divided by the picture width up to four times per edge to find each block's slice.

## Fix

All changes are in `crates/hevc`. They use no `unsafe`, add no dependencies, and leave the output identical sample for sample.

- **`put_uni` / `put_bi` in 16-bit lanes**, dispatched on constant block widths. Prediction samples are 14-bit values (at most about −10 200..26 600), so `s + off` fits an `i16`. For bi-prediction the exact identity `(a + b + off) >> s == ((a >> 1) + (b >> 1) + (a & b & 1) + off / 2) >> (s − 1)` keeps the sum in 16 bits.
- **8-bit first interpolation passes accumulate in 16-bit lanes.** The filtered value of 8-bit samples lies within −24·255..88·255 for every luma and chroma filter. Wrapping sums are exact whenever the final value fits.
- **Full-sample uni-prediction without weighting copies the reference straight into the picture** (`Frame::copy_block`, with edge replication). Block lines and window lines are copied as fixed-size arrays rather than through `memmove` calls.
- **Deblocking:**
  - Boundary strength takes the two slices from `edge_params` (no divisions).
  - Identical motion in the same slice returns bS 0 directly; the spec gives 0 for that case as well.
  - Luma edges are filtered on a gathered 4×8 block with checked slice access instead of per-sample indexing.
- **8-b…

title: Import Avid bins with OP-Atom relinking and bounded effects
author: whatever-industries
body:
An Avid `.avb` is an editorial bin, not a playable media file. Selecting one through **File > Import…** now opens a bin-wide preview: FilmCraft reads clips, subclips, sequences, metadata and media references, lets the user add media search folders, reports partial conversions, and applies the reviewed result as one undoable import. OP-Atom MXF picture and audio components are matched by source identity; the imported project no longer needs the original bin to reopen.

The importer preserves source/timeline clocks, supported sequence formats, media routing and offline diagnostics. Missing or ambiguous media remain visible for relinking. Referenced masters are retained in a dedicated bin, and supported subclips retain their validated ranges. File and graph limits bound malformed or oversized input.

This update also translates a deliberately bounded effect subset: Flip/Flip-Flop, static Resize, supported static 3D Warp geometry and Crop, selected AniMatte shape masks, and sampled Timewarp paths. It accepts only the parameter layouts the decoder can validate. Unsupported effect payloads receive a conversion warning; when an unambiguous underlying clip exists, FilmCraft imports that clip without the unsupported effect rather than replacing its media with an offline segment. The AniMatte subset includes fixed-topology masks and the tested one-point tracked rectangle, not general tracking or every AniMatte mode.

The separate JSON catalog-report route now checks media-reference locations against the report document’s path policy before binding, including metadata-only imports that retain those locations for later use. User metadata named `locations` remains ordinary metadata.

title: Linux: VA-API EncSlice probe and bounded export GPU wait (#1058)
author: vbasky
body:
## Summary

Linux AMD/Intel machines have VA-API decode and VCN/QSV **EncSlice**, but FilmCraft only registered **NVENC** for hardware H.264 export. On those GPUs NVENC declines (`libnvidia-encode.so.1` missing) and export GPU readback used `wgpu::PollType::wait_indefinitely`, which can never return on a wedged radv device (#1058).

- Probe `VAEntrypointEncSlice` / `EncSliceLP` and register that factory **in front of** NVENC so logs name the real path instead of only a missing NVIDIA library.
- A slice encoder is not implemented yet: the factory still returns `None` so NVENC (NVIDIA) then the software encoder run.
- Export / LUT / mask `map_async` waits **8 seconds** (Jev: `t8`), then the GPU path returns `None` and the CPU renderer can take the frame.

Fixes https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/issues/1058

title: #432: VP8 video decodes (clean-room pure-Rust VP8 decoder), so VP8 WebM no longer shows black
author: MrCloudy2
body:
Fixes #432.

## What was wrong

FilmCraft had no VP8 decoder. VP9 and AV1 WebM decode fine, but VP8, the older and very common WebM video codec (browser and screen recordings, older YouTube downloads, GIF-to-video converters), failed with `no decoder for VP8 video`. The clip imported, its audio played, and the picture stayed black, in the monitors and in exports.

## The fix

**New crate `crates/vp8` (L0, pure Rust, no `unsafe`, depends only on `thiserror`, builds for wasm32).** It's a complete VP8 decoder implemented from RFC 6386 sections 1-19:

- **Frame header:** segmentation, normal and simple loop filter with reference / mode deltas, 1-8 token partitions, frame and segment quantizers, golden / altref refresh, copies and sign bias, probability updates and `refresh_entropy_probs`.
- **Intra prediction:** 16x16, chroma and the ten 4x4 subblock modes with the key frame mode contexts and the RFC's edge rules.
- **Inter prediction:** NEAREST / NEAR / ZERO / NEW / SPLIT (all four partitionings), six-tap and bilinear filters, and full-pixel chroma, covering bitstream versions 0-3.
- **Frames:** hidden altref frames, and frame size changes at key frames.

The tables were extracted from the RFC text by `tools/extract_tables.py`, which cuts the text at section 20, so nothing comes from the reference decoder attached to the RFC. No code was taken from libvpx or FFmpeg; they are used only as fixture generators and test oracles, like the VP9 crate.

**Wiring (`crates/codecs`):**

- **Decoder registration:** `Vp8Decoder` / `vp8_factory`, for WebM / Matroska `V_VP8` and MP4 `vp08`.
- **Seeking:** `is_random_access` uses the key frame flag. `is_disposable` lets catch-up skip frames that change no later frame; it compares the frame header against the decoder's current state, so error-resilient temporal-layer streams qualify.
- **Transparent WebM:** the alpha layer (`AlphaMode` 1, #402) now works for VP8 as well as VP9. The alpha decoder already came from the codec registry; onl…

title: #1065: CinemaDNG / DNG import with a clean-room decoder
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1065.
Related: #383

## Problem
Camera RAW was at 0% (docs/codec-parity.md). CinemaDNG, the one cinema RAW format with a public specification, could not be read: `.dng` was not importable, and as a TIFF it would have gone to the TIFF decoder (at best the embedded preview). A CinemaDNG shot (a folder of numbered DNG frames) could not be edited.

## Spec basis
Implemented only from public specifications; no other decoder's source (dcraw, LibRaw, rawspeed, darktable, RawTherapee, FFmpeg, Adobe DNG SDK) was read. Editions are recorded in `crates/dng/README.md`:
- Adobe DNG Specification 1.4.0.0 – 1.7.1.0 (raw IFD, CFA / LinearRaw, linearisation, black / white levels, ActiveArea, DefaultCrop, the chapter 6 colour model)
- TIFF 6.0, TIFF/EP (ISO 12234-2), TIFF Technical Note 1 (SubIFDs)
- ITU-T T.81 Annex H: lossless JPEG, process 14
- CinemaDNG 1.1 (FrameRate, TimeCodes, ReelName), SMPTE ST 12-1 time code packing, Exif 2.3 LightSource
- Published papers: Malvar–He–Cutler 2004 (Bayer demosaic), McCamy 1992 (CCT)

## Fix
- **New L0 crate `filmcraft-dng`** (depends on `thiserror` and optionally `rayon`; builds for wasm; no `unsafe`):
  - TIFF container with SubIFDs. Hostile input is handled safely: offsets are checked, the walk stops at 64 IFDs and 4 levels, cycles end it, and allocations are capped by the image size and by the data present.
  - Raw data: 1–16-bit uncompressed and lossless JPEG (predictors 1–7, 1–4 components, point transform, restart intervals), in strips or tiles. Tiles decode in parallel.
  - DNG processing: linearisation, per-site black levels with row/column deltas, white level, as-shot white balance (clipped highlights stay neutral), Malvar–He–Cutler demosaic (bilinear for non-Bayer patterns), DefaultCrop, ColorMatrix / CameraCalibration / ForwardMatrix with illuminant interpolation, Bradford adaptation to linear Rec. 709, and BaselineExposure.
- **Media integration:** `dng` is now an importable still extension. A DNG develops into scene-linear…

title: #1039: HEVC decodes pictures on several threads inside (WPP rows, tiles, filters next to parsing)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3178. Part of #1039.

#1067 and #1053, which this builds on, are merged; the branch is up to date with `main` (merged, not rebased), so the diff now shows only this change.

## Problem
Frame-level threading decodes each picture on one thread. At 8+ threads the decoder waits on single-threaded pictures: each CTB row of a P/B picture needs reference rows that one thread produces. WPP entry points were parsed, but substreams (and tiles) were decoded one after the other. Frame threads gave 2.3–2.8× at 8 threads; ffmpeg gets 2.6–5.4× (analysis in #1039).

## Fix
With 4+ threads (`Decoder::with_threads` still bounds everything; one rayon pool, no new threads, no new dependency, no `unsafe`), a picture is split into units:

- **WPP** (`entropy_coding_sync_enabled_flag`): one unit per CTB row. Substreams start at `entry_point_offset_minus1` (7.4.7.1). These offsets count emulation prevention bytes, so the slice NAL now records where they were removed. A row decodes into a private window holding the row plus the bottom 4 lines of the row above. Before CTB x it copies in what the row above has published up to x+1: the bottom sample line, 4x4 block state and motion, CTB slice addresses and SAO parameters, and the contexts stored after its second CTB (9.3.1, 9.3.2.4; 2-CTB lag, above-right availability per 6.4.1).
  - A row whose row above is not far enough is **parked**: its CABAC engine state, contexts, qPY_PREV and window are saved, and the thread does other work.
  - The row above resumes it: a pool task once it is far enough, or the thread finishing that row adopts it. A parked row therefore never needs a free thread, and no thread waits on a row nobody decodes.
  - Helpers start lazily (a row starts one when its second CTB is done).
  - Measured before parking existed: blocking on the row above cost ~2 threads' worth of time at 8 threads.
- **Tiles** (without WPP): one unit per tile.
- **Other pictures** (no WPP/tiles, or entry points that don't fit the picture): p…

title: #1065: CinemaDNG in MXF and camera raw Source Settings
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #1065.

**Builds on #1068 (CinemaDNG / DNG import) and #1077 (DNG raw settings, faster decode). Merge those two first.** This branch contains both of them, merged rather than rebased.

## Problem
- CinemaDNG has two storage forms: a folder of DNG frames, and DNG frames wrapped in MXF. The CinemaDNG specification (§4.2) says a decoder shall read both. Only folders opened before this PR; an MXF file with DNG pictures showed the unreadable slate.
- DNG footage could only be developed exactly as the file says. Premiere's Source Settings for camera raw lets you change white balance, exposure and decode quality per clip; FilmCraft had nothing equivalent.
- Playback at reduced resolution still developed every frame at full size.

## Spec basis
- **Adobe CinemaDNG Image Data Format Specification 1.0.0.0 (September 2009), §7: the MXF mapping.**
  - Frame-wrapped DNG picture elements, element type 42h.
  - Essence container labels `06.0E.2B.34.04.01.01.xx.0F.0A.0D.0B.02.7F.01|02.00`, for CFA and LinearRaw.
  - An RGBA descriptor and no coding label.
  - These labels are the specification's **provisional, unregistered values** from Adobe's experimental range (byte 9 = 0Fh). The specification says so itself in §7.4.
- **SMPTE RP 224 register** (Labels.xml from registry.smpte-ra.org): the registered MXF-GC TIFF/EP container (`0D 01 03 01 02 14`) and the TIFF/EP picture coding labels (`04 01 02 02 03 02 01 xx`). These are also accepted.
- **RP 210 Elements register**: the PixelLayout, ComponentMaxRef and ComponentMinRef ULs written in the RGBA descriptor.
- **SMPTE ST 377-1, 379-1/2 and 336**, as the mxf crate already uses them.
- Raw settings behaviour and the white-balance tint sign come from Adobe's public Premiere Pro and Camera Raw help only.
- No other decoder's or demuxer's source was read. No tool we can run reads CinemaDNG MXF, so there is no external oracle.
- **Scope of the CinemaDNG-in-MXF claim:** verified against files written by our own writer; no third-par…

title: #1065: JPEG XL DNG behind an off-by-default feature (needs maintainer decision: new dependency)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #1065. **Needs maintainer decision: new dependency.** Builds on #1068 and #1077; merge those first. Once they are merged, this PR's own change is the last commit only.

## Problem
DNG 1.7 allows JPEG XL raw data (Compression 52546), and FilmCraft has no JPEG XL decoder. Writing one from ISO/IEC 18181 is a project of its own, so these files are refused.

## Spec basis
- DNG 1.7.1.0 Compression 52546: 8–16-bit integer or 16-bit float data, 1 or 3 planes, LinearRaw (not CFA), bare codestream or container.
- JPEG XL itself is decoded by [`jxl-oxide`](https://crates.io/crates/jxl-oxide) 0.12, used only through its public API.

## Fix
- A new `jxl` feature on `filmcraft-dng`, **off by default**, decodes each tile or strip with `jxl-oxide`.
  - Integer samples come back at the codestream's bit depth, so lossless JPEG XL decodes bit-exactly.
  - The decoder runs under `catch_unwind`, and its picture must match the tile or strip.
  - Float JPEG XL, CFA data, and builds without the feature get an error that names JPEG XL.
- The test writer gains `Compression::External` for strips coded by the caller.
- **The dependency:**
  - Licences of the whole tree: `jxl-*` crates MIT OR Apache-2.0, `brotli-decompressor` BSD-3/MIT, `alloc-*` BSD-3, `bytemuck` Zlib/Apache/MIT, `tracing` MIT, `once_cell` and `pin-project-lite` MIT/Apache.
  - `Cargo.lock` gains 16 crates when the feature is enabled; default builds are unchanged.
  - It builds for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.
- Nothing in the app turns the feature on. If you accept the dependency, enable it from `crates/media`.

## Tests
`tests/jxl.rs`:
- Lossless strips are encoded by `cjxl` at test time into `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR`; nothing is committed, and the tests skip when `cjxl` is not installed.
- They decode bit-exactly at 8, 10, 12 and 16 bits, with 1 and 3 channels, as one strip and as several.
- Lossy JPEG XL (`-d 0.5`) decodes close to the original.
- Every truncation and 1500 mutations run under `catch_unwind` without a pan…

title: #371: split stereo halves from FCP7 XML play on their own side
author: carlitosteso3
body:
Refs #371 (audio part only). The bitrate part of #371 (40 Mbps target producing 6.1 Mbps) is **not** touched here.

## Cause
Premiere represents a stereo clip in an FCP7 XML as two mono clips on two tracks, one per channel (`sourcetrack` / `trackindex` 1 and 2). FilmCraft imported each half as a one-channel clip, **centred**: a centred mono clip plays at unity on both sides. So the two halves summed on both L and R. That's about +3 dB for a stereo source with uncorrelated channels and +6 dB for dual-mono dialogue, compared with the source.

## Fix
- **Import** (`fcp7.rs`): when an imported clip takes one channel of a stereo media item (channel 0 or 1), its Panner balance is set to its own side (−100 / +100), so the pair plays back as the original stereo clip. An `audiopan` filter in the XML is read afterwards and still overrides this.
- **Export**: a one-channel clip always writes its Audio Pan filter, even when centred. A centred Breakout to Mono then round-trips centred instead of being re-panned to a side by the importer above.

## Tests
New in `crates/interchange/tests/fcp7.rs`:
- `split_stereo_halves_are_panned_to_their_side`: the A1 half is panned fully left and the A2 half fully right.
- `split_stereo_half_keeps_its_audio_pan`: an Audio Pan filter on a split half still wins.
- `centred_mono_breakout_round_trips_centred`: a centred one-channel clip exports its Audio Pan and imports back centred.

Measured in the cloud session where this was written:
- **Before:** the imported split stereo pair played +3 dB louder than the source with uncorrelated channels, and +6 dB with dual mono.
- **After:** 0 dB, identical to the source.

## Checks
- Rebased on current `main`. On Windows 11 (Rust 1.99): `cargo test -p filmcraft-interchange` passed 73 of 73. `clippy -D warnings` and `rustfmt --check` on the changed files are clean.
- In the Linux cloud session, `fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, `xtask layers`, `xtask assets` and `xtask wasm` pass. `cargo test --workspace` had 6 …

title: #1092: Project panel Shift-click selects the range from the anchor
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1092.

## Problem
Shift-click in the Project panel toggled a single item exactly like Ctrl/Cmd-click. The items between the first and the Shift-clicked one were not selected, and there was no selection anchor.

## Fix
`ProjectPanelUi::anchor` remembers the last item clicked without Shift. Shift-click selects the range from the anchor to the clicked item in the order the view shows (List, Icon, Freeform; search filter and twirled-open bins respected). Ctrl/Cmd+Shift adds the range to the current selection. Ctrl/Cmd-click still toggles and sets the anchor. Without a usable anchor, Shift-click acts as a plain click. The logic is a pure helper, `click_selection`, in `project_views.rs`.

title: #1091: Home / End and other jumps scroll the Timeline to the playhead
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1091.

## Problem
The Timeline followed the playhead only while playing. Home, End, edit-point and marker jumps while stopped moved the playhead but left the view where it was, so the playhead could be off screen (Premiere scrolls it into view).

## Fix
`TimelineView` remembers the last playhead it saw (per sequence, not serialised). When the shown sequence's playhead changes while stopped and lies outside the view, the view scrolls to it with the page-scroll margin (`scroll_to_reveal`). A tab switch does not count as a jump, so each tab keeps its own view.

## Tests
- `home_and_end_bring_the_playhead_into_view` (headless UI; fails without the fix)
- `reveal_tests` unit tests for `scroll_to_reveal`, including NaN and zero zoom.

title: Text editing on the Program monitor: double-click and Ctrl/Cmd+A select all the text (#1102)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1102. It covers both points of the issue:

1. **Double-click selects the whole text.** When you double-click a text layer with the Selection tool, the edit now starts with all of the text selected (anchor 0, caret at the end), so typing replaces it, as in Premiere. Before, the caret went to the click position. A click with the Type tool still puts the caret where you click.
2. **Select All selects the text being edited.** On macOS the native menu bar (muda) takes Cmd+A as the Edit ▸ Select All key equivalent before egui sees the key. It sent `edit.selectAll` to the command inbox, and that selected every timeline clip. The text editor's own Cmd+A handler never got the key. Now `menus::invoke` checks for this case: while a text layer is edited on the monitor, `edit.selectAll` selects all of that text and leaves the clip selection alone. Because the check is in `menus::invoke`, it covers every way to reach Select All: the native menu's Cmd+A, a click on Edit ▸ Select All in either menu bar, and the in-app shortcut. On Windows and Linux, Ctrl+A already reached the text editor's handler, because shortcuts pause while the text holds keyboard focus. Nothing changes there.

The text length comes from the layer being edited, found the same way `visible_layers` finds it. If no text is being edited, Select All works as before.

`docs/graphics.md` (Selection tool row) now describes both behaviours.

Test: `double_click_and_select_all_select_the_text_being_edited` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/graphics_handles_ui.rs`. It double-clicks a point text layer on the monitor and checks that the whole text is selected. Then it moves the caret to the end, sends `edit.selectAll` through the command inbox (the native macOS menu path), and checks that the text is selected again and the timeline selection is unchanged. Both checks fail without the fix.

The click-to-place-caret request in the issue comments is not part of this PR.

title: Engine: list edge, params and reverse in the sequence.applyAudioTransition schema (#1100)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1100.

`sequence.applyAudioTransition` shares `apply_transition` with `sequence.applyVideoTransition` and already reads `edge`, `params` and `reverse`, but its schema only advertised `clip`, `effect` and `frames`. Clients using `describe`, `commands --json` or MCP could not see that a fade can go on a clip's out edge.

The audio schema now matches the video one: `"edge":"in"|"out"?`, `"params":{param:value}?`, `"reverse":bool?`, and `effect` shows an example name (`constant_power|Constant Power|…`) in the same form the video schema uses. The handler is unchanged.

Test: `audio_transition_schema_lists_edge_params_and_reverse` in `mixer_tests.rs` checks that the schema contains these keys. It fails on `main`.

title: Timeline: keep continuous thumbnails fixed while the view zooms (#1094)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1094.

With **Show Video Thumbnails ▸ Continuous**, every zoom step changed the clip's on-screen width, so `thumbnail_tiles` gave every tile a new source time on every frame. Each new time missed the thumbnail cache (tiles went blank) and queued a new decode job. A short zoom queued hundreds of jobs that no longer mattered, and the frames for the settled view had to wait behind them.

**Change** (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs`):
- While the view zooms (a zoom-bar handle drag, or `pps` still animating towards `target_pps` after wheel, pinch or keyboard zoom), `TlState::thumb_pps` holds the zoom the gesture started at. It is set and cleared once per frame in `show`, next to the existing zoom animation.
- The new `zoomed_thumbnail_tiles` lays the Continuous tiles out at that held zoom and then stretches each tile to where its frame sits at the live zoom. Every tile keeps the frame it already showed (from the cache), stays over the right part of the clip, and requests no new frames for each zoom step. Head and Head-and-Tail don't depend on the zoom, so they are unchanged.
- When the zoom settles, the tiles are laid out once for the new view and only those frames are requested.

How this covers the issue's points:
1. Flicker while zooming: tiles keep their cached frames, so they no longer blank.
2. and 3. Missing tiles and the 20 s backlog after release: no obsolete requests are queued during the zoom, so the frames for the settled view are the only new thumbnail jobs. This PR doesn't add cancellation of queued prio-50 jobs in `frames.rs`. Those jobs also serve the Project panel thumbnails, so which of them count as "superseded" is a separate decision. With the source of the backlog gone, it isn't needed for this bug.

**Test:** `zooming_keeps_the_frames_shown_before_the_zoom` zooms a clip from 20 to 40 pt/s. It checks that the tiles keep the source offsets they had before the zoom and are stretched to their new positions, that the layout returns to the n…

title: Timeline: a press on the ruler moves the playhead at once (#1090)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1090.

A press on the Timeline ruler did nothing until the pointer moved past egui's drag threshold or the button came up: the playhead was only set in the `drag_started() || clicked()` branch. Premiere moves the playhead the moment the button goes down, then follows the mouse.

- `interact` now sets the playhead on the press frame when the press lands on the ruler (`Grab::Other(Hit::Ruler)`), in the same place that already records what the button went down on (#259).
- The scrub code (stop playback, frame snap, Shift / Snap-playhead snapping, exact marker position from #695) moved into a small `scrub_playhead` helper that the press and the existing drag/click path share, so both behave the same way. Drags and clicks behave as before.

Test: `playhead_jumps_to_a_press_on_the_ruler` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/settings_ui.rs`, next to the existing ruler drag test (#164). It presses on the ruler with no move and no release, checks that the playhead is already under the pointer, then checks that the release leaves it there. Without the fix the first assertion fails because the playhead stays at 0.

title: Type text committed by an input method into text layers on the monitor (#1083)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1083.

Typing into a text layer on the Program monitor with a Chinese input method did nothing, while English worked and the right panel accepted Chinese.

**Cause.** The monitor's text editing (`text_edit` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/graphics.rs`) already turns IME on (it sets `PlatformOutput::ime`), but it only inserted `Event::Text` and `Event::Paste`. An input method (Chinese, Japanese, Korean) hands over the finished text as `Event::Ime(ImeEvent::Commit)`, so that event was dropped. The right panel uses egui's `TextEdit`, which handles the commit, so it worked there.

**Fix.** The commit event now goes through the same arm as typed and pasted text: it replaces the selection and moves the caret, like egui's `TextEdit` does. Preedit (the text still being composed) is left alone; the input method shows it in its own candidate window at the caret.

**Test.** `text_committed_by_an_input_method_is_typed_on_the_monitor` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/graphics_handles_ui.rs` uses the Type tool on the monitor, types "A", then sends the events Microsoft Pinyin sends for 你好 (`Preedit("ni hao")`, `Preedit("")`, `Commit("你好")`). It checks that the layer's text is `A你好`. Without the fix the text stays `A`.

title: Export: unknown keys in `settings` are an error, not ignored
author: japbcoelho
body:
## What and why

A key inside `settings` that `ExportSettings` doesn't have was dropped without a word, and the export ran as if it were absent. `filmcraft-cli export --settings '{"loudnessLufs":-14}'` (the flat parameter put inside `settings`) exported at -18.3 LUFS instead of -14, and a misspelt nested key such as `effects.loudness.targetLoudness` did nothing either: `settings_from_params` merges the patch into the serialized settings and deserializes with `#[serde(default)]`, which ignores unknown keys.

It now compares the patch with the resolved settings and refuses the first key they don't have, matching keys as `merge` does, so the camelCase spelling of a snake_case field (#531) is accepted:

```
settings: unknown key `loudnessLufs` (see export.presets.get for the settings' keys)
```

A null value is accepted anywhere: it sets nothing.

## How it was tested

New test `export_tests::unknown_settings_keys_are_errors_not_ignored` in `crates/engine/src/export_tests.rs` (a top-level and a nested unknown key are errors; `target_lufs` and `targetLufs` both work; null is accepted). `nested_camel_case_settings_are_honoured` from #531 still passes. On main `0800a8b0`: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine` (543 passed) pass; the full `cargo xtask ci` is left to the checks here.

title: feat(web): share resident GPU sources and lazy CPU fallback
author: WavJaby
body:
Web preview extracts decoded pixels to CPU before uploading them for GPU rendering. Eligible WebCodecs frames now copy directly into a private GPU texture consumed by the shared source/effect/compositor path. Original YUV extraction starts only when a CPU consumer requests it; GPU-only rendering avoids `VideoFrame.copyTo`. A GPU -> GPU copy remains.

Based on Windows #1021 (`a9a5b69683c`), including API #1019 and main `cee1feb1`. Land #1019 -> #1021 -> #1114. The Web/shared overlay remains 24 paths; the cumulative diff includes prerequisites until they land. Superseded #462 implementation is excluded. Windows decode/storage/prefetch/seek policy stays intact; its adapter follows the shared API. CPU readiness, YUV/RGBA reconstruction, effect-pool lifetime and pending-error handling also affect desktop-used code.

Refs #30, #1373 and #1379: decoded frame -> private texture -> shared source/effect/compositor, with lazy original-YUV CPU access. GPU-to-encoder export, Linux/macOS interop and decoder/cache lifetime separation remain outside scope.

Resident eligibility requires full-visible, even-sized NV12/I420, matching coded/visible/display sizes, BT.709 metadata and no rotation/flip. Other inputs retain CPU extraction and Canvas recovery. The shared importer accepts YUV/RGBA; source reconstruction is separate from effects. CPU fallback retains original-picture YUV semantics. No eager YUV backup or decode/prefetch/seek/cache-policy change.

title: Wayland: native file drag and drop through a patched winit (#1022)
author: DomiLuebben
body:
Fixes #1022.

## Problem
On a Wayland session, dragging a file from a file manager onto FilmCraft shows the "no" cursor and does nothing. eframe 0.36 builds on winit 0.30.13, whose Wayland backend has no drag and drop (X11 has). #634 sends Wayland users to XWayland instead; this makes the native Wayland window take the drop itself, which also works on compositors whose X bridge doesn't carry drag and drop (niri's xwayland-satellite) and keeps native Wayland scaling and input.

## What it does
- `patches/winit` is winit 0.30.13 as published (first commit; its doc `.svg` and example `.png` images are left out, because `cargo xtask assets` would want a sidecar for each and nothing builds them for a dependency). It is wired in with `[patch.crates-io]` and excluded from the workspace.
- The second commit adds `patches/winit/src/platform_impl/linux/wayland/seat/dnd.rs` (about 300 lines, safe Rust): it binds `wl_data_device_manager` and one `wl_data_device` per seat. For a drag that offers `text/uri-list` it accepts the Copy action only (so the source never deletes a file because of us), reads the list through a calloop source and reports what the X11 backend reports: `HoveredFile` per file, `DroppedFile` on drop (also when the drop arrives before the whole list has), `HoveredFileCancelled` when the drag leaves. A drag without files is refused so the source shows "no drop here".
- The pointer sends nothing during a drag, so the drag position is reported as `CursorMoved`. FilmCraft needs nothing else: `drop_pointer` already falls back to egui's latest pointer position where the platform hook has no answer (Linux), so drops land on the Timeline where they are released.
- Only local `file:` URIs are accepted (`file:///…`, `file://localhost/…`, `file:/…`); other hosts and schemes are skipped, `%XX` is decoded to bytes, a path with a NUL byte is refused, and the list is capped at 4 MiB. The pipe is read with `std` from a duplicate of the descriptor, so no `unsafe` is added.

title: fix: シーケンス配置時の自動文字起こしを実行 #903
author: haranishi
body:

「Automatically transcribe clips」を有効にして既定の `sequenceClips` を使っても、音声をシーケンスに配置した際に文字起こしが実行されませんでした。配置後の有効な音声クリップを共通のコマンド処理で検出し、既存の認識器と文字起こし設定で自動生成します。

- Source Insert/Overwrite、Timeline配置、クリップからのシーケンス作成、Paste/Paste Insert、シーケンス展開を同じ検出処理で扱います。

title: fix(captions): apply body and div timing to TTML paragraphs (#895)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #895 The TTML/DFXP reader only applied `begin` from `
` elements. `begin`, `end` and `dur` on `` were never read, so a file with `` imported its captions five seconds early, with no warning. The reader now treats `body` the same as `div`, as a `par` time container. Begins add up down the tree, as they already did for nested divs. A container's end (from `end` or `dur`) clips the paragraphs inside it, and drops any that start after it. A paragraph with a begin but no end now runs until its container ends instead of being dropped, and so does an untimed paragraph inside a container that has an end. When an element has both `end` and `dur`, the earlier one wins. A paragraph whose time expression doesn't parse is still dropped with a warning, as before. `timeContainer="seq"` is still not supported, but the reader now warns about it instead of quietly timing it as `par`. Export needed no change. The writer puts absolute times on each `

` under an untimed body and div, so whatever times the reader resolved come back the same after a write and re-read. Tests: `crates/captions/tests/ttml_body_timing.rs` is the issue's test plus cases for a div begin, nested body/div/div offsets, timed spans under a body offset, clipping by a container's end and dur, paragraphs without an end, end vs dur, the seq warning, and export round-trip. Each case runs in both TTML and DFXP mode. Files without container timing come out unchanged, and the existing unit and round-trip property tests still pass. The issue's test failed on main with (1.0, 2.0) instead of (6.0, 7.0). Checks I ran: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-captions --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p filmcraft-captions` and `cargo xtask layers`. Release clippy on the whole workspace also passed. I didn't run the full workspace tests or the wasm step locally and left them to CI. title: fix(effects): keep a setParam keyframe outside the clip at its time (#1055)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
`effects.setParam` clamped an explicit `time` to the clip's first and last frame. A keyframe set past the end therefore landed on the last frame: it overwrote a keyframe already there (case A in the issue) or squashed a ramp so it finished at the clip end (case B). Times before the start were clamped the same way.

I went with the issue's first option. An explicit `time` (or `frame`/`seconds`/`timecode`) now puts the keyframe at that time, even outside the clip, so the visible part shows the right slice of the ramp. This matches what the repo already allows: `effects.moveKeyframe` takes any `to`, and keyframes left outside a trimmed clip keep working, which is also how Premiere treats them. Both ends behave the same way. When no time is given, the playhead is still pinned to the clip as before. Tick arithmetic saturates, so hostile times like `i64::MIN`/`i64::MAX` are safe. I updated the command's parameter doc string to describe this.

Tests: `set_param_keeps_a_keyframe_outside_the_clip_at_its_time` in `crates/engine/src/tests.rs` covers case A (three keyframes, the clip-end one intact), case B (75% at mid-clip for a ramp that ends one clip length past the end), the same thing before the start, extreme times, and the playhead fallback. It failed on main with `{"keyframes":2}`.

Locally I ran `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine` (543 pass), `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask wasm`. The one engine failure is `every_builtin_preset_exports_and_ffprobe_confirms` on its APV preset, because my local ffprobe 6.1 doesn't know APV. That has nothing to do with this change. I left the full workspace run to CI.

Not verified: I didn't try it by hand in the app or render the issue's repro clip, and I didn't check how the Effect Controls panel draws a keyframe placed this way (moveKeyframe could already put keyframes there).

Fixes #1055

title: fix(cli): fail export/render that drew offline media unless --allow-offline (#1054)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #1054

When a clip's media was missing, `filmcraft-cli export` wrote "media not found" placeholder frames, printed the normal result and exited 0. `render` did the same. Nothing in the output said the picture was wrong.

The engine now keeps track of what it actually drew. The export's media provider records the items it is asked for, and when the export finishes it checks which of them rendered as the offline slate (missing, made offline, or unreadable, using the same words as `media.status`). That list comes back as `offlineMedia` in the `file.exportMedia` result, in `jobs.list` entries for export jobs and in `export.queue` items. The bridge client and MCP long exports copy it from `jobs.list` too. Clips outside the export range aren't reported because they never get rendered. The engine still lets the export succeed, so the desktop app and MCP behave as before and each front end can decide what to do with the list.

The CLI now prints one stderr line per offline item for `export` and `render`, then exits 1 after writing the file. With `--allow-offline` it still prints the warning but exits 0. `filmcraft-cli help` and docs/agents.md cover the flag and the new field.

Tests:
- engine: export with one file deleted, both inside and outside the range, made-offline media, the queue, `jobs.list`, and a single rendered frame
- CLI integration test: online export is clean; missing media fails with exit 1 and a stderr message naming the file; `--allow-offline` exits 0 and still warns; same for `render`
- bridge unit test for the pass-through
- I reproduced the issue's own script on main, then ran it again with the fix (exit 1, item listed)

title: Window: redesigned menu bar with title and mode bars, system title bar option
author: rafi612
body:
### Overview

Ports the title-bar work from Photocraft and VectorCraft:
- [storytold/photocraft#1903](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/pull/1903) — system title bar (in-app mark/title hidden, file in the OS title)
- [storytold/vectorcraft#969](https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/pull/969) — compact app bar + system title bar option

### Redesign

On Windows/Linux the single 38 pt header is replaced with two bars, as in PhotoCraft:

- **Title bar (32 pt)** — brand mark, in-window menu bar (File … Help), centred document title, quick actions on the right (Discord, Appearance, Search, Workspaces), native-width caption buttons (Minimize / Maximize / Restore / Close).
- **Mode bar (38 pt)** — Home and Import / Edit / Export on the left, session actions (Quick Export, notifications, volume, full screen) on the right.

Only the free gap between the menus and the right cluster drags the window (a press on a menu title opens the menu, never moves it); double-click maximizes. Close goes through `app.quit`, so unsaved work still gets the Save / Don't Save / Cancel prompt. Narrow windows drop Discord first, then the theme toggle, then search — same order as PhotoCraft.

### Client-side decorations

New `ui-egui::titlebar` module (ported from PhotoCraft): caption buttons flush with the window edge, invisible 8 pt edge / 12 pt corner resize zones (`BeginResize`), and the KDE Wayland release workaround in `raw_input_hook`. The window is created borderless (`with_decorations(false)`); the brand mark is painted from the app icon like in PhotoCraft.

### System title bar setting

title: feat(platform): Intel Quick Sync Video (QSV) hardware encoding for Linux and Windows
author: AnarchByte0
body:
### Summary
This PR adds Intel Quick Sync Video (QSV) hardware video encoding to `crates/platform` using hardware Media Foundation transforms on Windows:
- **Codecs Supported**: H.264 (High Profile, 8-bit), HEVC (Main & Main 10 HDR), and AV1 (Main & Main 10 HDR).
- **Intel Hardware Filtering**: Selects Intel MFT transforms strictly matching Intel Vendor ID (`0x8086`) and friendly name, safely releasing COM activation objects.
- **Priority on Hybrid Systems**: Registered ahead of NVENC so NVENC takes precedence when an NVIDIA GPU is also available.
- **MP4 Payload Formatting**: Re-packages Annex B bitstream into 4-byte length-prefixed NALs and parses parameter sets (SPS/PPS/VPS) for compliant `AvcConfig`, `HevcConfig`, and `Av1Config` sample entries.
- **Portability**: All Windows-specific FFI and helpers are strictly isolated with `#[cfg(target_os = "windows")]` so 64-bit Linux builds remain clean.
- **Boundary Validation**: Declines odd, zero, or oversized resolutions exceeding 8192×8192.

Part of #30 (Hardware Acceleration) and Milestone M9 (Codec Parity).

### Verification & Receipts
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-platform --test qsv_export`: 6 tests PASS.
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-platform --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS (0 warnings).
- `cargo xtask layers`: PASS (`layers: ok`).
- Rule 0 (Never Crash): All background probe tasks use `catch_unwind`; handles `MF_E_NOTACCEPTING` and `MF_E_TRANSFORM_NEED_MORE_INPUT` gracefully without frame loss.

title: fix(menus): native menu follows command enablement (#902)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #902

On macOS the native menu bar created every item with `enabled = true`, and the update hook only ran when shortcuts or the language changed and never touched enablement. muda turns off AppKit's automatic enabling, so Edit > Undo and Redo stayed clickable with empty history (and so did every other unavailable command), and clicking them just put "nothing to undo" in the status bar.

What changed:

- `native_menu::install` creates items with the enablement from `menu_items`, like the in-window menus.
- The `shortcuts_changed` hook is now `menu_changed`. `FilmcraftApp::sync_native_menu` runs once per frame, computes the menu tree (the in-window menu bar already does this every frame on other platforms) and calls the hook only when it differs from the last one it sent. The three explicit hook calls (shortcut change, language change in prefs and from the menu) are covered by that and removed.
- The macOS updater remembers what each item shows and calls `set_text` / `set_accelerator` / `set_enabled` only for what changed, and retitles submenus only when the language changes.

The repo has no "Undo <action>" labels anywhere, so I left the labels alone.

Testing: a new unit test in `ui-egui` drives `sync_native_menu` with a capturing hook. With an empty project Undo and Redo come out disabled and File > New > Project enabled. A second sync with nothing changed doesn't call the hook. After an edit Undo is enabled, and after undoing it Redo is enabled. `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui`, clippy `-D warnings` on `filmcraft-ui-egui`, fmt, `xtask layers` and `xtask assets` pass locally. title: fix(timeline): snap sub-frame timeline.place to the frame grid; inspect counts export's frames (#1101)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #1101

`timeline.place` kept a `time` that fell between frames but rounded the duration to whole frames, so the clip ended after `time + duration`. In the issue's example it ended a third of a frame past frame 120. The sequence then ended between frames. `sequence.inspect` floored that to 120 frames while export counts the partial frame and rendered 121.

Two changes:

- `timeline.place` now snaps the start and the end (`time + duration`) to the nearest frame each, then places the span between them. A timeline drag already snaps to the nearest frame, so the command now matches the UI. I left `make_track_item` alone because voice-over recording places clips at sample-accurate, sub-frame starts on purpose and has tests for that.
- The sequence-level `durationFrames` in `sequence.inspect` now uses `filmcraft_export::frame_span`, the same function export and `export.resolve` use to count frames. The two numbers can't drift apart again, even when a sequence ends mid-frame some other way (for example `timeline.move` to a sub-frame time, which still keeps the exact time).

I also added a note to docs/agents.md about both behaviours.

Testing: two new engine tests in `source_placement_tests.rs`. The first is the issue's repro: a clip placed a third of a frame after frame 60 that should end on frame 120. The second moves a clip to a sub-frame time and checks that inspect and `export.resolve` agree on 49 frames. Both failed before the fix (the clip ended at 1273608000000, and inspect said 48 where export said 49). `cargo test -p filmcraft-project -p filmcraft-engine` passes, apart from `every_builtin_preset_exports_and_ffprobe_confirms`. That test fails the same way on main for me because my local ffprobe doesn't know APV. fmt, clippy `-D warnings` on the engine and `cargo xtask layers` are clean.

title: #395: Arabic and Hebrew in the interface: fallback fonts, captions in reading order
author: seif9116
body:
Arabic (and Hebrew) caption text shows as missing-glyph boxes in the Text panel's caption list and in the caption blocks on the timeline, while the Program monitor draws it correctly. Refs #395 and #135.

## What changes

- **Fallback fonts** (`crates/ui-egui/src/rtl.rs`, the same pattern as `cjk.rs`). The craft-fonts `Arab` / `Hebr` faces are used when present. Otherwise one installed face per script is looked up once, preferring Noto Sans Arabic, SF Arabic, Geeza Pro, Segoe UI, Noto Naskh Arabic, Tahoma, Arial and DejaVu Sans (Noto Sans Hebrew, SF Hebrew, Arial Hebrew… for Hebrew). That face goes last in every UI font family, so Latin text keeps Inter.
- **Reading order.** egui 0.36 shapes each font run with harfrust, so the letters join. But it places runs left to right in logical order with no bidi pass, so multi-word Arabic reads backwards. `rtl::Lines` fixes that in three steps:
  - It breaks lines on the logical text, as egui wraps it.
  - It reorders each line with `unicode-bidi` (UAX #9, the crate `crates/text` already uses for titles).
  - It gives every right-to-left word its own layout section, so egui's shaper runs it right to left.
  
  Brackets are mirrored, and Arabic-Indic digits keep their order.
- **Where it applies.** Caption blocks on the timeline use it: right-to-left captions start at the block's right edge, so a clipped block still shows the beginning. The Text panel caption list uses it too. While a caption is being edited, the field shows egui's logical order, because `TextEdit` maps the caret by character index and a reordered galley would put the caret in the wrong place. The field goes back to reading order when it loses focus.
- Text without right-to-left letters takes the old path unchanged.

## Not in this PR

- Other names (media, clips, track names) now get real glyphs with joined letters, but they keep egui's run order. `rtl::Lines` / `rtl::paint_line` can be adopted there next.
- Mirroring the interface for an Arabic translation.

title: fix(timeline): preserve explicit placement durations
author: Marssvoodoo
body:
Fixes #1101.

Related: #1139 proposes snapping placement starts and ends to the frame grid. This alternative preserves the requested sub-frame start and explicit duration, while retaining the existing defaults when duration is omitted.

`timeline.place` preserves a sub-frame start but currently rounds its duration independently. At 24 fps, a requested start of 638568000000 ticks and duration of 631512000000 ticks should end at 1270080000000 (5 seconds); rounding extends it into a 121st frame.

Preserve the exact tick duration only when a numeric `timeline.place.duration` is explicitly supplied, retaining the existing one-sequence-frame minimum. Apply the duration inside the placement transaction before insert/overwrite so linked video/audio and undo/redo use the same span. The shared project constructor, omitted durations, image-sequence defaults and source Insert/Overwrite keep their existing rounding behavior.

Sequence-level `durationFrames` now counts a partially occupied final frame using the same frame-span calculation as export. Clip frame-coordinate fields keep their existing behavior. The agent documentation explains the distinction.

Regression coverage includes audio-only and linked A/V insert/overwrite placement, source offsets, undo/redo, the one-frame minimum, omitted-duration rounding, unchanged source editing, empty sequences and partial final frames. The placement and inspection regressions failed against the original implementation. The full engine suite passes: 546 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored, including the existing image-sequence regression unchanged.

Six deliberate mutations were caught: rounded video duration, rounded audio duration, exact implicit durations, a two-frame minimum, changed source-edit duration, and a floored sequence frame count. All restored regressions passed. Dependency-layer, asset and WebAssembly checks pass (44 crates checked for wasm).

title: fix(audio): シャトル再生で音程維持設定を反映 (#959)
author: haranishi
body:
Timelineで「Maintain pitch while shuttling」をオンにしても設定が再生処理に使われず、倍速で声や音楽の音程が上がっていました。設定に応じて音程を補正し、現在音声が対応している0.5〜4倍速で元の音程を保ちます。

既存のRust製PitchShifterとStreamResamplerを使用します。速い再生ではレート変換前に補正し、遅い再生では内部サンプルレートを上げて高域を保ちます。4倍速は2段で補正し、処理の遅延分を事前に読み込んで再生位置に合わせます。通常速度は処理をバイパスします。

再生中に設定を変更すると、現在の再生位置から音声を再開します。設定オフは従来の音程変化を維持します。

検証：

- 修正前の実start_audio経路で、設定オンでも元の音程が失われることを合成PCMで再現。
- AudioOutへ渡される実際のサンプルで、設定オン・オフ、0.5/1/1.5/2/4倍速、左右の周波数、通常速度の同一出力、音声クロックと映像位置を確認。
- 44.1/48/96kHz、6チャンネル、18kHzまでの高域、ブロック分割、シーク、短い音の時間位置、不正な座標やチャンネル数を検証。
- `cargo xtask ci`成功：250テスト群・2,811 passed・41 ignored、fmt/clippy/layers/assets（69）/wasm（44 crates）。release検証時のみ`CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false`を指定し、リポジトリの設定は変更していません。
- ネイティブアプリのcontrol APIでLキー相当の倍速操作、再生中の設定チェックボックス切り替え、各速度での音声クロックと再生位置の進行を確認。プロジェクト内容が変わらないことも確認しました。
- Linux CI（fork）：[成功](https://github.com/haranishi/filmcraft/actions/runs/38171615472)。修正commit `f5a783769dd125697c970ab8dadd9ac7328b3820`を固定checkoutし、一致検査と品質ゲートを実行しています。

物理スピーカーでの聴感評価とブラウザーのWebAudio実動作は未検証です。音程の証拠は出力PCMの周波数検査です。

title: feat(ui): add on-screen transform gizmo for clips in Program monitor (fixes #639)
author: Azuras03
body:
### Summary

Implements on-screen direct manipulation (transform gizmo) for video clips in the Program monitor, addressing Premiere Pro UI parity gap **#639** (G8).

### Features & Capabilities

1. **Bounding Box & Wireframe**
       - Projects the active clip boundary using `filmcraft_render::motion_matrix` and sequence-to-screen view mapping (respecting display aspect ratio, zoom, and pan).

2. **8 Scale / Resize Handles**
       - 4 corner handles and 4 edge midpoint handles with rotation-adjusted directional resize cursors (`ResizeNwSe`, `ResizeNeSw`, `ResizeHorizontal`, `ResizeVertical`).
       - Supports uniform scaling by default (or toggleable with `Shift`), and non-uniform width/height stretching on edge handles.
       - Scales about the opposite handle, or about the anchor point when holding `Alt`/`Option`.

3. **Translation (Move)**
       - Dragging inside the bounding box updates clip `position` directly in sequence pixels.
       - Constrains to horizontal or vertical axis when holding `Shift`.

4. **Rotation**
       - Hovering outside corner handles activates the rotation zone and crosshair cursor.
       - Dragging rotates the clip around its anchor point, with 15° angle snapping when holding `Shift`.

5. **Anchor Point Repositioning**
       - Dragging the anchor point crosshair (`⨁`) updates `anchor` in clip space while compensating `position` so the visual clip remains stationary on screen.

6. **Direct Clip Selection**
       - Clicking an unselected clip directly in the Program monitor selects it on the timeline (`timeline.select`).

7. **Deterministic & Flicker-Free Interaction**
       - Transformations are computed deterministically against the initial drag state to prevent recursive feedback loops or tick-based scale oscillations.

8. **Undo/Redo & Keyframing**
       - Dragging gestures merge into a single atomic undo step (`Ctrl+Z` / `Cmd+Z`) via `effects.setParam` with `merge: true` and dedicated `merge_key`.

title: feat(export): advanced rate control (CQP/VBR multipass) and adaptive export UI
author: AnarchByte0
body:
### Summary
This PR adds advanced rate control modes and controls to FilmCraft's export pipeline:
- **Constant Quantizer (CQP)**: Direct quality control via quantizer parameters (`qp: 0..51`).
- **Advanced Encoder Controls**: Exposes multipass encoding, spatial adaptive quantization (Spatial AQ), and lookahead depth for supported hardware backends.
- **Adaptive Export UI**: Contextually displays CQP, QP sliders, multipass, and lookahead settings only when supported by the active format/encoder.
- **Buffer Safety**: Dynamically scales the encoder input surface ring buffer when lookahead is enabled to prevent frame submission stalls.

Resolves #371 and part of #30 (Hardware Acceleration).

title: i18n: add Czech (cs) interface language
