title: #1437: mpegts: drop TEI/duplicate packets, skip scrambled, first PMT wins
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1437

## Cause
`ts.rs` ignored `transport_error_indicator`, `transport_scrambling_control` and duplicate packets, so garbage / encrypted / twice-sent payload reached the splitter. PMT handling ignored `current_next_indicator` and `section_number`; a new PMT version only added PIDs (a PID that changed codec kept its old splitter, removed PIDs stayed); the CRC ran before the version check; the PAT was re-parsed on every repeat.

## Decisions (proposed, not yet confirmed by a maintainer)
- TEI packets are dropped; scrambled packets are skipped with a warning (not an error); exact duplicates are dropped, conservatively (same PID, same counter as the previous payload packet, identical payload bytes, has payload; anything else is kept). All three are counted in the scan warnings.
- A later PMT version still adds PIDs it newly lists; known PIDs are never changed or removed. A later PMT that changes the stream type of, or drops, a known PID is ignored for that part, with one warning. `current_next_indicator` 0 is ignored (PAT and PMT); a PMT must be section 0 of 0 (as H.222.0 requires, matching the existing single-section handling). The PAT is not processed once the PMT PID is known. The version check runs before the CRC (a repeat of the used PMT costs no CRC); a differing version is CRC-checked before it counts as a change.

## Notes
- `read_unit` applies the same TEI / scrambled / duplicate filter as the scan, so unit offsets into the elementary stream stay consistent.
- The TEI check runs before packet parsing, so a flagged packet with a garbage adaptation field is dropped rather than treated as lost sync. Scrambled packets still contribute their PCR and keep the continuity counter in step (no spurious CC error).
- PAT is not restricted to section 0 (a program may be listed in a later section; the existing code accepted the first program of any section).

## Tests (crates/mpegts/src/tests.rs)
TEI packet dropped; scrambled packet skipped with warning; duplicate dro…

title: #1436: mpegts: H.264/HEVC units are access units; H.264 recovery points are key
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1436

## Cause
`crates/mpegts/src/es.rs` made an H.264/HEVC unit out of one PES packet with a timestamp (the crate docs claimed access-unit splitting). Two defects followed:
- **B8**: several access units in one PES (only the first has a PTS) became one unit: several frames under one PTS to the decoder, `key`/`disposable` OR-combined.
- **B7**: H.264 `key` was IDR only (NAL type 5). Broadcast/camcorder/cut TS with non-IDR I pictures plus recovery point SEI had no (or only one) key unit, so `mpeg.rs` failed with "no random-access picture in the video stream" or seeks always went back to the start.

## User decisions implemented
- B8 (A): split units by access unit. A new unit starts at the first NAL that cannot belong to the slices already seen (H.264 7.4.1.2.3: AUD, SPS, PPS, SEI, NAL 14..18; H.265 7.4.2.4.4: AUD, VPS/SPS/PPS, prefix SEI, 41..44, 48..55) or at a slice with first_mb_in_slice == 0 / first_slice_segment_in_pic_flag. Only the first access unit of a PES keeps its PTS/DTS; later ones have none. A 4-byte start code's leading zero byte goes with its own NAL. Redundant pictures and arbitrary slice order are not specially handled (spec's frame_num/pps-id comparison needs the SPS; not done).
- B7 (A): an H.264 unit containing a recovery point SEI (payload type 6, found among other messages, emulation prevention removed) with `recovery_frame_cnt` 0 is `key`. A recovery point with `recovery_frame_cnt` > 0 (intra refresh) is not key. HEVC already marks IRAP (BLA/IDR/CRA) as key; gradual-refresh HEVC with only recovery point SEI is left as is.

## Behaviour at recovery points
`crates/codecs/src/mpeg.rs` is untouched. One decoder change was made, in commit 157cc6b5: the software H.264 `is_random_access` in `crates/codecs/src/video.rs` now accepts the same samples as the splitter's key rule, an IDR or a recovery point SEI with `recovery_frame_cnt` 0 (it reuses `sei_has_recovery_point`, exported from filmcraft-mpegts). Without it `gop.rs` walked a seek back to…

title: fix(media-browser): drag every selected file to the Timeline, not just one (#1360)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1360.

When several files were selected in the Media Browser and dragged onto the Timeline, only one of them was placed. `start_file_drag` imported the selection but started the drag with only the first new item. If the file under the pointer was already in the project, the drag carried only that item and imported nothing else.

The fix:
- Files from the selection that are already in the project are reused. Only the others are imported.
- When the drag carries more than one item, the Project selection is set to all of them, and the drag starts from the first one. The Timeline drop already places the whole Project selection when the dragged item is part of it (`dragged_selection`, the same path as a multi-item drag from the Project panel). So the files go in back to back, in one undo step. The bin drop in the Project panel also uses that selection.
- A drop that lands nowhere (or is cancelled with Escape) still undoes only the import done by this drag.

Tests:
- `media_browser_drag_places_every_selected_file` (headless, `crates/ui-egui/tests/project_panel_ui.rs`): selects two WAV files in the Media Browser, one already imported and one not, and drags them onto the Timeline. It checks that only the new file is imported and that both clips are placed. On `main`, only one clip is placed.
- A unit test for the helper that builds the dragged item list.

title: fix(bitstream): map se(v) through the 64-bit codeNum so i32::MIN round-trips
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1428.

`read_se` narrowed the codeNum to `u32` through `read_ue` before applying the signed mapping, so codeNum 2^32 (which is -2^31) was rejected, and codeNum 2^32 - 1 (+2^31) came back as `i32::MIN` via the `as i32` wrap. `write_se(i32::MIN)` needed codeNum 2^32 too, which overflowed the `u32` multiply (panic in debug, a silent `0` in release). Both now go through private `u64` codeNum helpers shared with `read_ue`/`write_ue`: the reader maps in `i64` and uses `i32::try_from`, so an out-of-range value is `InvalidExpGolomb` instead of a wrapped number, and the writer computes the code from `unsigned_abs()` in `u64`. Public signatures and `read_ue`'s `u32` range and 32-leading-zero limit are unchanged.

Validation:
- `signed_exp_golomb_extremes_roundtrip` (0, ±1, `i32::MAX`, `i32::MIN`): fails on main (`attempt to multiply with overflow`), passes here
- `signed_exp_golomb_reads_minimum_from_spec_bits` (codeNum 2^32): fails on main (`Err(InvalidExpGolomb)`), passes here
- `signed_exp_golomb_rejects_positive_overflow` (codeNum 2^32 - 1): fails on main (`Ok(-2147483648)`), passes here
- `unsigned_exp_golomb_keeps_u32_range`: guards that `ue(v)` still rejects codeNum 2^32
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-bitstream --lib`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-bitstream --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(monitor): the playback and paused resolution set the rendered frame size
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1420.

The monitor rendered at `min(resolution, on-screen size)`: before applying Playback/Paused Resolution it capped the scale at the frame pixels the monitor shows. On a typical layout the Program monitor shows a 1080p sequence at ~0.35, so Full, 1/2 and often 1/4 all rendered the same 0.375 frame and switching between them changed nothing. Now the frame renders at the chosen fraction of the frame size and the monitor scales it to fit, as Premiere does. The trade-off is that Full on a small monitor now renders every pixel of the sequence (that's what Full means, and lowering the resolution is the way to make it cheaper). Happy to switch to keeping the cap for Full only if you'd rather not pay for that.

Validation:
- `crates/ui-egui/tests/preview_resolution.rs`: fails on main (Paused Resolution Full shows a frame at scale 375 instead of 1000), passes here; 1/2 and 1/4 give exactly half and a quarter of the sequence's width and height
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui --test preview_resolution --test view_ui`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: #1449: mpegts: PCR from the PMT's PCR_PID, per-stream unwrap, SCR unwrap, sane language
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1449

## Cause
- `ts::scan` took the PCR of every PID and unwrapped them against one `last_pcr`; the PMT's `PCR_PID` was never read. Two PIDs with PCR bases 1000 and 2^32+5000 gave `pcr_range = (300000, 1288515988800)`.
- In program streams one `Unwrap` was shared by all elementary streams; a stream on another time base moved the shared `last` and shifted the others by 2^33 (PS only; TS streams share one clock). A pre-wrap timestamp arriving after a small first one was not corrected because of the `base > 0` condition. The doc said "relative to the first one", the code returns absolute values.
- The program stream SCR was never unwrapped; `pcr_range` doc said "First and last" but the value is min/max.
- PMT language used `from_utf8_lossy(..).trim()`: `00 00 00` gave `Some("\0\0\0")`.

## Fix
- New `ClockRange` (lib.rs): 27 MHz unwrap plus min/max. TS keeps one per PCR-carrying PID; `pcr_range` is the clock of the PMT's `PCR_PID` (section bytes 8..9). Rule: PMT `PCR_PID` if a PMT was parsed (so `None` for `0x1FFF` or a PID without PCR), otherwise the first PID seen with a PCR. The PS SCR uses the same type.
- TS keeps one `Unwrap` for the whole program (its streams share one clock); PS gets one per stream. Values stay absolute; before the first wrap a late pre-wrap timestamp goes below the wrap only when it is within 1 minute (90 kHz) of the wrap point and the last value is near zero (e.g. `5` then `2^33-3` gives `-3`). Any other forward jump (e.g. `90000` then `0x1_8000_0000`) is a new time base and is followed. Arithmetic saturates. Doc corrected.
- Language: exactly three ASCII letters, lowercased, else `None`.
- Docs of `File::pcr_range` and `Unwrap` match the code.

## Tests (crates/mpegts/src/tests.rs, deterministic)
`pcr_range_follows_the_pmt_pcr_pid`, `pcr_range_without_a_usable_pcr_pid`, `pcr_range_unwraps_the_33_bit_base`, `streams_sharing_a_clock_stay_in_step_across_the_33_bit_wrap`, `a_forward_jump_from_a_small_first_timestamp_is_followed`, `a_late…

title: ui: Ctrl-click multi-select in Effect Controls feeds Save Preset (#1394)
author: bfenty
body:
## What

Effect Controls rows now support Ctrl-click (⌘ on macOS) multi-selection, and **Save Preset…** captures every selected effect of the clip instead of only the right-clicked row. Fixes #1394.

## Why

The engine command `presets.save` already accepts an `effects: [index]` array, but the UI context menu hardcoded `vec![idx]` — a single row. Saving a multi-effect look meant one preset per effect.

## How

- `UiState.fx_multi: Vec<(ClipId, usize)>` tracks the multi-selection (per clip, ordered).
- Plain click on a row replaces the selection with that row; Ctrl-click toggles the row in/out (same modifier-detection idiom as the multicam panel, so synthetic `ui.click` modifiers work in tests).
- The row context menu's Save Preset… passes all selected indices of that clip (sorted) to `presets::open_save`; falls back to the clicked row when the menu is opened on an unselected row.

## Tests

`crates/ui-egui/tests/preset_multiselect_ui.rs` (headless kittest):
- `ctrl_click_multi_select_saves_all_selected_effects_into_one_preset` — two effects, Ctrl-click both, Save Preset… → draft carries both indices, saved preset lists both effects.
- `a_plain_click_replaces_the_selection_with_one_effect` — plain click collapses the selection to one row.

Red/green verified: both fail on main (context menu offers only single-row save), pass with the fix; negative control via stash round-trip. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets` clean.

title: mpegts: simplify and avoid redundant work
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1450

Behaviour is unchanged. One commit per change.

## Changes and proof

| Change | Proof |
| --- | --- |
| Remove unread `PesHeader.stream_id` / `packet_length` (`pes.rs`) | Simplification: existing `pes::tests` and all mpegts tests pass (the one assertion on `stream_id` is dropped). |
| Doc fixes: `Unit.pos` is a byte offset for TS too (scan stores `off + k * packet_size`); stale doc line above `frame_bytes` | Docs only. |
| Table-driven `crc32_mpeg` (`ts.rs`) | `work_tests::table_crc_equals_the_bitwise_crc` keeps the old bitwise loop as the reference: equal for all 256 single bytes, random inputs of 15 lengths 0..4096, the CRC-32/MPEG-2 check value `0x0376E6E7`, and section + own CRC == 0. No counter test: one lookup per byte instead of eight shift steps is not observable through a counter. |
| Cap the program stream window refill at the bytes left in the file (`ps.rs` `Win::get`) | `ps::tests::capped_window_returns_what_the_uncapped_window_returned`: the old refill is the reference, same slices for 10 file lengths x many positions x 10 sizes (incl. title: h264: validate malformed PPS fields instead of panicking (#1441)
author: bfenty
body:
## What

`Pps::parse` added offsets to input-derived fields before validating them, so six malformed-PPS fields panic (overflow checks on) instead of returning `Error::Invalid`. The panic reaches the public `Decoder::decode` API. Fixes #1441.

## Changes (`crates/h264/src/params.rs`)

- **Validate before incrementing**: `num_slice_groups_minus1 < 8`, `num_ref_idx_l0/l1_default_active_minus1 < 32` are checked pre-`+1`; the map-type-6 run-length count is bounded before `+1`.
- **QP/QS range checks per 7.4.2.2**: `pic_init_qp_minus26` must be in `-(26 + QpBdOffsetY)..=25` (bit-depth aware via the SPS) and `pic_init_qs_minus26` in `-26..=25`, checked before adding 26.
- **`weighted_bipred_idc`**: concealed `3 → 2` per the 7.4.2.2.1 fall-back rule ("shall be considered equal to 2") rather than rejected — matches the spec text, and the slice decoder already only distinguishes 0/1/2.

## Tests (`crates/h264/tests/pps_validation.rs`, 6 tests)

- The reporter's literal 12-byte SPS + 18-byte PPS: `catch_unwind` now sees `Err`, not a panic.
- Synthetic bit-built PPSes for hostile `num_slice_groups`, hostile `num_ref_idx_l1`, hostile `pic_init_qp`.
- `weighted_bipred_idc = 3` parses with the field concealed to 2.
- A well-formed minimal PPS still parses (control).

Red/green verified: reporter-literal and concealment tests fail on main (panic at params.rs:604 / silent accept), all 6 pass with the fix; negative control via stash round-trip. Full `filmcraft-h264` suite green (7 test binaries, 0 failures), `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-h264 --all-targets` clean.

title: bitstream: fix signed Exp-Golomb i32::MIN round-trip and overflow rejection (#1428)
author: bfenty
body:
## What

Fix the three signed Exp-Golomb boundary failures in `filmcraft-bitstream` (#1428), per H.264 9.1.1 / Table 9-3:

- `write_se(i32::MIN)` panicked with `attempt to multiply with overflow` (checked builds) — the codeNum mapping ran in `u32`.
- `read_se` accepted codeNum `2^32 - 1` (maps to `+2^31`, not representable) and returned `Ok(i32::MIN)` via wraparound.
- codeNum `2^32` (maps to the representable `i32::MIN`) was rejected because `read_se` narrowed through `read_ue() -> u32` first.

## How

Keep the raw codeNum in `u64` until the signed mapping is applied:

- New private `read_ue_raw() -> Result<u64>` holds the existing codeword parse (same 32-leading-zero limit); `read_ue` is now `u32::try_from` over it — **no behavior change for `ue(v)` callers**.
- `read_se` maps the raw codeNum (`odd → +(k+1)/2`, `even → −k/2`) in `i64` and rejects out-of-range results with `InvalidExpGolomb` via `i32::try_from`.
- `write_se` computes codeNum in `u64` (`-2i64 * v` for the negative branch), so `i32::MIN` → codeNum `2^32` encodes correctly through `write_ue_raw`.

Public signatures unchanged.

## Testing

Adds the reporter's three boundary tests verbatim plus a boundary roundtrip (`i32::MIN`, `i32::MIN+1`, `-1`, `0`, `1`, `i32::MAX-1`, `i32::MAX`):

- **Red on pristine main**: the 4 new tests fail exactly as the report describes (overflow panic; `Ok(i32::MIN)` for `2^32-1`; rejection of `2^32`).
- **Green with the fix**: `cargo test -p filmcraft-bitstream` → 12/12 pass.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` clean.

Reproduced at the library API level only; no application-level media repro claimed (matches the report).

title: Fix Intel Mac crash: probe Metal shader language version support
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes crashes on Intel Macs where all ArtCraft apps fail to launch with `Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'`.

The wgpu Metal backend was choosing MSL version purely from OS version, but legacy Intel GPUs have older Metal compilers that reject newer MSL versions.

## Solution

Vendors wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with the patch from gfx-rs/wgpu#10592:
- Probes the Metal compiler at adapter creation by compiling a test kernel
- Steps down from OS-selected version until compiler accepts it
- Modern Macs: tries Metal 3.2 → succeeds immediately
- Legacy Intel Macs: tries 3.2 → 3.1 → ... → 2.4/2.3 until one works

## Related issues

Refs storytold/photocraft#1859 (the `invalid value 'metal3.2'` log there is this bug; PhotoCraft needs the same patch, so this PR doesn't close it)
Refs storytold/artcraft#2126 (OCLP Intel Macs; not confirmed on hardware)

Not storytold/artcraft#2190: stock macOS 11 already gets MSL 2.3 from the OS gate, so the probe changes nothing there. That crash is the indirect-call validation pipeline, which #1493 fixed on `main`.

Complements #1493. That PR skips wgpu's indirect-validation compute pipeline. On OCLP Macs whose OS selects MSL 3.2 but whose Intel compiler rejects it, FilmCraft's own shaders and egui's would still fail to compile. This PR picks an MSL version the compiler accepts.

## Testing

- ✅ Compiles on macOS
- ✅ Passes clippy
- ⚠️ Untested on real Intel Mac hardware (awaiting community testing)

## Notes

The vendored wgpu-hal will be removed once upstream releases the fix and ArtCraft can bump to that version.

---
— sent on behalf of @mjohnson7cd by Claude Code

title: fix(dock): dock a panel along the edge of the whole workspace
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1463.

Every drop zone belonged to a single group: dropping a tab on the outer left of the leftmost panel split only that panel, so there was no way to put a panel beside the whole layout like in Premiere. This adds an outer zone, an 8 px band along the workspace border, that wins over the group under the pointer and previews a quarter of the workspace. The drop splits the root: the panel takes 25% of the width (left/right) or height (top/bottom) and the existing layout keeps the rest. It doesn't need a new shared action. `Layout::restore` already knows how to insert beside a whole sibling subtree, so passing it every remaining docked panel targets the root, inside the same validate/commit path as the other docking transactions. Gestures go through the catalog like the others: `window.dockPanel` without `anchor` and with a side `zone` docks along that workspace edge (documented in control-protocol.md). Floating groups over the border keep the drop, and Cmd still forces a float. The 8 px band and the 25% ratio are judgment calls, happy to switch (e.g. to a fixed width like the built-in side panels).

title: #262: Linux file dialogs shown off the UI thread keep case-insensitive filters
author: txiki739
body:
Follow-up to #262 / #390: a regression since #260.

**What broke.** #260 moved Linux file dialogs onto a worker thread (`run_dialog_off_thread` in `apps/filmcraft/src/main.rs`) so the XDG portal call no longer blocks the frame loop. That thread builds its rfd filters from the plain extension lists. The case-insensitive patterns of `file_filters::extensions` (#390: `mp4` → `mp4`, `[mM][pP]4`) are only applied by the synchronous pickers, and on Linux those are no longer used. So since 0.7.x every Linux dialog hides upper- and mixed-case files again: Import (`CLIP.MP4`, `clip.Mp4`), Link Media / proxies, Open file, Open / Save Project (`EDIT.FCPROJ`) and Save As.

**Fix.** `prepare_dialog` runs on the UI thread before the dialog thread starts, as the old filter-name translation did. It translates the filter names as before and turns every extension list into the `file_filters::extensions` patterns: `OpenFiles`, `OpenFile`, `SaveAs`, `Relink`. The project dialogs use `project_patterns()`. The literal extension stays first, so save dialogs still infer the normal suffix. macOS and Windows don't use this path and are unchanged.

**Test.** `off_thread_dialogs_keep_case_insensitive_filters` (Linux): each extension-taking dialog variant goes through `prepare_dialog` and comes out with `mp4` first plus `[mM][pP]4`, and the project patterns include `[fF][cC][pP][rR][oO][jJ]`. Before this change, the dialog thread passed `["mp4"]` unchanged (see the diff), which is what hid the files.

Run on Linux (Kali, i5-4310U), on `main` at `71438c62` (v0.7.2):

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check                             ✅
cargo clippy -p filmcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings ✅
cargo test -p filmcraft --bin filmcraft                ✅ 73 passed
```

title: Keep transform handles in reach when the picture is past the monitor edge
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #1393

When a clip's Motion (or Transform) box reached past the edge of the Program monitor, the handles out there could not be grabbed. They were drawn and hit-tested only at their true positions. The ui clip stops at the picture area plus 12 points, and the painter was clipped to the picture plus 12 points. So a still moved to the frame edge kept its resize handles off screen.

The fix, in `panels/transform_handles.rs`:

- A handle that would be off the monitor now stops just inside its edge (a new `within` helper). It is drawn and grabbed there, and dragging it scales as usual. The picture's position is not changed.
- The box and handles are painted over the whole monitor area instead of only the picture, so handles beside the frame (in the letterbox area) show up too.
- The interaction rect also covers the handles held at the edge.

Tests: a new headless test in `tests/transform_handles_ui.rs` centres the picture on the frame's bottom-right corner. It checks that the bottom-right handle is on the monitor, and that dragging it changes Scale and leaves Position alone. Before the fix the handle sat about 280 points right of the picture, off the monitor. There is also a unit test for `within`, which covers an empty or NaN view without crossed clamp bounds. The existing transform handle UI tests still pass.

What I ran: `cargo fmt --check`, plus clippy `-D warnings` and the tests for `filmcraft-ui-egui` (the lib and `transform_handles_ui`). I did not run the full `cargo xtask ci` locally because it builds every ui-egui test crate in release, so I'm leaving that to GitHub CI. I also haven't tried this by hand in the desktop app or the browser.

title: text: draw characters no loaded face covers with an installed font
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1475.

`fonts::fallback_for` only looked at system faces whose file was already loaded. Without craft-fonts (a plain `cargo run` from source), nothing ever loads Arial / Tahoma / Segoe UI for the text engine, and `resolve("Inter", ..)` doesn't even scan the system folders, so every Arabic letter in a graphic layer fell back to Inter and was drawn as .notdef. Now, when no bundled, craft-fonts or loaded face covers a character, the system folders are scanned on first need and probed with `Face::covers_text` (the same no-caching probe `cjk.rs` / `rtl.rs` use), upright regular faces first. The answer, found or not, is remembered per character, so each one is probed once per process and the first Arabic face found is then reused through the loaded-faces path, keeping a word in one face so it joins. The layer-name boxes in Essential Graphics are the UI font, which `rtl.rs` (#395) already covers with an installed Arabic face.

One cost to be aware of: the first time a character isn't covered, `covers_text` reads candidate font files whole until one covers it (on macOS that can include large files before an Arabic face turns up). It happens once per character per process, as cjk.rs / rtl.rs already do once per script; happy to switch to probing only the `cmap` if you'd rather keep that first lookup cheap.

Validation:
- `fonts::tests::arabic_falls_back_to_an_installed_font`: fails on main (every glyph is face 0 / Inter, glyph id 0), passes here; also red if the on-need scan is removed
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-text --lib fonts::tests`, `cargo test -p filmcraft-text --lib layout::tests`
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-text --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: fix(audio): crossfade audio transitions through the clip handles
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1473.

An audio transition only re-mixed each clip inside its own bounds. A transition centred on a cut (the default, and the one in the demo project) covers the tail of the outgoing clip's handle and the head of the incoming one's, but the outgoing clip stopped at the cut and the incoming one started there, so the two never overlapped: you heard a slight dip at the cut and nothing like a crossfade. The video side already reads frames from the handles. Now both sides of an audio transition are mixed over the whole transition, the clip lengthened into its handles with the same media timing (forward and reversed clips, any speed), so the transition actually crossfades. Where the source has no handle the media read is silent, as before. Remixed clips are left as they are, since they have no linear media to extend; happy to switch if you'd rather handle them differently.

Validation:
- `mixer_tests::audio_transition_on_a_cut_crossfades_through_the_handles`: fails on main (sample 42000 is 0.075, only the outgoing clip faded, instead of 0.0975), passes here

title: fix(codecs): in-band parameter sets compare without trailing zero bytes
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1483.

`parameters_changed` compared in-band parameter sets with the `avcC` / `hvcC` copies byte for byte, so ffmpeg's `hvcC` PPS, which keeps a trailing zero byte (`... 4c 90 00`) that the in-band PPS doesn't have, read as a parameter-set change and sent the whole stream to software from the first sample. A NAL unit never ends with 0x00 (H.264 7.4.1, H.265 7.4.2), so those bytes are trailing_zero_8bits, not part of the parameter set: both sides are now compared without trailing zero bytes, and nothing else is normalised. The same comparison serves H.264, so it gets the same treatment.

`changed_in_band_parameter_sets_switch_to_software` in `crates/platform/tests/fallback.rs` used exactly a trailing zero byte as its "different SPS"; it now flips `nal_ref_idc` instead (same SPS values, different bytes, so the software output it compares against is unchanged). Happy to switch to another fixture if you prefer.

Validation:
- `hw::tests::parameter_sets_compare_without_trailing_zero_bytes` (the bytes from the issue, plus a PPS missing a non-zero byte and a different PPS that must still count as changes): fails on main ("a trailing zero byte is not part of the NAL unit"), passes here
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-codecs --lib hw::`, `cargo test -p filmcraft-platform --test fallback`
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-codecs -p filmcraft-platform --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: macOS: open the window on Intel Metal by skipping indirect-call validation
author: fabian-co
body:
## What this changes

On a Mac whose integrated GPU is an Intel Iris Pro (MacBookPro11,3, macOS 12.7.6), FilmCraft can't open its window when it draws on that GPU (`FilmCraft could not start its window: WGPU error: Parent device is lost`). On this dual-GPU machine the default picks the NVIDIA GPU, so it shows with `WGPU_POWER_PREF=low`; a Mac with only that Intel GPU has no other adapter to fall to.

The cause is wgpu's indirect-call validation: when the device is created, wgpu compiles a compute shader to validate indirect draw/dispatch arguments, and Metal's Intel compiler aborts on it. The log shows:

```
ERROR [main] wgpu_core::indirect_validation: indirect-validation error: ComputePipeline(Internal("new_compute_pipeline_state: NSError { code: 2, localizedDescription: \"Compiler encountered an internal error\", domain: \"CompilerError\", .. }"))
ERROR [main] eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
```

and each attempt leaves `MTLCompilerService` crash reports ending in `IGILErrorMessageHandlers::reportUnsupportedMaxWorkGroupSizeMetadataError` (libIGIL-Metal).

FilmCraft draws and dispatches nothing indirectly (no `draw_indirect`, `draw_indexed_indirect`, `multi_draw_*` or `dispatch_workgroups_indirect` in `apps/` or `crates/`), so this removes `VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL` from the window instance's flags. `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL=1` turns it back on. This is the same fix VectorCraft already has (storytold/vectorcraft#651); PhotoCraft and LightCraft skip the check too.

No docs, asset or dependency change.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --locked -p filmcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

title: timeline: dragging a track's edge resizes only that track
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1485.

Every video track was drawn `video_track_h` high and every audio track `audio_track_h` high, and dragging any track's edge (or double-clicking its header) changed that shared value, so all the tracks of that kind moved together. Tracks now keep their own height in `TimelineView` (`video_heights` / `audio_heights`, track id -> height, same shape as `track_lanes`). A track that was never resized still uses the shared value, and the layout adds the rows up one by one. The commands that set the height of every track of a kind (Expand/Minimize All Tracks, Increase/Decrease Video/Audio Tracks Height, `ui.set` `videoTrackHeight`/`audioTrackHeight`) still set the shared value and also reset the tracks resized on their own, so "all tracks" really means all of them. Happy to switch to keeping each track's offset if you'd prefer that.

The per-track heights live in the UI state only, not in the per-sequence `SequenceView` that is saved with the project, so for now a project reopens with the shared heights. Adding them there means touching `filmcraft-project`'s `SequenceView` (which is `Copy` today). Happy to do that here or in a follow-up.

Validation:
- `timeline_track_height_ui::dragging_a_line_resizes_only_the_track_it_belongs_to`: fails on main (dragging V1's line takes V2 and V3 from 24 to 39 as well), passes here. The two existing outer-edge tests now check the dragged track's own row instead of the shared height.

title: timeline: a middle-button drag pans, whatever the tool
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1490.

The Program and Source monitors already pan with the middle button (#824), so this covers the Timeline half. The Timeline's area senses drags of any button, and the press handler only checks for a drag, not for which button started it. A middle-button drag therefore went down the same path as a left one: depending on the tool and what it started on, it selected and moved the clip, drew a marquee, scrubbed the ruler or cut with the Razor. Now a drag started by the middle button becomes the same `Drag::Pan` the Hand tool uses, whatever the tool and whatever it starts on, so it scrolls sideways and moves the tracks up and down. Escape puts the view back, as it already does for a Hand pan. The pan is anchored at the press point (only primary presses are recorded in `pressed`), so the view follows the pointer from the moment the button went down. A middle-button drag that starts on the ruler also pans rather than scrubbing; happy to switch if you'd rather keep the ruler scrubbing.

title: #1458: --graphics gl, an opt-in OpenGL mode for Intel Gen 9 graphics
author: malikbello
body:
Closes #1458.

On Intel Gen 9 graphics (UHD 6xx), Vulkan crashes in `igvk64.dll` and FXC rejects `fx.wgsl` under DirectX 12, so the automatic fallback from #820 ends on the CPU compositor there. OpenGL is where the GPU compositor runs on these machines, but it was only reachable through `WGPU_BACKEND=gl`.

## What changes

- `Mode::Gl` (`--graphics gl`, shown as "OpenGL only"): OpenGL alone, on Windows.
- It is a choice, never a step of the automatic fallback. `LADDER` is unchanged. A new `CHOICES` (the ladder, plus `gl` on Windows) is what `--graphics` and the saved state accept, so the AMD machines from #477 never get OpenGL unless the user asks for it.
- The choice is kept for later launches, like `--graphics dx12`. If a `gl` start dies twice in a row, or wgpu reports it can't start, the app hands over to the start of the automatic ladder instead of retrying OpenGL.
- The `--help` text, the README's Windows troubleshooting, `docs/gaps.md` (G4, including why `gl` is never automatic: AMD's `atio6axx.dll`, #477) and the Stability paragraph of `docs/target-app-parity.md` mention it, with a revision-history row in both docs. "OpenGL only" is added to all eight catalogs FilmCraft requires (es, fr, id, it, ja, ko, pt-br, zh-cn). The mode name reaches the notice through `i18n::t`, so the catalog-coverage test doesn't check it.
- Left as is: the notice still appears for any non-default mode, as it does for `--graphics dx12` today, and GPU export stays off outside the default mode.

New tests: `gl_is_picked_by_hand_only_and_hands_back_to_the_ladder` and `step_down_from_a_picked_mode_starts_the_ladder`, plus `gl` cases in the existing `--graphics` flag and argument tests and in `no_mode_validates_indirect_calls` and `only_the_windows_default_and_software_modes_choose_the_adapter` from #1532.

Rebased on `main` at `cee1feb`. The last rebase (from `1267e4e`) only merged translations and docs: upstream's new Spanish wording for "software rendering" is kept next to the new "Ope…

title: fix(timeline): stop Ruler timestamps disappearing while zooming (#1397)
author: Narmjep
body: The Ruler walked one grid (the tick stride) and labelled a frame only when it was also a multiple of the label stride. Chosen independently, the two need not divide: at 24 fps and 100 pt a second, 5-frame ticks against 48-frame labels meet only every lcm(5, 48) = 240 frames — one timestamp per 10 s, the rest returning at the next zoom step, where the ladder happens to divide. Take the tick stride as the finest division of the label stride that still leaves ticks 12 pt apart, so both are one grid. Every label then falls on a tick and can no longer be skipped, and the ticks stay evenly spaced around it instead of bunching either side. Labels are >= 110 pt apart, so a divisor of at most 9 always meets the minimum. The labelled stride, and so every timecode and the frame it is drawn at, is unchanged. Strides are clamped to >= 1 (the loop advances by one and tests the other for divisibility), and the ladder's products saturate, as FrameRate is plain serde data from the project file. --- This was the original issue: After zooming in: 00:00:05 and 00:00:15 disappear

title: fix(engine): preserve offline sources referenced through subclips
author: jnohclee-rgb
body:
Deleting a bin can remove a file still used by a surviving subclip, leaving its timeline clip unable to resolve media. This follows up #937 and #1050 by resolving valid file-backed timeline references and retaining their bounded subclip dependency chains before deciding which file sources to preserve as offline. Sequences included in the deletion no longer keep otherwise-unused sources alive.

Four regressions cover deleting a source bin used through a surviving subclip (including undo and removal of unused media), deleting a sequence together with its media, deleting a subclip together with its now-unused source, and preserving a nested subclip when an intermediate parent’s bin is deleted. Directly deleted subclips keep their existing deletion behavior. Generator-backed subclips are outside this file-media fix.

title: captions: preserve speaker names in TTML metadata
author: sanyamsingh001
body:
TTML export previously wrote speaker references without defining their agents, losing punctuation or changing literal underscores on import. TTML and DFXP now define each speaker label once as typed agent/name metadata. Import resolves those names so punctuation, Unicode, empty labels and whitespace survive a round trip.

The reader supports modern TTML and the April/October 2006 draft metadata namespaces, including April's unqualified agent IDs. Legacy reference fallback remains available. Unrelated application agent definitions and qualified application `type` attributes do not override TTML names. Multiple references become one ordered display label; individual agent identities and actor relationships are not retained. The caption README documents this mapping from [W3C TTML1](https://www.w3.org/TR/2018/REC-ttml1-20181108/#metadata-vocabulary-agent) and the [April 2006 draft](https://www.w3.org/TR/2006/WD-ttaf1-dfxp-20060427/).

The focused caption suite passed all 75 tests. Regressions cover speaker names, agent references, comment-separated name text, namespace precedence, CR/CRLF/LF/tab and timed-span speakers. The April opaque-ID case failed before its correction and passed afterward with unchanged tests; its legacy underscore fallback control passed both runs. A permitted application `type` attribute preceding the TTML name type also reproduced a wrong-name result in both TTML and DFXP before correction; that case and both controls passed afterward with unchanged tests.

All six required checks passed on the frozen source on Linux:

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`

title: Adjustment layers: a Transform replaces the picture below instead of drawing over it
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1524.

The adjustment layer composited its adjusted picture *over* the original with the layer's blend mode. That is the same thing as a cross-fade as long as the adjusted picture is opaque, which is why colour effects looked right, but Transform, Basic 3D and the other geometric effects leave transparent areas, and there the untouched original showed through, so you got the transformed copy on top of the original. With Normal blending the adjusted picture now replaces the original, weighted by opacity, opacity masks and the Motion region (`lerp(original, adjusted, weight)`, using the existing `mask::mix`). Other blend modes keep compositing over the original as before, since "replace" has no obvious meaning for them; happy to switch if you see it differently. Motion on the adjustment layer still only limits the region, as `motion_and_masks_restrict_the_region` specifies. Frames with an adjustment layer are always rendered on the CPU (`plan::layered_at`), so the GPU path picks this up too.

Validation:
- `adjustment_tests::a_transform_replaces_the_picture_below`: fails on main (the corner outside a 50 % Transform is still `[1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0]`, the original red), passes here
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-render --lib -- adjustment_tests par_tests region_tests nest_tests`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: fix(mcp): a slow bridge command no longer blocks every later call
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1538: the bridge staying blocked.

The bridge talked to the app over one connection behind a mutex held for the whole round trip, so a command the app was slow to answer (a screenshot that never came back, #1539) held every later call behind it for up to 90 s, plus a retry. rmcp doesn't drop a tool call when the client cancels it, so each call the client gave up on stayed queued on that mutex, and every new one timed out behind the backlog: restarting the app didn't help, only restarting the MCP server cleared it. Now a request takes an idle connection (or opens one) for its own round trip and puts it back only once the reply is read. A slow request only delays itself, and one that is abandoned takes its connection with it, so its late reply can't be read as the answer to the next call. Up to 4 idle connections are kept (the app serves 16), happy to switch to another number.

#1539 (why `render_frame` doesn't return on that footage) is still open; this only stops it from taking the bridge down with it.

Not done here: telling whether a call that timed out was applied (with the bridge responsive again, `project_inspect` answers it), honouring the client's cancel in `call_tool`, and the retry after the 90 s timeout, which resends the same request and can apply a non-idempotent command twice; that was already the case and I'd rather do it separately.

Validation:
- `bridge::tests::a_slow_command_does_not_block_later_calls`: fails on main (the second call is still waiting after 5 s), passes here
- `bridge::tests::an_abandoned_call_leaves_no_late_reply_behind`: fails on main (the next call gets `"slow"`, the abandoned call's reply), passes here
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-automation --lib bridge::`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-automation --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Embed craft-fonts by default via .cargo/config.toml [env]
author: sblount2025-design
body:
A plain `cargo build --release` from a clean clone silently produces a CJK-blind binary. build.rs warns and carries on:

```
warning: no craft-fonts embedded: Chinese and Japanese text will render as empty
boxes. Clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts next to this repo and
rebuild with CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=../craft-fonts
```

With craft-fonts already cloned beside the repo exactly as the warning asks, the build *still* needs `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` passed by hand on every invocation. A build-time requirement that lives only in a warning is one that gets forgotten, and then comes back as a bug report about missing glyphs.

This adds it to `.cargo/config.toml`:

```toml
[env]
CRAFT_FONTS_DIR = { value = "../craft-fonts", relative = true }
```

**This is not a new convention — it mirrors `deckcraft/.cargo/config.toml`, which already ships this exact block.** The other craft apps that read `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` don't, which is the inconsistency this closes.

Properties:

- `relative = true` resolves against the repo root, so no absolute path is committed.

title: MCP: bridge render_frame no longer returns the Program monitor's stand-in picture
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1541.

In bridge mode `render_frame` / `render_preview` move the playhead and screenshot the Program monitor. Until the frame at that time is decoded, the monitor shows a stand-in: the nearest picture it already has, or black. `ui.screenshot` waits up to 5 s for the exact frame and then captures whatever is on screen, without saying so. With slow media (1080p60 long-GOP H.264 decoded in software, as in the report) the frame takes longer than that, so the agent got the earlier picture back with the new timecode and without the captions. The timeline itself was fine, which is why the export was correct. Edits made over the control channel bump the same project revision as edits made in the UI, so no cache is left stale. To reproduce on macOS, turn off hardware decoding and seek deep into a 40 s GOP. Every screenshot then takes 5.5 s and shows black or the previous frame.

`ui.screenshot` now reports `settled: false` when it gave up waiting. The bridge `render_frame` takes the screenshot again (3 tries, about 16 s at most) and, if the monitor still hasn't settled, returns an error asking the agent to call again. Apps that don't send the flag are treated as settled. The retry count is a judgement call and I'm happy to change it. Returning the picture with a warning instead of an error would also work.

Validation:
- `server::tests::bridge_render_does_not_return_a_monitor_stand_in` (a fake control server whose monitor settles late or never): fails on main (one screenshot, returned as the frame), passes here
- by hand against `filmcraft --control`: `ui.screenshot` reports `settled: false` while the frame is still decoding and `true` once it is shown
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-automation -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(control): sequence.settings without params reports the settings instead of opening a dialog
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Refs #1540.

Engine side only, complementary to #1854. #1854 keeps `engine.execute` from opening any parameter dialog over the control channel; this one fixes what the engine command itself does when it gets nothing to change, for every engine client (CLI, scripts, the control channel when a call reaches it).

Before, `sequence.settings` with no params ran an empty edit and pushed a "Sequence Settings" undo step that did nothing. Now it changes nothing, records no undo step, and answers `{"settings": …}`, the active sequence's settings as `sequence.inspect` reports them: the same shape #1854 returns for `sequence.settings {}` over `engine.execute`, so the command answers one way whichever channel calls it. With params it still applies them and returns `{"scaledClips": n}`, as on main.

It touches only `crates/engine`, so it merges cleanly with #1854 in either order (`git merge-tree` shows no conflicts both ways).

Validation:

title: Graphics: show each family in its own face in the Font menu
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1536, fixes #1464.

The Font menu of a text layer (Properties / Essential Graphics) now shows each family's name in that family's own face, so you can pick one without applying it first. A family whose face doesn't have the glyphs of its own name (symbol and braille fonts, for example) keeps the plain label, and so does a row whose sample isn't ready yet.

title: Export: captions past the last clip no longer extend the range
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1543.

`Sequence::duration()` counts caption tracks, and the export range without In/Out (and `range: "entire"`) ended at that duration, so an SRT whose last cue ran a frame or two past the clip added black frames showing only that caption. The export now ends at the last video or audio item (`Sequence::export_end`); a sequence holding only captions still ends with them, and In/Out or a custom range still export anything you ask for. Nothing is clamped on import and the timeline keeps showing the whole caption, so no caption data is lost. `sequence.inspect` `durationFrames`, documented as the frames export renders, follows the same end (`duration` stays the timeline length). I went with cutting at the media end rather than trimming cues on import or warning, since it's the least invasive; happy to switch if you'd rather clamp on import or keep captions in the range.

Validation:

title: export: GPU compositing in the standalone CLI, GPU status in export results, renderer-pool hang (#799)
author: bsoulai
body:
From Sublime Focus Studio's pipeline: we run FilmCraft headless against our vertical show (2160x3840, 11 layers, ProRes 4444 and H.264), which is the fixture every number below comes from.

Three things, found while chasing #799:

### 1. The standalone CLI had no GPU backend
A CLI built on its own (`cargo build -p filmcraft-cli`, `cargo install`) got no wgpu backend: filmcraft-gpu asked for none and the CLI added none, so `ExportRenderer::new` returned `None` and every frame was composited on the CPU without a word. Release builds got the backends by feature unification from the workspace, which is why a release binary can't be explained by this alone. filmcraft-gpu now has a `backends` feature (metal, vulkan, dx12, gles) and the CLI turns it on. `WGPU_BACKEND` is honoured.

### 2. Nothing said which path ran
The export device now records its adapter, or why there is none (no backend, no adapter, device failed). Every export of a sequence reports `gpu {requested, adapter, reason, frames, cpuFrames}` in its result, and `perf.stats` repeats the last one as `export.gpu`. `file.exportFrame` takes `gpuRendering` (default off, like exports) and reports `gpu` the same way. This is the part the Linux reporter of #799 hit: there was no way to tell "no backend", "no adapter", "adapter but every frame fell back" and "GPU used" apart. Documented in docs/agents.md, control-protocol.md, architecture.md, monitors.md.

### 3. The renderer pool could hang an export
With a backend present, the first `gpuRendering: auto` export of the fixture hung for good at 0 % CPU. A stack sample: four export threads each held a pooled GPU renderer while decoding ProRes 4444 on rayon, and the frame jobs waiting for a renderer had been stolen onto those same threads. The same blocking pool ships in 0.6.0. title: gpu: interpolate a scaled-up Y'CbCr layer in linear light, as the CPU does (#1558)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1558 (confirmed by @bsoulai on the reported frames).

The colour tags turned out not to matter: an untagged 1080x1920 H.264 decodes to the same BT.709 limited-range frame on both paths (default_matrix keys on SD size, so portrait vs landscape gives the same answer), and the GPU uniforms follow `frame.color` exactly like the CPU conversion. The difference is the order of operations when a Y'CbCr layer is magnified. The CPU decodes to a linear image and resamples that; the shader interpolated the Y/Cb/Cr code values between texels and only then converted to linear light. Mixing gamma-encoded values pulls bright/dark transitions down, so fine bright detail scaled up (a graphic bumper at 200%) comes out darker on the GPU, while smooth camera footage barely moves, which fits the other frames of the report passing.

When the layer is scaled up along either axis (the new `magnified` flag in the previously unused `p3.w`), the shader now converts each of the four neighbouring texels to linear premultiplied colour and interpolates those, as the RGBA path already does through the sRGB texture. Each of those texels takes its chroma from the chroma texel that covers it, like the CPU (`x >> 1` for 4:2:0), so a magnified sample is 12 texture reads (16 with alpha).

Only magnified draws change. 1:1 and scaled-down draws (the common case: a 4K clip in a 1080p monitor or export) run main's sampler unchanged: code values interpolated at the sample position and converted once per tap.

Validation:
- `blend_tests::upscaled_yuv_detail_matches_cpu` (3 px luma stripes in a 270x480 untagged frame, drawn at 200%): fails on main (p99 51, mean 16.3 vs the p99 ≤ 6 / mean < 1.5 parity criterion), passes here (p99 1, mean 0.10)
- `blend_tests::upscaled_yuv_chroma_edges_match_cpu` (sharp red/white chroma edges at 200%): p99 67 on main, 0 here
- `blend_tests::yuv_not_magnified_keeps_code_value_sampling`: 1 px columns of Y' 236/60 drawn half a texel off at 1:1 and at 50% with every tap betwee…

title: render: trim transparent 4:4:4 overlays before GPU upload
author: Gustitolito
body:
Full-frame ProRes-like overlays can contain only a small credit or banner, but the GPU planner currently prepares and uploads all four 16-bit planes and draws the full quad. Trim transparent borders for plain one-to-one 4:4:4 layers before upload, restoring their position with an integer translation.

The fast path is deliberately narrow: 9–16-bit 4:4:4 with alpha, Normal blend, no effects or colour-management transform, no scaling/rotation/fractional translation, valid plane lengths, and at least 50% of source area removed. Keep a one-texel rim for bilinear loads. No media/project changes or dependencies; the CPU renderer is unchanged. This complements the GPU output/readback and texture-pooling work without changing those paths.

Measured against 0.7.2 / `71438c6`, Windows 10, Ryzen 5 4500, 16 GB RAM, RTX 3080, NVIDIA 616.92, Vulkan, Rust 1.99 release, six Rayon threads. Four alternating runs per binary, 10 warm-up + 60 measured frames per run:

| 1080p synthetic scenario | Before | After | Time change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Sparse video overlay | 33.266 ms | 26.718 ms | −19.7% |
| Opaque video control | 34.894 ms | 35.161 ms | +0.8% |
| Sparse still overlay | 32.139 ms | 27.620 ms | −14.1% |

title: feat(plugin): sandboxed WebAssembly (WASM) plugin system with SDK, engine and UI integration (G11)
author: Mahmoud-MAHMALAT
body:
### Summary

This PR addresses **G11 ("No plugin hosting")** by introducing a fully sandboxed, safe WebAssembly (WASM) plugin architecture and authoring SDK for FilmCraft, following **ADR 0002**.

In strict accordance with FilmCraft's Rule 0 ("Never Crash") and workspace-wide `unsafe_code = "forbid"` constraints, this implementation executes untrusted third-party effects inside an isolated Wasmtime sandbox rather than loading unsafe native dynamic libraries (`.dll`/`.dylib`/`.so`). Any division by zero, out-of-bounds memory access, or panic within a plugin is caught cleanly as an execution error without affecting host stability.

---

### Key Components & Changes

1. **`crates/plugin-sdk` (L0 Foundation):**
   - Safe, ergonomic Rust SDK for authoring plugins with zero `unsafe` code required from plugin authors.
   - Provides safe abstractions for video processing (`VideoFrame`, `PixelRgba8`) and audio blocks (`AudioBlock`).
   - Single-macro export (`export_video_effect!`) handling C-ABI bindings, memory allocation, and manifest emission.
   - Example plugins provided: `invert.rs` (color inversion) and `gain.rs` (audio/gain processing).

2. **`crates/plugin` (L2 Plugin Host Runtime):**
   - Wasmtime-backed WebAssembly runtime with linear memory sandboxing and strict memory limits.
   - Trap containment and error handling ensuring host processes never panic or crash on bad plugin code.
   - Declarative manifest parsing (`plugin.toml` / JSON schema) supporting parameters (`Float`, `Int`, `Bool`, `ColorRgba`, `Choice`, `Text`).
   - Plugin registry for scanning, loading, and querying available plugins.

3. **`crates/render` & `crates/project` Integration:**
   - Integrated `plugin_bridge` connecting sandboxed effects with the video rendering pipeline.
   - Project model integration mapping effect parameters to sequence evaluations.

4. **`crates/ui-egui` Integration:**
   - Dynamic parameter inspectors for plugin parameters.

title: Interchange: Premiere's nested-sequence clips import centred from FCP7 XML
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1562.

Premiere writes a nested-sequence clip item's Basic Motion `center` half a frame up and left of where a media clip at the same spot would have it (`-0.5 -0.5` for a centred nest, with `centerOffset` 0 0), and reads it back the same way, so the file re-opens centred in Premiere. The importer read it as the spec says, so nests landed with their centre in the top-left corner. Now, for a clip item that references a `<sequence>` and whose `center` parameter carries `authoringApp="PremierePro"`, the centre gets +0.5 +0.5 before it's mapped to pixels. I applied it as a constant offset (static value and every keyframe), not only to the exact `-0.5 -0.5` case, so a nest the editor moved or animated keeps its placement too. Documents without the Premiere marker, including FilmCraft's own FCP7 export (which doesn't write `authoringApp`), are read as before. Happy to switch to the narrower `-0.5 -0.5` rule if you prefer.

@bsoulai, if you could try this branch on your full file and check where the two nests land, that would confirm it beyond my hand-written fixture.

Validation:
- `premiere_nested_sequence_centre_is_offset_by_half_a_frame` (crates/interchange/tests/fcp7.rs): fails on main (the nest's position comes out at `0, 0`), passes here. It also checks a keyframed Premiere nest and that a nest without the Premiere marker still reads `-0.5 -0.5` as the top-left corner.

title: Media Foundation hardware H.264 / HEVC encoding on Windows (#30)
author: ComfyChloe
body:
## What this adds

**Hardware H.264 and H.265 export on Windows for every GPU vendor, not just NVIDIA.**

`register()` on Windows registered NVENC and nothing else, so a machine with no NVIDIA driver fell
back to the CPU: Export ▸ Hardware encoding logged `no NVIDIA encoder driver` and did nothing, and
**H.265 was greyed out in the format list** because the list asked NVENC whether a session opens.
There is no software HEVC encoder, so on those machines H.265 export simply did not exist.

Media Foundation is the vendor-neutral path Windows already uses for hardware *decode*. This adds the
encode side, so one backend reaches Intel, AMD and Qualcomm GPUs:

| machine | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Snapdragon X, Adreno X1-85 (Windows 11 ARM64) | CPU encode; H.265 greyed out | H.264 **and** H.265 on the GPU |
| Radeon RX 6900 XT | CPU encode; H.265 greyed out | H.264 **and** H.265 on the GPU |
| NVIDIA | NVENC | unchanged — NVENC still wins |

## What it fixes

Four defects, each found by running this and caught because the export or its output was checked
rather than assumed:

- **The H.264 profile the export asks for was never sent.** `EncSpec` had no profile field, so the
  encoder chose: Qualcomm picks High (which is why it went unnoticed), AMD picked Main while the
  export said `high`. Now `MF_MT_MPEG2_PROFILE` carries it, verified per profile on both machines.
- **The first keyframe of every session carried stale driver memory into the file.**
  `IMFMediaBuffer::Lock` returns the *buffer's* size and an encoder MFT recycles one buffer across
  every picture; only `GetCurrentLength` is this picture. The first keyframe carried 9 kB of leftovers
  out to offset 262 kB. Later pictures had a zeroed tail, which is why the files still probed
  correctly and this was invisible until a hardware export came out **larger** than the software one at
  the same bit rate. Now 19% smaller, which is what it should be.
- **An AMD H.264 MFT delivered about twice the requested bit…

title: Timeline: Select Clip at Playhead selects the gap over empty time
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1577.

`timeline.selectClipAtPlayhead` (D) only collected clips under the playhead on the targeted tracks, so over empty time it selected nothing, even though a gap is already a selectable object (`timeline.selectGap`, #648/#668). Now, when no targeted track has a clip at the playhead, D selects the gap there through `timeline.selectGap`, so Delete / Shift+Delete close it as they do after clicking the gap. Over a clip nothing changes, except that D now also drops a previously selected gap, as `timeline.select` already does. Only one gap can be selected at a time, so with several targeted tracks D takes the first targeted, unlocked one that has a gap at the playhead (V1 upwards, then the audio tracks). Happy to switch that order if you'd prefer another one. Cmd+Up/Down with nothing selected still go through the clip-only path.

On Premiere: I couldn't find this in Adobe's docs, but users report D picking up gaps too (accepted answer in https://community.adobe.com/t5/premiere-pro-discussions/short-cut-to-select-next-empty-space/m-p/9262013: "pressing D can select the actual clip or gaps too").

title: #1221: H.264 High 10 and High 10 Intra export in the built-in encoder
author: JordyUSA
body:
Part of #1221: stage 1 (**High 10**, 4:2:0 at 8–10 bits) and the intra-only option from stage 5. High 4:2:2, High 4:4:4 Predictive and lossless are still to come.

title: timeline, panels: only the primary button starts a gesture; a right-button drag no longer draws a box
author: ReReddo
body:
## What and why

Fixes #1592.

A right-button drag over empty space in the Timeline drew a selection box and selected clips, and the same press could start a move, a trim or a cut. The Timeline's press handling (and the drag-and-drop sources in several panels) started on `Response::drag_started()`, which is true for any button.

The primary button now starts selecting, moving, trimming and cutting; the middle button keeps panning (#1496); the right button opens the context menu on release and starts nothing.

Applied wherever a drag begins a gesture or a drag-and-drop:

- Timeline: the press handler, the zoom bar, caption lanes, volume lines, keyframe lanes.
- Drag sources: Project items and bins, Effects and presets, graphics templates, Media Browser files, the Source monitor picture, the Source range handles, the monitors' zoom bar.

Value sliders and faders are left as they are; they change a value rather than start a gesture.

## How it was tested

title: dock: a divider changes only the two panels beside it
author: ReReddo
body:
## What and why

Fixes #1595.

Moving a divider also resized panels that were not next to it. Panels are stored as nested splits, most of them as ratios, so moving an outer divider changes the area of a whole subtree and every ratio split inside it scales with it. In `Source | (Program | Properties)` dragging the first divider also made Properties wider or narrower. Narrow panels such as Tools and the meters, when they sit in a ratio split of a rearranged layout, drifted to widths well beyond their usual size the same way.

When a divider moves, the sizes of the splits behind it are adjusted in the same step:

- the panel next to the divider takes the change, the other panels keep the size they had;
- a fixed-size panel keeps its size, and the next panel takes the change instead (so Tools stays 64 points when the Project divider moves, as before);
- panels stacked across the divider all change with it, as they must;
- the minimum size is unchanged.

It applies to dragging and to the keyboard (arrow keys on a focused divider), which share one path. Saved workspaces and the dock model are unchanged: only the sizes that are written differ.

I could not find a separate size cap in the dock code that the panels exceed; the growth came from the ratio scaling above, and fixed-size panels already keep their size.

## How it was tested

- Unit tests in `dock.rs` build the layouts and drag a divider the way the layout does: the outer divider of `Source | (Program | Properties)` leaves Properties alone; the divider between the last two leaves Source alone; the Editing bottom row keeps Tools at 64 and the meters at 116 while the Timeline gives way; a column of two beside a third changes both of the column; a drag far past the limit keeps every panel above the minimum and the area filled.

title: fix(media): respect EXIF orientation for imported still images
author: UdayaSri0
body:
## Summary

Fixes #1583. Imported stills with EXIF orientation metadata were decoded in their stored pixel orientation, so portrait phone photos appeared sideways or mirrored and reported the stored dimensions.

## Root cause

The still raster path decoded pixels and dimensions but never applied orientation metadata. Those raw dimensions flow into still MediaInfo and the frame used by import and Motion sizing.

## Implementation

- Applies the existing image decoder's orientation for JPEG and ordinary TIFF before converting to RGBA, covering EXIF orientations 1–8 with no resampling.
- Keeps DNG and custom YCbCr TIFF on their dedicated decoder paths.
- Adds generated-image coverage for JPEG orientations 1–8, malformed EXIF fallback, ordinary TIFF orientation, upright raster/frame/MediaInfo dimensions, and no double application.
- Documents the supported format boundary and credits the contributor as requested.

## Tests

Passed:
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-media` (77 unit tests and 9 integration tests)
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-media --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo xtask layers`
- `cargo xtask assets`
- `cargo xtask wasm`

`cargo xtask ci` could not complete: workspace clippy could not build `alsa-sys` because this Linux environment lacks the ALSA development package (`alsa.pc`). The media crate checks above passed.

## Compatibility

JPEG and ordinary TIFF orientation metadata is applied at decode. DNG and custom YCbCr TIFF remain on dedicated paths. No external image fixture or dependency was added.

title: fix(control): process remote commands when Wayland window is hidden
author: UdayaSri0
body:
## Summary

This draft addresses [issue #1584](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/issues/1584). Control requests could wait for a repaint that Wayland never scheduled for a hidden workspace window. The server could then report a generic timeout while the request remained queued and ran later.

## Root cause

The TCP server enqueued control requests and called `egui::Context::request_repaint()`. On native Linux, eframe forwarded that through winit as a window redraw request. When the Wayland compositor withheld frame callbacks for the hidden window, FilmCraft did not process the queue. The former 60 second timeout did not cancel the request, so later execution could follow a client retry.

## Implementation

- Linux control launches use eframe's external winit event loop and send a reserved user-event marker through `EventLoopProxy`. The wrapper directly dispatches a root-window redraw for that marker, independent of a Wayland frame callback.
- Multi-frame synthetic gestures send one continuation marker while input remains queued, then stop after the final input pass. Other eframe repaint events keep their normal behavior.
- Request tickets atomically distinguish queued, executing, cancelled, abandoned, and completed requests. A timeout cancels work only if it wins before dispatch; after execution begins, the response reports an unknown outcome and tells callers to inspect application state before retrying.
- Control input is bounded to 32 clicks, 128 drag steps, and 16 KiB of UTF-8 text per request.

## Tests

Passed:

- `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui --lib control` — 21 passed, including request lifecycle races, continuation scheduling/termination, and input bounds.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `git diff HEAD --check`
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --lib -- -D warnings`
- A temporary isolated compile harness for the external eframe/winit event-loop API compiled successfully.

Unavailable or blocked in this environment:

- `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui` fa…

title: widgets: drag across checkboxes to check or uncheck several
author: ReReddo
body:
Fixes #1546.

## What and why

Press on a checkbox and drag over its neighbours: each checkbox the pointer goes over takes the new state of the first one, until the button is released. A click toggles one checkbox, as before. VectorCraft (storytold/vectorcraft#1600) and PhotoCraft (storytold/photocraft#3521) build the same behaviour, so the Craft apps work alike.

FilmCraft had no shared checkbox: about 70 calls to `Ui::checkbox` and `egui::Checkbox` in 27 files. They now go through one trait method, `widgets::DragCheckbox::checkbox_drag` (and `checkbox_drag_enabled` for the disabled-capable form), so Preferences, dialogs and panels get it at the same time. A checkbox that is disabled stays as it is during a drag.

The sweep state is the new state of the checkbox the press began on (what a click would give it), kept while the primary button is down. If the pointer leaves that checkbox the release is not a click on it, so it takes the state too and does not toggle back. `Response::changed()` is marked for each checkbox a drag sets, so callers that act on a change see it.

title: fix(files): prevent silent replacement of existing files
author: UdayaSri0
body:
## Summary

Issue #1615 reports that saving to an existing location silently replaces the old file. This change adds an explicit Replace / Cancel confirmation to desktop save and export flows and makes engine writes refuse existing paths unless `overwrite: true` is supplied. Ordinary Save to the currently open project remains an intentional update.

## Root cause

Several paths wrote directly to destinations: exporters used truncating file creation, and project Save As/Save a Copy and other command paths could bypass the UI. Export Frame had a confirmation flow, but normal Export Mode and Quick Export did not consistently share it. Queue entries also did not reject duplicate output paths.

A disposable reproduction used a temporary file containing `ORIGINAL-USER-CONTENT` and the same `File::create` behavior as the exporter; the bytes were truncated without a prompt.

## Implementation

- Resolve export destinations, including their final extension, before checking for conflicts.
- Add one UI confirmation dialog with the destination path, Replace and Cancel actions, keyboard cancellation, and automation IDs; wire save dialogs, Export Mode, Quick Export, Export Frame, and menu export commands through it.
- Refuse existing output paths in engine commands by default. Programmatic callers can opt in with `overwrite: true`; normal Save to the current project path remains unchanged.
- Stage native media exports beside their final destination and publish only after encoding succeeds. New destinations use exclusive create semantics. Image-sequence frames stage before publication and roll back earlier publishes on a later filesystem error.
- Reject duplicate queued paths. Keep project Save As state unchanged until its write succeeds.
- For native single-file exports with caption sidecars, snapshot prior files and restore them if sidecar publication fails.
- Document replacement, cancellation, retry, and platform-specific limits in `docs/control-protocol.md` and `docs/project-…

title: feat(updater): crash-resilient self-updating for desktop app
author: ARYAN007H
body:
### Summary

Part of #1272

Implements self-updating for the FilmCraft desktop application on **Linux tarball installs** via a new, dependency-light L5 crate (`filmcraft-updater`) and wires it end-to-end into the desktop app and UI. macOS and Windows report "download the installer"; Flatpak, Snap, AppImage, Nix and `/usr` installs are told to use their package manager.

The updater adheres strictly to FilmCraft's **"Never Crash"** rule, clean-room standards, and zero-bloat principles: pure Rust (rustls + RustCrypto TLS, flate2, tar), no C code, zero `unsafe`, and zero background daemons.

---

### Architecture & Pipeline

```text
check()    GET github.com/storytold/filmcraft/releases/latest (redirect → vX.Y.Z; no API tokens / rate limits)
           GET …/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/SHA256SUMS.txt (pinned domain allowlist)
stage()    Stream tarball to .part with size cap & live SHA-256 → rename on match
           Safe extraction (no .., absolute paths, links, or zip bombs; fsync durability)
           Smoke test: execute <staged>/bin/filmcraft --version (catches incompatible glibc / arch before touching disk)
           Write staged.json
apply()    Helper mode (`--update-apply`): wait for parent PID exit → <name>.new fsync → <name> to <name>.prev → atomic swap
on_boot()  Track unconfirmed boots. If a new version crashes twice before `confirm()`, the 3rd start restores .prev
           and relaunches the restored executable (keeps broken build as .broken)
confirm()  Called on healthy app launch (after 2 painted frames). Old `.prev` backups are cleaned after 7 days
```

---

### Key Features & Guarantees

1. **Zero-Rate-Limit Discovery (`net.rs`, `release.rs`):**

title: scrub bars: dragging the playhead keeps the audio stream open instead of stopping it every move
author: ReReddo
body:
## What and why

Dragging the playhead along a monitor's scrub bar was choppy and silent, while dragging its timecode scrubbed smoothly and played audio. The scrub bar called `stop()` on every move of the drag. With nothing playing, `stop()` still stops the audio output, which closes the scrub stream the drag had just opened (`scrub.rs` keeps one stream open for the whole drag and only re-aims it), so the next frame built the sequence's mix and reopened the output on the interface thread, again for every move; and each new stream was stopped by the next move before it could play a grain. The timecode drag does not call `stop()`, which is why it was fine.

`FilmcraftApp::stop_for_scrub` stops only when something is playing or about to (preroll). The four surfaces that move the playhead on a press or drag use it: the Program Monitor's scrub bar, the Timeline ruler, the Effect Controls ruler and the transition controls' ruler. Pressing one while playing still stops playback, as before.

- `dragging_a_scrub_bar_keeps_one_output_stream_open` (`meters_ui`): drag along the Program Monitor's scrub bar and the Timeline ruler; the output is started at most once during the drag (it was started on each of the 8 moves for the monitor bar) and the callback produces sound.

title: window: Toggle Full Screen fullscreens on the Program monitor (#1369)
author: notdezzi
body:
Fixes #1369

## What
`window.toggleFullScreen` (View menu / Ctrl+`) already put the OS window into full screen, but the whole editor layout stayed on screen — the reporter's "it just does a full view of the app". As in Premiere, entering full screen now also maximizes the **Program monitor**, so the picture fills the screen; leaving full screen brings back exactly the layout that was there before (or the panel that was maximized before, if any, e.g. via `window.maximizeFrame`).

## How
- New pure state machine `fullscreen_maximize` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/keyboard.rs`, driven by the existing `KeysState` (new `saved_maximized` / `full_screen` fields, serde-defaulted so existing saved states keep loading): enter → save the current maximize state and maximize the Program monitor (reusing `apply_dock(Activate)`); exit → restore. A repeated enter while already in full screen keeps the original layout saved (guards against viewport-state lag / double fire).
- The command route calls it right after sending `ViewportCommand::Fullscreen`.

## Tests
- 4 new headless unit tests in `keyboard.rs` (enter/exit round-trip, restore of a previously maximized panel, double-enter, exit-without-enter) — `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui --lib keyboard`: 5 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

title: ui: keep the waveform anchored while a remix drag previews (#1424)
author: bfenty
body:
## Problem (#1424)
Dragging a clip edge to remix it made the waveform jump/squash mid-drag: while the preview was active the clip body shrank to the new width, but the waveform still mapped through the *original* item, so the whole waveform squeezed into the previewed width until the drag committed.

## Fix
In the `Drag::Remix` arm, insert an edited item into the `edited` map the way Trim and Roll already do — clone the item and bump only `duration` (the commit path keeps `start`/`source_in` and changes only duration). The preview render loop then derives the waveform mapping from the edited item, so media-per-pixel stays constant during the drag.

## Tests
Headless egui test `remix_drag_keeps_the_waveform_anchored` (in `panels/timeline.rs`): starts a remix drag and asserts the waveform's media-per-pixel scale under the preview equals the committed scale.
- RED without the fix (original duration over previewed width ≠ 1/pps)
- GREEN with the fix
- Negative control: reverting only the fix hunk makes the test fail again
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets` clean, `cargo fmt` clean

title: captions: pin the setStyle margin contract with a regression test; clearer track error (#1542)
author: notdezzi
body:
Fixes #1542

## Investigation
I could not reproduce the reported placement on current main. With the reporter's exact parameters (1080×1920 sequence, `captions.setStyle {anchor: "bottom", margin: 0.31, size: 78}`), `render_caption` puts the caption's bottom edge at y=1325 — 595 px above the bottom, i.e. exactly `0.31 × frame height`, matching the documented contract. The burn-in code is byte-identical between v0.6.0 (what the reporter used) and main, and the Program monitor preview, `render_frame` and exports all go through the same `caption_overlays` path.

The reported position (~200 px ≈ 0.1 of the frame) matches the **default** margin (0.08 ≈ 154 px), which points at the margin never having reached the rendered track's style in that session — most plausibly a `track` id mismatch whose error was swallowed by the client (the reporter also noted they had not retested on 0.7.2). The reporter's workaround (anchor middle) ignores margin by design, which is why it "worked".

## What this PR does
- Adds a regression test pinning the documented contract in `crates/captions/src/burn.rs`: bottom anchor → content bottom edge at `h − margin·h`, top anchor → top edge at `margin·h`, and margins 0 / 0.45 / out-of-range-clamped stay inside the frame.
- `captions.setStyle` now names the offending track value in its error ("no such caption track (…) — pass the track id from captions.list, or \"C1\"…") so a silently-swallowed id mismatch is diagnosable.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-captions --lib`: 43 passed (incl. the new `margin_is_a_fraction_of_frame_height`).
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine --lib captions`: 6 passed. Clippy (`-D warnings`) and fmt clean on both crates.

If the reporter can retest on 0.7.2+ with the improved error message, a remaining reproduction would pinpoint the client-side path; the rendering contract itself is now test-enforced.

title: mcp: --automation-read-root / --automation-write-root confine the server to folders (#985)
author: notdezzi
body:
Fixes #985

**What:** `filmcraft-cli mcp` now accepts `--automation-read-root <dir>` and `--automation-write-root <dir>` (each an existing folder; repeat/missing-value rejected), the flags VectorCraft and EffectCraft ship. While roots are in force every command may only read under a read root and only write under a write root — a root left out grants no access of its kind; without both, behavior is unchanged.

**Why:** an agent connected to the server could read/write anywhere the user can (#985, follow-up to #476/#595).

**How:** enforcement lives in `FilmcraftMcp::run` (the one funnel for `command_run`, `command_batch`, `media_import` and long exports), so both the headless engine and `--bridge` are covered (in bridge mode commands are checked in the CLI before they reach the app; the desktop app process itself is not confined — out of this issue's scope). Paths are resolved (links followed, `..` and dangling links refused, Windows device names refused) and compared component-wise against the canonicalized root; rejections are tool errors naming the root. 30 read + 34 write commands are tabled, plus a sweep of any other absolute path in params; the UI-driving tools (`ui_click`/`ui_key`/ui_control`) are refused while confined, since they could drive the app's native file dialogs — mirroring EffectCraft.

**Tested:** 12 new roots unit tests (containment, traversal, links, Windows case/devices), 2 new server tests, CLI flag-shape tests; `cargo test -p filmcraft-automation` 33 passed, `cargo test -p filmcraft-cli` 19 passed; fmt + clippy `-D warnings` green; end-to-end stdio run verified reads/writes outside the roots are refused and in-root writes land.
