title: Timeline: a clip moved to another track keeps its time over a nearby cut
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1893.

While a clip is dragged, the move snaps the block's start or end to the nearest edit, playhead or marker, and the clip's own time is never a candidate (the moved clips are excluded). So when you carry a clip up or down to another track, any cut within a few pixels pulls it off the time it had. Now, when the drag changes track (or makes a new one) and the clip's original time is within snapping reach, that time wins, the way Premiere does it. A drag along the same track is unchanged and still snaps to the nearby edit. Without that limit a clip would stick to its own position and couldn't be nudged onto a close cut. Happy to switch if you'd rather have the original time win on the same track too.

Validation:
- `timeline_move_snap_ui::moved_to_another_track_a_clip_keeps_its_time_over_a_nearby_cut`: fails on main (the overlay lands on the V1 cut 4 px away), passes here

title: #1877: graphics.set can put keyframes on the properties it sets
author: Guilhermeb-Ferrarezi
body:
Fixes #1877

`graphics.set` takes a `time`, but `time` only says where a keyframe-aware change lands: a property that is already animated gets or changes a keyframe there, and any other property changes its fixed value. A script that called it at two times (the report's ellipse at x = 300 and x = 1600) got the last value, no keyframes and no error.

## What changes

- `graphics.set` takes `keyframe: true`: every property in `props` gets a keyframe at `time` (default the playhead) and becomes animated, the same as `effects.setParam` with `keyframe: true` (it uses `Param::put_keyframe`). The result is `{"keyframes": {"<property>": <count>, ...}}`.
- A property that cannot be animated (for example `font`) is refused with an error instead of being set.
- Calls without `keyframe` behave exactly as before and still return `null`, so the Essential Graphics panel and the other callers of `set_props` are unchanged.
- The command's description now says what `time` does and what `keyframe` does (`describe graphics.set`).

## Tests

`graphics_tests::set_with_keyframes`:
- `keyframe_true_animates_the_property`: the report's steps with `keyframe: true` give keyframes at 0 (x = 300) and at 1.5 s (x = 1600), the results report 1 and then 2 keyframes, and halfway the ellipse is between the two positions.
- `without_keyframe_the_last_call_wins_as_before`: the old behaviour, result `null`.
- `a_property_that_is_already_animated_keeps_following_time`: once animated, a call with `time` and no `keyframe` adds a keyframe, as before.
- `one_undo_step_per_call_and_properties_that_cannot_be_animated_are_refused`: undo takes back one keyframe; `font` and an unknown property are errors.

`cargo test -p filmcraft-engine`: 637 passed. `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

title: packaging: RPM requires library sonames, so openSUSE can install it
author: tydude001
body:
## What and why

FilmCraft's RPM requires Fedora package names: `libxkbcommon`, `(vulkan-loader or libglvnd-egl)`, `alsa-lib`.
openSUSE has no `libxkbcommon`, `vulkan-loader` or `libglvnd-egl` package, so zypper refuses it with
`nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` (exit 4, which the ArtCraft Launcher shows as "error 4";
storytold/craft-launcher#341). Fixes #1727.

This requires the libraries' sonames instead, as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft already do, so the same RPM
resolves on Fedora/RHEL and openSUSE. It also declares the binaries' glibc floor, matching the deb's
`libc6 (>= 2.35)`, in place of `glibc >= 2.35` (#93). The floor names libm, not libc: the
binaries' only GLIBC_2.35 symbols are `hypot` and `hypotf` from libm, and RHEL 9's current glibc
(`2.34-283.el9_8`) provides `libc.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)` through backports but not libm's. `docs/releasing.md` now says so too.

## How it was tested

FilmCraft 0.7.2's released x86_64 binaries, repackaged with nfpm 2.47.0 and this branch's `nfpm.yaml`, then
installed with the distro's own package manager in a fresh x86_64 container and run with `filmcraft-cli --version`.
The released RPM is the same test on the release's own package.

| | released 0.7.2 RPM | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Fedora 44 | installs, runs | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Tumbleweed | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Leap 15.6 | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| Rocky Linux 9 (glibc 2.34) | refused: `nothing provides glibc >= 2.35` | refused: `nothing provides libm.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)(64bit)` |

The aarch64 RPMs get the same requires. I checked that side on FilmCraft only: its 0.7.2 arm64 binaries need
GLIBC_2.35 for the same two libm symbols, and its branch RPM installs and runs on arm64 Fedora 44,

title: #1885: Proxy ▸ Create Proxies… from the item menu takes the whole selection

title: edit: preserve identities in repeated move and copy plans
author: nuclearspike
body:
Closes #1903.

A move plan naming the same clip twice can place one identity at multiple timeline positions. `move_items` now rejects repeated IDs before changing the sequence. A failed public `timeline.move` leaves the project, next ID, and Undo/Redo history unchanged even when a new destination track was requested. Selection-derived plans keep each ID once, and toggling a selection clears all stored occurrences.

Explicit `timeline.move` copy requests can repeat a source; each occurrence is planned at its requested destination, while a later overwrite can remove an earlier copy. When each linked source is repeated equally at the same offset across multiple destination tracks, copies pair by destination track shift instead of request order; a single copy of each linked source stays linked even at different time offsets. For repeated sources with unequal destination-shift sets, only matching shifts form cohorts; a cohort can omit a video or audio partner, and unmatched copies remain unpaired. This does not infer caller-intended groups from request order. An overwrite can leave several live fragments of one copy, so `copy_items` now returns only surviving fragment IDs in request order, with each request’s fragments ordered by start. The public command reports and selects that list. Interactive Option-drag normalizes the selected clips to one occurrence per ID. Surviving linked partners and copied fades or crossfades follow the live source edge or cut; a vertical copy at the original time keeps both original IDs.

Synthetic regressions cover direct edits, public commands, mixed destinations, overwrites, links, transitions, selection, Undo/Redo, and the headless Frame Hold → Option-drag journey. The branch is merged with current main, retaining the new-track count limit and transactional command checks.

The latest merge retains upstream transition bounds after regular trims and non-ripple speed changes together with the copy-specific fade adjustment.

title: #1871: Lens Blur works out its disc offsets once per frame, not per pixel
author: Guilhermeb-Ferrarezi
body:
Refs #1871

The Lens Blur transition blurs both pictures with a disc of golden-angle samples (`disc_blur`). Every sample's offset (`sqrt`, `cos`, `sin`) was computed again for every pixel, although it depends only on the radius and the number of samples: at 1080p with the default radius that is about 50 million square roots, sines and cosines per picture, two pictures per frame.

## What changes

- `disc_offsets(r, n)` works the offsets out once; `disc_blur_with(img, x, y, &offsets)` samples with them. Lens Blur builds the two sets (outgoing and incoming radius) once per frame.
- The arithmetic is the same (`x + rr * a.cos()` with `rr * a.cos()` computed first), so the pixels are **bit for bit** what they were.

## Measured

`cargo test --release -p filmcraft-render --lib lens_blur_frame_time -- --ignored --nocapture`, one 1920x1080 picture, radius 30, 24 samples, Windows 11, 20 threads:

| | per picture |
|---|---|
| offsets per pixel (before) | 95.2 ms |
| offsets once per frame | 50.3 ms (1.89x) |

A Lens Blur frame blurs both pictures, so about 190 ms becomes about 100 ms. The rest is the bilinear sampling itself; the report's 1 fps on a laptop CPU will improve but not reach real time with this change alone, hence `Refs`.

## Tests

- `disc_blur_with_shared_offsets_is_bit_identical`: the old per-pixel function and the new one agree to the bit on a test picture for radii 0 to 200 and sample counts 1 to 48 (including the no-blur cases).
- The transition goldens (`golden_fingerprints`, which include `lens_blur` at 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75) are unchanged.
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-render`: 195 passed. `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

title: Basic 3D: Distance to Image keeps its perspective at every render scale
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1920.

The Program monitor renders at the resolution the picture needs on screen, so zooming changes the render scale. Basic 3D's focal length follows the working image (`max(w, h) * 1.2`), but Distance to Image was added to the camera depth in full-resolution pixels without `px_scale`. At a lower scale the plane sat relatively further back, so the picture shrank and its perspective changed with the zoom (and with 1/2 or 1/4 playback resolution). The fix scales the distance by `px_scale`, the same way 3D Rotate already treats its Z. Full-resolution renders and exports don't change.

Validation:
- `adjustment_tests::basic_3d_keeps_its_perspective_at_every_render_scale` renders a red matte under an adjustment layer with Basic 3D (swivel, tilt, distance) at scale 1, 1/2 and 1/4. It then compares the picture's coverage and its bounds in sequence pixels. It fails on main (at 1/2 the picture covers 0.30 of the frame instead of 0.49) and passes here.
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-render --lib adjustment_tests`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: #1216: the decoders and the H.264 encoder an export starts keep to its maxThreads
author: Guilhermeb-Ferrarezi
body:
**Stacked on #1870** (its commit is the first one here; review only the second, `8b9080ee`, or merge #1870 first). This is the follow-up @maxm11 described on #1216: with `maxThreads` set the export's own rendering runs on a pool of that size, but the decoders it starts and the H.264 encoder sized their thread pools from all the cores, so a capped export still used far more than *N*.

## What changes

- **A thread cap hint** in `filmcraft_media::cancel`, next to the background / draft hints: `with_thread_cap`, `thread_cap`, `capped_threads` (and `set_thread_cap` for a pool's start handler). `cancel::Context` carries it, so it reaches the decode pool the same way the other hints do.
- **Export** (`export/src/lib.rs`): a capped export always runs on a pool of its own, `min(cap, the caller's pool)` threads (still never more threads than before), whose start handler marks every thread with the cap. Before, a cap at or above the caller's pool ran in place, and the other workers then started uncapped decoders. The H.264 encoder gets `cfg.threads = cap`. Its slices depend on the frame size only (`h264_slices`), so the file is unchanged.
- **Decoders** (`codecs/src/video.rs`): H.264, HEVC, VP9 and AV1 decoders made under the hint use at most that many threads, keep that count across `reset`, and report `thread_limited()`, so a capped decoder that playback later picks up from the shared decoder pool is swapped for a full one, the same as a background decoder.
- **GOP caches** (`codecs/src/gop.rs`): `isolated` runs a cache's decoding on a decode pool of the cap's size (one per cap, kept for the next export) instead of the shared all-cores pool when the hint is set.

ProRes, DNxHR and APV already encode on the current rayon pool, the capped one.

## Measured

`filmcraft-cli export` of 4 s of a 2560×1440 60 fps H.264 clip to H.264 (no audio), release build, 20-thread CPU. Cores = process CPU time / wall time:

| maxThreads | #1870 alone | this PR |

title: media: keep TGA metadata out of image payloads
author: nuclearspike
body:
Fixes #1931.

A TGA that declares two pixels but contains only one can consume footer or optional metadata bytes as the missing pixel. The decoder now bounds raw and RLE reads at a recognized TGA 2.0 footer and at referenced metadata starts within the image body, including payloads that precede their directory. It ignores out-of-range pointers, pointers before the pixel-data start, incomplete directory entries, and zero-length developer payloads. Complete images remain readable when malformed optional records point outside the body or their payloads begin after the pixels.

Two boundaries are byte-ambiguous. An in-body optional-metadata pointer inside the declared pixel span can describe either corrupt metadata on a complete image or metadata filling missing pixels; this patch rejects that overlap. A synthetic regression uses a structurally complete two-entry developer directory whose second payload points at the first pixel. An inflated developer count can also scan later physically complete ten-byte chunks as entries; an apparent payload inside pixels is rejected under the same policy. Pointers before the calculated pixel start are ignored to keep complete ID and palette data readable, so a malformed record there can still supply missing palette bytes. A terminal TGA 2.0 signature is treated as a footer only when its 26-byte trailer begins at or after byte 18. A footerless legacy file whose final 26 bytes mimic that trailer remains ambiguous whenever the putative trailer begins at or after byte 18; even a complete image whose apparent trailer starts inside its image ID or pixels may be rejected. An 18- or 25-pixel signature-ending legacy image whose putative trailer would start inside the header stays readable. These compatibility choices need maintainer review.

title: matroska: bound recursive chapter and tag parsing
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Prevents stack exhaustion when importing Matroska files containing
excessively nested ChapterAtom or SimpleTag elements.

- Limit recursive chapter and tag parsing to 64 levels.
- Preserve metadata parsing within the supported nesting depth.
- Ignore deeper descendants instead of continuing recursion.
- Add regression tests using 100,000 nested EBML elements for
  both chapter and tag structures.

Addresses the Matroska recursion finding in #1888.

## Validation

Two regression tests added. Rust tests and CI have not been run.

title: cli: reject deeply nested dotted parameters before parsing
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Prevents stack exhaustion when filmcraft-cli receives an excessively
deep dotted parameter key.

Previously, insert_dotted recursively constructed a JSON object
without limiting nesting depth.

Changes:
- Enforce a maximum of 64 nested parameter levels.
- Return a descriptive parsing error when the limit is exceeded.
- Preserve existing behavior for supported dotted parameters.
- Add regression coverage for accepted and rejected nesting depths.

The limit also avoids constructing JSON objects too deeply nested
for normal serialization.

Addresses the CLI recursion finding in #1888.

## Validation

Boundary regression test added. Rust tests and CI have not been run.

title: Saturate crop and field-height math on hostile Matroska/MXF/AAF headers
author: Ni-zav
body:
## Summary

Prevents integer overflow when media containers and interchange
documents specify extreme crop values or field-based frame heights.

Changes:
- Matroska: use saturating arithmetic when combining pixel crops.
- MXF: saturate field-based frame-height multiplication.
- AAF: apply the same overflow protection to imported picture sources.
- Add regression tests for extreme crop values and frame heights.
- Verify ordinary pixel-aspect calculations remain unchanged.

These changes prevent debug-build arithmetic panics and release-build
integer wrapping caused by malformed media headers.

Addresses the dimension overflow finding in #1888.

## Validation

Regression tests added for Matroska and MXF.
The equivalent AAF arithmetic correction is included.

Rust tests and CI have not been run.

title: fix(media): time Counting Leader beeps by source frame rate
author: nuclearspike
body:
Fixes #1947.

Universal Counting Leader gates its beep for about 1/24 second even when the source uses another frame rate. At 48 kHz and 60 fps, the old gate lasts roughly 2,000 sample positions, with floating-point boundary drift, instead of the source frame's half-open range [0, 800). This change uses the source's rational frame rate and integer sample positions to gate one frame at each second mark. A waveform sample inside that range can itself be zero. The carrier and video output are unchanged; malformed rates use the existing 24000/1001 fallback.

Counting Leaders with distinct stored source rates no longer consolidate as duplicates, so the edit command cannot silently replace a placed leader's beep timing. Other generator duplicate grouping is unchanged. This changes played and exported audio for existing projects with non-24-fps Counting Leaders. At 48 kHz, the gate spans 800 positions at 60 fps, 1,600 at 30 fps, and 2,002 at 23.976 fps, compared with roughly 2,000 before. Downstream timeline/sample rounding and long-duration carrier precision are separate.

Five generator tests cover integer, fractional and custom rates, exact boundaries, split requests, malformed rates and hostile sample rates. The edit-command regression verifies that Consolidate Duplicates preserves distinct-rate leaders and still merges equal-rate copies. Reproduce the boundary and duplicate behavior with `cargo test -p filmcraft-media --lib --locked counting_leader` and `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine --lib --locked consolidate_keeps_counting_leaders_with_distinct_source_rates`.

title: Decode Blackmagic RAW (.braw) through Blackmagic's runtime (Linux, Windows, macOS)
author: txiki739
body:
#290 asks for Blackmagic RAW (`.braw`) support. This adds it the way the project's rules allow: `.braw` files open through **Blackmagic's own runtime** when the user has installed it (Blackmagic RAW 6.0+, or DaVinci Resolve 21's identical Linux copy). FilmCraft neither bundles nor reverse engineers anything: the runtime is loaded at run time, only when the first `.braw` file opens, and without it a `.braw` file fails to open with a message saying what to install. That is the same shape as the NVENC path (a vendor library used as an accelerator), and it widens ADR 0001 from OS media APIs to a vendor's runtime, so the ADR's addendum is marked **proposed** for #383.

## What changes

- **Linux, Windows and macOS.** `libBlackmagicRawAPI.so` on Linux, `BlackmagicRawAPI.dll` on Windows, `BlackmagicRawAPI.framework` on macOS. The 6.0 runtime needs no COM registration on Windows; on macOS the framework is loaded through `CFBundle`, the way Blackmagic's own dispatching loader loads it.
- **Opening.** A `PathOpener` registry in `media/codecs` lets media SDKs that open files by path take part before the regular readers. `filmcraft_codecs::open_by_path` hands a file to the opener that takes it. When none does in a build (the web app, FreeBSD), it refuses a format that only such an opener decodes (`filmcraft_media::PATH_ONLY_FORMATS`) before any read, instead of reading a camera clip whole. `MediaPool::open_file` and `probe_file`, and the CLI's `probe` and `bench-decode`, all use it. `braw` joins `VIDEO_EXTENSIONS`.
- **Signed macOS builds.** Library validation under the hardened runtime refuses a framework another team signs, so `packaging/macos/entitlements.plist` and a new `entitlements-cli.plist` carry `com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation`, with the reason in a comment (an xtask test checks both).
- **What you get.** Frames decoded and processed by Blackmagic's decoder with the clip's own settings (as recorded, or as its sidecar file sets them) to 8-bit Rec. 709…

author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/format/src/autosave.rs:74 (list_auto_saves / rotate, called from write_auto_save at :102)` (no existing issue): Auto-save rotation deletes the newest auto-save (and can overwrite one) when the local clock goes back at the end of daylight saving time.

## Cause
Auto-save files were named and sorted by the local wall-clock stamp. When daylight saving time ends, the clock goes back. A newer save then sorts before older ones, so rotation deletes it, and a save in the repeated hour can get the same name as an earlier one and overwrite it.

## Fix
Auto-save names now end with the unix time: `<name>-YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS-<unix>.fcproj`. `list_auto_saves` sorts by that unix time, so rotation removes the truly oldest file, and saves in the repeated hour get different names. Older files without the unix suffix are still recognised, sort before all new ones, and can still be rotated out. The module docs and `docs/project-files.md` describe the new name.

## Verified
- Regression tests `rotation_survives_the_clock_going_back_at_the_end_of_dst`, `repeated_wall_clock_hour_does_not_overwrite_earlier_saves`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-format --lib autosave::tests`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `the_notice_follows_the_interface_language`, `alt_box_selects_only_video_and_delete_keeps_linked_audio`, which also fail on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
Existing auto-save files are not renamed. The local stamp stays in the name for people to read. Display and `civil` are unchanged.

title: render: Transform with its own shutter angle stays on the CPU (the GPU path dropped its motion blur)
author: schnierk
body:
## What

With **Use Effect Shutter Angle** on and a shutter angle above 0.5°, the CPU renders Transform with a seven-sample motion blur: `vfx::apply` sends it to `distort::transform_fx` (`crates/render/src/vfx/mod.rs`, the `"transform" if bv(e, "shutter_override") && fv(e, "shutter_angle", cx) > 0.5` arm).

The GPU path accepted the same effect by its id alone (`plan::gpu_chain`), and `FxOp::eval` for `transform` places one picture without looking at the shutter. So with GPU compositing on, the Program monitor and GPU exports silently dropped the blur and showed a different picture from the CPU renderer.

## Fix

`FxOp::eval` declines `transform` under exactly the CPU's condition, using the same helpers (`vfx::bv` / `vfx::fv`). The planner collects a clip's chain all-or-nothing (`FxOp::eval(..).filter(FxOp::gpu_ok)`), so that clip is rendered on the CPU, with its blur.

The CPU path is unchanged. `effects::apply` runs `vfx::apply` first, and `vfx::apply` handles this case before `FxOp::eval` is reached. Every other caller of `FxOp::eval` uses default parameters, where the override is off.

A GPU port of the shutter blur can replace this later.

## Tests

- New `gpufx::tests::transform_with_its_own_shutter_angle_stays_on_the_cpu`. It checks four cases:
  - a moved Transform is a GPU op;
  - with the override on at the default 180° it goes to the CPU;
  - at 0° it is back on the GPU;
  - an angle without the override stays on the GPU.
- `cargo xtask ci` on Linux (Mint 22.3, Ryzen 7 9800X3D): fmt, clippy, layers, assets and wasm pass, and every test passes except `dev_icon::tests::desktop_file_matches_the_packaged_fields`. That test fails on main too and has nothing to do with this change: 69a6c4b6 added `MimeType` to the packaged desktop entry but not to the dev entry. I am sending the one-line fix as a separate PR.
  - The wgpu tests ran on the integrated Radeon through RADV. CUDA was hidden for this run because the RTX 5090 was busy with another job.

title: #1910: Interpret Footage from the item menu takes the whole selection
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1910

## Cause
The Project panel item context menu sent `clip.interpretFootage` with `{"items": [<right-clicked id>]}`, so the dialog and the override only ever covered that one clip. The engine command (`footage_targets`) and the dialog already handle many items in one undo step.

title: #1089: open Kdenlive projects (`.kdenlive`, MLT XML) through File ▸ Import
author: guillehr2
body:
Fixes #1089. A `.kdenlive` project now opens the way the other interchange documents do: File ▸ Import (or the Media Browser, or `filmcraft-cli import`) reads it with a new `filmcraft_interchange::mlt` module and merges its bins, media and timeline into the project as one undoable step. The media found on disk is then linked, and missing files are listed offline. `Format::Mlt` is import only. `Format::can_export()` keeps it out of `file.exportInterchange`, whose accepted names and error message are unchanged.

What is read:

- **Profile → sequence settings:** frame size, frame rate (`frame_rate_num/den`) and pixel aspect. Without a `<profile>`, MLT's documented default (DV PAL, 720×576 at 25 fps), with an info entry.
- **Producers and chains with a `resource` → media:** one item per file. Relative paths resolve against `<mlt root>`, else the document's folder. `color` producers become colour mattes (Black Video for black). The bin's clips (the `main_bin` playlist `<mlt producer>` names) are imported even when the timeline doesn't use them.
- **Timeline:** the tractor `<mlt producer>` names, else the document's last tractor, looked through when it only wraps another one (a project tractor around a Kdenlive sequence). Each track is a playlist, or a tractor of playlists (a Kdenlive track). `<entry producer in out>` becomes a clip (`out` is inclusive), `<blank length>` a gap. An entry without `in`/`out` takes its producer's. Times are read as frame counts, clock values (`HH:MM:SS.mmm`, rounded to the nearest frame, exact at NTSC rates) and SMPTE timecode (`HH:MM:SS:FF`, drop-frame `;FF`).
- **Video vs audio:** `kdenlive:audio_track`. For MLT documents without Kdenlive properties, a track that hides only its video (`hide="video"`) is audio. A hidden video track is turned off and a hidden audio track muted. `kdenlive:track_name` and `kdenlive:locked_track` are kept. Kdenlive's black background track is left out. Video tracks keep MLT's stacking order (V1 at the bottom). K…

title: Add Reactor FastH3 Omni generation to FilmCraft desktop
author: willemhelmet
body:
## Summary

Add optional FastH3 Omni generation directly to FilmCraft desktop, using each user's own Reactor account. Open **Window → Reactor**, dock the panel beside the timeline, describe a shot, and generate it without leaving the editor. Completed clips are saved beside the project and imported into its bin automatically.

## Demo

[Watch the Loom walkthrough](https://www.loom.com/share/df38f56186224d46be89b1f68559f0be)

## Workflow

- **Set up once:** Settings → Reactor saves/removes the API key in the OS credential store and links to API keys and account billing. No shared FilmCraft key or central billing service is introduced. Keys stay outside project files, preferences, and serialized UI state.
- **Compose:** prompt, duration, aspect ratio, and optional image/audio references. Square reference tiles show actual image previews and inline audio playback with a seekable waveform. Current frame captures the Program monitor into an image reference.
- **Keep editing:** queue up to eight shots, submitted one at a time. Cards show upload, queue, generation, download, and import status. Closing the panel keeps the queue running. Queued requests can be cancelled before submission.
- **Iterate:** switch between grid/list views and reuse a shot's prompt, settings, and reference paths. Completed cards use thumbnails decoded from the downloaded local clip.
- **Keep media with the project:** uniquely named MP4s go into `<project file stem> Media/Reactor/`. Unsaved projects use the standard project Save action once; generation does not open a clip save dialog. Requests retain their original project/bin. Switching projects never imports a result into the wrong project, and queued work waits until its original project is active.

The implementation uses FilmCraft's existing docking, media, audio output, import, command, and automation interfaces. The desktop HTTP worker uploads references, submits/polls the generation endpoint, and downloads the output. It reserves writable …

title: ui: Interpret Footage takes the whole Project panel selection (#1910)
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
When several clips are selected in the Project panel, Interpret Footage… from the context menu only interpreted the clip that was right-clicked — the menu action passed a single item while the engine command and the dialog already accept a list. The action now takes the whole open selection when the right-clicked item is part of it (the same rule the bin-drop code uses) and only that item otherwise, so one dialog applies the colour-space override to every selected clip in one undo step. The menu button also gets an automation id (`project.itemMenu.interpretFootage`). Fixes #1910

title: ui: playhead.set while playing moves the playhead and playback continues from it (#1622)
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`playhead.set` through the control-channel/menu dispatcher moved the stored playhead during playback, but the next tick derived it from the old clock anchor and lost the move. It now reanchors playback at the requested position and restarts the audio stream when the device owns the clock. Restarting also resets the audio-stall watchdog, matching the existing stream-restart paths.

The regressions exercise the real `playhead.set` dispatcher and a restarted device that initially reports zero played frames. They check that playback continues from the moved playhead and keeps the audio clock. The branch includes current main and uses its time-aware `start_audio(now)` API. All 10 audio-recovery tests and 202 UI library tests pass on macOS arm64. The timing comment explains that a command invoked between egui passes sees the preceding pass's time.

This addresses only `playhead.set` being ignored during playback. It does not address the dropped-frame performance report in #1622 or change the separate start/end/step command paths.

Refs #1622

author: woldercraft
body:
On Linux systems running native Wayland compositors (such as KDE Plasma with Dolphin), winit currently lacks full Wayland drag-and-drop data transfer, preventing files from being dropped onto the window.

title: enhancement: Program monitor shows the motion path of a clip's animated Position
author: aw4e
body:
Closes #1961

## What
When a clip with at least two Motion > Position keyframes is selected and the playhead is on it, the Program monitor draws its path of travel from the first keyframe to the last, as Premiere Pro does:

- dotted line through the keyframe values
- a square on every keyframe (automation id `program.motionPath.<clip>.keyframe.<time>`)
- a direction arrow in the middle of each leg
- a dot at the position under the playhead

## How
New `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/motion_path.rs`, called from `monitor.rs` after the mask overlay. Position interpolation eases both components with the same factor, so every leg is a straight line between its two keyframe values whatever the interpolation (easing changes speed, not route). The path is therefore the keyframe values joined up; nothing is sampled per frame.

Never-crash: no `unwrap`/indexing; NaN/inf values and a zero frame size draw nothing; keyframes are capped at 512.

## Not included
- Keyframe squares are display-only; dragging them to edit Position is not implemented (follow-up).
- No toggle; the overlay shows for every selected clip with an animated Position.
- Hold legs are drawn as a faint line with no arrow (nothing travels on them).

## Checks
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets` pass. `clippy -D warnings` is clean for the new file; on current main it reports three `nonminimal_bool` errors in `file_dialogs.rs` and `timeline.rs`, which this PR does not touch. `xtask wasm` and the full workspace tests are left to CI. Not yet checked by eye in the running app with two different keyframe values.

Replaces #1968, which carried unrelated commits from a stale local `main`.

title: Add Craft AI: the family's built-in local assistant (Gemma 4 catalogue, loopback runtimes, shared models folder)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

**Craft AI** — one assistant across the ArtCraft family, as a dock panel in FilmCraft. It talks to a local model runtime on this machine and never to a cloud service:

| | |
|---|---|
| **Local and private** | Every request is `http://127.0.0.1` — Ollama (11434), LM Studio (1234) or llama.cpp's server (8080), whichever answers. No account, no key, no telemetry, and no address a cloud service could be reached at exists in the code. |
| **Light by design** | No inference engine, no weights, no GPU code enters the app. The runtime the user already has (or installs) does the running — Craft AI is a loopback conversation. |
| **Optional** | Without a runtime or a model the panel says so and touches nothing beyond loopback. Downloading is a button, never a default. |
| **Specialised** | The system prompt tells the model it is inside FilmCraft and names this app's world — the timeline and its tracks, cuts and J/L cuts, transitions, effects and keyframes, Lumetri colour, the mixers and ducking, titles and captions, markers and timecode, export — so answers are about this app, not generic advice. The ready-made tasks (cut plan feedback, caption and transcript cleanup, pacing and montage advice, effect or transition choice, name this sequence) are framed for it, with the honesty clause: never invent panel names. |
| **One download serves every app** | The model file lands in a shared folder the whole family reads — `<data_home>/ArtCraft/Craft AI/models` — so a model downloaded here is already there in every other ArtCraft app, no second download. Ollama's own store works the same way machine-wide. |

- **Assistant** — runtime and model pickers, the task, the question, the answer; the conversation is kept, copyable, and Arabic answers are drawn through the same visual-order pass as the rest of the Arabic interface. Worker thread, so the UI never blocks; a busy timer ticks while the model thinks.

title: Add filmcraft-hub: the CraftHub client path (the v3 adapter, spec §3.6 phase C / §18.4 row 8)
author: hasan-sdaif
body:
## What this is

`filmcraft-hub` — the app-side binding that speaks the generalized collaboration core ([`craft-collab`](https://github.com/hasan-sdaif/crafthub), extracted from figcraft's proven `figcraft-collab` and proposed as `storytold/craft-libs#128`). This is FilmCraft's row of the adoption table — the **timeline row**, §18.4 row 8 — with the three decisions that row names: region locks of the `TimelineRange` shape, presence carrying the playhead, and heavy media as deferred assets.

Nothing here changes user-visible behavior. The session wiring (a v3 `NetLink` behind the app's `crafthub` feature flag, default off) lands as the pilot follow-up once this contract is reviewed.

## The honest map

FilmCraft's project is a bin tree plus a flat item map, and every id type (bins, items, tracks, clips, transitions, captions) draws from **one monotonic counter** — so a single 64-bit id names any object, and the ids ride as space-0 `NodeId`s directly, no translation map (unlike DeckCraft's `u32` row).

- **Bins and items** (media, sequences, subclips, adjustment layers, graphics) sync as objects with the bin tree as their parent axis; the root bin *is* the file root, its name syncing as `rootName`.
- **Tracks** are objects whose parent is their sequence, in four lists (video, submix, audio, caption); the track kind rides the node kind (`videoTrack`/`audioTrack`/`submixTrack`/`captionTrack`). **Clips, transitions and captions** are objects whose parent is their track. A sequence's payload syncs *without* its track lists — they are the tree.
- **Clip order is time, not paint order.** A track's items are sorted by `start` (the model's own invariant, `Track::sort`), so the sibling keys are subordinate to it: the adapter assigns keys by current order at first sync, the LIS discipline keeps them under edits, and `apply` re-sorts every touched track by start at the end of the batch — deterministic on every replica, which is why the schema's `recompute` is honestly empty.

title: codecs: avoid duration-sized silence allocation for damaged MP4 audio
author: nuclearspike
body:
A damaged MP4 AAC packet can carry a very large `stts` duration. The existing decode-failure path allocated that many silence samples per channel even when the caller requested only a short audio window. This change records the packet failure without allocating packet-sized audio, then zeroes only the requested span in the source-rate output buffer. Earlier decoded samples are concealed where packets overlap; later valid packets still overwrite that span in normal order. The same failure path covers other compressed MP4 audio codecs. The packet's raw track-timescale duration is still treated as a frame count in this concealment path; correcting that pre-existing timing behavior is separate.

A synthetic AAC-LC MP4 with an empty access unit and a 1,000,000-unit sample duration verifies that the failed packet holds no duration-sized samples and that a 128-frame request returns stereo silence. Two further regressions cover overlap with earlier decoded audio and extreme timestamp/duration bounds.

Validation on the exact PR head `56d3a70a1ecaf60794c457f423beb37423d83fa6`:

- macOS: `cargo fmt --check`, release workspace Clippy, `cargo test -p filmcraft-codecs --lib` in debug and release, and `cargo xtask wasm` with the WASM target installed passed.
- Ubuntu 26.04 ARM64 with Rust 1.99.0, on this exact head: `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked --offline -- -D warnings` passed; `cargo test -p filmcraft-codecs --lib --locked --offline corrupt_audio_tests` passed 3 tests, and `cargo test -p filmcraft-codecs --lib --locked --offline` passed 127 tests. title: macOS: open files from Finder, the Dock and Open With
author: gkistlergit

`open -a FilmCraft clip.mp4`, a Finder double-click, Open With and a drop on the Dock icon arrive as the open-documents (`odoc`) Apple event, not as an argument. winit 0.30 owns the application delegate and never handles that event, so AppKit fell back to its own document handling and showed "FilmCraft cannot open files in the “MPEG-4 movie” format"; the file never reached the app. The quit Apple event (Dock menu, log out, AppleScript) was ignored the same way. title: Time Remapping: play static speeds and keyframed ramps, with linked sound (#510)
author: ZorudaRinku
body:
Time Remapping's Speed was saved but never read (#510): `TrackItem::source_time_at` ignored it, so a static value or a keyframed ramp changed nothing on screen, in playback or in export. #1491 and #1709 reported the same. This makes Time Remapping play, as in Premiere, and lets the linked sound follow it.

**Picture.** A static Speed is the clip's speed: setting it is a Speed/Duration without ripple, and Speed/Duration, Rate Stretch and imports show up in it. A keyframed Speed sets how fast each part of the media plays. Its keyframes sit at media times like every other effect keyframe, so a ramp stays on the frames it was set on through razor cuts, trims, rolls, slides, slips and through-edit joins. A new speed keeps the clip's media and changes its length: a slower clip grows up to the next clip on its track and stops there, as Speed/Duration does without ripple.

**Sound.** With the new Remap Audio checkbox on (the default), the linked sound from the same source takes the picture's speed, or a copy of its curve, and plays varispeed, its pitch following the speed. Off, the sound plays at normal speed, as Premiere's picture-only Time Remapping does. The sound's copy of the curve is hidden in Effect Controls and follows the picture.

**How**

- `filmcraft_project::time_remap::TimeMap` (new): Φ(m), the timeline time to play the media up to media time `m`, is the integral of 1 / speed. It is built once per curve as a table of knots (64 Simpson pieces per eased segment, one per hold or flat segment, at most 16 384) and read by straight interpolation, so it is strictly increasing and every media time has exactly one timeline time and back. Speeds are clamped to 1–10 000 %; NaN and ∞ play at 100 %.
- `TrackItem` gains `time_map`, `is_remapped`, `media_after`, `timeline_span`, `timeline_time_of`, `keyframe_near` and `source_clock` (the curve built once for many reads: audio samples, waveform pixels). `moving_source_time_at` and `source_out` go through them. For a clip that…

title: fix: satisfy clippy::nonminimal_bool on Rust 1.96
author: ssandweiss
body:
### What was wrong

`cargo xtask ci` stops at clippy on the current stable toolchain (1.96.1). `clippy::nonminimal_bool` flags three expressions on `main` (four errors). Each crate's errors only show once the crate before it builds:

- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/file_dialogs.rs:134`: `open && !(r.should_close() && !ctx.input(...))`
- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs:268`: `!ph.is_finite() || !scroll.is_finite() || !(pps > 0.0 && pps.is_finite())`
- `apps/filmcraft/src/audio.rs:330`: `!lost && !(self.pending_error && stalled)`

The CI workflows build but don't run clippy, so nothing catches this upstream. Every contributor running the gates on stable 1.96 hits it.

### Change

All three expressions are rewritten by De Morgan's laws to the forms clippy suggests:

- `open && (!r.should_close() || ctx.input(...))`
- `!(ph.is_finite() && scroll.is_finite() && pps > 0.0 && pps.is_finite())`
- `!(lost || (self.pending_error && stalled))`

The truth tables are the same, including NaN, since `pps > 0.0` is false for NaN either way.

### Gates

Locally on macOS, toolchain 1.96.1:

- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, in dev and `--release`: pass. Both failed before this change.
- `cargo fmt --check`: pass
- `filmcraft-ui-egui` lib tests `timeline` and `file_dialogs`: pass

title: fix(timeline): Option-click Razor and Option-drag trim affect one clip (#1945)
author: ssandweiss
body:
Fixes #1945 for the Razor and trim tools.

### What was wrong

With the Razor, Option-click still cut the clicked clip's linked partners (the sound under the picture, or the other way round). Dragging an edge with Option held still trimmed both. In Premiere, Option makes these act on the clicked clip alone, which is how J- and L-cuts are made. The Selection tool already honoured Option (`timeline.select` / `timeline.move` take `linked`). The Razor and the trims always went through `with_links`.

- **Timeline:**
  - A Razor click sends `linked: !Option`.

Other tools named in the issue (slip, slide, rate stretch, roll) are not changed here.

`split_edit_tests`, new:

- `razor_cuts_the_linked_partner_unless_linked_is_false`: a plain cut makes 2 + 2 clips; `linked: false` makes 2 + 1.

title: fix(engine): Unlink a selection that also holds unlinked clips (#1103)
author: ssandweiss
body:
Fixes #1103.

### What was wrong

Unlinking several clips at once could do nothing. The Timeline's context menu labels the item "Unlink" when any picked clip is linked, but `clip.link` only unlinked when every selected clip was linked. title: Properties: with text selected, the character controls show the selection's style (#1996)
author: wstock
body:
Fixes the first problem in #1996 (the colour picker not following a change made with text selected). Saved/recent colours, the second one, is a separate feature and not addressed here.

## Root cause
With a Type-tool selection, `Ctx::set` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/graphics.rs` routes character properties to `graphics.setCharStyle`, which stores them as per-character runs on the layer (`LayerExtra::runs`) and leaves the layer's own `fill_color` / `size` / … untouched. Every control, though, read its value with `pv(e, id, mt)`, i.e. the layer's parameter — so after changing Fill (or typing into R, G or B) with "Drive" selected, the text turned red but the picker and the fields still showed the layer's white, and the next edit started from that stale value.

## Fix
- `Ctx::value(id)`: with a selection, a character property (font, style, size, fill, bold/italic/underline, tracking, baseline shift, caps) reads the selected characters' own style at the start of the selection, via a new `graphic_design::char_style_at(runs, i)` (the merge `apply_char_style` leaves there); anything not overridden, and every other property, still reads the layer's value. Without a selection nothing changes.
- The colour button, checkboxes, hot-number fields, choices and the Font / Font Style combos read through it.

## Tests
- `graphic_design::tests::char_style_at_reads_the_overrides_covering_a_character` — overlapping runs merge in order; outside them the style is empty.
- `panels::graphics::tests::controls_read_the_selected_characters_style` — a text layer with "Drive" styled red/120/bold: with that selection the controls report the red, 120 and bold; a non-overridden property and `position` still report the layer's; with "Night" or no selection selected, the layer's fill and size. title: codecs: the pixel-format label comes from the SPS before the avcC/hvcC fields
author: wstock
body:
Addresses the one unfiled row of the corpus report #1959: *"4:0:0" shown for two 4:2:0 files* (pixel format label check, 70/92). No separate issue was opened for it.

## Cause
`pixfmt_label` in `crates/codecs/src/mp4.rs` trusted the container record first: for H.264, `avc_format` read `chroma_format` / `bit_depth_luma_minus8` from the `avcC` High-profile extension whenever its reserved bits were set, and only fell back to the SPS without one; for HEVC it used the `hvcC` record's own `chroma_format_idc` / `bit_depth_luma` fields and never looked at the SPS it carries. Both records are written by the muxer and can say `chroma_format` 0 (a `0xFC 0xF8 0xF8` extension, or an hvcC with the fields left at 0) for a stream whose SPS — the thing the decoder actually decodes, and decodes fine — says 4:2:0. That file then reads "YUV 4:0:0 8-bit" in Media File Properties.

## Change
- H.264: the first SPS is parsed first; the `avcC` extension is only consulted when no SPS parses (an unreadable SPS and no extension still gives "", not a guess).
- HEVC: new `hevc_format` parses the first SPS from the record's NAL arrays (the same call `hw.rs` already makes); the record's fields remain the fallback.

Existing labels don't move: every case in `avc_pixel_format_comes_from_avcc_not_the_profile` and `hevc_pixel_format_comes_from_hvcc` is unchanged, because there the record and the SPS agree (or there is no SPS).

## Tests
- `avc_pixel_format_comes_from_avcc_not_the_profile`: an avcC extension claiming 4:0:0 with a 4:2:0 SPS labels "YUV 4:2:0 8-bit" (the #1959 case); the same extension without a readable SPS still labels 4:0:0.
- New `hevc_pixel_format_prefers_the_sps_over_the_hvcc_fields`, with a small synthetic HEVC Main SPS writer (H.265 §7.3.2.2): hvcC fields at 0 + SPS 4:2:0 8-bit → "YUV 4:2:0 8-bit"; fields saying 4:2:0 8-bit + SPS 4:2:2 10-bit → the SPS; 4:4:4 12-bit; and a record without an SPS still reports its fields.

body:
Fixes #2020.

AAF/OMF import extracts embedded WAVs to predictable names. If one already existed, the native host's atomic write could replace its bytes; the browser host could replace an occupied virtual-file entry. Extraction now requests exclusive creation and tries numbered names when a destination is occupied, then updates the imported media reference to the path actually written. The native host stages and syncs a complete WAV in the destination directory and publishes it without replacing an existing file or symlink. The browser's in-memory file table checks and inserts in one synchronous borrow; OPFS extraction returns an unsupported error because it cannot provide this exclusive-create contract. Other `Services` hosts must implement the new method to support extraction; its default fails closed.

Synthetic AAF and OMF import regressions preserve pre-existing bytes, exercise a symlink and multiple collisions on Unix, and verify references use the extracted file. A browser-host test for occupied virtual entries compiled for WASM but was not run in a browser; format-level tests cover failed partial staging writes. On macOS 27.0 arm64 with Rust 1.97.1, the isolated patched-base `cargo xtask ci` run passed 3,498 tests, zero failed and 45 ignored, plus formatting, release Clippy, layers, assets, and 49-crate WASM compilation. Browser runtime and Windows/Linux behavior were not exercised. The native `filmcraft-format` crate adds permissively licensed `tempfile` (already present transitively); no assets are added.

The filename search is bounded to 1,000 candidates. A later extraction failure can leave earlier newly created WAVs unreferenced, though existing files remain unchanged. Browser virtual entries are not persisted across reload. Directory metadata sync is best effort. On filesystems using the dependency's hard-link fallback, an unlink failure may leave a temporary staging alias after publication; without no-replace rename or hard links, extraction fails cl…

title: fix(effect-controls): a dropped graph keyframe stays where it was dropped
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1918. Part of #1921 (the keyframes there are Linear, so the curve stays straight until Bezier is picked from the right-click menu; see below).

The drag itself works: releasing a graph keyframe does write the new value (the parameter row shows it). What made it look broken is that `graph_rows` fits the value range to the keyframes again on the next frame. With two keyframes, one of them is always the minimum and the other the maximum, so the keyframe you dragged is drawn straight back on the bottom (or top) edge and the curve keeps the same shape; only the range labels change. That is the "snaps back" in #1918 and the "graph is fixed" in #1921.

The fix keeps the graph's range while it stays open: it can widen when a value goes past it, but it no longer shrinks under the pointer, so a dropped keyframe stays where it was dropped. Closing the graph, collapsing the effect or switching clips starts it fitted again. Happy to switch to another rule if you prefer (for example a range taken from the parameter's soft min/max).

Two related things this doesn't change: on Linear keyframes the graph has no influence handles, so the curve stays straight until the keyframe is set to Bezier from the right-click menu (#962), which is the situation in #1921's screenshot; and the handles only move sideways, since the keyframe model has influence but no tangent value, so dragging them up or down isn't possible yet.

Validation:
- `graph_drag_tests::a_dropped_graph_keyframe_stays_where_it_was_dropped`: fails on main (`dropped at [460.0 76.1], drawn at [460.0 96.1]`), passes here
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui --lib graph_drag_tests`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: fix(shortcuts): Nest… can be bound to a key
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2024.

The Keyboard Shortcuts editor lists only the commands that need no required parameter, and `clip.nest` declared `name` as required. It never was: `nest()` already falls back to the next unused "Nested Sequence NN", and the UI opens the name dialog whenever the command runs without parameters, so a key does exactly what the clip menu's Nest… does. This marks `name` optional, so Nest… shows up in the editor and can be bound. It gets no default key in FilmCraft Default or Premiere Pro Compatible, as in Premiere; the Final Cut Pro preset already mapped it to ⌥G (New Compound Clip), which now also shows in the editor.

Validation:
- `shortcuts_tests::nest_is_bindable_without_a_default_key`: fails on main (Nest… is not in the editor's command list), passes here
- `sequence_tabs_ui::nest_can_be_assigned_a_key_that_asks_for_the_name`: searches "Nest" in the editor, records a key, presses it with a clip selected, gets the name dialog and nests on OK; fails on main (no `shortcuts.row.clip.nest`), passes here

title: fix(mcp): retain request ownership after stdio failures
author: jahvari
body:
## Summary

Keep admitted MCP requests and started blocking work owned through stdio failure and shutdown. Reject new requests during shutdown and retain export files when ownership or completion cannot be confirmed.

- Report stdin I/O/invalid UTF-8 errors instead of treating them as EOF.
- Preserve output, service and cleanup diagnostics together without requiring a logger; keep single-error variants.
- Include the engine failure reason when observing a failed cancelled export, while retaining uncertain output.
- Keep the existing bounded stdin bridge, two-second output join, 60-second cancellation and 65-second request drain policies.

See the [lifecycle design note](https://github.com/jahvari/filmcraft/blob/a62b82f621a13c7f246bbdf5a6ea1acacb6f539a/docs/mcp-request-lifecycle.md) for ownership, deadlines and limitations. The focused diff preserves original authorship, excludes the duplicate formatter prerequisite, and introduces no Media V1 dependency.

## Verification

Exact head: `a62b82f621a13c7f246bbdf5a6ea1acacb6f539a`; committed tree `cb3fbbce86f71233130a44e9889595121c825a63` exactly matches the tested candidate.

- Six new runtime failure regressions were reproduced before the fix; all **76 automation tests** now pass.
- Both real Windows CLI stdio process tests passed, including output failure while input stays open.
- Formatting, strict release all-target automation/CLI Clippy and the 49-crate WASM gate passed on Windows Rust 1.99.1 using a private target.
- Full GitHub CI passed on this exact head; previous-head results remain historical. Current CodeRabbit feedback is tracked separately.

## Limits

Timeouts cannot stop arbitrary native work. A blocked OS stdin read can outlive its input runtime until EOF/process exit. Dropping the entire service future does not promise orderly awaited drain. Uncertain output ownership always causes retention. Maintainer architecture review of the lifecycle note remains requested.

title: Import: EDL / FCP7 XML / FCPXML / OTIO / AAF / OMF land in the Project panel's current bin (#2036)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #2036

## What was wrong

`file.import` resolves the `bin` param (the UI sends the Project panel's current bin) and uses it for media files and image sequences, but interchange documents go through `crate::interchange::import`, which had no bin parameter and merged with `merge_into(proj, fragment, None)`. Their bins, media and sequences always landed at the project root.

## The fix

- `interchange::import` takes `bin: Option<BinId>` and hands it to `merge_into`, which already falls back to the root for a bin that doesn't exist (any bins the document brings come along inside the target bin).
- `file.import` passes its `bin`.
- `file.importAaf` gets an optional `bin` param (`{"path":str,"bin":binId?}`), so agents can aim it the same way; without it nothing changes.

Thanks to @Sixelax for the report with the cause and the patch direction.

## Tests

New `crates/engine/src/interchange_bin_tests.rs`:
- an FCP7 XML and an EDL imported into a nested bin ("Avis" ▸ "Kordex", as in the report) put every new item (sequence and media) in that bin, and undo takes it all back out;
- an AAF exported from a session lands in the bin through `file.import` and through `file.importAaf`;
- a bin id that doesn't exist imports at the root (guard for the fallback).

The first two fail on `main` (items at the root / in the document's own bin at the root) and pass with the fix.

Local (Linux, Gentoo), on top of main 8309f21a: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine` (642 passed, 3 ignored), `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets`. Not run locally: `cargo xtask wasm` (no wasm32 std in this toolchain; only `crates/engine`, an L5 crate, changes) and the full workspace sweep, left to CI.

title: render: box blur runs its column passes in cache-sized strips instead of transposing — same bits, 1.3–3.3× faster
author: aloysiocg
body:
The CPU box blur (`box_blur`: Gaussian Blur, Unsharp Mask, Sharpen, Lumetri's Sharpen, the glows, the blur transitions) ran its vertical passes as row passes over a transposed copy of the picture: two strided copies of every pixel into fresh full-size images, and a separate sweep of the whole picture per radius. At the radii Lumetri's Sharpen uses in an export at ½ render scale (σ 0.6: radii 0, 0, 1) the transposes cost more than the passes.

## What changes

- A row's passes run back to back while the row is in cache: one sweep for all radii instead of one per radius.
- The columns are cut into strips of about 256 KiB of floats. A strip is gathered once, all its passes run on it, and the last pass writes straight back into the picture's rows. The rows are split into disjoint slices per band of strips (`split_at_mut`), so the bands run in parallel without `unsafe`.
- The unsharp mask's first row pass reads the picture itself instead of a copy of it.
- Every pixel goes through the same floating-point operations in the same order, so the result is the **same bits**.

## Measured

`cargo test --release -p filmcraft-render --lib perf_box_blur -- --ignored --nocapture`, Apple M4 (10 cores), best of 7, ms:

| picture | σ | box blur | unsharp mask |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1920×1080 | 0.6 (Lumetri Sharpen at ½ scale) | 8.9 → **3.5** | 11.0 → **4.9** |
| 1920×1080 | 10 | 11.4 → **8.0** | 13.7 → **9.2** |
| 3840×2160 | 0.6 | 52.3 → **16.0** | 59.4 → **22.3** |
| 3840×2160 | 40 | 66.7 → **30.9** | 75.8 → **39.3** |

(all eight rows in `docs/performance.md`)

A real export: a two-camera 4K course lesson exported by the CLI to 1920×1080 ProRes 422 on Linux (i5-13400F, 16 threads, CPU compositor), with Lumetri (Sharpen 8) on both cameras and on a masked picture-in-picture. 60 s of it (1,800 frames), the CLI built at 0.8.0 and at this branch on 0.8.0, three rounds in alternating order, nothing else running:

| build | wall time (s) | frames/s | CPU ms per frame |
|---|---|---|---|

title: codecs: an ipcm/fpcm entry declaring zero bits decodes to silence
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`decode_pcm` guards `channels` with `.max(1)` but takes `bits` straight from the file (`crates/codecs/src/audio.rs:730`): `0usize.div_ceil(8)` is `0`, so `bps * ch == 0` and `data.len() / 0` panics the audio worker. `PcmConfig.bits` is attacker-controlled for `ipcm`/`fpcm`: `a.sample_size` is applied unchecked (`crates/isobmff/src/codec.rs:996`) as is the `pcmC` bits byte — while the sibling `sowt`/`twos`/`raw` arms of `qt_pcm` (`codec.rs:1084`) explicitly default 0 to 16/8, and MXF's own `decode_pcm` (`crates/mxf/src/essence.rs:218`) rejects `bps == 0` with an error. This arm just never got the guard. Trigger: open a crafted MP4/MOV whose audio sample entry is `ipcm`/`fpcm` with `sample_size == 0`, then play/scrub/export → the audio worker panics (sink at `crates/codecs/src/mp4.rs:380`, same in `mkv.rs`/`avi.rs`).

**Fix:** early-return empty channels when `cfg.bits == 0` — there are no samples to decode, and downstream resamplers already treat empty packets as silence. Fixed at the shared choke point, so all three container callers are covered.

**Regression test:** `zero_bits_decode_to_empty_channels_without_panicking` — on main it panics with *divide by zero* at `crates/codecs/src/audio.rs:733`; with the guard it decodes to empty channels. Full `filmcraft-codecs` lib suite green (125 passed).

title: interchange: a self-referential FCPXML media reference warns instead of overflowing
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`Imp::media` fills its `media_items` memo only *after* the nested `sequence()` returns (`crates/interchange/src/fcpxml.rs:278`), and the `reserve_sequence` inside `sequence()` is not visible to this lookup — so the old "Reserve first so recursion terminates" comment doesn't hold for this path. A 20-line `.fcpxml` whose `<media id="b">` sequence spine contains `<ref-clip ref="b">` loops `media → sequence → storyline → element ("ref-clip") → media` and overflows the stack on import.

Every peer in the repo guards this: the FCP7 importer inserts into `seq_items` before recursing and keeps an `in_progress` set (`fcp7.rs:307`, warns "recursive nested sequence ignored"), OTIO export has `stack.contains(&base)` (`otio.rs:268`), the FCPXML *exporter* guards cycles with a `building` set (`fcpxml.rs:968`) — only the import side was missing it.

**Fix:** a `media_progress: HashSet<String>` mirroring FCP7's `in_progress` — a re-entry warns `recursive <media> id="…" ignored` and returns `None`; the id is removed when expansion completes.

**Regression test:** `recursive_media_reference_is_a_warning_not_a_stack_overflow` — on main the test aborts with a fatal stack overflow; with the guard the import succeeds with the warning in the report and the project still has items. Full `filmcraft-interchange` lib suite green (22 passed).

title: captions: TTML nesting depth is capped instead of recursing per level
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`walk` (`crates/captions/src/ttml.rs:559`) and `collect` (`:437`) take no depth parameter: `<div>`/`<span>` nesting in a `.ttml`/`.dfxp` caption file is attacker-controlled depth, and the `collect` catch-all descends into *any* element — so the walkers recurse once per level with no bound (at sufficient depth the recursion overflows the stack; measured at 1000 levels on main, the document is simply walked in full and cues are emitted with no complaint).

Every other nestable-document walker in the repo is capped: AAF/OMF at depth 32 (`aaf/read.rs:252`, `omf/read.rs:209`), `aaf/store.rs` MAX_DEPTH 200, comp/essence MAX_NESTING 16, render MAX_NEST_DEPTH 8. `roxmltree`'s own parse is iterative, so the crash/behavior lands in our walker.

**Fix:** thread `depth: usize` through both walkers with `MAX_DEPTH = 32` (the AAF/OMF bound) — `walk` warns ("deeply nested … ignored") and skips the subtree; `collect` stops descending, keeping the text collected so far.

**Regression test:** `hostile_nesting_depth_is_capped_not_a_stack_overflow` — on main a 1000-deep `<div>` document produces cues and no warning (assertion fails); under the cap both the `<div>` and `<span>` shapes import empty with the "deeply nested" warning. Full `filmcraft-captions` lib suite green (43 passed).

title: project: a moved auto point counts as modified
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`param_eq_default`'s `Vec2` arm ignores `v` entirely (`crates/project/src/lib.rs:693`): whenever the *default* is the NaN "auto" point — motion `position`/`anchor` default to `(NaN, NaN)` (`effect.rs:270`) — **any** value compares equal to the default. So `has_modified_intrinsics()` (`lib.rs:682`) never fires for a moved clip, and three consumers misbehave: the timeline fx/modified badge (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs:948`), the render fast-path check (`crates/render/src/preview.rs:520`), and multicam `take_intrinsics` (`crates/edit/src/multicam.rs:183`) all treat a moved clip as untouched. The arm exists because NaN ≠ NaN would otherwise flag everything as modified — it overcorrects. Inconsistency proof: the interchange twin `param_modified` (`crates/interchange/src/common.rs:607`) uses the correct rule (modified unless *both* components are NaN), so import/export and the project model disagree.

**Fix:** the arm returns `vv.x.is_nan() && vv.y.is_nan()` — an auto default only equals a value that is itself still auto — mirroring `param_modified`.

**Regression test:** `auto_point_default_only_matches_unset_points` — on main a moved `(960, 540)` point equals the NaN default (assertion fails); under the rule only a still-NaN point does, and ordinary parameters are unaffected. Full `filmcraft-project` lib suite green (66 passed).

title: captions: a cue-text arrow survives the VTT write/parse round trip
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The VTT writer escapes a cue-text `-->` as `-->` (`crates/captions/src/vtt.rs:140` — a bare arrow would parse as a timing line elsewhere), but the parser joins cue payload lines verbatim (`:104`) and never decodes it — the pre-existing test even pins that `&` stays literal, proving no entity decoding happens. So any caption containing `A --> B` exports and re-imports as `A --> B`: permanent text corruption on every VTT sidecar/export round trip (`engine/src/export_tools.rs:446` included). The existing round-trip test passes only because no sample cue contains an arrow.

title: fix(codecs): don't divide by zero in decode_pcm when ipcm/fpcm bits=0 (#2064)
author: rollroyces
body:
Closes #2064.

**Cause.** `crates/codecs/src/audio.rs:730` computed `bps = cfg.bits.div_ceil(8)` and then `data.len() / (bps * ch)`. An `ipcm` / `fpcm` entry declaring `bits == 0` (which the spec allows) made `bps` 0 and panicked the audio worker.

The other arms in `crates/isobmff/src/codec.rs` (`sowt` / `twos` / `raw`) already default a 0 sample size to 16/8, and MXF's `decode_pcm` in `crates/mxf/src/essence.rs:217` rejects `bps == 0` outright. The isobmff path was the one that fell through.

**Fix.** Return an empty buffer of the right channel count when `bits == 0`, so the worker returns silence instead of crashing. The decode `match` already returned `0.0` for the `bits == 0` arm, so the per-sample value is unchanged.

**Tests.** `decode_pcm_tests::bits_zero_does_not_divide_by_zero` exercises the new guard (`bits=0, channels=2` → 2 empty channels). `decode_pcm_tests::sixteen_bit_little_endian_mono_decodes` is a sanity check that normal 16-bit LE mono still decodes to ±1.0 at full scale.

**Build.** `cargo test -p filmcraft-codecs` → 126 passed, 0 failed (plus the dependents' suites).

title: fix(macOS): show file dialogs as sheets instead of a nested modal run loop (#2018)
author: vark-debug
body:
Closes #2018.

## Root cause

On macOS, the synchronous `rfd::FileDialog::pick_file` runs the `NSOpenPanel` with `run_modal` — a nested, blocking run loop — inside the winit event-handling scope (Lumetri ▸ Input LUT ▸ Browse… → `show_lut_dialog` → `FileDialog::run_now`).

While that modal loop is running, a Finder drag onto the open panel queues a winit event. winit's `maybe_queue_event` sees that an event is currently being handled and posts the deferred `handle_event` call as a block on the common modes of the host `CFRunLoop`. The nested modal loop executes those blocks, so `ApplicationDelegate::handle_event` re-enters while the outer `handle_event` still holds the `RefCell` borrow — the re-entrancy guard panics. Because the deferred block was scheduled by winit as `panic_cannot_unwind`, the panic is not catchable by the UI's `catch_unwind` guard and the process aborts (SIGABRT).

This matches the reporter's observation (crash log shows the panic in the re-entrancy guard; the `.ips` shows SIGABRT), and why it depends on the macOS version: on some builds the modal run loop executes common-mode blocks (drag-and-drop events arriving during the dialog), on others it does not.

## Fix

macOS now implements the `HostHooks::run_dialog` channel (#260, already used on Linux via the XDG portal): `apps/filmcraft/src/main.rs` registers a `run_dialog_sheet` hook that

- creates the `rfd::AsyncFileDialog` future on the main thread (AppKit requirement) and begins the panel with a completion handler — the frame loop keeps running while the dialog is open, so there is no nested run loop and no re-entrancy;
- awaits the future on a worker thread under `catch_unwind` and sends the resulting paths back through the existing `mpsc` answer channel, where `poll_native_dialog` delivers them to the pending dialog continuation each frame, exactly as on Linux.

`prepare_dialog` and `project_patterns` (project-file extension filters) move from `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]` to `#[cfg(any(targ…

title: HEVC: select the x86-v3 inverse transform at runtime, retaining the baseline path
author: fanthomas-creator
body:
Refs #1039. Draft for discussion of a small, localized software-decoder optimization.

The inverse transform currently uses the baseline target even when a compatible x64 CPU could compile the same integer kernel with x86-v3 features. This change caches Pulp's safe CPU/OS feature token once, then selects the appropriate compiled kernel in the same executable. Older x64 processors and other architectures retain the baseline implementation. There is no launcher, global target-CPU flag, new frame buffer or second source implementation.

`pulp` 0.22.3 is MIT-licensed and already present transitively in the workspace lockfile. The change adds a direct x64-only dependency with `std` and `x86-v3`. The existing matrix regression test now compares automatic dispatch and forced baseline against the independent specification formula over 6,000 cases, including 8/10/12-bit shifts. An ignored decode benchmark records every sample and output checksums, with validation and hashing outside the clock.

### Evidence and tradeoff

On a Windows x64 i5-10400F, four paired AB/BA rounds (12 decodes per variant and fixture) gave median decode-time reductions of 1.2% for 1080p Main and 1.8% for 4K Main 10. Output checksums matched. The performance-test executable grew by 35,332 bytes; this is not a full-app size measurement. Both compiled kernels remain in the executable, and the OS manages code-page residency. The cache measured 8 bytes on this target; this is not total application RAM.

On a physical Sandy Bridge i5-2400S with 4 GiB RAM and Linux Mint 22.3, runtime detection correctly selected the baseline path. All 34 required compatibility steps passed: 29 HEVC unit tests, 24 exact pixel-hash comparisons across 12 fixtures at one and four decoder threads, GUI import/playback, rendering, H.264 export/redecode, and project save/reopen. All 529 package files passed integrity checks. [Physical-machine report and diagnostic records](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/issues/1039#issuecom…

title: Reject .3dl LUTs whose input mesh is larger than 256 entries
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/lut.rs:371` (no existing issue): color: a .3dl LUT with a huge input mesh overflows `n*n*n`; release builds accept an empty cube and panic when it is applied.

## Cause
`Lut::parse_3dl` took the cube size `n` from the number of values on the mesh line with no upper bound. `n * n * n` then overflowed. In debug builds parsing panicked. In release builds the product wrapped to 0, so an empty cube was accepted and the first `apply()` panicked with an index out of bounds.

## Fix
`parse_3dl` now rejects mesh lengths outside 2..=256, the same range `.cube` allows for LUT_3D_SIZE. With that cap `n³` always fits, so the row-count check and the data allocation cannot overflow. The regression test covers a 2^22-entry mesh and a 257-entry mesh.

## Verified
- Regression test `huge_3dl_mesh_is_rejected`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-color --lib huge_3dl_mesh_is_rejected`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `dev_icon::tests::desktop_file_matches_the_packaged_fields`, which also fails on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
The `.cube` parser and `Lut3d` indexing are unchanged.

title: Add native NTSC DV25 decoding for MOV imports
author: andymenard
body:
NTSC DV camera MOV files currently import without a usable native video decoder. This adds a dependency-free, pure-Rust decoder so FilmCraft can play and seek the original files directly, alongside its existing PCM audio support.

The new `filmcraft-dv` L0 crate implements 525/60 DV25/DVCPRO25 4:1:1 decoding from SMPTE 314M-2005 (stabilized 2013): DIF indexing, three-pass AC bit allocation, VLC/escape decoding, inverse quantization, 8×8 and 2-4-8 IDCT, and macroblock unshuffling. The MOV demuxer recognizes `dvc ` and the video registry routes it to the decoder. Native 4:1:1 chroma is replicated into the compositor's existing 4:2:2 representation. No runtime FFmpeg dependency or media conversion is introduced.

MOV integration currently covers the `dvc ` sample entry and 720×480 NTSC DV25. PAL DV, DV50/DVCPRO50, DVCPRO HD, raw DV audio demultiplexing, AVI DV and DV encoding remain unsupported. The crate README records the specification edition and the interpretation of four abbreviated printed VLC words.

Tests generate fixtures locally through `filmcraft-testkit` (`FILMCRAFT_REQUIRE_ORACLES=1` makes a missing ffmpeg a failure); no private media or binary fixtures are included:

- Eight patterns compared against an external FFmpeg oracle (maximum sample error ≤3, mean squared error <0.5, over the whole picture and over the clipped rightmost chroma columns), cached in `target/fixtures/dv/` (`cargo xtask fixtures dv`). They cover the 8×8 and 2-4-8 DCT: the interlaced pattern is encoded with `+ildct`, and two patterns have every chroma block switched to 2-4-8, since FFmpeg's encoder never codes chroma that way.
- DIF/header/VLC bit mutations and truncated packets checked for panics.
- Macroblock layout coverage.
- MOV import with big-endian stereo PCM: random and sequential seeks compared against FFmpeg's frames, 4:1:1 chroma replicated into 4:2:2, PCM sample-exact.

Real camera footage (not committed): a 285-frame NTSC DV25 QuickTime clip decodes within maximum sample …

title: #776: Corner Pin gets corner handles on the Program monitor
author: ruck-syu
body:
Refs #776.

Corner Pin's four points could only be set by typing numbers in Effect Controls: with the effect selected, the Program monitor showed nothing to grab. Now, while Corner Pin is the selected effect of a selected clip under the playhead, the monitor draws the outline through its four corners with a handle on each:

- dragging a handle moves that corner (`effects.setParam` on `upper_left` / `upper_right` / `lower_right` / `lower_left`), with a resize cursor pointing the way the corner faces;
- dragging inside the outline moves all four corners together (move cursor), so the pinned picture can be repositioned without leaving the monitor;
- each drag is one undo step (`merge`), and "auto" (unset) points start on the clip's corners where the render puts them.

The corners are mapped to the screen the way the render applies them: Corner Pin warps the clip's own pixels, then Motion places the result (`motion_matrix` after the clip-pixel → frame mapping), so the handles stay on the warped corners when the clip is scaled, moved or rotated. Handles that would fall off the monitor are kept in reach like the transform box's. New automation ids: `program.cornerPin.box`, `program.cornerPin.handle.0`–`3` (Upper Left, Upper Right, Lower Right, Lower Left).

`selected_placement` is split so Motion/Transform and Corner Pin share `selected_effect`; `within` is made generic over the number of points. No change to the transform box.

**Not in this PR:** the render crops the warped picture to the clip's own frame, so pulling a corner outward past the clip's edge clips the picture there. Letting Corner Pin stretch past its source bounds is a renderer change I'd rather send separately.

## Testing

- New `corner_pin_handles_move_its_corners` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/transform_handles_ui.rs` (fails on main: no `program.cornerPin.handle.0`): handles appear only while Corner Pin is selected and start on the picture's corners; dragging handle 0 moves only `upper_left` and the handle …

title: Write the output bit depth in exported .3dl files
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/lut.rs:410 (to_3dl) and :379 (parse_3dl)` (no existing issue): A dark LUT exported to .3dl is read back about 4x too bright, because the file doesn't say its output bit depth.

## Cause
`Lut::to_3dl` always writes 12-bit output values but wrote no `Mesh <in> <out>` header. `parse_3dl` then guessed the output depth from the largest value in the file. For a dark LUT (peak ≤ 1023) it guessed 10-bit or 8-bit, so the outputs were read back about 4x too bright.

## Fix
`to_3dl` now writes `Mesh 10 12` before the input mesh line. The parser already reads this header, so the output depth is stated and no longer guessed. The existing 3dl test now expects the header on the second line (index 1) and the mesh line on the third line (index 2).

## Verified
- Regression test `dark_lut_3dl_roundtrip_keeps_output_depth`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-color --lib dark_lut_3dl`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The `bit_max(peak)` fallback in `parse_3dl` is unchanged. It is still used for third-party `.3dl` files that have no `Mesh` header.

title: feat(media): import PSD files as their flattened composite (Merge All Layers)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
PSD files now import as stills (and as image sequences): the clip is the document's flattened composite.

When you import a layered PSD, Premiere asks how to bring it in, and "Merge All Layers" gives a single still of the whole document. This PR does that part only, with no dialog: it reads the composite image Photoshop stores at the end of every PSD (the image data section, after the colour mode data, image resources and layer section, which are skipped by their lengths), following Adobe's public Photoshop File Formats Specification. Grayscale and RGB at 8 or 16 bits per channel, uncompressed or PackBits; 16-bit is kept at 8, as DPX does today. The first extra channel becomes the clip's alpha only when the layer count is negative, which is how the spec marks the composite's transparency; otherwise extra channels are saved selections and are ignored. A file saved with "Maximize Compatibility" off (the version info resource says the image data is not the real composite) is refused with a message saying to resave it with that option on. PSB, bitmap, indexed, CMYK, multichannel, duotone, Lab, 32-bit and ZIP-compressed documents get a clear "not supported" error, and size limits and truncation are checked like the other still decoders. Left out for later PRs: the import dialog with Merged Layers / Individual Layers / Sequence, which need a real layer reader and compositor. Happy to keep 16-bit as float instead of 8-bit if you prefer.

Unblending from white: Photoshop stores a transparent composite blended over white, so the colour is unblended back to straight alpha, at the file's depth before the reduction to 8. This is not in Adobe's specification. It came from a reviewer pointing to what psd-tools (`_remove_white_background` in `api/pil_io.py`) and ImageMagick (`CorrectPSDAlphaBlend` in `coders/psd.c`, on by default, `psd:alpha-unblend`) do; the 4-byte padding of the global tagged blocks came from the same review and psd-tools.
