title: export: GPU-rendered SDR exports read back the finished sRGB RGBA8 frame (1.6× faster NVENC export)
author: MasakatsuFunaki
body:
With **GPU Rendering** on, opaque SDR exports read back the finished 8-bit sRGB `RGBA8` frame directly from the GPU instead of reading back 16-bit half-floats and converting `f16 → f32 → 12-bit sRGB lookup table` on the CPU.

## Output Accuracy

- **When `GPU Rendering` is `Off`:** **100% byte-identical.**
- **When `GPU Rendering` is `On` (opaque SDR exports):**
  - **Old GPU export path:** Read back `Rgba16Float` to the CPU and approximated linear-to-sRGB through a **12-bit (4096-entry) lookup table**. Because 4096 buckets are too coarse for steep parts of the sRGB curve, that CPU lookup table rounds the wrong way by `1` code on ~0.8%–3.3% of channels.
  - **This PR's GPU RGBA8 path:** Evaluates the continuous sRGB transfer function in the shader and rounds directly to the nearest 8-bit integer.
  - **EVERY SINGLE PIXEL IS THE SAME OR MORE ACCURATE THAN THE OLD METHOD: ACROSS ALL 691,200 CHANNELS PER FRAME (VERIFIED ON RTX 5070), THIS GPU PATH HAS 0 MISSES AGAINST THE EXACT `f64` SRGB FORMULA, WHEREAS THE OLD CPU LOOKUP TABLE WAS OFF BY 1 CODE ON ~6,000–22,000 CHANNELS PER FRAME.**

## Benchmark (1080p23.976 HEVC NVENC, 3138 frames, RTX 5070 Laptop / i7-13650HX)

| Build | GPU Rendering | Export Time | Worker CPU Time | NVENC Busy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | On | 17.6 s | 99.6 s | 38–40 % |
| **This PR** | **On** | **11.1 s (1.6× faster)** | **12.2 s (8× less CPU)** | **60–62 %** |
| `main` | Off | 15.2 s | 172.6 s | — |
| This PR | Off | 15.2 s | 174.5 s | — |

title: Ignore unusable M2 speeds in EDL import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/interchange/src/edl.rs:373 (parse at :201-206, applied in Ctx::lay)` (no existing issue): EDL import: an `M2` motion line with a non-finite or tiny speed gives the clip a NaN, infinite or zero speed.

## Cause
The EDL parser reads the `M2` speed with `f64::parse`, which accepts `nan`, `inf` and `1e300`. `Ctx::lay` turned that value into the clip speed with no check. The clip then got a NaN, infinite, huge or (after rounding) zero speed, which froze it or blew up its source range.

## Fix
`import_event` now checks each `M2` speed before the clips are laid. A speed must be 0 (a freeze) or finite, and its ratio to the timecode base must lie between 0.0001 and 1000. A speed that fails this check is dropped with a warning in the import report, and the clip keeps speed 1.0.

## Verified
- Regression test `hostile_m2_speeds_keep_normal_speed`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-interchange --lib hostile_m2_speeds_keep_normal_speed`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The `fps == 0.0` freeze-frame path and the parsing of `M2` lines are unchanged. `Ctx::lay` is unchanged, because it only receives speeds that have already been checked. EDL export and the editing layer's speed checks are unchanged.

title: #2020: AAF / OMF import never replaces a file already at an embedded audio's path
author: 00xJS
body:
Addresses the first problem in #2020: importing an AAF or OMF with embedded audio extracted the WAVs next to the document with names unique within the document only, and `Services::write_file` (an atomic rename) replaced whatever was already at that path. Re-importing, or importing a document whose embedded names collide with existing media, destroyed local files without a prompt, and undoing the import could not bring them back.

Extraction now never replaces a file. Before writing, the importer checks the path: a file holding the same bytes (a re-import) is reused as it is, so repeated imports neither rewrite nor duplicate anything; a different file there is left untouched, the audio is written beside it under the first free `name (2).wav`, `name (3).wav`, …, the imported item points at that file, and the import report says so. The check goes through `Services` (`file_size`, `read_file`), so the browser host's virtual files are covered the same way.

Out of scope here, from the same report: the project being cleared before a failed import's error (the `replace: true` and misdetected-document cases), which is a separate change in `file.import`.

title: #1947: the counting leader's beep lasts one frame of its own rate, not a fixed 1/24 s
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes #1947. The Universal Counting Leader's beep at each second mark was gated on a fixed 1/24 s, whatever frame rate the leader was made at, so at 60 fps the first beep ran 2000 samples (48 kHz) instead of one frame's 800, through the second and third frames.

`GeneratorSource::audio` now passes the source's own frame length (from its video stream's frame rate; 1/24 s when there is none) to the sample generator, and the beep lasts exactly that: 800 samples at 60 fps, 2000 at 24, 1920 at 25, 1602 at 29.97. The other generators (Bars and Tone, Tone, the demo scenes) are unchanged.

Test: `counting_leader_beep_lasts_one_frame_of_its_rate` in `crates/media/src/generators.rs` checks, for 60, 24, 25 and 29.97 fps leaders at 48 kHz, that the first beep ends at the frame's last sample, that the rest of the second is silent, and the same for the second beep. The 60 fps case fails before the fix with the beep ending at sample 1999, as the report measured.

Gates run locally on Windows 11 (x86_64, Rust 1.99): `cargo fmt --check -p filmcraft-media`, `cargo test --release -p filmcraft-media generators`.

title: #1903: timeline.move refuses a clip listed twice (it left one clip id on two tracks)
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes the move half of #1903. A `timeline.move` whose `moves` listed one clip twice (two destinations) applied both: the same `ClipId` ended up on both tracks, and nothing that addresses clips by identity could tell the two apart afterwards. The same happened with `insert: true`.

A move now takes one destination per clip: a repeated clip id is refused with an error naming it, before the transaction starts, so the project, the selection and the undo history are untouched and the caller can correct the request. `copy: true` still accepts a repeated source, since each copy gets its own id (linked partners were already added to the plan once).

Not in this change: the copy case the report also describes, where two copies of one source with different destinations both land on the new track and only one survives. That is a separate defect in destination allocation for copies.

Test: `move_refuses_a_clip_listed_twice` in `crates/engine/src/locked_clip_edits_tests.rs`: the duplicated move (overwrite and insert) errors, the project JSON and undo length are unchanged, every clip id is on exactly one track, and a copy with a repeated source yields two distinct new clips.

Gates run locally on Windows 11 (x86_64, Rust 1.99): `cargo fmt --check -p filmcraft-engine`, `cargo test --release -p filmcraft-engine locked_clip_edits`.

title: #1984: silence concealing an MP4 audio packet that will not decode is bounded (its duration is the file's)
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes #1984. When an MP4 audio packet failed to decode, `Mp4Source::audio_packet` concealed it as silence sized by the sample's `stts` duration, a number straight from the file. A corrupt AAC access unit declaring 1,000,000 samples allocated two 1,000,000-sample float vectors for a 128-frame request, and nothing bounded it, so a damaged file could run the audio worker out of memory during playback or export (AGENTS.md §0.4: every input-derived number is hostile; cap allocations sized by input).

The concealed silence is now bounded by `concealment_len(declared, sample_rate)`: the declared duration, but never more than one second at the stream's rate (itself clamped to 8 kHz–384 kHz against a hostile rate). No audio codec's packet is longer than that (AAC 1024/2048, Opus at most 5760, AC-3 1536, MP3 1152), so a well-formed packet is unaffected and a corrupt one costs at most a second of silence per channel. Packets that decode are unchanged.

Test: `concealed_silence_is_bounded_by_a_second` covers normal AAC and Opus packet sizes (unchanged), the report's 1,000,000-sample duration (bounded to 48,000), `u64::MAX`, and hostile sample rates of 0 and `u32::MAX`.

Gates run locally on Windows 11 (x86_64, Rust 1.99): `cargo fmt --check -p filmcraft-codecs`, `cargo clippy --release -p filmcraft-codecs -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --release -p filmcraft-codecs concealment`.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * When an audio packet fails to decode, playback now substitutes silence capped at one second. This prevents corrupted audio metadata from causing excessively long silent sections. The cap accounts for the audio sample rate and declared duration.

title: fix(macos): decode interlaced H.264 with VideoToolbox's software decoder (#1750)
author: ssandweiss
body:
Draft for #1750. It needs a maintainer's call before it's ready: the question in https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/issues/1750#issuecomment-6203010864 is whether VideoToolbox's software decoder is acceptable for this case.

### What was wrong

Interlaced H.264 (field pictures or MBAFF, as HyperDeck and many broadcast recorders write) imported but showed MEDIA UNREADABLE for every frame, on macOS too:

- our software decoder rejects it by design (`Sps::check_supported`: "interlaced (field / MBAFF) coding", as documented in `crates/h264/README.md`);
- `videotoolbox::layout` declined `info.interlaced` streams up front;
- removing that check alone fails at `VTDecompressionSessionCreate` with **-12911**. The session requires the hardware decoder, and the Apple-silicon media engine doesn't take interlaced H.264.

### Change

`crates/platform/src/videotoolbox.rs`, about 10 lines:

- **Interlaced streams:** the session sets `RequireHardwareAcceleratedVideoDecoder` to false. VideoToolbox then uses Apple's software H.264 decoder, which outputs woven frames.
- **Unchanged:** progressive streams still require hardware, and are declined to our own decoder when it can't decode them. The hybrid decoder's mid-stream fallback is unchanged. Turning hardware decoding Off in Settings still leaves interlaced streams unreadable.

### How close it is to ffmpeg: not bit-exact

`videotoolbox::interlaced_h264_is_close_to_ffmpeg` compares VideoToolbox's frames with ffmpeg's raw decode. It uses three x264 MBAFF fixtures (640×360, 50 frames each), cached under the fixtures dir like the other oracle fixtures:

| Fixture | Checks |
|---|---|
| top field first, P-frames only | frame count, presentation order, full woven size; **luma bit-exact**; every frame ≥ 35 dB PSNR (all planes); same after reset + reseek to the last sync sample |
| bottom field first, P-frames only | same |
| top field first, B-frames (x264 defaults: implicit weighted bi-prediction, B-pyramid) | count, order, size; every…

title: fix(gpu): FXC compiles the effect stage, so DX12 keeps GPU effects (#1616, #1425, #1458)
author: derektrimm
body:
Fixes the DX12 half of #1425 and #1458, and the CPU fallback of the Windows export instance in #1616.

## Problem

wgpu compiles DX12 shaders with FXC unless `dxcompiler.dll` is shipped, and FilmCraft's Windows builds don't ship it. FXC aborts on the `fx_px` entry point of `fx.wgsl`:

```
ERROR wgpu::backend::wgpu_core: Shader translation error for stage ShaderStages(COMPUTE): FXC D3DCompile error (Unspecified error (0x80004005)): internal error: compilation aborted unexpectedly
ERROR filmcraft_ui_egui: GPU error, switching to the CPU compositor: Validation Error
ERROR filmcraft_ui_egui: GPU compositor failed to initialise; compositing on the CPU
```

(0.8.0, `--graphics dx12`, Intel UHD Graphics 630.) So every device created through DX12 composites on the CPU: the export instance wherever wgpu's default adapter is a DX12 one (#1616, reported on an NVIDIA laptop; the AMD report there was corrected, and on an RX 6900 XT the export instance renders on the GPU on current main), and the DX12 fallback on Intel integrated graphics (#1425, #1458).

I translated every WGSL module with naga 30.0.1 using wgpu-hal's DX12 options (shader model 5.1, `restrict_indexing`, `force_loop_bounding`, `zero_initialize_workgroup_memory`) and ran each entry point through `D3DCompile` from `d3dcompiler_47.dll`. Only `fx_px` fails. Stubbing one `case` of `pixel()` at a time pins it on `OP_UNSHARP` alone: its loop writes `o[k]`, which naga emits as a write to a dynamically indexed component of a local `float4` inside a `while (true)` loop, and FXC cannot compile that. With that case removed `fx_px` compiles; with only that case kept it still fails.

## Fix

Unsharp Mask does the same per-channel arithmetic as vector math:

```wgsl
let d = o.rgb - bq.rgb;
let sharpened = max(o.rgb + d * amount, vec3(0.0));
return vec4(select(o.rgb, sharpened, abs(d) >= vec3(th * o.a)), o.a);
```

Each channel is independent and alpha is only read, so this is the loop's result, as in `effects::unsharp_boxes`. A…

title: Stop Lumetri Shadows from turning near-black pixels into blue specks
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2094

## Cause
The Lumetri Highlights/Shadows step multiplied every channel by `new luma / luma`. This gain has no upper limit as luma gets close to 0, so a nearly black pixel with a slight colour cast had that cast multiplied 10 to 100 times. At Shadows 8, sRGB [0,0,1] came out as about [0,0,100], a saturated blue speck.

## Fix
The per-channel gain is now capped at 4 (`LUMETRI_TONE_MAX_GAIN`), and any lift beyond that is added equally to all channels. Dark pixels still get brighter but keep their hue. The change is the same in all three copies of the formula: the CPU `lumetri`, the CPU reference in `gpufx.rs` and the GPU shader `fx.wgsl`.

## Verified
- Regression test `lumetri_shadows_do_not_saturate_near_black_pixels`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-render --lib lumetri_shadows_do_not_saturate_near_black_pixels`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Pixels with luma at or below 1e-5 (pure black) are still left unchanged, as before. The shape of the Shadows/Highlights curve is the same, and so are the other Lumetri controls.

title: Reject non-numeric --seconds and --scale in CLI render
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `apps/filmcraft-cli/src/main.rs:468` (no existing issue): CLI `render` silently renders frame 0 when `--seconds` (or `--scale`) is not a number.

## Cause
`render` parsed `--seconds` and `--scale` with `.and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(default)`. A value like `1s`, `1,5` or `abc` was silently replaced by 0 (or 1.0 for `--scale`). The command rendered the wrong frame and exited 0.

## Fix
Added a `finite_opt` helper that parses the option and calls `usage(..)` (exit 2, with a `filmcraft-cli:` message naming the option) if the value is not a number or is NaN/inf. The default applies only when the option is absent. `render` uses it for both `--seconds` and `--scale`.

## Verified
- Regression test `render_rejects_bad_numbers`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-cli --test cli render_rejects_bad_numbers`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `dev_icon::tests::desktop_file_matches_the_packaged_fields`, which also fails on `main` without this change (macOS); the remaining CI steps pass.

## Not changed
Range checks on negative or zero values and the other subcommands' option parsing are unchanged. Behavior for valid values is unchanged.

title: fix(export): tag SDR exports with a colr box (#2142)
author: ssandweiss
body:
Fixes #2142.

### What was wrong

`ColorSignal::apply_to` wrote the sample entry's `colr` box only for HDR, returning early for SDR. AVFoundation, which QuickTime Player and Final Cut Pro use, takes the colour of the MOV codecs only from `colr`, not from ProRes's or DNx's own header fields. So SDR ProRes, DNxHR and APV exports had no colour as far as Apple's apps are concerned, and they had to guess. H.264 and HEVC were fine because AVFoundation reads their VUI.

### Change

`apply_to` writes `colr` for SDR too, with the export's own `ColorSignal`. That's BT.709 1/1/1 by default, or whatever the sequence's colour pipeline signals. MOV gets `nclc` and MP4 gets `nclx` (limited range, as the encoders write). The `mdcv` / `clli` boxes stay PQ-only.

Not changed: **MJPEG**. Its YCbCr follows JFIF (BT.601, full range) rather than the export's matrix, so a BT.709 `colr` there would be wrong. It needs its own decision, so I left it untagged. PR #1827 tags its new uncompressed formats in its own code path and doesn't overlap.

### Verification

Each export's video track was read through AVFoundation (`CMFormatDescription` colour extensions), the same values QuickTime's Movie Inspector and Final Cut use. This is current `main` vs this branch, exporting 1 s of the demo with `filmcraft-cli`:

| Format | `main` (primaries / transfer / matrix) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| ProRes 422 HQ (MOV) | – / – / – | ITU_R_709_2 ×3 |
| DNxHR (MOV) | – / – / – | ITU_R_709_2 ×3 |
| APV (MOV) | – / – / – | ITU_R_709_2 ×3 |
| H.264 (MP4) | ITU_R_709_2 ×3 (from the VUI) | ITU_R_709_2 ×3 |
| HEVC (MP4, VideoToolbox) | ITU_R_709_2 ×3 (from the VUI) | unchanged |

### Tests

- `hdr_tests::sdr_gets_a_colr_box_and_no_hdr_metadata`: SDR gives `nclc` 1/1/1 for MOV and `nclx` 1/1/1 limited for MP4, with no `mdcv` / `clli`.
- `tests::sdr_exports_carry_a_colr_box`: real SDR ProRes, DNxHR, APV and H.264 exports are parsed back, each with the expected `colr` and no HDR metadata.
- Without the change, both tes…

author: sanyamsingh001
body:

Custom range parsing now uses the target sequence’s frame rate and drop-frame flag, separately from output FPS overrides. Six command-only `export.resolve` regressions on empty sequences cover frame indices, absolute timecodes, drop-frame interpretation, output-rate overrides, seconds and active-target controls. - Focused AFTER: **6 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored**. Test formatting changed between runs; the six inputs and assertions were preserved.

title: fix(macos): colour-match the window on wide-gamut displays (part of #2115)
author: ssandweiss
body:
The macOS part of #2115. Windows still needs an ICC-profile transform in FilmCraft itself, and that is not included here (see the issue).

### What was wrong

On a wide-gamut Mac display, which covers most MacBooks and Studio Displays (Display P3), FilmCraft's picture and UI were shown without colour matching, so BT.709 content looked oversaturated next to QuickTime Player, Final Cut or Premiere.

- The window's `CAMetalLayer` has no colour space. For the sRGB surface colour space, which is what egui-wgpu uses because it doesn't expose one, wgpu sets it to nil (`wgpu-hal` `metal/surface.rs`).
- A nil colour space means the layer's values go to the display as they are.
- FilmCraft's pixels are sRGB-encoded BT.709 (the GPU resolve applies the sRGB curve, and egui's colours are sRGB), so on P3 they were shown as if they were P3.

**Measured on a MacBook Pro (Liquid Retina XDR, Display P3), macOS 26.6.2.** A pure-red BT.709 clip (decoding to RGB 252/0/0) was shown in FilmCraft's Program monitor and in QuickTime Player side by side, and the screen captured with `screencapture`. These are display (Display P3) pixel values:

| | FilmCraft `main` | FilmCraft, this PR | QuickTime Player |
|---|---|---|---|
| Red clip | **253, 0, 0** (P3 full red, oversaturated) | **232, 51, 35** | **232, 51, 35** |
| UI greys (panels, header, timeline) | 1d1d1d / 666666 | unchanged | – |
| After resizing the window | – | 232, 51, 35 | – |

### What this does not change: tone

This PR matches QuickTime on **gamut only**. Tone (gamma) is unchanged from `main`, and it deliberately still differs from QuickTime. A lossless BT.709-tagged grey-step clip, shown the same way (display pixel values, R channel):

| | | | | | | | | |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Source code values | 48 | 75 | 99 | 125 | 151 | 176 | 202 | 226 |
| FilmCraft, `main` and this PR (≈ gamma 2.2) | 49 | 75 | 100 | 125 | 151 | 177 | 202 | 226 |

title: fix(import): import files a macOS drag only promised (Photos.app videos arrived as JPEGs)
author: scottyallen
body:
## The bug

Dragging a video out of Photos.app imported a **still image**. Photos offers the movie only as a *file promise*; the drag's one real path is a JPEG poster frame inside the Photos library, and winit asks the pasteboard for `NSFilenamesPboardType` alone, so that poster frame is what we imported. The drop looked successful, which is worse than failing: the still only gives itself away on the timeline.

The drag pasteboard from Photos.app, dumped with a test harness (macOS 26):

```
com.apple.pasteboard.promised-suggested-file-name = IMG_5691.MOV
com.apple.pasteboard.promised-file-content-type  = com.apple.quicktime-movie
public.file-url       = …/Photos Library.photoslibrary/resources/derivatives/D/<uuid>_1_102_o.jpeg
NSFilenamesPboardType = [ …/derivatives/D/<uuid>_1_102_o.jpeg ]
```

Rewriting the path to the original is not a fix: an iCloud asset has no local original at all (the library's `originals/` had no file for this UUID) until the promise is fulfilled and Photos downloads it.

## The fix

`crates/platform` gains `file_promise`, which takes over the two dragging-destination methods on winit's window delegate. A drop whose pasteboard carries promises is claimed there and fulfilled into the host's directory; **every other drop is forwarded to winit untouched**, as is a promise that cannot be asked for, so no drag is ever lost. It lives in `crates/platform` because that is the one crate allowed `unsafe`, same as `cursor` (AGENTS.md §0.3, ADR 0001): safe `bool`-returning API, `// SAFETY:` on every block, no-op on every other platform.

Two macOS details shape the implementation, both found the hard way:

1. The receivers may only be read in `performDragOperation:`. `readObjectsForClasses:[NSFilePromiseReceiver]` **claims** the promises, so reading them during the hover leaves the drop with none and it silently falls back to the poster frame. The hover asks `availableTypeFromArray:` instead.
2. `receivePromisedFilesAtDestination:options:operationQueue:…

title: fix(timeline): preview every track a Project drop fills (#1887)
author: ssandweiss
body:
Fixes #1887.

### What was wrong

Dragging a Project item over the Timeline drew one preview box, on the row under the pointer. The drop itself (`timeline.place`) puts the picture on the video destination and the sound on the audio destination, and with several audio clips (Modify ▸ Audio Channels, extra container audio streams) or with the nest toggle off, on further tracks as well. So the preview hid most of what the drop would overwrite:

- **An A/V clip over V2:** the box showed only V2, but the sound landed on A2 too and overwrote whatever was there.
- **A picture-only item (still, color matte) over an audio row:** the box showed the audio row. The clip actually went to the video track of the same number.

### Change

- **`Session::placement_lanes(item, range, video, audio)`** (`crates/engine/src/commands.rs`) says how many video and audio tracks a placement fills, counted from the destination tracks. It uses the same rules as `place_item`:
  - one lane per stream the item carries;
  - audio lanes from `audio_placement_specs`, the function `place_item` itself uses;
  - with the nest toggle off, one lane per source-sequence track that has clips in the range.
- **The Timeline's drop preview** (`panels/timeline.rs`) draws a box on every one of those tracks: video from the destination up, audio from the destination down. It uses the same destination tracks the drop sends to `timeline.place`, including the "new track" drop above the top video or below the last audio track. Each box gets an automation id `timeline.dropPreview.V2` / `.A2` (the track label), so tests and agents can read the preview.
- **Not covered:** a lane on a track the drop would add (for example a third audio clip when the sequence has two audio tracks) is not drawn, except the new track under the pointer.

### Tests

- **`placement_lanes_are_the_tracks_a_placement_fills`** (engine) checks the lanes against the tracks a real `timeline.place` fills, for picture + sound, picture only and sound only.…

title: #2094: the Lumetri shadow lift no longer amplifies near-black chroma into blue specks
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes #2094.

**What happened:** Lumetri's highlight / shadow lift is hue preserving: it computes the new luma `nl` and scales the pixel by `nl / l`. For a near-black pixel that factor is the whole lift divided by almost nothing (tens of times), so a trace of blue chroma bleed beside a bright orange (4:2:0 sharing a chroma sample with the neighbour, often with the red channel slightly negative) came out as a saturated blue block. Pure black (`l == 0`) was not lifted at all, which also put a step between black and near-black.

**Change (reworked after review):** the lift is exactly what it always was at and above a luma floor, `LIFT_LUMA_FLOOR = 0.02` (encoded, about 5/255 in sRGB): the scale is `nl / l` and nothing is added, so every lit pixel renders as before at every Shadows setting. Below the floor the scale is held at the floor's, `1 + (nl - l) / 0.02`, and the rest of the lift is added equally to the three channels, so the luma still lands exactly on `nl` (`l * k + add == nl`), the two sides of the floor are continuous, and a trace of chroma in a near-black pixel is no longer multiplied into a speck. Black now lifts by the same amount as near-black. Applied in the three implementations that must agree: `fn lumetri` (CPU), the `FxOp::Lumetri` CPU fallback in `gpufx.rs` and `lumetri_op` in `fx.wgsl`, through one `lift_scale` helper on the CPU side.

**Threshold, stated:** pixels with encoded luma ≥ 0.02 are unchanged at any Shadows / Highlights value. Below it, at Shadows 8 the near-black scale is at most 2.4 (was up to ~7 for the report's pixel and unbounded towards black); at Shadows 100 it is at most 18.5 (was unbounded).

**Tests:**
- `lumetri_shadow_lift_is_unchanged_at_and_above_the_luma_floor`: a lit shadow pixel (luma 0.097) at Shadows 50 comes out exactly as the plain `nl / l` scale gives, and `lift_scale` is continuous across the floor.
- `lumetri_shadow_lift_does_not_amplify_near_black_chroma`: the report's pixel (about (0, 2, 6)/255 with a slightly n…

title: Read a hyphen as minus only at the start of a number
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/tts-text/src/normalize.rs:89` (no existing issue): TTS text normalizer reads a hyphen before digits inside a name as "minus" ("COVID-19" → "COVID minus nineteen").

## Cause
The `'-'` arm in `normalize` turned any hyphen followed by a digit into the word "minus". It never looked at the character before the hyphen, so names and model numbers like "COVID-19" and "F-16" were read as "COVID minus nineteen" and "F minus sixteen".

## Fix
The hyphen is now read as "minus" only when it is at the start of the text or follows whitespace or an opening bracket (`(`, `[`, `{`). In any other position it stays a plain punctuation token, so "COVID-19", "F-16", "B-52", "Windows-11" and "pre-2020" no longer get a "minus". The new test also checks that "Temp: -5" and "(-5)" still read as "minus five".

## Verified
- Regression test `hyphen_inside_a_name_is_not_minus`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-tts-text --lib hyphen_inside_a_name_is_not_minus`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Hyphens after other punctuation (for example "Temp:-5") are no longer read as minus. The issue's rule covers only start of text, whitespace and opening brackets, so I kept to that. Number ranges such as "3-5" are also no longer read as "minus". I changed nothing else in number, date or money parsing.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: #1994: the main window remembers its position, size and maximized state between launches
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes #1994; also the two halves of #2042 (position, and window / full-screen state).

**What happened:** the main window opened at the default 1600×980 in the default place on every launch. eframe can remember the window, but the app built it without the `persistence` feature, so nothing was stored (on any platform).

**Change:** the app enables eframe's `persistence` feature with `persist_window: true`, pointing `persistence_path` at `window.ron` in the data directory (next to `preferences.json`, the logs and recovery; `--data-dir` / `FILMCRAFT_DATA_DIR` move it with the rest). eframe restores the position, inner size, maximized and full-screen state, clamps the size to a monitor and moves a remembered position back onto a monitor (an unplugged display does not leave the window off-screen). `FilmcraftApp::persist_egui_memory` returns false so only the window geometry is stored: the UI state has its own storage and egui's memory (open menus, scroll offsets) still starts fresh.

**Checked on Windows 11:** moved and resized the window, closed it, relaunched: it came back where it was; maximized, closed, relaunched: maximized. `window.ron` appears in the data directory.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and the build pass.

title: Improve phrase-aware music remix planning
author: straywill
body:
Music duration adjustment can miss usable short arrangements or join incompatible phrases. This change adds a bounded phrase-aware arrangement search while keeping source playback rate and pitch.

The search compares ordered pitch/register patterns, immediate and wider context, harmonic/timbral support and beat-phase compatibility. Closing-phrase protection avoids using the ending in an intermediate repeated section. Alternative shortening suggestions can combine up to four edits. With matchMelody enabled, an unsuitable target leaves the project unchanged and returns other durations for the user to choose.

Analysis caches retain source identity and include media range, sample rate and audio stream, preventing reused project/item IDs from reusing another track's analysis. Regressions cover project-ID reuse and extend/revert/shorten.

This revision contains only the search and its engine integration. Fork branding, seam rendering, waveform/markers and Essential Sound UI changes have been removed from this PR's current diff. SeqUp and Project-to-Program drop features are excluded. UI controls are retained separately in #2448 rather than removed; no maintainer agreement to remove them is assumed.

Earlier validation on head 1fda7440: Windows GNU Rust: 3557 workspace tests passed, 46 ignored, 0 failed, with exactly one proven pre-existing NVIDIA HDR test excluded. title: fix(export): unpreset H.264 exports start from the default preset
author: derektrimm
body:
**Built on #2432.** The `bitrateKbps` fix this PR used to carry is now #2432, as asked in review; its commit is the first one here and drops out when #2432 merges. Review the second commit, `fix(export): unpreset H.264 exports start from the default preset`.

**This changes the output of every scripted H.264 export that names no preset**, so it needs a maintainer's decision. How a script keeps the earlier output is below.

## Problem

An H.264 export that names no preset builds its settings from `ExportSettings::default()`: a fixed 20,000 kbps, whatever the frame size. Export mode and Quick Export start from the default preset instead, "Match Source - Adaptive High Bitrate" (0.2 bits per pixel). So the same export comes out at a different rate depending on how it was started:

| Sequence | Export button (default preset) | `file.exportMedia` / MCP / `filmcraft-cli export --format h264` |
|---|---|---|
| 720x480, 29.97 | 2,072 kbps | 20,000 kbps |
| 1920x1080, 29.97 | 12,429 kbps | 20,000 kbps |
| 3840x2160, 29.97 | 49,717 kbps | 20,000 kbps |

Found exporting an 11-minute 720x480 camcorder edit through the control channel on Windows (0.8.0): a 1.58 GB MP4 at 20.0 Mbit/s for standard-definition video. The paths affected are `file.exportMedia`, `export.queue.add`, `export.resolve`, `export.presets.save` without `from`, and `filmcraft-cli export` with `--format` and no `--preset`, i.e. every agent-driven export that doesn't name a preset.

## Fix

In `settings_from_params` (`crates/engine/src/export_tools.rs`), with no preset named, an export whose format is H.264 (named flat or in `settings`, or none named, since H.264 is the default format) starts from the built-in default preset, as Export mode does (`find_builtin(DEFAULT_PRESET)`). Other formats keep `ExportSettings::default()`, because the preset's AAC audio would replace a QuickTime or MXF file's PCM. `docs/architecture.md` describes it under Presets, with the settings below.

title: Fix TTS reading of prices with more than two decimal digits
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/tts-text/src/normalize.rs:352 (parse_amount, used by parse_money at :266)` (no existing issue): TTS normalizer reads a price with more than two decimal digits as hundreds of cents ("$3.459" → "four hundred fifty-nine cents").

## Cause
`parse_amount` parsed every fractional digit after a currency amount (up to 9) as one integer of minor units. It only special-cased a single digit. So `$3.459` produced a minor value of 459 and was read as "four hundred fifty-nine cents".

## Fix
`parse_amount` now keeps only the first two fractional digits for the minor part, so it never exceeds 99. `$3.459` reads as "three dollars and forty-five cents", `$1.999` as "one dollar and ninety-nine cents", and `$1.250` as "one dollar and twenty-five cents". A regression test covers EnUs and EnGb.

## Verified
- Regression test `money_fraction_beyond_two_digits_is_not_hundreds_of_cents`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-tts-text money_fraction_beyond_two_digits_is_not_hundreds_of_cents`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Digits beyond the second are truncated, not rounded. Rounding could carry into the major unit (`$1.999` would become `$2.00`), which this change avoids. Single-digit (`$1.5`) and two-digit fractions behave as before.

title: add Nix flake for building and installing on NixOS
author: Yuna404
body:
## What

Adds a Nix flake so FilmCraft can be built, run and installed on Nix/NixOS straight from this repository:

- `flake.nix`: exposes `packages.x86_64-linux.default`, an overlay and a dev shell
- `nix/package.nix`: the derivation (`rustPlatform.buildRustPackage`), building `filmcraft` and `filmcraft-cli`
- `flake.lock`: pins nixpkgs (nixos-unstable)
- `README.md`: a "Nix / NixOS" entry in the Linux downloads section

## Why

There is no way to run the prebuilt Linux binaries on NixOS out of the box (no FHS, no global libs). Building from source with Nix gives Nix users a one-line install, and the flake can follow the repository instead of living in a separate fork.

## How it works

- Builds from the repository itself (`src = self`) using `Cargo.lock`
- Installs the desktop entry, MIME types and icons from `packaging/linux/` and `assets/app-icon/hicolor`, so there is no duplicated metadata
- Wraps the binary with the runtime libraries it loads dynamically (Wayland, Vulkan, libxkbcommon, VA-API, ALSA, X11)
- `doCheck = false`: the test suite needs ffmpeg and external fixtures

## Usage

    nix run github:storytold/filmcraft

## Testing

Built and run on NixOS (nixos-unstable) with niri (Wayland) and an NVIDIA GPU: the app starts and NVDEC hardware decoding is detected. Other platforms are not covered (`x86_64-linux` only).

## Maintenance note

`Cargo.lock` has a git dependency (`craft-ui`), so `nix/package.nix` pins its hash in `outputHashes`. It needs updating when that dependency's revision changes. Happy to maintain this, or to adapt it to the project's conventions (e.g. an `xtask` check or CI job).

## Checklist

- [x] No changes to Rust code
- [x] No new assets

title: fix(project): validate dimensions and preserve browser recovery
author: nuclearspike
body:
Fixes #2227.

Project decode now rejects oversized media video metadata and graphic or adjustment-layer canvases with an item-specific error before `file.open` replaces the current project. The same validation runs before manual and automatic saves, native recovery-journal and browser OPFS snapshots (a rejected revision is not retried until the revision changes), template export, selection export, and Project Manager writes, preventing an invalid live project from replacing a reopenable file. While metadata remains invalid, new edits are not captured by recovery; any earlier valid snapshot is retained while recovery remains enabled. The browser status bar shows the dimension-validation warning while recovery is blocked; other status messages take priority until they expire, then the warning returns. Embeds that hide the status bar show a separate recovery warning. Saving the same invalid revision does not dismiss either warning; a repaired revision clears it after validation. 

Web-host recovery dialogs wait for FilmCraft's named fonts before drawing; the first recovery frame no longer panics in egui. An asynchronous OPFS write can still fail after scheduling; the existing retry policy handles that failure, but this patch does not add a persistent status message for OPFS I/O errors. 

If a loaded OPFS snapshot fails project decode, or a dirty snapshot is intentionally skipped with `?fresh` or `?norecover`, the browser pauses new recovery writes, blocks generic engine exports from targeting its reserved OPFS recovery directory, and keeps a recovery prompt open while offering the original bytes for an immediate download. A failed-open snapshot keeps its original bytes in private recovery state, independent of the writable virtual-file table; a skipped `?fresh` or `?norecover` snapshot stays as an OPFS-backed Blob without loading the project contents into wasm memory. author: MarekSpodBiedry

Fixes #2223.

With Track Select Forward (or Backward), a drag on the timeline moved nothing when one of the tracks was locked, for example a music track locked so that the edit above it can be moved. title: fix(media): validate decoded image-sequence frame sizes
author: nuclearspike
body:
Fixes #2235.

A decoded image-sequence frame can exceed FilmCraft's supported frame-size limit and still become sequence metadata or enter the frame cache. This change validates the first frame and every later decoded frame before either use, returning a path-specific decode error for unsupported sizes. It moves the existing shared frame-size validator into the media crate so the media and project layers use the same limit. The existing eight-candidate search can hold a nearby valid frame. A later rejected frame is retried on the next request when the host supplies live file reads; a rejected first frame requires reopening or reimporting, and hosts that snapshot frame bytes need a reopen to see a replacement.

Synthetic first-frame and later-frame tests exercise an over-width PNG safely, the valid side boundary, the nearby-frame hold, and retry of a repaired later frame through a live loader. Validation on macOS 27.0 arm64 with Rust 1.97.1: `cargo xtask ci` passed (3,496 tests, 45 ignored), including release Clippy, formatting, layers, assets, and 49 WASM crates. Native UI and Windows, Linux, and browser runtime paths were not exercised. The check runs after still-image decoding; decoder-internal and accepted-frame rendering allocations are outside this fix. No dependencies or assets are added.

title: #1916: the keyframe menu's interpolation and Clear apply to the whole selection, as one undo step
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes #1916.

**What happened:** with several keyframes selected in Effect Controls, choosing a Temporal Interpolation from the right-click menu changed only the keyframe that was right-clicked. Which one that was looked random because the menu ignored the selection entirely. Clear behaved the same way.

**Change:** `effects.setInterpolation` and `effects.deleteKeyframe` take a `keyframes` list (the same `{clip, effect, param, mask?, time}` references as `effects.moveKeyframes`). Every reference is checked before anything changes, then all of them change in one undo step ("Keyframe Interpolation" / "Delete Keyframes"), so a selection cannot be half edited; a bad reference, a duplicate, an empty list or more than 4096 keys is refused with nothing changed. title: Don't snap to clips on hidden video layers in the timeline
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2243

## Cause
`snap_to` in the timeline panel collected snap candidates from every track in the sequence. It never checked a video track's `enabled` flag, which the eye toggle sets. Clips on a hidden layer therefore stayed snap targets.

## Fix
`snap_to` now skips video tracks with `enabled == false` when it collects candidate edges. Clips on a hidden layer no longer attract the dragged time, so placement near them is free. Playhead drags go through the same function, so they stop snapping to hidden layers too.

## Verified
- Regression test `clips_on_a_hidden_video_layer_are_not_snap_targets`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui --lib clips_on_a_hidden_video_layer_are_not_snap_targets`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Audio tracks are unchanged. Their `enabled` flag means 'not muted', and the audio rows have no eye toggle. Markers, in/out points and the playhead remain snap targets.

title: Read every digit of numbers longer than 20 digits individually
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/tts-text/src/normalize.rs:570 (parse_number_core, overflow branch at :589)` (no existing issue): TTS normalizer reads only the first 20 digits of a very long number digit by digit and reads the rest as a cardinal.

## Cause
In `parse_number_core`, the digit scan stopped after the 20th digit and set an `overflowed` flag. The unread tail went back to the main loop as a new number, so it was read as a cardinal (or with different leading-zero handling) instead of digit by digit.

## Fix
The scan no longer stops at 20 digits. It consumes the whole digit run, and any run longer than `MAX_CARDINAL_DIGITS` is read digit by digit, as the docs say. The `overflowed` flag is removed.

## Verified
- Regression test `numbers_longer_than_twenty_digits_are_read_fully_digit_by_digit`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-tts-text --lib numbers_longer_than_twenty_digits_are_read_fully_digit_by_digit`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Numbers of 12 digits or fewer, and the continuation, year and grouping handling, are unchanged.

title: Ignore out-of-range AUD channels in EDL import
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/interchange/src/edl.rs:211-216 (parse, AUD handling; consumed by Ctx::track_index/lay at :341-380 and Builder::ensure_tracks in common.rs:411)` (no existing issue): EDL import: an `AUD` line with a huge channel number creates millions of audio tracks (memory/CPU exhaustion).

## Cause
The EDL `AUD` continuation line parsed each token as a `usize` and turned it into an audio channel with no bounds check, unlike `parse_channels`, which accepts only A1..A99. On import, `ensure_tracks` then created one track per index, so `AUD 3000000` created 3,000,000 audio tracks. Larger values could exhaust memory or hang the importer.

## Fix
`AUD` channels are now accepted only in 1..=99, the same range `parse_channels` allows. Any other value is dropped and a warning is added to the import report.

## Verified
- Regression test `aud_line_out_of_range_channel_is_ignored`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-interchange --lib aud_line_out_of_range_channel_is_ignored`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`parse_channels`, `ensure_tracks` and the track layout code are unchanged. Tokens that are not valid `usize` values are still skipped silently, as before.

title: fix(interchange): FCPXML zero frameDuration no longer divides by zero on export
author: Wbunker
body:
## What

`rate_from_frame_duration` only checked the numerator of an FCPXML `<format frameDuration>`, so `100/0s`, `0/100s` or a negative part produced a frame rate with a zero numerator. Exporting the imported project then divided by zero in `fmt_time` (`fcpxml.rs`) as soon as the sequence had a start timecode or any marker. That is a panic in release builds too (`AGENTS.md` section 0).

## Repro

```xml
<format id="f1" frameDuration="100/0s" width="1920" height="1080"/>
...
<sequence format="f1" tcStart="3600/1s" tcFormat="DF"> ...
```

Import it, then export the sequence as FCPXML: `attempt to calculate the remainder with a divisor of zero` at `fcpxml.rs:81`. A plain clip with `tcStart="0s"` and no markers does not hit it, which is why it went unnoticed. Found by mutating every attribute value of a seed document with hostile numbers in a debug build.

## Fix

Both parts of `frameDuration` must be positive. An invalid value falls back to the default frame rate and the import report says `format "f1" has an invalid frameDuration "100/0s"; the default frame rate was used`, so nothing is substituted silently.

## Tests

- `rational_times_are_exact` also asserts that six bad values (`100/0s`, `0/100s`, `-100/2500s`, `100/-2500s`, `0s`, `x`) are rejected.
- New `zero_frame_duration_falls_back_to_the_default_rate` imports and exports a document with each bad value, with a start timecode and a marker. With the fix reverted it panics at `fmt_time` (`fcpxml.rs:81`); with the fix it passes.
- `crates/interchange/README.md` documents the behaviour.

## Gates (Linux x86_64, release)

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --release -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets` and `cargo xtask wasm` pass. All `filmcraft-interchange` tests pass.

title: fix(interchange): FCPXML connected-clip lanes are capped instead of becoming tracks
author: Wbunker
body:
## What

A connected clip's `lane` in an FCPXML became a track index: `Builder::place` creates every track up to it, with no cap. One attribute in an imported file therefore decides how much memory the importer allocates (`AGENTS.md` section 0: cap allocations sized by input).

Measured on this branch's base (debug build, capped memory):

| `lane` | tracks created |
|---|---|
| 100000 | 200 002 |
| 1000000 | 2 000 002 (0.19 s) |
| 10000000 | exceeded a 4 GB cap |
| -1000000000 | what a mutation fuzz produced; it grew until a 246 GB machine ran out of memory |

## Repro

```xml
<asset-clip ref="a1" offset="0s" duration="5s">
  <asset-clip ref="a1" lane="1000000" offset="0s" duration="1s"/>
</asset-clip>
```

Import it and count the tracks. (Do not try a lane in the billions without a memory limit.)

## Fix

Lanes beyond 999 are skipped, with a warning in the import report: `<asset-clip> on lane N is beyond the 999 lanes a sequence can have; skipped`. 999 is the engine's per-sequence track limit (`sequence_tools::MAX_TRACKS`); interchange sits below the engine, so it has its own constant, documented next to it. The cap is applied to the combined lane, because nested lanes add up, and that addition is now saturating. This also removes a `-lane - 1` negation overflow for `i32::MIN`. The largest lane that fits (999) is still imported.

## Tests

`huge_lanes_are_skipped_not_turned_into_tracks` imports lanes 100000, -100000 and nested 600 + 600, and checks the track count and the warning, plus that lane 999 still imports. With the cap removed it fails on the track count; with it, it passes. The values are deliberately moderate so reverting the fix cannot exhaust memory. `crates/interchange/README.md` documents the behaviour.

## Gates (Linux x86_64)

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy` on `filmcraft-interchange` and `filmcraft-engine` (`--all-targets --release -D warnings`), all `filmcraft-interchange` tests, and the engine library tests (639) pass. I did not run the full …

title: Refuse numbers separated by spaces or a unit in number fields
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/ui-egui/src/calc.rs:34-41 (eval)` (no existing issue): Number-field calculator merges numbers separated by spaces or a unit: "10 x 20" gives 1020, "1920 1080" gives 19201080.

## Cause
`calc::eval` deleted all whitespace, letters, `%` and `°` before parsing. Its guard only refused letters sitting directly between two digits. So `10 x 20`, `1 e 3` and `1920 1080` fused into the single numbers 1020, 13 and 19201080, instead of giving `None`.

## Fix
The guard now scans the raw text. It returns `None` if a digit or `.` is followed by any run of spaces, letters, `%` or `°` and then another digit or `.`. The same check also covers the old `1e3` and `10x20` cases, so it replaces the old letter-only check.

## Verified
- Regression test `numbers_separated_by_spaces_or_a_unit_are_not_merged`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui --lib calc::tests::numbers_separated_by_spaces_or_a_unit_are_not_merged`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The parser and the operator handling are unchanged. Units and spaces next to operators or at the ends (`1920 px / 2`, `-6 dB`, `100 * 2`) still parse as before.

title: fix(render): bound offline placeholder images and cache
author: nuclearspike
body:
Fixes #2267.

Offline placeholders previously rendered at source-derived dimensions. A valid large source could allocate an unnecessarily large float slate and RGBA copy while offline. Generated slates now stay within 1,280 pixels per side and 921,600 pixels total without changing the stored source dimensions. Invalid direct-helper requests return an error. Long or control-containing names render a bounded generic notice while their original paths remain in project metadata.

Each media pool's slate cache admits at most 64 MiB across sixteen entries. Concurrent requests for one slate share generation; cold slates render one at a time per pool to bound simultaneous working memory, while cached frames remain available. New, Close, Demo, template, and project-open transitions get a fresh pool, so cached frames from a previous project cannot occupy the new project's hot set. In-flight readers and queued exports retain their captured pool and project snapshot. Regressions exercise extreme dimensions, cache bounds and concurrent misses, long names, project switching, template media registration, and a queued export compared byte-for-byte against the original project's control export. On macOS 27.0 arm64 with Rust 1.97.1, an isolated current-base `cargo xtask ci` run passed 3,510 tests, zero failures and 45 ignored, plus formatting, release Clippy, layers, assets, and 49-crate WASM compilation.

The 1,280×720 working cap also applies to offline frames in larger exports, so warning text and stripes can be softer than a full-resolution slate. At extreme aspect ratios the short side can be two pixels and text may be unreadable. The cache limit is per media pool, not process-wide: active callers and queued exports can retain frames, and temporary render memory is separate. The direct `slate` and `slate_rgba8` helpers now return `Result`; `MediaError` implements `Clone` to share a failed concurrent generation. No dependencies or assets are added. title: fix(render): bound graphic effect working rasters
author: nuclearspike
body:
Fixes #2270.

A valid large graphic with an enabled standard effect or opacity mask could allocate a source-sized RGBA float working image even for a much smaller preview. At 32,768×8,192, that image alone is about 4 GiB. This caps the effect/mask working raster at 8,294,400 pixels and uses its actual width-derived scale for both drawing and downstream placement. Graphics with only disabled standard effects use direct vector drawing in the CPU renderer and the existing tight-raster path in the GPU plan; neither enters the bounded effect working raster.

Regressions exercise ordinary and extreme dimensions, odd-size rounding, downstream scale, the actual working-image path, a small effected graphic, and the disabled-effect CPU/GPU path. On macOS 27.0 arm64 with Rust 1.97.1, an isolated current-base `cargo xtask ci` run passed 3,498 tests, zero failures and 45 ignored, plus formatting, release Clippy, layers, assets, and 49-crate WASM compilation. No dependencies or assets are added.

Effect and mask previews, including exports that use this path, can have less detail above the cap. The outer float image can still use about 127 MiB per frame at the cap, and this change does not bound the separate layer-raster cache or all temporary rendering memory. The vector-only path and stored project dimensions are unchanged. Windows, Linux, browser runtime, and native UI paths were not exercised.

title: render: Warp Stabilizer analyses a clip once, in bounded memory
author: daveinme
body:
Fixes #291, fixes #1381.

## Problem
The frame workers rendering neighbouring frames of a stabilised clip each missed the path cache and ran the whole Warp Stabilizer analysis concurrently: 6 workers decoded 432 frames for a 72-frame clip instead of 72. Every analysis also held the grey pyramids of all the clip's frames at once (~0.7 MB a frame), which means gigabytes for a long clip (more with Detailed). That stalled playback and could run out of memory on long 4K clips.

## Fix (`crates/render/src/vfx/temporal.rs`)
- **One gate per clip key:** the first caller runs the analysis; the others wait and read the cached path.
- **Bounded memory:** frames are decoded and tracked 64 at a time, carrying the last frame across chunks. The resulting steps are unchanged.

Regression tests in `crates/render/src/vfx/tests.rs`: `warp_stabilizer_analyses_a_clip_once_for_concurrent_frames` (concurrent callers decode each source frame once) and `warp_stabilizer_analysis_tracks_across_chunks` (a 72-frame clip spanning two chunks recovers the known per-frame jitter at every step, including the chunk boundary).

## Testing
- Manual (Linux): playback of a stabilised clip at full resolution is smooth, with CPU at about 22%. Before this change playback stalled.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets`, `cargo xtask wasm`: pass.
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-render`: pass. `filmcraft-engine` stabilizer tests pass.
- The workspace-wide test failures I saw locally come from the environment, not from this change: the ffmpeg oracle tests need ffmpeg ≥ 5.1 (`-fps_mode`) and I have 4.4. `dev_icon::tests::desktop_file_matches_the_packaged_fields` also fails on current `main`, because the packaged `.desktop` file gained `MimeType=` but `desktop_file_content` doesn't emit it.

Related: #1865 and #1866 each address one half of this (chunked analysis / analyse once); this PR does both in one change.

title: fix(interchange): absurd frame rates and start timecodes are bounded on import
author: Wbunker
body:
## What

Importers accepted any positive frame rate and any start timecode. Three ways an imported number overflowed the frame arithmetic of the export (all panics in debug builds, wrapped values in release):

| Input | Where it overflowed |
|---|---|
| FCPXML `frameDuration="1/9223372036854775807s"` (also FCP7 `<timebase>9223372036854775807</timebase>`, not NTSC) | `frames_round`, `common.rs:187`: `frame_at` clamps to `i64::MAX`, then `f + 1` |
| FCP7 `<timebase>` near `i64::MAX` with `<ntsc>TRUE</ntsc>` | `rate_from_timebase`, `tb * 1000`, on import |
| FCP7 `<frame>18446744073709551615</frame>` start timecode | `edl.rs:698` `rec_frames`: saturates to `i64::MAX`, then the sum overflows |

The first and third need a start timecode or a marker in the sequence, which is why a plain document does not hit them. Found by mutating every number in exported documents with hostile values.

## Fix

- Rates are limited to **1 000 000 per second** (`common::MAX_RATE`). That is far above video and above the 192 000 Hz OTIO audio uses as a time base, and far below where the arithmetic overflows. The FCP7 `timebase` is clamped to it, and an OTIO rate beyond it uses the default (as a non-finite one already did).
- One pass after every import (`lib.rs`, `bound_start_timecodes`) resets a sequence or media frame rate beyond the limit, and start timecodes beyond 360 000 000 000 frames (about 100 hours at the highest accepted rate), each with a warning in the report (`implausible frame rate`, `out-of-range start timecode`). A single pass covers every format, so `fcpxml.rs` is not touched.

## Tests

- `tests/rates.rs`: FCPXML with three absurd `frameDuration`s, exported to every format, plus the warning.
- `tests/fcp7.rs`: absurd `timebase` with and without `ntsc` (and a negative one), and the absurd start timecode, all exported to every format.
- `common::tests::rates`: the clamps and the 192 000 Hz case.

With the limits lifted these panic at `common.rs:187`, at the `* 1000` multiply…

title: fix(interchange): a huge duration times a speed saturates instead of overflowing
author: Wbunker
body:
## What

`common::scaled` multiplied a duration by an integral speed with a plain `*`:

```rust
if s == s.round() && s < 1e6 { Tick(d.0 * s as i64) } else { ... }
```

A duration read from a file times a speed from the same file can exceed an `i64` of ticks: `attempt to multiply with overflow` (a panic in debug builds, a wrapped time in release builds). `scaled` serves the EDL, FCP7, FCPXML and OTIO importers and exporters, so one cause is reachable from all four formats. Found by mutation fuzzing (hits: EDL 3, FCP7 2, OTIO 1, FCPXML 1 in 4000 mutations each).

## Repro

```
TITLE: Seq
FCM: NON-DROP FRAME

001  A        V     C        00:00:00:10 00:00:04:04 00:00:00:00 2147483647:00:03:18
M2   A              072.0                00:00:00:10
* FROM CLIP NAME: A.mov
* SOURCE FILE: /media/A.mov
```

Import it as an EDL: a record-out timecode of 2147483647 hours with an `M2` speed change panics at `common.rs` in `scaled`.

## Fix

The multiply saturates (`d.0.saturating_mul(s as i64)`), like `Tick`'s own `Add`/`Sub`/`Neg`. One line; the float branch already saturates in Rust's `as` cast, and `signed_scaled` in `edl.rs` is already safe because `Tick`'s negation saturates.

## Tests

- `tests/edl.rs::huge_duration_with_a_speed_change_does_not_overflow`: the EDL above, imported and exported in every format.
- `common::tests::scaled_saturates`: unit assertions at `i64::MAX / 2` and `i64::MIN / 2`, plus ordinary values (`1000 * 3 = 3000`, `* 0.5 = 500`) so the normal path is unchanged.

Both fail at `common.rs` `scaled` with the fix reverted (checked) and pass with it. `crates/interchange/README.md` documents it.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-interchange -p filmcraft-engine --all-targets --release -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, all `filmcraft-interchange` tests and the 639 `filmcraft-engine` library tests pass. I did not run the full `cargo xtask ci` for this change.

title: fix(interchange): OTIO export stops writing nested-sequence copies past a limit
author: Wbunker
body:
## What

OTIO has no references, so the exporter writes every use of a nested sequence in full. Compound clips that each hold several uses of the next one make that exponential in the nesting depth. The other exporters (FCPXML, FCP7 XML, EDL, AAF, OMF) reference nested sequences and stay instant.

A 3 KB FCPXML whose `<media>` nest 12 deep with 3 `ref-clip`s each imports as 14 items (the importer memoizes nested sequences), and then the OTIO export runs for minutes and grows until memory runs out. Measured on `main`, release build, uses = 3:

| nesting depth | OTIO export |
|---|---|
| 3 (22 uses each) | 2.2 s, 105 MB |
| 4 (3 uses each) | 0.55 s, 32 MB |
| 5 (3 uses each) | 3.7 s, 216 MB (about 7x more per level) |
| 6 and deeper | did not finish in 20-60 s under a 4 GB cap |

Every clip is about 10 KB of pretty-printed JSON (full media reference and the `filmcraft` metadata), which is why the output size is dominated by clips, not by copies.

## Repro

```
CASE: media m0 .. m11, each a sequence with 3 <ref-clip ref="m{n+1}"/> (the last holds 3 <asset-clip>), project spine = <ref-clip ref="m0"/>.
Import as FCPXML, export as OTIO.
```

Run it under a memory limit (`systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=4G -p MemorySwapMax=0 ...`), not on a machine you care about.

## Fix

The exporter counts clips written inside nested sequences (`Exp::nested_items`). After `MAX_NESTED_ITEMS = 25_000` (about 250 MB of JSON) further nested sequences are written as gaps, with one warning: `more than 25000 clips written inside nested sequences: the rest are gaps (OTIO repeats a nested sequence for every use)`. The sequence being exported is never truncated, only the nested copies past the budget. Real projects use far fewer. With the check, the depth-12 document exports in about 10 s under a 4 GB cap (depth 30: about 22 s, output near 250 MB), where it never finished before.

A first version capped the number of nested copies instead; that does not bound the size, because one copy ca…

title: fix(cfb): adding a child is O(1), not a scan of every sibling (AAF export of 20 000 markers took a minute)
author: Wbunker
body:
## What

`cfb::Writer::add` rejected a duplicate name by comparing the new name with **every sibling** through `compare_names`, which allocates two `Vec<u16>` per call. Adding n children to one storage therefore costs n² allocating comparisons. An AAF export puts all markers and components of a mob in one storage, so it is quadratic in the size of the project. Every other exporter is linear.

AAF export, release build, from an FCPXML (generated: one clip with N markers, or N clips):

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 5 000 markers | 4.1 s | |
| 10 000 markers | 14.6 s | |
| 20 000 markers | 57.7 s | **0.38 s** |
| 100 000 markers | did not finish (no result in 120 s) | **2.0 s** |
| 20 000 clips | 55.8 s | **0.23 s** |
| 20 000 connected clips | 86.6 s | **0.45 s** |

Doubling the input quadrupled the time. A 1 MB FCPXML is enough to hang the export for minutes (and to freeze the UI if it runs there).

## Fix

Each storage keeps a `HashSet` of its children's names as sibling order compares them (UTF-16 code units, upper-cased with the existing `upper`), so the duplicate check is a lookup. The result is the same: case-insensitive, also beyond ASCII, per storage. `compare_names` is unchanged and still orders the siblings at `finish()`.

## Tests

New file `crates/cfb/tests/writer_scale.rs` (a new file so it does not collide with other PRs editing `src/tests.rs`):

- `adding_many_children_is_not_quadratic`: 40 000 children must take under 3 s. It takes 0.02 s now and 21 s with the old check (checked by restoring it), so the limit separates them by orders of magnitude on any machine.
- `duplicate_names_are_still_rejected`: `ALPHA` / `alpha` against `Alpha`, a name differing only in length, the same name in another storage (allowed), and non-ASCII case (`Ünï` / `ÜNÏ`).

`crates/cfb/README.md` documents it.

## Gates (Linux x86_64)

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-cfb -p filmcraft-interchange --all-targets --release -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask l…

title: fix(ui): draw the toast the engine sets
author: switch87
body:
## What

The engine leaves messages in `FilmcraftApp::toast` — "Exported frame to
…", "Refreshed *n* media item(s) changed on disk", media missing, project
upgraded — and the desktop UI never read the field, so none of those
messages ever reached anyone. The web app draws its own; the desktop app
collected them and dropped them.

`toast::show` draws the current message bottom-centre for 3.5 seconds and
wires it in next to the graphics notice.

## Why it is a `Label` and not painted text

Most of these messages hand over a path or a command:

```
Exported frame to /tmp/scene-0001.png
```

Painted text can only ever be looked at. A `Label` can be selected and
copied, which is usually the whole point of a message like that.

## Details

- Expiry is on wall-clock time, not on the next event: an idle window
  repaints every 250 ms while a toast is up, so the toast cannot linger
  for the rest of the session after the last event.
- The call is wrapped in `catch_unwind` exactly like `graphics_notice`, so
  a broken toast drops itself instead of taking the session down.
- The window is untitled, fixed, non-movable, anchored bottom-centre, and
  capped at 560 px so long messages wrap instead of running off-screen.

## Tests

Two, in `toast::tests`: a fresh toast is laid out as a widget (a rect of
its own, and the message is taken from the app), and an expired one is not
drawn. The frames are driven through `RawInput { time }` so neither test
depends on the wall clock.

`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui

title: fix(fcpxml): import and export adjust-conform (fit by default) (#2218)
author: Wbunker
body:
Fixes #2218.

## Problem
In FCPXML a clip with no `adjust-conform` means `fit`: the picture is scaled into the sequence frame before its `adjust-transform`. The importer ignored the element, so a 3840x2160 clip in a 1920x1080 sequence landed at scale 100 and was cropped.

## Change
- **Import:** a missing element or `type="fit"` sets the clip's existing `scale_to_frame` flag; `type="none"` clears it. The render step already scales by `min(frame_w/src_w, frame_h/src_h)` with the real source size, and multiplies it into the clip's own Scale, which matches "conform first, then transform". No new model or render change.
- **`fill`:** there is no equivalent (the flag is fit-only), so it imports as `fit` with a warning in the import report. Supporting it needs a new field on the clip (project format + render); I'd like a maintainer's view on that before building it, see the question below.
- **Export:** a clip without the flag is written with `<adjust-conform type="none"/>` before `adjust-transform`. Without it, FilmCraft's own clips would come back as `fit` on re-import and change size.

## Tests
New file `crates/interchange/tests/fcpxml_conform.rs` (kept out of `tests/fcpxml.rs` so it does not conflict with open PRs):
- missing element and `fit` give the flag, `none` clears it, `fill` warns and fits;
- export writes `none` exactly for unfitted clips and the flags survive a round trip;
- a proptest (48 cases) of random flags on three video tracks round-trips.

The round-trip tests fail against `main`'s `fcpxml.rs`; the `none` test passes either way because it matches the old behaviour.

## Checks
`cargo fmt --check`, clippy on the interchange crate, and `cargo test --workspace --release --no-fail-fast`: 3454 passed, 2 failed, both failing on a clean `main` and unrelated (`dev_icon::desktop_file_matches_the_packaged_fields`, fixed by #1958; matroska oracle `mjpeg_ac3`). title: h264: High 10 / High 4:2:2 decoding, intra and inter (Sony XAVC S-I and S)
author: kottav
body:
Scope: this PR now holds only the software decoder and the all-intra plumbing (parts 1 and 2 of the review). The NVDEC-on-Windows part is split out into #2431 (draft).

Closes most of gap G3 / #626 (no software 10-bit / 4:2:2 H.264 decode on Windows): camera files such as the Sony A7R V's XAVC S-I (H.264 High 4:2:2 Intra, 10-bit, 4K, HLG) and long-GOP XAVC S now decode.

**filmcraft-h264: High 10 / High 4:2:2, intra and inter.** The decoder is generic over the sample type (picture::Sample: u8 / u16): planes, intra prediction, transforms, motion compensation, weighted prediction and deblocking. 8 to 10 bits, 4:2:0 and 4:2:2, CAVLC and CABAC; QpBdOffset and negative QPs; the 4:2:2 chroma DC (2x4) transform and QP'c+3; 8x16 chroma intra prediction; 4:2:2 chroma deblocking (four horizontal edges); bit-packed I_PCM; 4:2:2 chroma motion compensation; weighted-prediction offsets scaled by bit depth. Picture gains y_wide / u_wide / v_wide, bit_depth and chroma_422 (8-bit pictures still use y / u / v). 4:4:4, lossless and more than 10 bits stay Unsupported.

**8-bit 4:2:0 speed.** The crate's 1080p benchmark (examples/h264dec with H264_BENCH_ITERS=10 H264_THREADS=1 on the perf fixture, best of 10), three alternating runs each on the same machine, against the merge base (09aaf9bf, built separately): 94.3, 86.8 and 91.6 fps before; 86.3, 86.3 and 82.9 fps after (a later build, with the u8 clip constants: 88.7, 91.9 and 91.9 against 94.8, 94.5 and 89.0). So within about 0 to 7 percent, the same as run-to-run noise on this machine; I do not claim it is free. Sample::clip is the constant 255 for u8 to keep the 8-bit paths free of runtime clamp bounds.

title: AVI: recover the video when its idx1 entries are damaged
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Found while reviewing AVI import in EffectCraft (storytold/effectcraft#1739; tracking issue storytold/effectcraft#1701).

## Problem
An AVI whose `idx1` entries for the video were damaged opened as an **audio-only file**, with no error, even though every picture was still in the movie data.

To reproduce: take a 1-second Motion JPEG + PCM AVI (25 video chunks, 47 audio chunks) and point only the video's `idx1` offsets past the end of the file. That changes 100 bytes; the headers and the `movi` payload stay intact. The file then opened as audio only, and EffectCraft imported it as audio footage with no warning.

**Why:** `open_with` gave up on `idx1` and scanned `movi` only when the index held **no** chunk for **any** stream. The audio's intact entries kept the empty video table. `AviSource` then picked no video stream (it needs one with chunks) and reported `MediaKind::AudioOnly`.

## Fix
- **`filmcraft-avi`:** after reading `idx1`, a stream that declares data (`dwLength > 0`) but that the index left without a single chunk, while other streams have theirs, gets its chunks from a scan of the first `movi` list, as a file without an index does (`scan_missing`).
  - Its key frames are then unknown (`keyframes_known = false`). The H.264/HEVC key-frame detection in `filmcraft-codecs` already handles that.
  - The indexed streams keep their tables, and the scan only adds chunks to the streams it is looking for.
  - Only the first `movi` list (the one `idx1` covers) is rescanned, and before the AVIX extensions are scanned, so such a stream keeps its first-RIFF frames ahead of the extensions'. (A file whose `idx1` gives no stream a chunk is scanned in full, as before; that check now runs before the extensions are read too, so such a file with extensions no longer opens with only their chunks.)
  - A stream that declares no data (an audio track that never recorded a sample, an empty text stream) is not looked for, so a healthy file with an empty stream still opens from `idx1`…

title: AVI: decode H.264 and HEVC with their parameter sets in the stream header
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Found while reviewing AVI import in EffectCraft (storytold/effectcraft#1739; tracking issue storytold/effectcraft#1701). Independent of #2302 (index recovery), though both touch `crates/codecs/src/avi.rs` in different places.

## Problem
The bytes after an AVI video stream's `BITMAPINFOHEADER` (`BitmapInfo.extra`, the codec setup) never reached the decoder: `AviVideo::make_decoder` always built `H264Decoder::annexb()` / `HevcDecoder::annexb()` with nothing in them. Every H.264 AVI whose parameter sets aren't repeated in its chunks failed.

| File (ffmpeg) | Header holds | Before | After |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `-c:v libx264 -flags +global_header` | Annex B SPS / PPS (38 bytes) | 0 / 25 frames (`missing parameter set: PPS 0`) | 25 / 25, bit-exact |
| H.264 copied from an MP4 as it is (`-c:v copy`, `avc1`) | an `avcC` record; chunks length-prefixed | 0 / 25 (`forbidden_zero_bit set`) | 25 / 25, bit-exact |
| HEVC, `+global_header` (tagged `HEVC`) | Annex B VPS / SPS / PPS | — | bit-exact |
| Default ffmpeg H.264 AVI (parameter sets in band) | nothing | decodes | unchanged |

## Fix
- **`video.rs`:** `H264Decoder::annexb_with(setup)` / `HevcDecoder::annexb_with(setup)` take Annex B parameter sets from a container's header. The decoder gets them before the first sample and again after every `reset()` (a seek), through the same `make_inner` the other constructors use.
  - If the header's sets don't decode (damaged, or an unrelated `strf` extra that starts with a start code), `annexb_with` logs a warning and builds the in-band decoder instead, and later resets don't retry them. So `annexb_with` can't fail, and a file that repeats good sets in band plays as it did when the header was ignored.
  - `annexb()` is now `annexb_with(Vec::new())`, which builds the same decoder.
- **`avi.rs`:** a `NalSetup` reads the header's setup as what it is.
  - Annex B parameter sets go to the decoder as they are.
  - An `avcC` / `hvcC` record gives its parameter sets (through `hw::NalStream…

title: edit: ripple trims move sync-locked caption tracks, as insert and extract do
author: KLQ1986
body:
## Problem

A ripple trim leaves caption tracks behind. `ripple_trim_group` (`crates/edit/src/lib.rs`) shifts the video and audio tracks (the members' tracks and the sync-locked ones) but never touches `seq.caption_tracks`, while `insert` and `extract` in the same file do (`captions::insert_gap` / `captions::extract_range` on every unlocked, sync-locked caption track). After a ripple trim, every caption after the cut drifts off its picture by the trimmed amount.

Repro: a caption over each of two adjacent clips on a sync-locked caption track; ripple-trim the first clip's out point by −15 frames. The second clip moves 15 frames earlier; its caption stays where it was.

## Fix

Sync-locked, unlocked caption tracks now follow the same edit, at the same cut the media tracks shift from:

- shorter (`shift < 0`): `captions::extract_range` over the stretch the trim closes (a caption across it is cut, later ones move up), the same closing range the media tracks use for the sync-lock check;
- longer (`shift > 0`): `captions::insert_gap` at the cut.

For an in-point trim the cut is the clip's start (`main_from - 1`), so the trimmed clip's own caption is shortened or moved with its words rather than split.

## Test

`ripple_trim_moves_sync_locked_captions` in `crates/edit/src/tests.rs`, next to `ripple_trim_shifts_following`: shorter by 4 frames (the first caption is cut at the new end, the others follow), longer by 2 (they move back out), and a caption track that is not sync-locked stays put. It fails on `main` without the change.

Checked: `cargo test -p filmcraft-edit` (70 passed), `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-edit --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, and `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine -- trim caption ripple` (60 passed). I did not run the full `cargo xtask ci`.

Found while driving FilmCraft 0.8.0's web build from another app, where captions built from a script drifted after every ripple trim.

title: #654: rename video and audio tracks from the Timeline header
author: matheusosan
body:
Closes #654 (again). Supersedes #689, which was merged and then reverted on main.

## Problem

Tracks can be renamed through `timeline.setTrack {track, name}` (control channel, CLI, MCP), but the
Timeline only *shows* the name in the track header: there is no way to rename a video or audio track
from the UI. Issue #654 asked for it; #689 added it but was reverted the same day because its own UI
test failed on main together with other track-header changes that landed that day (the name stayed
"Video 1").

## What this PR does

Rename a track **in place, from its header**:

- **Double-click the track name** (or right-click the header ▸ **Rename**) → a single-line field opens
  over the name with the current name, focused.
- **Enter** or a **click elsewhere** commits it through the existing `timeline.setTrack {track, name}`
  command, so it is **one undo step**, saved in the project, and nothing new in the engine or the file
  format.
- **Escape** cancels. An **empty, whitespace-only or unchanged** name changes nothing (and adds nothing
  to the history). Surrounding spaces are trimmed (`"  Microphone  "` → `"Microphone"`).
- Works for **video and audio** tracks alike.
- A **double-click elsewhere on the header** (outside the name) still **toggles the track height**,
  exactly as before. Only a double-click on the name itself renames.

## Implementation

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `crates/ui-egui/src/state.rs` | `TimelineView.rename_track: Option<TrackRename { track, text }>` (`#[serde(default)]`), so `ui.inspect` reports the edit in progress (`ui.timeline.rename_track`) and old saved UI state still loads. |

title: Premiere: import .prproj projects with source provenance
author: willluecke
body:
Adds bounded native Rust `.prproj` import through File → Import, CLI and MCP `premiere.import`, with immutable source snapshots and explicit loss diagnostics. Native rendering remains the default; this PR adds no FFmpeg renderer or Python runtime.

> **Updated head:** `9da54b3e`, rebased onto upstream `fa550ce2` (the craft-media dependency migration). Includes cshapiro's fidelity additions below, with original authorship and two non-squashed merges preserved.

### Import and provenance

- Linked or copied timeline media, nested sequences, exact timeline ticks, per-sequence video rates and constant positive speed. Media and nests follow object references; ObjectUID sequence identity handles renamed clips and duplicate display names. Unresolved references use only a warned, unambiguous title fallback.

- Linked imports retain bounded size/head/tail fingerprints; `premiere.hashMedia` explicitly observes current full hashes without rewriting provenance. Copies retain verified SHA-256 identities. Import is one undo step; snapshots survive undo and provenance survives save/reopen.
- Source Text uses the component MatchName and parameter data, never a renamed layer label. Unsupported clips/transitions skip with named warnings after graph validation. Diagnostics aggregate unknown effects by name and native identifier.
- Capacity: 512 MiB plain/expanded XML, 64 MiB compressed input, 16 million nodes; traversal work scales with actual node count and charges repeated references. Sequence/track/item limits remain enforced.

Contributed by [@cshapiro](https://github.com/cshapiro) in [fork PR #1](https://github.com/willluecke/filmcraft/pull/1) and [#2](https://github.com/willluecke/filmcraft/pull/2):
