title: timeline: End parks flush with the last clip; D selects the gap under the playhead
author: WilltheRanger
body:
## What was wrong

**End stopped inside the last clip.** `playhead.end` asked for the sequence end and
`set_playhead` rounded it *down* to a frame boundary. A sequence can end between frames (a clip
moved to a sub-frame time, sound that runs to the sample), and then End parked up to a frame
short. The timecode read the end, but a sliver of the last clip still showed past the playhead.

**D did nothing in a gap.** Select Clip at Playhead only selected clips. With the playhead in
empty time between two clips, nothing was selected and Delete had nothing to close.

## What changes

- **End** rounds up to the first frame boundary at or after the sequence end, so the playhead sits
  flush with the last clip's end as in Premiere Pro, never inside it. A sequence that ends on a
  frame is unchanged.
- **D**, with no clip under the playhead on a targeted track, selects the gap there: the first
  targeted, unlocked track that has one (V1 upwards, then A1 down). Delete or Backspace then closes
  it, as when the gap is clicked (#648, #668). With a clip under the playhead, D selects it as
  before, and now also drops any selected gap, so Delete acts on the clip.
- A selected gap narrower than 3 pt (a frame or two, zoomed out) is drawn 3 pt wide, over the clips'
  edges, so it shows as a thin line instead of disappearing.
- `docs/keyboard.md` notes D's gap behaviour.

## Tests

- Engine: `end_parks_after_a_last_clip_that_ends_between_frames`, plus five `d_…` tests in
  `gap_selection_tests.rs`: in a gap, on the cut before a gap, a one-frame gap, after the last
  clip or on locked tracks, and the targeted track.
- UI (`timeline_playhead_gap_ui.rs`, the real app under egui_kittest with screenshots):
  D then Delete, a one-frame gap zoomed out, and End against the clip's on-screen edge. All three
  failed before the change.
- Unchanged and passing: the engine lib (651), `timeline_gap_ui`, `timeline_scroll_ui`,
  `keyboard_ui`, `timeline_marquee_ui`. rustfmt and clippy `-D warnings` a…

body:
The goal is agents doing all of the editing in the live app. Every control should be clickable by
id, there should be a way to check that, and the app should start when an agent needs it.

Measured with the new `ui.coverage` (widgets a pointer can reach): before this change, 7 of 158

header rows and the status bar. With a clip in Effect Controls it was 51 of 252: the parameter value

title: Slip Monitor: a live four-up in the Program monitor while slipping
author: inspiretelapps
body:
> **Stacked on #2365 and #2366** (split out as requested in review). This branch contains their two commits followed by the feature commit. Only the last commit, `Slip Monitor: a live four-up…`, is new here. Once those two are merged, I'll rebase this PR so that it shows only the feature.

### What and why
With the Slip tool (Y), dragging a clip computed the slip but showed nothing until release. `preview_drag` had no `Drag::Slip` arm, and the Program monitor never knew a slip was happening, so you couldn't see which frames you were choosing.

Now, as in Premiere, the Program monitor shows four frames in a row while you drag:

| Previous clip's Out | New In | New Out | Next clip's In |
|---|---|---|---|
| fixed | follows the drag | follows the drag | fixed |

Under them are the new source timecodes and the offset ("Slip: +25 frames", or "· at the media limit" in red when the media's end holds it back). Releasing commits `timeline.slip`. Escape drops it. Either way the normal Program monitor is back on the next frame.

### How
- **Same maths as the commit.** `engine::slip::preview` (`timeline.slipPreview`) runs `slip_linked`, the function `timeline.slip` now calls too, on a copy of the sequence. The preview equals the committed result at every delta. Linked picture and sound are clamped together (#529, #594), and speed, reverse and mixed frame rates go through `TrackItem::source_time_at`. Nothing in the project changes and no undo step is made.
- **Reuses the Trim Monitor.** `panels::slip_monitor` draws with the Trim Monitor's `picture()` (now `pub(crate)`). The preview lives inside `Drag::Slip` and is recomputed only when the delta changes, so it ends with the drag and nothing stale outlives it.
- **Decoding never blocks the UI, and the newest frame wins.** Each of the four pictures asks for frames in its own frame-server view (`FrameServer::request_in_view`, from #2366). Without separate views, the In and Out frames (same item, same size) would cancel each other's …

title: Add a hex field to colour parameters in Effect Controls
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
## What this adds

Part of #1561, which asks for three things on the keying effects. Re-testing it on 0.9.0 ([comment](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/issues/1561#issuecomment-6250274711)) showed the two eyedroppers work and transparent export is there via ProRes 4444; manual **HEX** entry was the one part still missing. This adds it.

A `#rrggbb` field now sits beside every colour parameter in Effect Controls, next to the swatch and the eyedropper:

- **Ultra Key ▸ Key Color**, **Color Key ▸ Key Color** — the ones the issue is about;
- and, because the row is shared, every other colour parameter (Tint, Lumetri's Shadow/Highlight Tint, Change to Color, …).

That matters when the colour is already known and no pixel on screen holds it: a green screen's published value, a brand colour, a value read off another shot or a style guide. The picker's R/G/B fields could already do it in 8-bit or float, but not in the notation people actually exchange colours in.

## One fix that came with it

Review flagged that the swatch read the parameter through egui's `Rgba`, which is **linear**, while the hex field reads it directly. Checking the renderer settled which is right: `ultra_key` runs each pixel through `effects::enc` (linear → sRGB) before comparing it with the key colour, and uses the key colour exactly as stored (`render/src/vfx/color.rs`). The stored components are therefore **sRGB**.

So the swatch was showing the wrong colour: Ultra Key's default `[0.0, 0.8, 0.2]` is `#00cc33`, but the picker opened on `#00e77c`. It now reads and writes `Color32` through `color_edit_button_srgba`, which puts the swatch, the picker and the hex field on the same value — and on the one the keyer actually uses. Alpha is untouched, as before. `color_parameters_are_stored_srgb_encoded` pins the convention so a change back to linear fails loudly instead of shifting every colour parameter.

The Lumetri Color panel's Shadow Tint and Highlight Tint went through `Rgba` in the same way, in…

title: fix(engine): timeline.slip by i64::MIN clamps instead of overflowing
author: inspiretelapps
body:
Split out of #2351, as requested in review.

### What
`slip_together` (`crates/engine/src/commands.rs`) scaled the linked partners' deltas using `i64::abs()` of the requested delta. A hostile `timeline.slip {"delta": i64::MIN}` overflowed, and so did a `deltaFrames` that saturates to i64::MIN. That is a panic in debug builds, which the command guard reports as an internal error. Release builds wrap the value instead.

### Fix
`unsigned_abs` on both operands. The slip now stops at the start of the media, like any other slip that is too long, with picture and sound together.

### Test
`clip_ops_tests::slipping_by_the_most_negative_delta_clamps_instead_of_overflowing`:
- `delta: i64::MIN` (on the picture) and `deltaFrames: i64::MIN` (on the sound) both clamp to source In 0 for the linked pair.

title: perf(ui): Trim Monitor pictures at a cut inside one take stop cancelling each other
author: inspiretelapps
body:
Split out of #2351 as requested in review, with before/after measurements for the Trim Monitor.

### Problem
A prio-0 `FrameServer::request` replaced every waiting or running foreground job for the same **target and size**: the frame server assumed one picture on screen per target and size. At a cut inside one take, the Trim Monitor's outgoing picture (the last frame of clip A) and incoming picture (the first frame of clip B) are the same media item at the same size. Each refresh, the request for one side dropped or cancelled the other side's decode. The two sides took turns until one decode happened to finish within a single refresh.

### Change
- `FrameServer::request_in_view(key, time, scale, project, view)`: a prio-0 request with a **view** id. `request` is view 0, so every other caller behaves as before.
- Replacement (now the pure function `same_view`) applies only within one view and target and size. Each picture still drops the positions it has moved past, which is what scrubbing needs.
- The Trim Monitor asks for its outgoing and incoming pictures in views 1 and 2 (`trim_monitor.rs`).

### Measured: before (`main`) and after
Release build, 4K 25 fps testsrc2, Apple Silicon under load (absolute times run higher than on an idle machine). Eight runs of each side with the ignored test below, three of them alternating before/after so load hits both sides alike. A cut inside one take at media frame 187 (deep inside a 250-frame GOP), with the roll edit point selected, then 12 roll steps (one per refresh, as holding the trim key does). Times are until **both** pictures show their exact frames. "Given up" counts jobs cancelled while running plus jobs dropped while still waiting (`perf.stats` `frames.cancelled` + `frames.replaced`; the first version of this table counted only the running ones).

| media | select edit point: time | jobs / given up | after 12 roll steps: time | jobs / given up |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| H.264 GOP 250, before | 2314–4654 ms | 26–274 / 92…

title: fix(hevc tests): skip Main10 fixtures an 8-bit-only libx265 cannot encode
author: adventurelands
body:
On aarch64 Arch Linux, nine HEVC Main10 tests fail on main. The decoder is not the problem. Arch Linux ARM's x265 4.3 is built for 8 bits only (`build info ... 8bit`). Asked for `-pix_fmt yuv420p10le`, ffmpeg encodes an 8-bit stream without an error, and the reference decode scales it to 10 bits, so the decoder's output is exactly a quarter of the reference (`got 74 want 296`). With real Main10 streams made by an x86 x265 (8bit+10bit+12bit), the same nine tests pass bit-exact on aarch64.

A 10-bit fixture whose stream ffprobe does not report as `yuv420p10le` is now deleted, so a stale cache cannot linger, and skipped with the reason through `filmcraft_testkit::skip`. With `FILMCRAFT_REQUIRE_ORACLES=1` it still fails loudly instead of passing by skipping.

Tested on aarch64 Arch Linux, on current main: with the native 8-bit x265 the hevc crate passes 76 tests and the Main10 tests print the skip reason; with `FILMCRAFT_REQUIRE_ORACLES=1`, `intra_main10` fails naming the reason; with x86-made Main10 fixtures, all Main10 tests pass.

title: #1356: every effect preset is a command that a key can apply
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Effect presets could only be applied by dragging them from the Effects panel; nothing in Keyboard Shortcuts could be bound to one, so neither a key nor a hardware controller (Stream Deck and the like) could apply a preset.

Every preset, built-in or saved, is now a bindable command: `presets.apply.<name>`, the name lower-cased with every run of other characters as one `-` (`Blur In (Short)` → `presets.apply.blur-in-short`), listed in Keyboard Shortcuts under Presets by the preset's own name (the built-in names are translated). Running it is `presets.apply` with that preset on the selected clips — one undo step, the same as dropping it.

The shortcut registry gets a third source of commands next to the engine's and the frontend's: commands made from data (`Shortcuts::set_dynamic`). The session fills it at start (built-in presets), when the data directory loads the user's presets, and after every successful presets.save / delete / rename / import. `Session::execute` resolves a `presets.apply.<name>` id that names a preset, so the CLI, the control channel and macros can use the same ids.

title: Lumetri: Auto Color Correction for clips or the whole sequence (#1152)
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Adds `lumetri.autoBasic` (Clip > Auto Color Correction, Cmd+Alt+L, and an Auto button in Lumetri > Basic Correction). It solves a starting grade in Lumetri's own Basic sliders from each clip's picture, so the result stays an ordinary, editable grade:

- white balance: grey world over the near-neutral pixels only, capped at +-40; a shot with too few neutral pixels (sunset, aurora, neon) keeps its colours
- exposure: log-average luminance towards 18 % grey, 50 % strength, within +-1.5 stops
- whites / blacks: the 0.5 / 99.5 % percentiles stretched to 2 / 98 %, only ever expanding, within +-50 (whites untouched in HDR)
- contrast / highlights / shadows reset; saturation, other sections and the Input LUT are kept

Targets are the selected video clips, or every picture clip of the sequence with `scope: "sequence"`; all of them in one undo step. Lumetri Color is added where missing. `whiteBalance: false` leaves the balance.

The solver lives in filmcraft_render::auto_tone with unit tests; engine tests cover a dulled demo clip and the whole-sequence scope; a UI test covers the button and the shortcut.

title: Read currency amounts with a scale word as scale then unit
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/tts-text/src/normalize.rs:266-285 (parse_money)` (no existing issue): TTS normalizer reads a currency amount followed by a scale word wrongly: "$2.5 billion" becomes "two dollars and fifty cents billion".

## Cause
`parse_money` read the number after the currency symbol and always appended the currency unit (and cents). It never checked for a following scale word. "$5 million" came out as "five dollars million", and "$2.5 billion" as "two dollars and fifty cents billion".

## Fix
`parse_money` now looks for a whole-word `thousand`, `million`, `billion` or `trillion` (any case) after the amount. If one follows, it reads the number (with "point" and the fraction digits if there are any), then the scale word, then the plural currency unit. That gives "five million dollars" and "two point five billion dollars". Amounts without a scale word read as before.

## Verified
- Regression test `currency_followed_by_scale_word_reads_scale_before_unit`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-tts-text --lib currency_followed_by_scale_word_reads_scale_before_unit`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Abbreviated scale forms ("$5M", "$2bn", "$3k") and plural forms like "millions" are still read as before. Oversized amounts keep their digit-by-digit reading.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

* **New Features**
  * Currency amounts followed by “thousand,” “million,” “billion,” or “trillion” are now spoken with the scale included. Fractional digits are read individually after “point.”
  * Scale words are recognized regardless of capitalization and may be separated from the amount by whitespace.

title: Fix TTML/DFXP export overflow for cue times near i64::MAX
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/captions/src/ttml.rs:58 (clock)` (no existing issue): TTML/DFXP export panics with 'attempt to add with overflow' for cue times near i64::MAX (e.g. an MCC with a huge timecode).

## Cause
`ttml::clock` added the rounding half-millisecond to the tick value in plain i64. For a cue time near i64::MAX, such as an MCC with a huge timecode that saturates to i64::MAX, the addition overflowed. That panics in debug builds and wraps in release builds.

## Fix
`ttml::clock` now calls the shared `format_clock(t, '.')` in lib.rs, which already does the arithmetic in i128. TTML and DFXP clock times now format the same way as SRT and VTT. The `TICKS_PER_MS` import in `ttml.rs` was no longer used, so it is removed.

## Verified
- Regression test `ttml_and_dfxp_write_survive_tick_max`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-captions --test ttml_clock_overflow`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The frame-offset path in `time_expr` and the TTML parser are unchanged.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved TTML and DFXP subtitle output for cues with very large end times, ensuring the end timestamp is included.
  * Standardized TTML clock formatting to improve timestamp consistency.

title: Playback: Linux audio through PipeWire/PulseAudio's native protocol, with reconnects and the ALSA fallback (#106, #2117; part 2 of 2, on #2644)
author: adventurelands
body:
Fixes #106 and #2117. Part 2 of 2: the app side. **It is on top of #2644 (part 1, the protocol client, now its own crate `crates/pulse`)**, split at @FredApps's request; until #2644 merges its three commits show here too, and the last three commits are this PR. Supersedes #332, at @Chace-Berry's request: the client in #2644 starts with his commit, and `pulse_out.rs` here starts from his #332 (co-authored).

**What it changes** (`apps/filmcraft/src/pulse_out.rs`, `audio.rs`, `main.rs`; the playback clock in `ui-egui/src/lib.rs` and `source_playback.rs`):
- **Backend choice:** on Linux, with the default device class and a reachable PipeWire or PulseAudio socket, playback goes through the native client; otherwise, and for `PULSE_SERVER=tcp:…`, through cpal/ALSA as before. Settings ▸ Audio Hardware ▸ Device Class "ALSA" keeps cpal. This is a default change for Linux users with a sound server, which is a maintainer's call; it can also be made opt-in behind the device class.
- **Output:** the sink chosen in Settings, or the default one, with its own channel count, so a 5.1 sequence plays discrete on a 5.1 sink and Settings shows the sink's channels (it was fixed at stereo).
- **Reconnects:** a stream the server drops while playing is reconnected every 250 ms for up to 3 s (a server restart), at most 3 drops in 10 s. Meanwhile the output reports `waiting` and the UI clock holds instead of giving up on the sound at its 1 s stall limit.
- **Fallback to ALSA:** a first stream the server refuses, or reconnects that run out, hand the same mixer to cpal, the clock going on from the mixer's position (from CodeRabbit: it used the frames heard). When cpal runs at another rate than the mixer (it falls back to a device's default rate when the one asked for is unsupported), the mixer now plays resampled to the device's rate, with the clock counted at the mixer's rate, instead of the handover giving up and leaving playback silent until restarted (from your re-review). Test: `the_alsa_h…

title: audio: work around distorted Razer 7.1 WASAPI output
author: trikesh32
body:
Razer’s “7.1 Surround Sound” WASAPI endpoint can produce distorted/hissing audio with the float format FilmCraft previously preferred, including in the bundled demo (#2411). Prefer advertised signed 32-bit PCM for that endpoint using the existing conversion path, following the workaround reported in [CPAL #892](https://github.com/RustAudio/cpal/issues/892#issuecomment-2364194193).

Settings ▸ Audio Hardware now has **7.1 surround compatibility (Windows)** with three modes:
- **Auto** (default): match the exact case-insensitive name `7.1 Surround Sound` or `Razer 7.1 Surround Sound`, either alone or as a parenthesized suffix such as `Speakers (7.1 Surround Sound)`. Arbitrary substring matches no longer trigger the workaround.
- **Off**: restore the previous format-selection behavior, including default-rate fallback, even for a matching name.
- **On**: prefer supported PCM on the selected WASAPI output even if renamed. This is a global audio preference, not a per-device override. All modes leave non-WASAPI hosts unchanged.

The preference persists and is exposed as `audioHardware.surroundCompatibility` (`auto`, `on`, `off`) through the existing preferences commands and UI automation. Selection preserves the default channel count and requested rate when supported, tries PCM at the default rate when the requested rate is unavailable, and falls back to advertised formats if PCM is unavailable.

The display name remains a heuristic, not a vendor identity. CPAL 0.16’s common device interface does not expose hardware IDs, and we have no verified device-ID or uniquely identifying format signature from the affected machine. Another driver could use the same name; Off provides an escape hatch. Windows/Razer hardware validation is still outstanding: the tests do not establish that the hiss is gone or that hardware channel mapping and timing are correct.

title: #1616: perf.stats says how many export frames the GPU rendered and why it is off when it is
author: 00xJS
body:
For #1616 (its third point): an export that asked for the GPU and rendered on the CPU looked exactly like a slow GPU export, because the only trace of the fallback was a `log::error!` and `filmcraft-cli` runs no logger.

**Change:** `perf.stats` ▸ `export` gains `gpu`: `frames` the GPU frame renderer composited, `fallbacks` it handed to the CPU, and `disabled`, the reason GPU rendering is off for this process once it is (`null` while it renders or before an export asked). The reason comes from the export renderer: the first device error or device loss (`mark_device_failed`, which already logged it), and now also a missing adapter or device at creation. It is kept once, bounded to 500 characters. `GpuRenderStats` carries it (so it loses `Copy`; its one destructuring use is unchanged).

**Why not stderr:** `perf.stats` is already where a CLI session reads the hardware decode / encode counters, and a bridge session can ask the live app the same question.

This is the diagnostic half of the issue only: it does not change which adapter the export instance opens (#2138 fixes the FXC compile that caused the fallback). Measured together on an RX 6900 XT, see the issue.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings` and the engine / export / gpu tests pass.

author: 00xJS
body:
For #2421 (its first half, layout changes lost between launches; the demo-project half is a separate question, see the issue).

title: Keep '#' inside a quoted .cube TITLE when parsing
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/lut.rs:236 (parse_cube strips '#' comments before reading TITLE); writer at to_cube ~line 290` (no existing issue): A .cube TITLE containing '#' is truncated on the write/parse round trip.

## Cause
`Lut::parse_cube` strips everything after the first '#' from every line before it reads the keyword. A title such as `TITLE "Look #2"` was therefore cut to `Look`.

## Fix
The TITLE branch now reads the title from the raw line. If the title is quoted, it takes the text up to the closing quote, so a '#' inside the quotes is kept. An unquoted title, or one with a trailing comment such as `TITLE "Look" # note`, still uses the comment-stripped line.

## Verified
- Regression test `lut::tests::cube_title_with_hash_roundtrips`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-color cube_title_with_hash_roundtrips`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Comment stripping for all other keywords and data rows is unchanged. I also left `parse_3dl` alone, because its writer puts the title in a `#` comment and never reads it back.

title: interchange: FCP7 retimed clips read and write <in>/<out> in the scaled domain
author: danusiojr
body:
### The bug

In Final Cut Pro 7 XML, when a clipitem carries a Time Remap (`timeremap`) filter, `<in>` and `<out>` are in the **scaled** domain: source time ÷ speed, so `out − in == end − start` like any other clip. Premiere Pro reads them that way. A 50% clip with `<in>` = frame 408 plays from frame **204** of the source.

`fcp7.rs` turned `<in>` into ticks with no speed applied, so a retimed clip played the right *length* from the wrong *place*, and slow clips near the end of a take ran past the end of their media. The exporter wrote the same real-time domain, so FilmCraft's own round trip stayed consistent while Premiere read those files offset. Nothing reported it.

### Measured on real material

52 retimed clips from a finished Premiere project: 59.94p camera files in a 29.97 sequence, constant speeds from 30% to 80%. For each clip, the source range Premiere used was read from the `.prproj`. An xmeml with `<in>`/`<out>` in the scaled domain was written and imported with `filmcraft-cli exec file.import`, then read back with `inspect sequence`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| clips whose source in **and** out match Premiere's within one source frame | 2 / 52 (both start at 0 s, where ÷speed changes nothing) | 51 / 52; the last is 16.7 ms off, the frame rounding of integer `<in>`/`<out>` times the speed |
| FilmCraft in ÷ Premiere in | 1 / speed on every clip | 1 |
| largest in-point error | 79 s (a 40% clip) | 16.7 ms |
| clips running past the end of their media | 12 | 1 (Premiere's own range ends 3 ms past it too) |

A rendered frame confirmed the "before" column. At the middle of a 60% clip, `filmcraft-cli render` matched the source at `in / speed` (mean abs diff 2.5 / 255) and not the frame Premiere shows (31.4 / 255).

### The change

- **Import:** for a forward constant speed ≠ 1 read from `<in>`/`<out>`, the source in/out are multiplied by the speed (`common::scaled`) before the clip is built. Freeze frames, reverse clips, the no-remap ratio path and…

title: fix(export): a bitrateKbps in settings is the bitrate over an adaptive preset
author: derektrimm
body:
Split out of #2189, as asked in its review.

## Problem

A `bitrateKbps` given inside `settings` is ignored when the starting settings have an adaptive bitrate, which every Match Source preset does. `ExportSettings::resolve` uses `adaptive_bitrate` in place of `bitrate_kbps` whenever it is set, and only the flat `bitrateKbps` parameter clears it. So on 720x480 at 29.97:

| Parameters | Bitrate before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `preset: "Match Source - Adaptive High Bitrate", bitrateKbps: 5000` | 5,000 kbps | 5,000 kbps |
| `preset: "Match Source - Adaptive High Bitrate", settings: {bitrateKbps: 5000}` | 2,072 kbps (the preset's 0.2 bits per pixel) | 5,000 kbps |

The same applies to `export.queue.add`, `export.resolve`, `export.presets.save` and `filmcraft-cli export --preset ... --settings '{"bitrateKbps": ...}'`, which all go through `settings_from_params`.

## Fix

In `settings_from_params` (`crates/engine/src/export_tools.rs`), a `bitrateKbps` in `settings` clears the adaptive bitrate, as the flat parameter does, unless `adaptiveBitrate` is given with it. `docs/architecture.md` says so under Presets.

## What does not change

- Without a preset, or with a preset that has a fixed bitrate, the settings resolve as before: `adaptive_bitrate` is already `None` there.
- `adaptiveBitrate` given in `settings`, with or without `bitrateKbps`, is used as before.
- Unpreset H.264 exports still start from `ExportSettings::default()`. That part of #2189 stays there for a maintainer to decide.

## Tests

`export_tests::settings_bitrate_replaces_a_presets_adaptive_bitrate`: over the default preset, `bitrateKbps: 5000` in `settings` and flat both resolve to 5,000 kbps with no adaptive bitrate; without a preset, both forms resolve to 5,000; `adaptiveBitrate: 0.1` given with it still resolves adaptively (1,036). The preset alone resolves to 2,072. Without the change it fails on the first `settings` case (`left: Some(0.2)`, `right: None`).

title: #2185: preview files are read in place, not loaded whole
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:

title: #1142: no 60 Hz polling for queued frames, no media file list every frame
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:

title: Reject unsupported Time Remapping speed edits
author: jackcanon
body:
Time Remapping Speed accepts values and keys, persists them, and displays interpolated percentages even though the render clock does not consume this intrinsic parameter. Users can receive a successful edit with unchanged output.

Reject unsupported `time_remap.speed` edits with an actionable error directing users to `clip.speedDuration` / Clip > Speed/Duration for constant speed. Guard direct named/indexed parameter edits, animation toggling, individual key edits and grouped moves. Grouped validation rejects the whole request before mutation. Existing project data remains readable; deleting legacy inert keys and resetting the static value remain possible. Reset alone preserves keys.

This does **not implement speed ramps**, migrate existing ramps, or change media-time mapping. Related: #510 (the feature gap remains open).

Validation:

- Three synthetic engine regressions cover unsupported routes without project mutation, legacy cleanup and mixed supported/unsupported grouped moves, and supported constant speed plus ordinary animation. Before the guard: two fail and the supported-control test passes.

title: #1564: Sequence ▸ Auto Reframe Sequence…
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
A copy of the active sequence in another aspect ratio — Vertical 9:16, Square
1:1, Vertical 4:5 or Horizontal 16:9 — whose video clips follow their
subject, as Premiere's command does. The new frame keeps the old one's short
side (1920×1080 → 1080×1920, 1080×1080, 1080×1350), the copy opens, the
original is untouched, and the whole thing is one undo step.

The Auto Reframe effect alone could not do this: it works inside the clip's
own picture, so it can pan a window across it but not grow it, and a 16:9
clip in a 9:16 frame stayed letterboxed (measured: the top rows of the frame
were black). So every video clip with a picture of its own is scaled to fill
the new frame — Motion Scale and its keyframes by how much more of the frame
the picture must cover there than in the old one, Scale to Frame Size folded
into the Scale, Position offsets from the centre scaled with it — and gets
Auto Reframe set to the target aspect and the chosen Motion Preset (slower /
default / faster), which then picks the window that shows. Graphics,
adjustment layers and audio stay as they are.

Engine: `sequence.autoReframe {sequence?, aspect, motion?, name?}`
(crates/engine/src/auto_reframe.rs). UI: the menu entry opens a dialog with
Sequence Name, Target Aspect and Motion Preset (the default name follows the
aspect until it is edited); automation ids `autoReframe.*`. The menu label is
translated in the catalogs the coverage test requires.

Fixes #1564

title: #2194: FCPXML <title> imports as editable text instead of being skipped
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
DaVinci Resolve writes its Text and Text+ titles, and Final Cut Pro its
titles, as FCPXML `<title>` elements. The importer skipped them with a
warning, so titles were lost and left gaps.

A `<title>` now imports as a graphic clip with one text layer:
- the text of its `<text>` runs, in the first run's `text-style-def` style:
  font, size (scaled from 1080 lines, as title templates are authored),
  face, colour, bold / italic, alignment, stroke and shadow (FCP's
  `shadowOffset` angle converted to the graphic shadow's convention);
- at the title's `Position` parameter (pixels from the frame centre, y up);
- with its timing, lane, label, enabled state, markers, and `adjust-transform`
  / `adjust-blend` on the clip, like other clips.
The template's own animation and look are not carried; the import report says
so once per title, and names titles whose runs have different styles. A title
without text, or on an audio lane, is skipped and reported.

Test: a Resolve-style document with a connected title and a primary-storyline
title (style, position, timing, opacity, shared graphic item, report lines).

Refs #2194: this is the import side. The export half (a round trip that keeps titles) stays open in #2194 and #2222, so merging this should not close #2194.

title: #1584: control: a request that timed out is cancelled, never run later
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
The control server answered `timeout` after 60 s but left the request queued for the UI thread.
On Wayland a hidden window draws no frames, so the queue only drained when the window showed
again, and then the command ran anyway: a client that retried after the timeout applied its
edit twice.

A `ControlRequest` now carries a small state shared with the transport (`ControlTicket`):
waiting, running, taken, abandoned. The UI thread claims a request before handling it
(`begin`) and drops one the transport abandoned; a `Retry` outcome puts it back to waiting.
On timeout the transport abandons a request still waiting, so it can never run, and replies
`{"ok": false, "ran": false, …}`; if the request already ran it replies `ran: true` (its effect
stands, only the reply is late) or passes on a reply that landed in the meantime. A request
the app dropped is no longer reported as a timeout. Documented in docs/control-protocol.md.

Not changed: on Wayland a hidden window still does not drain the queue (it needs a wake-up
outside the egui frame); the timeout is now safe to retry instead.

Tests: control_server (timeout before the UI took it, after it ran, after a retry, a reply in
time, a dropped request; the UI side is played synchronously in the wake hook, so nothing
depends on thread timing) and ui_control_input::a_request_its_transport_gave_up_on_never_runs
(the real app drops the abandoned playhead edit; the same request not abandoned moves it).

Refs #1584 (the late-run part; #1618 / #2376 address the hidden-window part)

title: Preserve remix seams, waveform and manual Out trimming
author: straywill
body:
Remixed clips persist optional local seam-level envelopes, draw waveforms through the playback reader and show splice markers at output-piece boundaries. Selection-tool Out trimming preserves the stored arrangement and can restore a trimmed tail to the plan end. Older plans without joinLevels retain their original playback.

title: Link stacked video clips that overlap the same audio together
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2433

## Cause
When more than one video clip was selected, `clip.link` gave each video clip its own link and let each audio clip join only one of them. A second video clip stacked over the same audio (for example a nest duplicated onto V1 and V2) found no audio left to pair with and stayed unlinked.

## Fix
`clip.link` now finds each video clip's overlapping audio partners without excluding audio already claimed by another video clip. Video clips that share an audio clip are merged into one link, so stacked clips and their audio all get the same link ID.

## Not changed
Side-by-side video/audio pairs that share no audio still get one link per pair (#507). The rule that a clip with no partner stays unlinked is unchanged, and so is the single-video path that links everything into one link.

title: Preserve per-channel shaper domain in .cube round trip
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/lut.rs:290 (Lut::to_cube, the `both` branch)` (no existing issue): .cube with both a 1D and a 3D table loses per-channel input domains on write/parse round trip.

## Cause
`Lut::to_cube` wrote a shaper's domain as `LUT_1D_INPUT_RANGE` using only channel 0 when the LUT had both a 1D and a 3D table. `parse_cube` accepts per-channel `DOMAIN_MIN`/`DOMAIN_MAX` for the shaper in that case, so channels 1 and 2 lost their domain on a round trip.

## Fix
In the both-tables case, `to_cube` now writes `DOMAIN_MIN`/`DOMAIN_MAX` for the shaper when its domain differs between channels. A domain that is the same on every channel is still written as `LUT_1D_INPUT_RANGE`.

## Verified
- Regression test `lut::tests::cube_shaper_per_channel_domain_round_trips`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-color cube_shaper_per_channel_domain_round_trips`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `dev_icon::tests::desktop_file_matches_the_packaged_fields`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
The 3D cube's `LUT_3D_INPUT_RANGE` output is unchanged. In the both-tables case the format has no way to express a per-channel cube domain, and `parse_cube` only produces a uniform one. Single-table output is unchanged.

title: #1680: copy and paste effects and effect settings in Effect Controls
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Closes #1680.

Effects can be copied and pasted in Effect Controls. The Timeline's Paste Attributes… already copied whole clips' attributes; now single effects can be copied too, as in Premiere.

**Engine** (new module `effect_clipboard.rs`)

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| `effects.copy {clip?, indices?}` | Copies effects with their settings, keyframes and masks. Without params it copies the effect selected in Effect Controls. |
| `effects.paste {clips?}` | Pastes onto clips of the same kind (video/audio). A standard effect is added. A fixed effect (Motion, Opacity, Volume…) takes the copied settings instead of being added twice. By default the targets are the selection plus its linked partners; clips named in the call are used as given. |

- Each paste is one undo step.
- These requests are refused with an error, and the project and history stay unchanged:
  - pasting with nothing copied;
  - an unknown clip or index, or a non-list `indices`;
  - an empty copy;
  - pasting video effects onto an audio clip;
  - Paste Settings onto an effect of another kind.

**UI**
- The effect header's right-click menu has **Copy**, **Paste** and **Paste Settings**. Paste Settings is enabled only when the copied effects include this effect's kind.
- In Effect Controls, Cmd/Ctrl+C copies the selected effect and Cmd/Ctrl+V pastes onto the clip it shows. These keys no longer reach the Timeline clip clipboard there.

title: Fix AudioSamples time display for negative times
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/time/src/lib.rs:418 (format_time, TimeDisplay::AudioSamples)` (no existing issue): Audio Samples time display shows a malformed value for negative times.

## Cause
The AudioSamples branch of `format_time` used `div_euclid` and `rem_euclid` and then formatted the signed seconds directly. For a negative time, the minus sign ended up inside the seconds field (`00:00:-1:00000`). The sample remainder was also taken from the floor second, so fractional negative times got the wrong sample count.

## Fix
The AudioSamples branch now works on the absolute tick value. It splits that into hours, minutes, seconds and samples, and puts a leading `-` in front when the time is negative. This matches the Timecode, Frames and Feet modes. The regression test covers `-1 s` (`-00:00:01:00000`) and `-1.5 s` (`-00:00:01:24000`).

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::audio_samples_negative_time_has_leading_minus`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-time audio_samples_negative`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `dev_icon::tests::desktop_file_matches_the_packaged_fields`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed

title: #2469: the media pool closes least recently used decoded stills past a budget
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Closes #2469. It is also the pool-side half of #2464; the narrow Media Browser fix is still separate.

Decoded stills (and animated images) used to stay in the media pool until the project closed, so memory grew by one decoded picture per still ever rendered. The pool now keeps a byte budget and closes the least recently used sources that hold decoded pictures.

**Changes**
- `MediaSource::resident_bytes()` is a new trait method, defaulting to 0. It returns:
  - for `StillSource`: the decoded frame;
  - for `AnimatedSource`: all its frames;
  - for the pool's wrappers (`UnsupportedAsSlate`, `DamagedAsSlate`, `ProxySource`): what they wrap.
- `MediaPool`:
  - records when each cached source and proxy was last asked for: every cache hit in `resolve` / `proxy_source`, and every insert;
  - after each insert, closes the least recently used sources with `resident_bytes() > 0` until the total fits `DEFAULT_RESIDENT_BUDGET` (1 GiB) or `set_resident_budget`;
  - never closes the source just inserted (it is about to be used), and never closes video demuxers (they report 0).
  - Closing only drops the pool's `Arc`. A render still holding the source keeps it alive, and the next use opens it again from its file.
  - Offline status and damaged-frame counts live outside the sources, so they are untouched.
- `perf.stats` now also reports `media.residentBytes`.
- Lock order is `sources → proxies → used` everywhere, and no lock is held across the opener calls.

Not in this PR: a Settings ▸ Memory field for the budget. The API is there (`set_resident_budget`) if the maintainers want one.

**Test** (`media_pool::tests::decoded_stills_past_the_budget_are_closed_least_recently_used_first`):
- Imports 8 PNGs and renders each with a 3-still budget, then checks:
  - the resident bytes never exceed the budget, and exactly the 3 most recent stills stay open;
  - using an older still again reopens it and evicts the least recently used one;
  - a source a render still holds keeps working after…

author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Fixes part 2 of #2430 (caret positioning). Parts 1 and 3 (clipboard pasting, rich text formatting) are not in this PR.

**Bug:** while editing text on the Program monitor, a plain click inside the text did nothing (`_ if in_edit => {}` in the click branch of `panels/graphics.rs`). title: fix(mcp): pin doc_inspect's sequence to the reported active id (#1477)
author: MichaelMuClaude
body:
## Summary

`#1477` reports that bridge-mode project inspection sometimes returns answers that aren't quite right, without pinning down which field. This finds and fixes a real race: `doc_inspect` composes `project.inspect` and `sequence.inspect` as two separate round trips to the app (two lock scopes in headless mode, two TCP round trips in bridge mode). `sequence.inspect` with no `item` answers for whichever sequence is active *now*, not the one `project.inspect` just reported — so if the active sequence changes in that window (another MCP client, or the app's own UI, switching sequence tabs), the pair comes back inconsistent: `project.activeSequence` names one sequence while `sequence` describes a different one.

## Reproduction

Built this branch's `filmcraft-cli` and ran it as a real bridge-mode MCP client (`mcp --bridge`) against a live `filmcraft --control` app with two sequences. While hammering `doc_inspect` through the real MCP stdio protocol, an independent control-channel connection flipped `sequence.open` between the two sequences as fast as it could. Result: **~298/300 `doc_inspect` calls** came back with `project.activeSequence` and `sequence.id` naming different sequences. This is a wide window, not a rare edge case — it should reproduce for anyone running two concurrent clients against the same bridge, or an agent polling `doc_inspect` while a person switches timeline tabs.

## Fix

Read `project.inspect`'s `activeSequence` id first, then pass it explicitly as `sequence.inspect`'s `item` parameter, instead of letting the second call fall back to whatever is active at the time it happens to run. This makes the pair self-consistent: `sequence`, when not null, always describes the sequence `project.activeSequence` names.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `doc_inspect_pins_the_sequence_to_the_reported_active_id` (`crates/automation/src/server.rs`): a fake bridge-mode app answers `project.inspect` with `activeSequence: 21` and answers `sequence.inspect` for whi…

title: #2253: Ctrl+Plus no longer scales the interface one way only; View > Reset Interface Zoom
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Closes #2253.

**Cause.** In the default (Premiere) keyboard layout, the Timeline binds Ctrl+= and Ctrl+- to Increase/Decrease Video Track Height, and Ctrl+0 is Toggle All Video Targets. FilmCraft's shortcut handler consumes those keys before egui's built-in interface zoom sees them. Ctrl+**Plus** was bound to nothing: that is the `+` key, i.e. Shift+= on US layouts, the keypad `+`, or what a mouse button mapped to "page zoom" sends. So it fell through to egui and scaled the whole interface. The way back, Ctrl+- and the reset Ctrl+0, was taken by FilmCraft, so the scale could only grow until restart. That matches the report on Windows 11.

**Fix**
- `menus::bindings`: a chord on `=` also takes `+` with the same modifiers and panel, unless something is bound to `+` itself. Ctrl+Plus now does what Ctrl+= does in each layout, so the interface can no longer be scaled one way only. The FilmCraft preset (`=` zoom in, `-` zoom out) is unchanged.
- New **View ▸ Reset Interface Zoom** (`view.resetInterfaceZoom`). It sets the interface back to Settings ▸ Appearance ▸ UI Scale, or the system scale with Auto, whatever scaled it. It has no default shortcut, because Ctrl+0 is taken; users can bind one. It is translated in the eight required catalogs.

**Test:** `tests/interface_zoom_ui.rs`. With the Timeline focused, Ctrl+Plus leaves the interface scale alone and makes the video tracks taller, as Ctrl+= does. On `main` the scale becomes 1.1. After a zoom to 1.75, View ▸ Reset Interface Zoom returns it to 1.0.

title: #1985: a panel closed while floating opens again floating where it was
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Closes #1985.

A panel closed while floating (its ✕, Close Panel, or the control channel) used to come back **docked** when opened again from the Window menu, because `show_panel` always re-docks a missing panel with `open_near`.

**Change**
- `apply_dock` remembers the floating rect of a panel closed while floating, in `UiState::closed_floating`, which is `serde(default)` so older state loads. A panel closed while docked forgets any remembered rect.
- `show_panel` docks the panel as before. If it was closed while floating, it then floats it again at its last rect with `Action::Float`, through the shared docking model, so the layout stays valid. Non-finite rects are ignored, and a tiny one is grown to a usable minimum size.

**Test:** `shared_docking_ui::a_panel_closed_while_floating_reopens_floating_where_it_was`. It floats Info, closes it, and reopens it from the Window menu: it floats again with the same rect. Docked and then closed, it reopens docked.

body:
## Summary

`#1845` reports several issues with `clip.audioChannels`; this addresses the concrete, minimal repro from that issue: a format-only (or otherwise `channels`-less) call made while the project selection happens to be empty silently resets the timeline clip's `source_channels` to `[]` instead of being rejected.

## Root cause

`audio_channels()` took its "timeline clip" branch (which only ever reads the `channels` param) whenever **either** no project item was selected **or** `channels` was given:

```rust
if items.is_empty() || p.get("channels").is_some() {
    // timeline audio clips: which source channels each plays
    ...
    let chans: Vec<u16> = p.get("channels")....unwrap_or_default();
    ...
    it.source_channels = chans.clone();  // [] when `channels` was never given
```

So with no project item selected and no `channels` key at all (e.g. a stray `{"format": null}`, or even `{}`), the branch still ran and `unwrap_or_default()` quietly replaced the clip's existing channel map with `[]`.

## Fix

Only `channels` now decides which branch runs. The one combination the command genuinely can't act on — no project item selected **and** no `channels` — is now a `clip.audioChannels` error (`"select a clip with audio, or a project item to set its format"`) instead of a silent reset.

This fixes the issue's minimal repro specifically. The issue also describes dialog-UX behavior (truncating on untouched OK, nonexistent mono channels in the picker), downmixed nested-channel selection, and Breakout to Mono channel counts — those are separate problems in different code paths and aren't addressed by this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `audio_channels_rejects_a_channel_less_call_with_no_item_selected` (`crates/engine/src/clip_ops_tests.rs`): sets `channels: [1]` on a timeline clip with no project item selected, then confirms both a `format: null` call and a bare `{}` call are rejected and the clip's `source_channels` survives unchanged.
- [x] Verified the new te…

title: GPU: bound export read-back waits
author: jahvari
body:
## Summary

Bound GPU export read-back polling and callback waits so unavailable results can fall back to CPU rendering. This is the independent GPU split from #1575; original authorship is preserved.

The review follow-up retires staging buffers after failed mapping or conversion. title: Tools: reflow into columns, widening the strip to fit (builds on #2178)
author: liangforstudy
body:
**Builds on #2178.** Until that lands this PR also shows its commits; the change here is the last commit, `tools: reflow into columns, widening the strip to fit (#1983)`. It is one of three ways to keep every tool reachable when the Tools panel is too short (#1983); the alternatives are #2168 and #2496.

- When the Tools strip is too short for one column (Program dragged down over it, or a large UI scale), its tools fill a second column, then a third, top to bottom, with 8 pt left under the last row. Before, the ones that didn't fit weren't shown at all.
- The strip widens to fit: its minimum width is as many columns as its height takes (48 pt for one, 36 pt more for each other). With #2178's shrink-then-push, that room comes from the nearest panel that isn't a strip. Made taller again, Tools narrows back to the width it had.

**Why it needs #2178:** the columns themselves (`columns`, `width_for`) are plain functions in `tools.rs`, but a 64 pt strip only fits one column. Widening the strip to fit more needs the dock to know a panel's minimum and give it room, which is #2178's per-panel minimum (`min_extent`, `fit_minimums`).

**Tests:**
- `dock::tests::tools_strip_widens_adds_column`: a shorter Tools strip widens, and a taller one goes back to its width.
- `panels::tools::tests::a_short_panel_shows_every_tool_in_more_columns`: every tool stays inside a panel 700, 150, 80 and 40 pt tall.

**Checked** (Windows 11): `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, the `dock` and `panels::tools` tests (14 passed).

**Tested by hand** (release build, Windows 11, 125% display scaling): Tools reflowing into columns and widening as Program is dragged down over it, and narrowing back.

title: #2022: simplified Chinese glyph forms and simplified-only characters in the Chinese interface
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Fixes #2022 (both parts: Japanese glyph forms such as 确, and missing simplified-only characters such as 运, in the Simplified Chinese interface).

**Causes**
- `theme::install` always put the Japanese craft-fonts **before** the Chinese faces. The hanzi both have (确, 直, 骨…) therefore took Japanese forms, even in the Chinese interface.
- Without craft-fonts, `cjk.rs` picks an installed face that covers `SAMPLE`. That sample had no simplified-only characters, so a Japanese-first face such as Hiragino could be picked. It lacks 运, 简 and 单, which showed as boxes.

**Changes**
- `theme::font_definitions(language)`: in the Chinese interface the Chinese faces (craft-fonts Hans/Hant, else the system face) come before the Japanese ones. In every other language the order is as before: Japanese first, so Japanese text keeps Japanese forms.
- The app installs the fonts again when the interface language changes. Before, the stack was built once per theme install.
- `cjk::SAMPLE` now includes 运确简单, so only a face that really has the simplified forms is taken.
- `cjk::install` is split into `install_chinese` / `install_korean`. Korean still comes last.
- Two existing font tests (`japanese_renders_with_craft_fonts`, `japanese_needs_an_installed_font`) assumed nothing follows the craft fonts in a stack. With craft-fonts on a machine that has a Hangul system face (Apple SD Gothic Neo, Malgun Gothic), `system-korean` comes after them and they failed; that happens on `main` too. They now skip installed system faces the same way they already skipped the Hebrew one.

**Tests**
- `theme::tests::chinese_faces_come_first_only_in_the_chinese_interface` checks that `chinese_first` is true only for zh-CN. With a Japanese craft font and a Chinese face both present, it also checks the order in the real stack: Chinese before Japanese for zh-CN, the other way round for English.
- `cjk::tests::the_chinese_sample_has_simplified_only_characters`.

Run both with and without craft-fonts (CLAUDE.md, fonts)…

title: #2445: Korean (and other IME) text being composed shows on the monitor and is kept
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Fixes #2445 (Korean typed on the Program monitor doesn't appear). It is probably also the cause of #1999 (Korean subtitles can't be entered) and #1299 (Chinese input in the Text feature), but those aren't verified with a real IME here.

**Cause.** The monitor's text editor handled only `Ime(Commit)` (#1083). Korean IMEs commit a syllable only when the next one starts; until then the syllable is a *preedit*, which the editor never drew. So while typing nothing appeared, and when the edit ended (Escape, a click elsewhere, another panel) the last syllable, which was never committed, was lost. The Properties panel uses egui's own `TextEdit`, which draws and keeps preedit text; that is why Korean works there.

**Changes** (`panels/graphics.rs`)
- `GfxEdit` gets `preedit`, `serde(default)`. `Ime(Preedit)` updates it, and a commit clears it before inserting.
- The composing text is drawn at the caret, underlined, on a dark backing so it reads on any picture. It has the automation id `program.textEdit.preedit`, and the IME rectangle grows to include it.
- `end_edit` commits a pending preedit into the layer's text (replacing a selection) as one `graphics.setText`, as a text field would. This covers every way an edit ends: Escape, a click elsewhere, leaving the panel.

**Test:** `graphics_handles_ui::korean_being_composed_shows_and_is_kept_when_the_edit_ends`.
1. Types "A", then sends the IME events for 한 (ㅎ → 하 → 한) and checks that the preedit element shows 한.
2. Sends Commit(한) plus Preedit(구), and the text is "A한".
3. Presses Escape: the edit ends and the text is "A한구".

Not verified with a real Korean IME on Windows or macOS; the events are the ones egui-winit forwards.

title: Count decoded standalone audio against the shared media budget
author: jackcanon
body:
Dependent draft: this branch is stacked on @Felix-Helleckes’s existing #2475, exact head `183e36a10556a6e7973d0f054320d610e988469d`. That proposal owns the shared resident-byte interface, pool eviction and telemetry infrastructure; its commits retain their original authorship. Our incremental correction makes standalone decoded audio participate in that mechanism. Please merge the dependency and rebase this contribution before integrating it.

Standalone `AudioFileSource` and the Vorbis path in `OggSource` currently report zero retained sample bytes, so they stay outside the proposed shared budget. This change measures allocated planar sample capacity once when decoding finishes and exposes that stored count through `resident_bytes()`. All three standalone construction paths are covered. Pool lookups do not scan samples or decode under the pool lock. Streamed Opus behavior, decoding, resampling and file/project formats are unchanged.

Related to #2473; this is a bounded first step, not a full streaming fix. The existing pool policy retains the source just opened even above budget, and external live references remain usable after eviction. A single active long file still decodes whole. Encoded-file storage, decoder temporaries and allocator page retention are not included in the sample counter. Reopening costs a full decode; live playback and other-platform qualification remain open. Do not close #2473 based on this draft.

title: #2473: standalone audio holds its decoded PCM in a shared byte-budgeted cache
author: chiragjangiir
body:
Fixes #2473

## Problem

Standalone audio sources hold every decoded sample for the life of the project. `AudioFileSource` (MP3, MP2, AAC, FLAC, AIFF) and `OggSource`'s Vorbis path both keep planar f32 in a field: ~23 MB per minute of stereo 48 kHz, so a 5 MB MP3 costs ~230 MB and a podcast edit (2–3 hours across a handful of files) holds 3–4 GB. Video containers already share the GOP cache under `FRAME_BUDGET` and WAV reads in place; audio had no counter and no bound, and `perf.stats` showed nothing for it.

## What changed

This is the smaller of the two options in the issue (byte-budgeted shared cache with whole-file re-decode on a miss), as suggested there.

- **`crates/media/src/cache.rs`**: new `AudioCache` next to `FrameCache` — byte-budgeted LRU of planar PCM keyed by `u64`, with `get` / `insert` / `get_or_insert_with` / `remove` / `clear` / `stats`. Eviction drops least-recently-read entries until under 90% of budget, but never the entry just inserted: a file whose PCM alone exceeds the budget still plays, since re-decoding it on every read would cost more than the memory it holds. Unit tests cover LRU-by-bytes, the oversized-entry rule, decode-once, remove and clear.
- **`crates/codecs/src/audio.rs`**: `AudioFileSource` keeps the file's `bytes` and a cache key instead of `samples`. `decode()` runs the decode once, inserts the PCM into the process-wide cache (`AUDIO_BUDGET` = 512 MB, ~22 min of 48 kHz stereo); `audio()` reads through `get_or_insert_with`, re-decoding the file on an eviction miss.
- **`crates/codecs/src/ogg.rs`**: `Kind::Pcm` stores `(rate, pcm_key)`; a read after eviction re-runs `decode_vorbis` from the demuxed file, which the source already holds. `OpusState` moves inside a `Box` (the enum-size lint fires now that `Kind::Pcm` no longer balances `Kind::Opus`).
- **`crates/engine/src/perf.rs`**: `decode.audioCacheMB` and `decode.audioCacheBudgetMB` next to `cacheMB`/`cacheBudgetMB`, as the issue asks. (`stillsCacheMB` isn't on main yet, so …

title: platform, gpu: support Windows on ARM64 NVENC (RTX Spark) and fix off-screen wgpu readback
author: mweinbach
body:
## Summary

- **Windows on ARM64 NVENC (`crates/platform`)**: On Windows on ARM (`aarch64-pc-windows-msvc`), NVIDIA's `nvEncodeAPI64.dll` in `System32` is an `x86_64` binary for x64 emulation, so `LoadLibraryExW` fails with `ERROR_BAD_EXE_FORMAT` in native ARM64 builds (such as on NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X). Load the native ARM64 `nvEncodeAPIa64.dll` first on `target_arch = aarch64` (falling back to `nvEncodeAPI.dll` and `nvEncodeAPI64.dll`), while keeping `nvEncodeAPI64.dll` first on `x86_64` Windows so standard RTX devices are unaffected.
- **NVENC SDR colour signalling (`crates/platform`)**: Align `NvencEncoder::sample_entry` and `nvenc_hevc_hdr_export` with `ColorSignal::apply_to(&mut e, false)` from `#2142` so SDR NVENC exports carry the explicit BT.709 `colr` box without HDR metadata.
- **Off-screen wgpu adapter selection & multi-threaded readback (`crates/gpu`, `crates/golden`, `crates/ui-egui`)**:
  - Add `adapter::offscreen_instance` and `adapter::offscreen_adapter` so off-screen GPU rendering (`ExportRenderer`, benchmarks, and GPU tests) excludes OpenGL on Windows (`wgpu::Backends::PRIMARY` unless `WGPU_BACKEND` is set) and uses `adapter::pick`, matching the main application window.
  - Share a single off-screen `(wgpu::Instance, wgpu::Device, wgpu::Queue)` across `filmcraft-gpu` and `filmcraft-golden` test suites instead of opening a separate instance/device per test across concurrent threads.
  - Pass the `wgpu::SubmissionIndex` into `wait_mapped` and poll until the `map_async` channel receives its result (or the 8-second deadline expires) rather than calling `rx.recv()` unconditionally, preventing hangs/races when multiple threads submit and poll on a shared `wgpu::Device`.
- **Contributors (`contributors/people.toml`)**: Add `[people.mweinbach]`.

title: Transcribe runs in the background with progress and Cancel
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Transcribe used to run on the UI thread: on a long clip (or with the larger Whisper models) the whole editor froze until it finished, with no progress and no way to stop it. This follows #2507 (G19), which puts speech-to-text in release builds, where this matters.

**Engine (`transcript.rs`)**
- `transcript.generate` and `sequence.transcribe` get `"wait"`, default **true**, so agents, the CLI and scripts behave as before.
- With `"wait": false`, the work runs as a background job (`jobs.list`; `jobs.cancel` or the job's cancel flag stops it):
  - the targets, sources, recogniser and options are resolved on the calling thread, so bad requests still fail at once;
  - audio decoding and recognition run in the job's thread;
  - progress comes per clip from the recogniser's own progress callback, and cancel is checked there too.
- `transcript::poll`, called with the other job pollers in `Session::poll_persistence`, stores the transcripts of a finished job as **one undo step**.
- A cancelled job stores nothing. So does a job whose project was replaced meanwhile (open, new, close); that check uses `project_generation`, identical to #2437 and #2470.
- New `transcript::running_job`. The job helpers in `narration.rs` are now `pub(crate)` so the two job kinds share them. The engine re-exports `filmcraft_speech` as `filmcraft_engine::speech` (like `project`, `render` and `time`), so hosts and tests can install a recogniser.

**UI**
- The Text panel's Transcribe and Sequence ▸ Transcribe Sequence… run with `"wait": false`.
- While a transcription runs, the Transcript tab shows what it is doing, a progress bar and **Cancel** (`text.transcribing.{progress,cancel}`). The rest of the editor stays usable.

title: #2494: Font Size drags and shows the selected characters' size
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Fixes #2494 (Properties ▸ Text ▸ Font Size: dragging does nothing; a typed size changes the text but the field doesn't change).

**Cause.** With characters selected by the Type tool, the character properties (Font Size, Tracking, Baseline Shift) are applied to the selection as a character style (`graphics.setCharStyle`). But the field kept **showing the layer's value**. So:
- a typed size took effect but the field stayed at the layer's size;
- a drag computed every frame's value from the layer's size again. Each frame wrote layer size + that frame's delta, so the size moved one step at most (100 → 105 for an 80 px drag) and looked like nothing happened.

**Fix** (`panels/graphics.rs`, `Ctx::shown`): with a Type-tool selection, a character property's field shows the first selected character's own style when it has one, otherwise the layer's value. A drag therefore starts from the real value and accumulates, and the field shows what was set. Without a selection nothing changes.

**Test:** `graphics_ui::font_size_follows_the_selected_characters` types a word, selects it all, and drags Font Size 80 px. The characters grow past 120 px. On `main` the test fails with 105.

title: render: cross-dissolve transparent and non-fullscreen clips via transition step
author: wulu-epic
body:
When applying a Cross Dissolve transition between two clips where either clip contains transparency (e.g. cutouts, PNGs, titles, translucent color mattes), non-fullscreen scaling/positioning, or non-default opacity/blend effects, the outgoing clip did not fade out during the transition. Instead, it stayed at 100% opacity until abruptly cutting out at the edit point.

### Cause
In `crates/render/src/plan.rs`, the Cross Dissolve branch was optimized to composite outgoing clip `A` at 1.0 opacity and incoming clip `B` over it at progress `p`. For full-screen opaque video clips, premultiplied "over" blending against an opaque background matches a linear cross-fade without dipping. However, when clip `A` or `B` contains transparent regions, translucent color mattes, or is scaled down, clip `A` remains visible at full opacity underneath clip `B` and pops off when the transition concludes.

### Solution
- Introduced `is_fullscreen_opaque()` to verify whether an item is guaranteed to be a 100% opaque, fullscreen clip with default blend mode and identity transform. Translucent `ColorMatte` generators (`color[3] < 1.0`) are also classified as non-opaque.
- In `crates/media/src/generators.rs`, updated `GeneratorSource::new` to accurately mark `has_alpha` on `ColorMatte` with alpha `< 1.0`.
- When either `A` or `B` has transparency, non-fullscreen bounds, or custom effects, route the cross dissolve through `PlanStep::Transition` so both inputs are rendered to independent layers and blended with proper linear fading ($1 - p$ for outgoing, $p$ for incoming).
- For standard full-screen opaque clips, retain the existing direct layer stack optimization.

### Validation
- Synthetic regression tests in `crates/render/src/tests.rs`:
  - `cross_dissolve_transparent_clip_fades_out`: verifies pixel colors and alpha channels at the transition midpoint ($p = 0.5$) for scaled-down clips with transparency.
  - `cross_dissolve_translucent_color_matte_fades_out`: verifies that a full-frame trans…

title: fix(timeline): a press hits only the track rows of its own pane when tracks are scrolled
author: 4waymedia
body:
## Problem

When the video or audio track area of the Timeline has a scroll bar and is scrolled, presses on audio tracks go to the wrong track:

- clicking an audio clip doesn't select it (a marquee drag still works);
- dragging an audio clip up or down to another audio track doesn't move it.

## Cause

`Layout::row_at` (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs`) returned the first row whose rectangle contains the pointer's y. Rows aren't clipped to their pane: when the video tracks are scrolled, V1's row extends below the video/audio divider by the scroll amount (`video_row_tops`), and video rows are listed before audio rows, so a press on the top audio tracks hit the hidden V1 row. Likewise a scrolled audio row reaches above the audio pane (over the divider) and below it (under the Mix row). Hit-testing (`timeline_hit::hit`), the vertical clip drag and the drop targets all go through `row_at`.

## Fix

`row_at` now only matches a video row above the divider (`y < split_y`) and an audio row between the divider and the Mix row (`split_y + DIVIDER_H <= y < content.max.y - MASTER_H`), which is where each pane draws its rows. No other behaviour changes.

## Tests

- New `rows_only_hit_inside_their_own_pane_when_scrolled`: a scrolled V1 reaching below the divider, a scrolled A1 reaching above it, and an audio row under the Mix row. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-ui-egui --lib panels::timeline` (32 passed), `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --lib --tests -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.
- Checked by hand on Windows: with both track areas scrolled, audio clips select on click and move between audio tracks by dragging.

title: NEST-2379: track thumbnail dependencies and reuse unchanged nested pictures
author: jackcanon
body:
Changing Position or Scale on a plain nested clip rebuilds unchanged inner pictures and invalidates thumbnails that did not change. This tracks reachable thumbnail dependencies, keeps guarded transformed nests as clipped source-sized pictures, and reuses those pictures across outer-only edits in the native frame server.

Child edits, undo/redo, rendered metadata names (including shared aliases), explicit source/proxy refreshes and render-context changes invalidate correctly. Draft/prefetch, pending/cancelled/failed jobs, masks, standard effects, rotation and unsupported cases preserve conservative behavior. The shared cache and each active job's staging cache are separately bounded to two pictures and 64 mebibytes of logical pixel payload; this is not a total process-memory limit. Idle workers do not retain the new completed cache after its owner disappears.

Builds on @00xJS's source-image placement and cross-drag reuse directions in [the issue discussion](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/issues/2379#issuecomment-6256780451). Related to #2379; the reported Windows interaction was not validated here, so this does not claim the entire issue resolved. Generated fixture coverage overlaps #2505, which remains a separate test-only contribution.

title: Preserve exact custom metadata field identity in project columns
author: whatever-industries
body:
Custom metadata headings can collide with FilmCraft properties or with another heading differing only in case. For example, `Scene` and `scene` previously displayed the same first matching value, while editing an imported `Name` could rename the clip.

This change keeps stored keys exact and adds explicit `metadata:<key>` selectors for collisions. Project columns, sorting, Find/search bins and the Metadata editor can address the stored values independently. Custom Name/Label/File Path fields appear in a separate Metadata section. title: render: Video De-Noise, temporal and spatial (#2514)
author: danielbanariba
body:
## Video De-Noise: temporal and spatial noise reduction (part 1 of #2514)

Adds **Video Effects > Noise & Grain > Video De-Noise** (id `video_denoise`), CPU only. It cleans grain and sensor noise using the neighbouring frames first and the neighbouring pixels second, so still areas get cleaner without the detail loss of a blur.

### Parameters
- **Luma Noise Level** (30 %) and **Chroma Noise Level** (50 %), 0 to 100, where 100 % is 0.10 in display units: the noise to remove from brightness and from colour.
- **Temporal Radius** (1), 0 to 2: frames read on each side of the current one; 0 is spatial only.
- **Preserve Detail** (50 %): how strictly the spatial pass matches a pixel's surroundings; higher keeps more texture.
- **Show Only Noise** (off): shows what was removed, around mid grey, at 4x contrast.

### How it works
Straight, display-encoded values are split into luma and the two colour differences, filtered as two groups, each with its own level and weights. Alpha is never changed; transparent and non-finite pixels are left alone and never used as samples. The sRGB curve is mirrored around 0, so a negative (out-of-gamut) channel is denoised and keeps its sign, while a channel that was 0 or more never comes out below 0.

1. **Temporal.** Each neighbouring frame (read through `FxEnv::frame`, so it carries the effects above this one) is compared with the current one on a 3 x 3 patch and averaged in with a weight that falls off once the patch distance exceeds what noise alone explains (`2 s^2`).
2. **Spatial.** Each pixel is averaged with the pixels in a small window (radius 2 at full size, scaled with `px_scale`) whose patch looks like its own. The pass trusts the match less where the temporal pass found few matches.

The weights come from Tomasi and Manduchi (bilateral filter, ICCV 1998), Dubois and Sabri (temporal filtering of image sequences, IEEE Trans. Communications, 1984) and Buades, Coll and Morel (non-local means, CVPR 2005). No implementation was consu…

title: Re-open a failed audio output while playing instead of going silent for good
author: justacalico
body:
## Summary

- A stream the device drops while playing (ALSA `poll() returned POLLERR`, an unplugged device, a failed open) muted playback until pause/play, because `AudioOut` gives up and playback keeps the dead clock forever.
- `Playback` now arms an `audio_retry_at` deadline when the clock is lost or an open fails; while playing, `advance_playback` re-opens the output every `AUDIO_RETRY_S` (2 s) at the current playhead — exactly what pause/play does by hand. A recovering or newly appearing device (headphones, a PipeWire node coming back) brings the sound back without user action.
- The Source monitor gets the same treatment (`start_source_audio`).
- Intentionally silent paths do not retry: unsupported shuttle speeds, sources without audio, and a stream that opened but never consumes samples (#136, where a retry would only freeze the playhead again).

#### Test plan

- [x] `audio_recovery_tests::a_lost_output_is_reopened_and_the_sound_returns`: dead stream → clock lost → retried → sound returns on the device clock
- [x] `audio_recovery_tests::a_device_that_appears_mid_playback_starts_sounding`: failed open at play start → device appears → picked up mid-playback
- [x] `playback_clock_ui` (3 tests, incl. the #136 stalled-device case)
- [x] `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets`, `cargo check --all-targets`

title: #2553: fall back to the integrated GPU when the chosen one can't draw to the window
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Fixes #2553. Also addresses #2581 (the software-mode dead end, split out of #2553): when every mode failed, the next start goes back to the default.

On a hybrid Intel + NVIDIA laptop (NVIDIA 470, KDE Wayland), wgpu picks the high-performance GPU. That GPU claims the window's surface, then fails `Surface::configure` with `Invalid surface`. wgpu turns that into a panic, so the app exited with code 101. After that, the saved fallback went straight to software rendering, which dead-ends when lavapipe isn't installed.

## Changes
- **New Linux fallback mode `low-power` ("integrated GPU")** between the default and software. It sets `power_preference = LowPower`, which is the reporter's verified `WGPU_POWER_PREF=low` workaround. Linux ladder: default → low-power → software. `--graphics low-power` picks it by hand.
- **A panic out of `run_native` before the app exists counts as a failed graphics start.** The next mode is saved at once, and FilmCraft starts itself again in that mode (same arguments, `--graphics <next>`; the AppImage via `$APPIMAGE`), waits for it and exits with its code. The new process doesn't relaunch again (`FILMCRAFT_GRAPHICS_RELAUNCHED`): a panic there saves the next mode for the next launch and ends with the usual "could not start its window" dialog instead of a crash. A panic after the app was created propagates as before.
- **No dead end when every mode failed.** If the last fallback also fails (e.g. no software adapter), the saved mode goes back to the default for the next start. The error dialog says so and points to `--graphics <mode>`.
- `--help`, `docs/gaps.md`, and translations for the new mode label (de/es/fr/it/ja/ko/zh-cn).

## Tests
- `graphics.rs`: the Linux ladder moves default → low-power → software; low-power sets `LowPower` without an adapter selector and without indirect validation.
- `args.rs`: `--graphics low-power` is accepted where the platform has it and refused elsewhere.
- `main.rs`: `a_caught_panic_keeps_its_message`.

title: #2295: the status bar's text can be selected and copied
author: ksaxena149
body:
Closes #2295.

## What changes

The status bar painted its hint and messages with `painter().text`, so a path, a file that would not open or the reason an export stopped could be read but not selected, copied, found by a screen reader or read by an agent. It is now a selectable `egui::Label` in the same 20 px bar:

- **Select and copy.** Drag across the message and press Ctrl+C.
- **Long messages** end in "…" before the running job's "Exporting… 42%" and progress bar, instead of running underneath them. Hovering shows the full text.
- **Clicks.** The 8 s auto-clear stays. A click *beside* the text still dismisses the message, as before. A click *on* the text starts a selection instead. The cancel button keeps its own click.

## Copying with the keyboard

The issue asks for text that can be copied, and the label alone was not enough. A selected egui label is copied only through the Copy event (Ctrl+C), but Ctrl+C on selected text also reached the app's own Copy shortcut (`edit.copy`) through `clipboard_events_as_keys`. With clips selected, it copied the clips and put their names on the clipboard. With no clips selected, it replaced the message being copied with "command `edit.copy` is not available right now: no clips selected".

Selected label text now keeps Copy and Cut, the same way a focused text field does, so the message can actually be copied. The check (`LabelSelectionState::has_selection`) runs before `input_mut`, so the plugin lock is never taken inside the input lock. title: #2528: emoji in text layers fall back to the system emoji font
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Refs #2528 (the first step: emoji show up; colour emoji are still to come).

Emoji typed or pasted into a text layer (e.g. from the Windows emoji panel, Win + .) were added to the text but drew nothing or a box. The text engine falls back per character to bundled fonts, craft-fonts and faces that are already loaded. System faces are found at start-up but only loaded when used, so the system emoji font (Segoe UI Emoji on Windows, Noto Emoji on Linux) was never asked.

## Changes (`crates/text`)
- **Emoji fallback:** for a pictograph no loaded face covers (`fonts::is_emoji`: the emoji blocks, symbols, arrows, regional indicators, tags), `fallback_for` asks the system faces whose family name contains "Emoji". Faces not loaded yet are probed with `covers_text`, which reads the file into a temporary buffer, and the answer is cached per character (keyed on the face count, so fonts added later are still found). Discovery already leaves out faces without outline tables (`sfnt::read_faces`), so what's found can be drawn.
- **Sequences stay together:** variation selectors (VS16), the zero-width joiner, skin-tone modifiers, tag characters and the keycap mark take the face of the character before them, and an emoji after a ZWJ prefers that face. The font then shapes the whole sequence, and a joiner never falls back to a face where it would draw a missing-glyph box.

## What this doesn't do yet
Our rasteriser draws glyph outlines into a coverage mask, so emoji draw in the text's fill colour (Segoe UI Emoji's monochrome outlines), not in colour. Colour emoji need the COLR layers / sbix and CBDT bitmaps (skrifa reads all of them) drawn as RGBA through the text compositing path, which is a bigger change. On macOS, Apple Color Emoji has bitmaps only (no outlines), so it isn't listed and emoji there still don't draw until colour support lands.
