title: CI: run cargo xtask ci on pull requests and pushes to main
author: FredApps
body:
Only path-filtered workflows (FreeBSD, Nix, packaging lint, Windows ARM64) run on pull requests today, so most PRs land with no test run at all. This adds `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, which runs the CLAUDE.md quality gate (`cargo xtask ci`: fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, layers, assets, wasm) on every pull request and every push to main.

- Ported from storytold/wordcraft#800, the same gate for wordcraft.
- Linux only, on a standard GitHub-hosted runner, with a read-only token, no secrets and `persist-credentials: false`.
- Actions are pinned to commit SHAs. craft-fonts is pinned to the same commit as `release.yml`.
- Adds `libasound2-dev` for `cpal` (audio playback).
- `docs/gaps.md` is left alone, so this doesn't conflict with other PRs. The CI gap row can be closed after merge.

Validation run in my fork, with the two fixes below: https://github.com/FredApps/filmcraft/actions/runs/39412094118 (green, 15 minutes).

**Merge #2572 and #2576 first.** Two tests have been failing on main, and this job would be red without them:
- #2572: `dev_icon::tests::desktop_file_matches_the_packaged_fields` (the `MimeType=` line, since 69a6c4b6)
- #2576: `i18n::tests::japanese_needs_an_installed_font` (installed right-to-left faces, since #395)

**Build time.** `cargo xtask ci` builds clippy and the tests with `--release`. With the shipped release profile (thin LTO, one codegen unit), linking the test binaries alone took over an hour on a runner. This job keeps the optimisation level but turns LTO off and uses 16 codegen units (`CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_*`), and the timeout is 120 minutes. Contributors running `cargo xtask ci` locally pay the same LTO cost, so a lighter test profile in the workspace may be worth considering.

title: fix(media): bound decoded stills in a shared cache (#2464)
author: scottyallen
body:
Fixes #2464. Related: #2469 (the pool itself never evicts; left as is here, see below).

Browsing a folder of photos in the Media Browser's thumbnail view grew memory without limit and never gave it back. Measured with the headless `egui_kittest` harness on 60 JPEGs of 4000x3000: RSS went from 483 MB to 3.3 GB and stayed there after leaving the folder. The issue reports 26 GB for a few hundred pictures on Linux.

Three things combined:

- `StillSource` decoded the whole picture at open and kept the RGBA frame as a field, so it bypassed every memory budget (`FRAME_BUDGET` only covers video GOPs).
- The Media Browser fabricates a synthetic project item per previewed file, and `MediaPool::resolve` opens a source for each one.
- The media pool keeps one source per item for the life of the project and never evicts.

This fixes the first point, one layer below the pool, the same way video is bounded by the GOP cache and image sequences by their per-source `FrameCache`:

- `StillSource` no longer owns its frame. All stills share one process-wide byte-budgeted `media::FrameCache<u64>` keyed per source (`still::STILL_BUDGET`, 1 GiB, the same as the video frame budget). The cache's LRU eviction already runs synchronously on insert, so the budget holds under a burst. Float stills (EXR, HDR, DNG) are 16 bytes a pixel, and the budget is sized so a two-layer frame of camera raws plays from the cache: a logo over a 61 MP raw, or a dissolve between two 24 MP raws. `insert` no longer evicts the entry it just added, so one still larger than the budget plays from the cache on its own and is pushed out only by the next still. Two 45 MP raws on one frame still decode again every frame, bounded.
- Each source keeps a cheap reload: the `SharedReader` it was opened from (a path plus a file-handle pool, so no pinned descriptor), or the bytes it was built from. On a miss it decodes again. The first decode still happens at open, from the bytes `open_reader_within` already read, so `info()` an…

title: FilmcraftApp::toast is gone; engine toasts reach the status bar (#2443)
author: rahul05ranjan
body:
## What's wrong

`FilmcraftApp::toast` was written in three places (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:431`, set at the Refresh media result and at every engine `Event::Toast`) and **read in none**, so no toast ever reached the screen (#2443). The 15 `Session::toast` / `Session::error_toast` messages — a project upgraded to a new schema version, recovered unsaved changes, media files that are missing, Scene Edit Detection finding no cut points, a failed mask track, a render job that ended with errors — reached the Events panel log and nothing visible.

The issue offered two ways to settle it: draw a real toast overlay, or drop the field and route to the status bar. This PR takes the second, because the web app already made exactly that choice by hand (`apps/filmcraft-web/src/lib.rs:195` keeps its own local toast and routes it through `app.status(t)`), and the desktop's status bar is drawn and auto-clears after 8 seconds — close to a toast's life.

## What the change does

- The `toast` field and its initialiser are removed.
- Refresh media's outcome and every `Event::Toast` call `self.status(...)` with the same message.

Unchanged: the Events panel still logs every event; the web app's own toast handling still runs (it writes the same message to the same status, so nothing doubles visually); `Event::Toast`'s error flag is dropped the same way the web app drops it today. If a red, fading toast overlay is preferred on the desktop, that remains a possible follow-up on top of this.

## Verification

Grepped the whole workspace (crates + apps) for every read and write of the field before and after the change — the desktop crate has no remaining reference, and `filmcraft-web` only has its own local variable, untouched. Read the status bar's drawing and auto-clear path (`show_status_bar` → 8-second clear) to confirm the messages are actually shown. `ctx` remains in use in both touched functions, so no unused-variable fallout.

title: CI: prove the GPU tests run on lavapipe; fail when they skip
author: FredApps
body:
Hosted runners have no GPU, but wgpu still returns a software adapter. With `mesa-vulkan-drivers`, which #2563's `ci.yml` installs, that is lavapipe, so the GPU-vs-CPU parity tests in `filmcraft-gpu` and `filmcraft-golden` already run in CI instead of skipping. Nothing showed it, though: a test that skips prints a note and passes, and `cargo test` hides the output of passing tests, so a broken Vulkan install would look green.

This PR:
- adds a "GPU tests on lavapipe" step after the gate. It reruns `cargo test --release -p filmcraft-gpu -p filmcraft-golden -- --nocapture` and fails if any test reports `no GPU adapter` or `SKIPPED (gpu…`, or if no test printed the adapter it ran on;
- makes the GPU test device helpers print `GPU test adapter: <name> (<backend>, <type>)`, and has `crates/gpu/src/tests.rs` reuse `blend_tests::device` instead of keeping its own copy;
- adds `libvulkan1` to the installed packages, and a note on running the GPU tests on lavapipe to `docs/testing.md`.

It follows the approach of storytold/lightcraft#1148, minus that PR's opt-in variable: lightcraft refuses software adapters, and filmcraft's test path doesn't.

Fork run, green: https://github.com/FredApps/filmcraft/actions/runs/39412302120. The step takes about 2 minutes and shows `GPU test adapter: llvmpipe (LLVM 20.1.2, 256 bits) (Vulkan, Cpu)` on 29 tests, with no skips.

**Stacked** on #2572, #2576 and #2563, whose commits appear here until they merge. The new commit is the last one, `0d4a48a`.

**One known gap:** if an adapter is found but `request_device` fails, `filmcraft-gpu`'s helper returns `None` without printing a skip note. The adapter line would still appear, so this step would not catch it. Printing a skip note there too would close that.

title: Escape tab/newline/CR in XML attribute values
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/interchange/src/xml.rs:7 (escape, used by start_tag for attributes)` (no existing issue): XML writer does not escape tab/newline in attribute values, so they become spaces on re-read.

## Cause
`escape` writes `\n`, `\r` and `\t` as raw characters. That is fine in element text, but XML parsers normalize them to spaces inside attribute values, so names and other attributes containing them changed on re-read.

## Fix
Added `escape_attr`, which writes `
`, `` and `	` for those characters and otherwise defers to `escape`. `XmlWriter::start_tag` and the attribute-position escapes in `fcpxml.rs` now use it. Regression test `xml::tests::attr_whitespace_roundtrip` fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-interchange --lib attr_whitespace_roundtrip`). `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Verified
- Regression test `xml::tests::attr_whitespace_roundtrip`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-interchange --lib attr_whitespace_roundtrip`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
`escape` is unchanged, so element text keeps raw newlines and tabs. The parsing side is not changed.

title: #1175: Halation effect (film-style red glow around highlights)
author: Mateo-RR
body: Closes #1175. Adds **Halation**, the red-orange glow that film stock shows around bright highlights (light scattering back through the emulsion off the film base). Premiere has no such effect, so it goes in a new top-level folder of the Effects panel: **FilmCraft Effects ▸ Lights & Glows ▸ Halation**. *Before / after on the demo project's City Night clip. The demo scene is dim, so this uses Threshold 50 %, Intensity 200 %; the other values are the defaults.* ## How it works `render::vfx::lights::halation`, on the CPU: 1. Highlight mask: the existing `highlights()` helper (soft knee above **Threshold**), reduced to luma. 2. Two Gaussian blurs of that single-channel mask, run in parallel with `rayon::join`: σ = Radius / 2 (scaled by `px_scale`) and 3σ, mixed 65 / 35 (tight halo plus a wide falloff). They reuse `effects::blur_plane`, which is now `pub(crate)`. 3. **Core Suppression** multiplies the glow by `1 − suppression × coverage`, where coverage is how much of the pixel is above Threshold (the alpha that `highlights()` returns). The highlight itself stays clean whatever its colour, and only the surroundings glow (as on film). 4. The glow is tinted with **Color** (linear) and added as light with `add_light`. | Parameter | Default | Range | |---|---|---| | Threshold | 80 % | 0–100 % | | Radius | 20 | 0–1000 (slider 0–200) | | Intensity | 100 % | 0–1000 % (slider 0–400 %) | | Color | (1.0, 0.4, 0.15) | | | Core Suppression | 50 % | 0–100 % | The defaults aim at real highlights (a sun, lamps, specular light) and give a subtle, believable glow there. ## The folder (the open question in #1175) #1175 asked where effects beyond Premiere's catalogue should go. This PR implements option A: a top-level `FilmCraft Effects` folder whose sub-folders reuse the existing category names (here `Lights & Glows`). The Premiere ca…

title: Centre Transform's auto points in the clip's picture on apply and reset (#2588)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2588.

The Transform effect's Anchor Point and Position default to "auto" (the centre). `effects.apply` resolved them in the sequence frame (for example 960,540 in a 1920x1080 sequence). Standard effects run on the clip's own source picture, though: effect params are in source pixels, and the renderer's `point()` centres in the working image. So on an imported image that is not the sequence size, the anchor landed off-centre and Scale grew the picture from one side.

- `effects.apply` now resolves auto points against each clip's source size (`Project::source_size`) and falls back to the sequence frame when there is none, as `remove_attributes` in `clip_ops.rs` already does.
- `effects.reset` / `effects.resetParam` (`reset_params`) used the sequence frame for everything, so resetting Transform moved the anchor back to the wrong place. They now get the clip's source size too: a standard effect centres its points in the source, and an intrinsic one (Motion) keeps frame-based Position with a source-based Anchor, the same split as clip placement and Remove Attributes.

Test: `applied_transform_centres_its_points_in_the_clip_picture` places a 960x1080 colour matte in the 1920x1080 demo sequence, applies Transform, and checks that Anchor and Position are 480,540. Then it checks the same after Reset Effect and after Reset Parameter. On main it fails with 960,540.

title: Fix audio track header buttons painting over the video half when scrolled
author: bfenty
body:
## Fix: audio track header buttons paint over the video half when the audio list is scrolled

**Closes #2538**

### Root cause
When the audio track list is scrolled so a track's header row crosses the video/audio split, `draw_headers` computes the row rect, intersects it with the audio half (`aclip`), and passes the result to the M/S toggles — but `letter_toggle` and `icon_toggle` painted with the panel's full-strength painter, ignoring the intersection. The row rect collapses to a degenerate/inverted sliver at the split, and its M/S buttons (and hover fills) kept painting right across the boundary into the video half.

### Fix
`letter_toggle` and `icon_toggle` now paint through `ui.painter().with_clip_rect(rect)`, so whatever rect the caller passes is also the paint clip. Callers that already pass an intersected rect (timeline headers, voiceover mic button) get correct clipping for free; callers whose rect is already inside the panel clip see no change. The voiceover mic button's hover fill had the same unclipped-paint bug and is clipped to `visible` now too.

title: Reject non-hex characters in colour hex parsing
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/lib.rs:298-302 (parse_hex); used by crates/engine/src/commands.rs:3615 (json_to_param, Color params)` (no existing issue): color::parse_hex accepts '+'-signed digits, so malformed hex colours are read as valid.

## Cause
`color::parse_hex` and `captions::parse_color` parsed each byte pair with `u8::from_str_radix(.., 16)`, which accepts a leading '+'. Neither checked that every character is a hex digit, and both stripped any number of leading '#'. A malformed colour such as `#+f+f+f`, passed to a Color parameter (for example via `effects.setParam`), was therefore read as a valid colour (#0f0f0f) instead of being rejected. There is no GitHub issue for this change.

## Fix
Both functions now strip at most one leading '#'. They return `None` unless every remaining character is an ASCII hex digit. The existing 6 or 8 length check is unchanged. Added a regression test for `parse_hex`, `tests::parse_hex_rejects_signs`, which fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-color parse_hex_rejects_signs`).

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::parse_hex_rejects_signs`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-color parse_hex_rejects_signs`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `dev_icon::tests::desktop_file_matches_the_packaged_fields`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
I did not add a separate test for `captions::parse_color` or a `json_to_param` test. `engine::settings::parse_hex` already had the guard, so I left it alone.

title: Fix false overlaps for empty time ranges
author: Lucenx9
body:
## Summary

`TimeRange::overlaps` reports a zero-duration range inside a clip as overlapping, even though `is_empty` is true and `intersect` returns `None`. Negative durations can produce the same false positive. Editing and audio callers use this predicate to detect occupied ranges.

```diff
 overlaps(a, b)
+  require both durations to be positive
   compare half-open endpoints
```

Add the missing empty-range checks, document the contract, and cover both argument orders, negative durations, adjacent ranges and genuine overlaps.

- Before: `cargo +1.96.0 test -p filmcraft-time empty_time_ranges_never_overlap` failed twice on `duration 0`.

title: platform: decode AV1 in hardware through VideoToolbox on macOS
author: monomadic
body:
**Stacked on #2180** (VP9 through VideoToolbox): this branch is that PR's head plus one commit, since #2180 introduced the `Stream` enum the AV1 variant slots into. Once #2180 merges this rebases to a single commit; until then its diff shows both.

## Why

AV1 (`av1C`) was decoded only in software on macOS: 4K AV1 plays at roughly 10 fps through our pure-Rust decoder on an M-series Mac, and an exact seek into a 250-frame GOP takes seconds. The media engine of the M3 and later decodes AV1, and VideoToolbox exposes it the way it exposes VP9. `filmcraft-platform` already has the AV1 stream info (`FrameStreamInfo`, used by Media Foundation), so this is the VideoToolbox half.

## What

- `VtDecoder::new_av1`: main profile, 8- and 10-bit 4:2:0; everything else (high / professional profile, 12-bit, monochrome) is declined up front and stays with our decoder, as does a Mac without an AV1 decoder (`av1_hardware_available` registers Apple's supplemental decoder first, as for VP9).
- The `av1C` payload goes into the `CMVideoFormatDescription` as a sample description extension atom (`atom_format_description`, now shared with VP9's `vpcC`), and each temporal unit is fed as it is (OBUs, no temporal delimiter), which is also what ffmpeg's `av1_videotoolbox` hwaccel does.
- A run starting at a key frame unit that carries no sequence header of its own gets the configuration OBUs put in front (as the Media Foundation path does).
- Colour follows the sequence header: `av1C`'s at session creation, an in-band one's from the sample that carries it, so pictures carry what our software decoder reports.
- No reordering (every sample is one shown picture), `is_random_access` / `is_disposable` answer as the software decoder.
- `render`: the preview cost counts AV1 as hardware-decoded on Apple silicon. An M1 / M2 has no AV1 decoder and gets the software estimate wrong there; the platform crate's availability query sits above the render crate's layer, so a comment records the trade.

title: render: VHS Look, a clip-level analog tape look (#2516)
author: danielbanariba
body:
## VHS Look: a clip-level analog tape look (#2516)

Adds **Video Effects > Stylize > VHS Look** (id `vhs_look`), CPU only. It gives a whole clip the look of a VHS recording: soft brightness, colour that smears past edges, wobbling lines, tape noise. The VHS Damage transition plays between two clips; there was no effect for one clip.

### Parameters
- **Luma Bandwidth** (3.0 MHz) and **Chroma Bandwidth** (0.3 MHz): the detail brightness and colour keep. Colour gets a tenth of the band, which is what makes edges bleed.
- **Chroma Shift** (2 px, -20 to 20) delays the colour, so it lands right of its edge. **Line Jitter** (1 px, 0 to 10) moves whole lines sideways.
- **Noise** (20 %), **Head Switching** (0 lines, 0 to 30: a torn, noisy band at the bottom) and **Dropouts** (10 %: short bright streaks).
- **Random Seed**.

### How it works
Each line goes to display-encoded Y'CbCr (ITU-R BT.601). Luma and the two colour differences are low-passed separately: the MHz values become cycles per picture width through the active part of a 525/60 line (about 52.6 us), so 3 MHz is about 158 cycles and the look is the same at any resolution. The filter is a Gaussian run as three box passes with fractional end weights (Wells, IEEE PAMI 1986; Gwosdek et al., SSVM 2011), so it costs the same at any width. Then come the colour delay, the line jitter, tape noise (correlated by the channel bandwidth), the head-switching band and the dropouts. Tape bandwidths follow IEC 60774-1 and Poynton (*Digital Video and HDTV Algorithms and Interfaces*, 2003): about 3 MHz of luma and 0.3 to 0.5 MHz of colour. The head-switching band sits where the heads take turns, about 6.5 lines before vertical sync (US patent 6,650,825), so on a real tape overscan usually hides it. No implementation was consulted; the module docs have the details.

title: Keep WebVTT cues whose identifier starts with NOTE
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/captions/src/vtt.rs:75 (parse, NOTE block check)` (no existing issue): WebVTT cue whose identifier starts with "NOTE" is dropped as a comment block.

## Cause
The WebVTT parser classified a block as a NOTE comment by looking only at its first line. A cue with an identifier like `NOTE 1` followed by a timing line was therefore stored as a comment block and the cue was lost.

## Fix
A block is now treated as a NOTE only when none of its lines contains `-->`. Cues with NOTE-prefixed identifiers are parsed as cues. A regression test covers this.

## Verified
- Regression test `vtt::tests::note_prefixed_cue_id_is_a_cue`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-captions note_prefixed_cue_id_is_a_cue`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

The STYLE/REGION block handling is unchanged.

title: Reject signed fields in SCC timecode parser
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/captions/src/scc.rs:37 (parse_timecode)` (no existing issue): SCC timecode parser accepts signed fields, yielding negative frames.

## Cause
`parse_timecode` only checked that each field was 1 to 3 characters long and then called `i64::parse`. That call accepts a leading '-' or '+', so a timecode like "00:00:-5:00" parsed as a negative frame number instead of being rejected.

## Fix
Each timecode field must now consist only of ASCII digits before it is parsed. Signed timecodes return `None`, so `SCC::parse` reports a syntax error for them like any other bad timecode.

## Verified
- Regression test `scc::tests::timecode_rejects_signed_fields`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-captions --lib scc::tests::timecode_rejects_signed_fields`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The field length limit (1 to 3 characters) and the timecode formatting code are unchanged.

title: G1: match Premiere 26.5.2 for Tint, Black & White, Gaussian Blur (Legacy), Brightness & Contrast, Posterize and Mirror
author: r5th
body:
## Summary

First G1 (`docs/gaps.md`) fixes from an automated Premiere comparison. The same still frame is rendered in Premiere Pro 26.5.2 and in `filmcraft-cli`, with the same effect and parameter values, and scored by PSNR. These effects were measurably off; each fix is its own commit, CPU and GPU (`fx.wgsl`) paths together.

```diff
 Tint, Black & White
-  luma = Rec.709 on linear light
+  luma = Rec.601 on encoded values
 Gaussian Blur (Legacy)
-  sigma = 0.5 x Blurriness, transparent edges
+  sigma = 0.28 x Blurriness, edge pixels repeated
-  default Blurriness 0
+  default Blurriness 25
 Brightness & Contrast (contrast c > 0)
-  slope = 1 + c/100
+  slope = 1 / (1 - c/100)        (c < 0 unchanged: 1 + c/100)
 Posterize (L levels)
-  round(v * (L-1)) / (L-1)
+  min(floor(v * L), L-1) / (L-1)
 Mirror
-  default Reflection Center (0.5, 0.5)
+  default Reflection Center (1.0, 0.5)  -> default Mirror is identity, as in Premiere
```

Clean-room: only rendered output was compared (AGENTS.md §2); no Premiere frames, presets or files are included here.

## Evidence

PSNR against Premiere 26.5.2 on an RGB test still (≥ 50 dB treated as a match, < 35 dB visibly different):

| Effect | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Tint | 15.9 dB | 79.3 dB |
| Black & White | 21.3 dB | 79.3 dB |
| Gaussian Blur (Legacy), various Blurriness | 26 dB | 38–49 dB |
| Gaussian Blur (Legacy), default | 19.9 dB | 41.1 dB |
| Brightness & Contrast, positive contrast | 35.3 dB | 87.0 dB |
| Posterize | 36.9 dB | 66.9 dB |
| Mirror, default | 3.2 dB | exact |

Three goldens are re-blessed in their own commit (`FILMCRAFT_BLESS=1 cargo test -p filmcraft-golden`): `gaussian_blur` and `mask_blur` (softer blur, no dark edges) and `mask_color` (Black & White luma, max 3 levels).

title: Reject signed fields inside multi-field timecodes
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/time/src/lib.rs:483 (parse_timecode, multi-field branch)` (no existing issue): parse_timecode accepts signed fields inside a timecode, yielding negative frame counts.

## Cause
In the multi-field branch of `parse_timecode`, each field was parsed with `p.parse::<i64>()`, which accepts a leading `-` or `+`. An input like `00:00:-5:00` was therefore read as an absolute timecode and returned a negative frame count (-125 at 25 fps).

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The leading `+`/`-` that marks a timecode as relative to the current position works as before. Empty fields still count as 0, and the bare-digit branch is unchanged.

title: Platform: a pure-Rust client for the PulseAudio native protocol (part 1 of #2407)
author: adventurelands
body:
Part 1 of 2 of #2407, split at @FredApps's request: the PulseAudio native-protocol client, on its own, in a new crate `crates/pulse` (`filmcraft-pulse`). Nothing in the app uses it yet; #2407 (part 2) wires it into playback. For #106 and #2117.

The first commit is @Chace-Berry's client from #332 as he wrote it (only its `crates/platform` part); the second is mine, from the reviews of #332 and #2407; the third moves it unchanged out of `crates/platform` into its own crate.

**Where it lives.** ADR 0001 and AGENTS.md keep `crates/platform` to OS media FFI, and this is audio output in safe Rust over a socket (CodeRabbit's point, and the scope point in the review of #2407). So it is `crates/pulse`: L5 beside `platform` in `cargo xtask layers`, the workspace lints with `unsafe_code` forbidden, Linux only and an empty crate elsewhere. `platform` no longer depends on `pulseaudio`; `docs/architecture.md` lists the new crate.

**What it does** (`crates/pulse/src/lib.rs`, about 1,250 lines with tests):
- **Connect:** to the server's Unix socket, found as libpulse finds it. The first `unix:` or absolute-path entry of `PULSE_SERVER` (also with a `{machine-id}` prefix) wins, else `$PULSE_RUNTIME_PATH/native`, else `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/pulse/native`. A `PULSE_SERVER` that names only network servers (`tcp:host:port`, `host`) gives no socket, so the caller uses ALSA, whose `pulse` plugin is libpulse and follows the variable there. Before, the crate's lookup skipped such a value and connected to the local server instead.
- **Handshake:** authenticate with the cookie (`PULSE_COOKIE`, `~/.config/pulse/cookie`, `~/.pulse-cookie`) and name the client. **Shared memory and memfd are both off** (`supports_shm: false`, `supports_memfd: false`), so audio goes over the socket as memblocks and nothing else is needed; the receipts below play on both servers that way.

title: perf(export): add opt-in SDR RGBA8 GPU readback fast path
author: ZpdyGonzales
body:
Summary

This PR introduces an opt-in RGBA8 GPU readback fast path for opaque SDR video exports.

Instead of reading back floating-point pixel data and converting it to 8-bit sRGB on the CPU, eligible frames can be read back directly as RGBA8.

The optimization is disabled by default.

Implementation

  • Adds an optional render_rgba8() method to the FrameRenderer interface.

  • Integrates RGBA8 readback into the GPU export renderer, CLI, and desktop application.

  • Enables the optimization only when FILMCRAFT_ENABLE_RGBA8_FASTPATH=1.

  • Restricts the fast path to eligible opaque SDR frames.

  • Falls back to the existing rendering path for HDR, transparency, unsupported effects, transitions, or invalid output.

  • Validates frame dimensions, buffer length, and alpha values before using the optimized output.

title: Stop writing an empty ref for FCPXML titles and adjustment layers (#2638)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2638.

The FCPXML export wrote a graphic (title) clip or an adjustment layer as `<asset-clip ref="">`. An empty `ref` is not a valid IDREF, so the file fails the FCPXML DTD and Final Cut Pro refuses the whole import.

These clips have no asset to reference, so the export no longer writes a clip element for them:

- **On V1 (primary storyline):** written as a `<gap>` with the clip's name, offset and duration, so the rest of the storyline keeps its timing. This is what the exporter already did for generators.
- **On other tracks (connected clips):** left out. A `<gap>` is only allowed in a spine and has no `lane` attribute, so a connected gap would fail the DTD too. The issue says leaving the graphic out is enough, as long as the report says so.

Each clip is still named in the export report, which now says what really happens to it (`graphic clip "Opening" at frame 12 is not supported in FCPXML: it is left out …` / `… it is written as a gap …`). Before, it said "a clip without media", which hid that the whole file was broken.

A connected generator had the same issue: it was written as a gap with a `lane`. It now uses the same rule as titles and adjustment layers (gap on V1, left out elsewhere). Both cases use one helper, `unsupported`, so they cannot drift apart. The FCPXML row of the "Graphics and adjustment layers" table in `crates/interchange/README.md` is updated.

Test: `fcpxml_has_no_empty_ref_for_a_title` in `crates/interchange/tests/uncarried_clips.rs`. It exports the existing fixture (a media clip on V1, an adjustment layer on V1, a title on V2) and checks four things: there is no `ref=""`, the adjustment layer is a primary gap, the connected title is absent, and both are named in the report. On `main` it fails on the empty `ref`.

title: #2419: Bokeh Blur runs on the GPU
author: ded-achtung
body:
Addresses the Bokeh Blur part of #2419, with the "right" fix from @00xJS's analysis in that thread.

### What was wrong
Bokeh Blur had no GPU op. A clip carrying it left the GPU compositor's layer path (`gpu_chain` returns `None`), so every frame with it was composited on the CPU while the GPU sat idle. The CPU gather takes up to 625 bilinear taps per pixel. The worst case is an amount just under 12 px, where no halving happens yet.

### Change
- **render** (`gpufx.rs`, `vfx/blur.rs`, `vfx/mod.rs`): Bokeh Blur is now an `FxOp`, following the recipe in `docs/contributing.md`:
  - parameters are evaluated in `FxOp::eval`, including how many times the working image is halved;
  - the existing CPU code becomes the reference in `FxOp::apply`;
  - the id goes into `GPU_EFFECTS`.
  
  The CPU output is unchanged. The one difference is that a non-finite amount is now a no-op instead of producing NaN pixels.
- **gpu** (`fx.rs`, `fx.wgsl`): the GPU version uses four kinds of passes. They work on the top-left part of the same-size working textures, so the ping-pong stage needs no new texture sizes:
  1. one halving per level (`Image::downsample2`);
  2. the highlight boost;
  3. the iris gather (`sample_bilinear_clamped` within the halved image; the taps are computed in the shader);
  4. the scale back up (`Image::transformed`'s bilinear, with the inverse computed in f64 as on the CPU).

### Numbers (1080p; RTX 4070 Laptop vs 16 CPU threads, release)

| Amount | Halvings | CPU | GPU (effect only*) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 6 | 0 | 947 ms | ~9 ms |
| 12 | 0 | 3 250 ms | ~39 ms |
| 20 | 1 | 617 ms | ~6 ms |
| 60 (default) | 3 | 62 ms | < 1 ms |

\* Each GPU figure is an `effect_image` call minus the same call with a trivial op (~11 ms of upload and readback).

### Tests
- `gpu_effects_match_cpu_exactly`: six Bokeh cases match the CPU reference to < 1e-6 (the gate is 1e-4), with no flips. They cover:
  - a no-op amount;
  - 0, 2 and up to 6 halvings on an odd-sized image;
  - cir…

title: #1673: the Program monitor keeps playing while a value is dragged
author: ded-achtung
body:
Fixes #1673.

### What was wrong
A value dragged in Effect Controls during playback (Crop in the report; Scale or any other value behaves the same) creates a new project revision on every UI pass. Two things then stopped the picture:

1. `FrameServer::schedule_playback` cancelled every job still rendering a frame for an older revision (`retain_queue(|k| ... k.revision == rev ...)`). The frames ahead were thrown away on each pass, before they could finish.
2. While playing, the Program monitor only showed frames at the current revision. `nearest_plan`, `nearest` and the 6-frames-back search all key on the revision, and `asked_before` is cleared while playing. With nothing ready at the current revision, it held the last presented picture.

Together, the picture stayed on the frame from before the drag until the mouse rested. Paused, this was already solved (`program_monitor_follows_a_value_that_changes_every_pass` and `a_newer_revision_keeps_the_frame_being_rendered`); playback had no equivalent.

### Change (`ui-egui`)
- `schedule_playback` still drops *queued* jobs of older revisions. A job *already rendering* a frame ahead of the playhead, for one of the last `PLAYING_REVISION_LAG` (64) revisions, is now left to finish. `retain_queue` keeps its behaviour through the new private `retain_jobs`.
- New `FrameServer::recent(key, max_back, lag)` finds the cached frame closest at or before the frame due (up to 6 frames back), preferring the newest of the last `lag` revisions. It works on plans or images, according to the target, and makes at most 7 × 65 hash lookups under one lock.
- The monitor uses `recent` as the last fallback while playing, on both the GPU plan path and the CPU image path. The paused behaviour is unchanged.

### Tests (`ui-egui/tests/perf_ui.rs`, next to the paused equivalents)
- `program_monitor_plays_on_while_a_value_is_dragged`: the demo project with Crop on the first clip is played while Crop's Left changes on every pass (90 passes, 16 ms apart).

title: Vertical pan drags now scroll the half of the timeline they started in
author: bfenty
body:
## Fix: vertical pan drags scroll the half of the timeline they started in

**Closes #2536**

### Root cause
The mouse wheel picks the half under the pointer (`p.y < layout.split_y` → video, else audio), but `Drag::Pan` — started by the middle button or the Hand tool — hardcoded `v_scroll += dy` for vertical movement and never recorded where the drag began. A vertical drag that started over the audio tracks scrolled the video tracks instead.

### Fix
`Drag::Pan` now carries `audio: bool`, set at drag start from the press position against `layout.split_y` (for the middle button, from `press_origin`, matching where the drag actually begins). The live drag moves `a_scroll` when `audio` and `v_scroll` otherwise — with the same sign convention the wheel uses (dragging up scrolls later audio content in, as before for video). The cancel/restore path restores whichever scroll the drag actually moved.

title: Warp Stabilizer 1/6: bounded trajectory tracking foundation
author: Firstbober
body:
Slice 1 of 6 from the Warp Stabilizer split agreed in #2021. Stacked; this PR contains only the tracking foundation the later subspace/planning PRs build on.

**Contents**

- `trajectories.rs` — persistent-trajectory collector: associates supplied Shi–Tomasi corners with active tracks via one pyramidal forward/backward LK pass; bounded active-track count (160), minimum track length (20), bounded observations.
- `epipolar.rs` — dynamic-scene rejection: normalized eight-point fundamental matrix checked every fifth frame; a trajectory is rejected only when more than a third of its checks violate the model. Depth parallax stays a valid observation (no similarity-fit gating).
- `trajectory_index.rs` — bounded CSR frame→track index so factorisation and mesh planning visit only observations that can exist at a frame.
- `trajectory_data.rs` — shared bounded observation set; the 160-track / 1e9-coordinate / 20-frame contract is defined once here (collector produces under it, index and factoriser validate against it).
- `track.rs` — bounded multi-frame preparation and LK entry points (unchanged existing tracker behaviour).
- `numerics.rs` — symmetric eigensolver used by the epipolar filter.
- `contributors/people.toml` — credit entry for this stack.

**Temporary scaffolding**: `solve()` and the data fields consumed by the stacked subspace/planning PRs (`segment_starts`, `saliency`, `PointConstraint`, index `frames` accessors, the whole collector entry) carry `allow(dead_code)` with the consuming PR noted; those allows are removed by the slice that wires them in.

**Verification** (Rust 1.95.0, focused): `filmcraft-render --lib` 208 passed / 0 failed; `clippy --release --all-targets -D warnings` clean. Machine: i9-13900K, 32 threads. No performance claims in this slice.

author: alexanderalber
body:
Adds Premiere's **WB Selector** to Lumetri ▸ Basic Correction: a pipette next to Temperature and Tint. Arm it, click something white or gray in the Program monitor, and Temperature and Tint are set so that point comes out neutral, in one undo step.

**What**

- `filmcraft_render::effects::lumetri_white_balance` inverts Lumetri's own white-balance gains: Temperature evens out red and blue, Tint brings green to their mean, both clamped to the slider range (a cast beyond it is removed as far as the sliders reach). The gains formula moved into `lumetri_wb_gains`, which the CPU path and the GPU op builder now both call, so they cannot drift apart.
- New engine command `lumetri.whiteBalance {clip?, x?, y?, color?}` (documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`). The point is read where the white balance sees it: the clip with the effects before Lumetri and its Input LUT, none of Lumetri's other settings and nothing after it. So the current grade does not skew the pick, and picking the same spot again gives the same result. Animated sliders get a keyframe at the playhead (`Param::set_at`, as `effects.setParam` does). `color` takes a linear colour instead of a point, for agents.
- Lumetri panel: a "WB Selector" row with the existing eyedropper icon (automation id `lumetri.wbSelector`). It reuses the Program monitor's eyedropper mode (crosshair, Esc disarms); on click the monitor runs `lumetri.whiteBalance` instead of `effects.setParam`. The new strings are translated in the catalogs that require `tl!` coverage (es, fr, it, pt-br, de, ja, zh-cn, ko, id).

**Not in this PR:** the Auto button. #2378 (Auto Color Correction, #1152) covers that and solves the same inversion inline. Once both have landed it can call `lumetri_white_balance` / `lumetri_wb_gains`.

**Tests**

- render: the solved sliders make the picked colour exactly neutral; exposure does not change the pick; a strong cast stops at ±100; black, negative, NaN and infinite picks solve nothing.

title: M8: Lumetri HSL Secondary Set / Add / Remove color pickers and Invert Mask
author: alexanderalber
body:
Adds the Key colour pickers and Invert Mask to Lumetri ▸ HSL Secondary. Until now the key could only be built by dragging Hue / Hue Range / Saturation Min / Luma Min / Max; now you arm a pipette, click the colour in the Program monitor, and the key forms around it.

The roadmap's M8 "HSL Secondary refine" item was already done (Denoise and Blur landed in 2a199425); this PR drops that stale entry and fills the parts of the HSL Secondary Key group that were still missing.

**What**

- `filmcraft_render::effects::lumetri_hsl_key_pick(e, t, working, colour, Set|Add|Remove)` returns the new key sliders. It reads the colour the way the key does (same HDR normalisation, factored into `hsl_unit`) and uses Soften as the margin, so the picked colour ends up fully keyed or fully out:
  - **Set color**: Hue on the colour, default Hue Range (30°), Saturation Min at half its saturation, Luma window of ±(Soften + 0.2) around it.
  - **Add color**: the hue arc grows from its far edge to the colour (capped at 180°, wraps through red), Saturation Min and the Luma window move out just enough. A colour already inside changes nothing.
  - **Remove color**: of the four edges that could leave the colour out (near hue edge, Saturation Min, Luma Min, Luma Max), the one with the shortest way to move. So a neighbouring hue gets cut on the hue axis and a darker shade of the keyed hue at Luma Min. A colour already outside changes nothing.
  - The exact rules are my own. I don't know what heuristic Premiere uses for Add/Remove; the behaviour above is documented in the function and `docs/architecture.md`.
- New engine command `lumetri.hslKey {clip?, mode: set|add|remove, x?, y?, color?}` (documented in `docs/control-protocol.md`). The point is read where the key sees it: the clip with Lumetri's grade up to HSL Secondary, but not HSL Secondary itself, Lumetri's sharpening or the effects after Lumetri. So picking the same spot again gives the same key. One undo step per pick, switches HSL Secondary…

title: #30: VA-API AV1 hardware decoding on Linux
author: OliWoly
body:
Part of #30.

On Linux, AV1 footage always decoded in software, even on GPUs that decode AV1 in hardware. For high-bitrate recordings that's slower than real time, and the Program monitor then shows almost nothing while playing or scrubbing. Example: a gpu-screen-recorder clip, AV1 2560×1440 60 fps 10-bit at ~49 Mbit/s, played back on an RX 7900 XTX (radeonsi). Software decode ran at ~24 fps, and the monitor froze on one frame for the whole play.

This adds AV1 Main (8- and 10-bit 4:2:0) to the VA-API backend, built the same way as the H.264 and HEVC paths.

**Change**
- **`filmcraft-av1`:** the OBU, frame-header and reference-state code moves out of `Decoder` into a public, header-only `Parser` that doesn't decode tiles. `Decoder` now uses it, so the software and hardware paths read the stream with the same code.
  - `TileInfo` keeps `uniform_tile_spacing_flag`.
  - `warp_valid()` exposes the shear-setup check, used for VA's global-motion `invalid` flag.
- **`filmcraft-platform`:**
  - FFI for `va_dec_av1.h`, with ABI tests whose sizes, offsets and bit positions were generated by a C program against libva 2.24.
  - `vaapi/av1.rs`: keeps the eight reference slots as surfaces and sends one picture-parameter buffer plus one slice buffer per tile. It handles `show_existing_frame` and reads each shown frame back immediately (AV1 has no output reordering).
  - `VaDecoder::new_frame`, and `vaapi_factory` / `hardware_decoder_for` now route `av1C` entries to it.
  - Film grain, scalable streams, size changes and scaled references are returned as errors, so `HybridDecoder` carries on in software (film grain is applied by our decoder).
- **Docs:** platform README, README, roadmap / gaps, and the Settings ▸ Playback help text, updated in all 8 catalogs.

**Results** (RX 7900 XTX, Mesa 26.2.4 radeonsi)
| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Decode speed, the clip above (`filmcraft-cli bench-decode`) | 24.4 fps | 64.4 fps |
| Program monitor, 6 s of playback | froze after 20 frame…

title: Text: 縦中横 (tate-chu-yoko) for vertical titles
author: midasdf
body:
## What changed

A vertical title stacked "12" one digit per cell — the text engine had no horizontal-in-vertical
setting, so the standard Japanese title treatment 縦中横 (tate-chu-yoko) was impossible. This PR
adds it as a layer property and a per-character style, and lays it out in the text engine.

**縦中横** — with the new `tate_chu_yoko` property on a text layer (Text section ▸ **Tate-Chu-Yoko**,
off by default, enabled only while **Vertical Text** is on), 2–4 consecutive half-width printable
ASCII characters set with it share one cell of the vertical column: they stand upright side by side
across the column, and the rows after the group move up by the cells it saves — so the text after
the group, the title's alignment and its origin all stay on the same grid. The cell keeps one caret
stop per character boundary, so the caret, clicks, selection, hit testing and underlines keep
working; horizontal text ignores the property, as Premiere does.

- **filmcraft-project**: `tate_chu_yoko` on `CharStyle` (per-character ranges, saved with
  `LayerExtra`) and as a layer parameter of the hidden `graphic_text` effect; `TextProps` and
  `eval_layer` carry it. Project files need no migration: parameters are additive and older files
  read the default (`false`).
- **filmcraft-text**: `TextStyle::tate_chu_yoko` (hashed for the layout cache); vertical layout
  groups flagged cells into one row of the column instead of one row each.
- **filmcraft-render**: the layer flag reaches the base `TextStyle` and character-style runs

title: Lumetri: Luma vs Sat and Sat vs Sat stop wrapping; hue curves meet exactly at red
author: alexanderalber
body:
## What and why

**Luma vs Sat and Sat vs Sat wrapped around like hue curves.** Both went through `hue_lut`, which repeats the points one period left and right. Their axes run black to white and grey to full saturation; the ends are not neighbours (in Premiere these curves do not wrap either). A Luma vs Sat curve with points (0.5, 0.5) and (0.9, 0), i.e. "desaturate the highlights", gave black a value of 0.04 instead of the neutral 0.5, so the darkest pixels lost about 93% of their saturation. They now use a plain monotone curve (`vs_sat_lut`), neutral 0.5 without points and flat beyond the outermost points, in the render and in the curve editor's drawing.

**Hue curves had a small step at red.** The hue curves are periodic, but the LUT slice was off by a third of a sample: entry `i` held hue `(3i+1)/(3n-1)` instead of `i/(n-1)`, leaving a 0.23 degree gap where 360 meets 0. With a steep curve through red (points at 7 and 353 degrees) the probe measured 0.4893 at hue 0.99997 against 0.5098 at hue 0, a step of 0.02 (for Hue vs Hue that is a 7 degree jump in output hue). Sampling `3n - 2` entries puts the slice on the exact grid, so the first and last entries are both red and equal, and the slopes on both sides agree. The curve editor uses the same function now instead of its own copy.

Not changed, checked: Hue vs Hue's rotation already wraps (`rem_euclid`), the HSL Secondary key uses a circular hue distance, and the GPU path hands every non-empty curve to the CPU, so there is no second implementation.

## How tested

New tests, all three failed before the fix:
- `effects::curve_tests::hue_curve_has_no_seam_at_red`: first and last LUT entries equal, value at red midway, slopes match across the wrap, control points land on their grid entry.
- `effects::curve_tests::vs_sat_curves_do_not_wrap`: black and white follow the left and right point.
- `effects::tests::luma_vs_sat_highlight_point_leaves_shadows_saturated`: end to end through Lumetri, a dark red keeps its saturat…

title: fix(ui): submit clip dialogs on Enter key (#2659)
author: kk376
body:
Fixes #2659.

### Problem
When a modal clip dialog (such as **Clip Speed / Duration** (`clip.speedDuration`)) was open, editing a field and pressing `Enter` failed to submit or close the dialog, forcing the user to reach for the mouse to click "OK".

Two issues contributed:
1. Application-wide shortcuts (specifically `Enter` mapped to `sequence.renderEffectsInToOut`) intercepted and consumed the `Enter` key event before modal dialogs were rendered.
2. `clip_dialogs::show` only handled `Escape` cancellation and lacked an `Enter` submission trigger for the `OK` action.

### Changes
1. In `crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs` (`FilmcraftApp::handle_shortcuts`), yield application shortcuts when `self.ui.clip_dialog.is_some()`.
2. In `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/clip_dialogs.rs`, trigger the `ok` action when `Enter` is pressed and no pointer is held.
3. In `crates/ui-egui/tests/clip_dialogs_ui.rs`, add a headless UI regression test verifying that pressing `Enter` submits the `clip.speedDuration` dialog and applies the modified parameters.

title: #2489: an imported shortcut set is always listed; .kys files explain why they can't be read
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Refs #2489 (the FilmCraft round trip is fixed; importing Premiere's own `.kys` files is not supported yet).

#2489 reports two things: shortcuts imported from Premiere don't show up in the preset dropdown, and neither does a set exported from FilmCraft and imported back.

## The round trip (fixed)
Exporting a built-in set suggests `FilmCraft Default.json` (or `Premiere Pro Compatible.json`), and the file carries that built-in name. On import, a built-in name in the file fell back to the file's name, which is the same built-in name. The preset was saved and made active, but `user_presets` leaves built-in names out of the list, so it never appeared in the dropdown.

`import_name` now picks the set's own name, else the file's, and adds " (Imported)" when that is a built-in preset's name. An exported built-in set comes back as "FilmCraft Default (Imported)", listed and active.

## Premiere `.kys` files (explained, not imported)
The Import dialog only offered `.json`, so a `.kys` couldn't even be picked. It now accepts `.kys` too, and reading one gives a clear error: Premiere Pro .kys files can't be imported yet; choose the "Premiere Pro Compatible" preset for Premiere's default keys. Reading Premiere's own command names into FilmCraft ids is a separate feature.

Also: shortcut files over 8 MB are refused before reading (hostile input, capped allocation).

## Tests
`shortcuts_tests` (the save/load/export/import test) now exports the active "FilmCraft Default" to `FilmCraft Default.json` and imports it back, expecting "FilmCraft Default (Imported)" active and in `custom`. A `.kys` file gives the explanatory error.

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine shortcut` pass (macOS). `docs/keyboard.md` describes Export/Import.

title: fix(media): bound decoded animated GIF and APNG frames in shared cache (#2474)
author: kk376
body:
Fixes #2474. Sibling to #2464 / #2469.

### Problem
`AnimatedSource` (`crates/media/src/animated.rs`) decoded every frame of an animated GIF or APNG at open time and retained all decoded RGBA frames as an owned `Vec<Arc<VideoFrame>>`. Because the media pool never evicts open sources for active project items, importing reaction GIFs or screen recordings permanently inflated process RSS by hundreds of megabytes to gigabytes with no eviction mechanism or LRU ceiling.

### Solution
Mirrors the bounded frame cache architecture used for stills and video GOPs:

- **Shared Frame Cache**: Animated sources no longer own decoded frames. Decoded pictures live in a process-wide byte-budgeted `FrameCache<(u64, usize)>` (`ANIMATED_BUDGET` = 1 GiB), keyed by `(source_id, frame_index)`.
- **Lightweight State**: `AnimatedSource` retains its duration/timing table (`starts: Vec<Tick>`), raw frame mapping (`raw_indices: Vec<usize>`), and encoded file bytes (`bytes: Arc<[u8]>`), keeping source structs at ~kilobytes instead of tens or hundreds of megabytes.
- **On-Demand Decode**: On a cache miss in `video_frame`, frames are streamed from the file's encoded bytes up to the requested frame. Intermediate frames encountered along the way are populated into the cache.
- **Eviction & Cleanup**: When an `AnimatedSource` is dropped, `cache.retain(|&(id, _)| id != self.id)` immediately frees all of its cached frames.
- **Telemetry**: `perf.stats` now exposes `decode.animatedCacheMB` and `decode.animatedBudgetMB`.

### Testing
- Added regression test `animated_sources_share_a_bounded_cache_and_decode_again_after_eviction` verifying eviction under memory budget, deterministic on-demand re-decode, and source drop eviction.
- All 84 tests in `crates/media` and engine `perf.stats` tests pass cleanly.
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-media -p filmcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean.

title: #2679: effects.setParam refuses values outside the parameter's range
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Fixes #2679.

`effects.setParam` saved any number for a float parameter, even far outside the range `effects.list` publishes for it. Levels gamma 1.1 (a factor where the parameter is a percentage, 10–1000) was stored, and the frame rendered almost black. Lumetri saturation 500, vibrance −300, opacity 250 and Motion scale −50 went through the same way. Agents and scripts (CLI, MCP, control channel) get no hint until they look at the picture.

## Change
`effects.setParam` checks a float value against the parameter's hard `min`/`max` (`ParamKind::Float`, which `effects.list` reports) before writing. A value outside the range is refused with ``"`gamma` must be between 10 and 1000, got 1.1"``, and nothing is saved, so there's no undo step either. The ends of the range are accepted. The UI already clamps typed values to the same hard range, so interactive editing doesn't change. Mask parameters, which have no definition, are left as they were.

## Tests
- New `vfx_tests::set_param_refuses_values_outside_the_range`: the five values from the issue are refused with the range, the project and undo history are unchanged, and in-range values (including both ends) still go in.
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine -p filmcraft-ui-egui -p filmcraft-cli` passes with no failures, so no UI or CLI path relies on out-of-range values. `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` also pass (macOS).

title: #2689: Reveal in Finder resolves project-relative paths; Reveal Proxy in Finder
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Fixes #2689.

**Reveal in Finder** on a Project panel clip could open Documents instead of the clip's folder. `file.reveal` (and **Edit Original**, which shares the code) handed the *stored* media path to the file manager. A project stores paths relative to itself when it was moved, shared, or imported from another editor, and the media pool resolves those against the project's folder when it opens the files (`MediaPool::follow`). Reveal didn't. It passed `take.mp4` on as-is, and with a relative path the file manager falls back to its default folder (Explorer's `/select,` lands in Documents).

## Changes
- `edit_original` / `file.reveal` resolve each path through `MediaPool::follow`, the same resolution the media pool uses to open the file. A path that `doc_path` refuses (another computer's, a network share) gives an error naming it instead of a wrong folder.
- New **Reveal Proxy in Finder** (`file.revealProxy`) in the Project panel's **Proxy** submenu (`project.itemMenu.proxy.reveal`), enabled when the clip has a proxy attached. It shows the proxy file, resolved the same way. That's the explicit proxy action the issue asks for, while Reveal in Finder keeps showing the original media. The label is translated in the full catalogs.

## Tests
- New `project_tools_tests::reveal_resolves_paths_stored_relative_to_the_project`: a clip with an attached proxy is saved, the project file is rewritten with paths relative to it, and the project is reopened. Reveal and Reveal Proxy give the real media and proxy files. Before the fix, Reveal returned `take.mp4` and failed.
- The existing `file_reveal_enabled_for_imported_clip` still passes, along with `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine project_tools`, the i18n catalog tests, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` (macOS).

The issue's report isn't reproduced on Windows itself; the relative stored path is the cause I found in the code, and the test covers it.

title: #2714: Linux: start on Xwayland so files dropped from a file manager arrive
author: OliWoly
body:
Part 1 of #2714. winit 0.30 (eframe 0.36 / 0.37) implements no file drag-and-drop on Wayland, so files dragged from Dolphin / Nautilus never reach the Project panel or the Timeline on a Wayland desktop. Its X11 backend does, also through Xwayland.

## Changes
- **`apps/filmcraft/src/display.rs`** (ported from DeckCraft): start on X11 when `DISPLAY` is set. `FILMCRAFT_WAYLAND=1` keeps native Wayland; a local `DISPLAY` with no X server falls back to Wayland; no display at all gets a plain message. Unit tests included.
- **Drop position under X11:** XDND sends the target no pointer motion and winit discards the drop coordinates, so a Timeline drop landed where the pointer last was. When started on X11, `HostHooks::cursor_screen_position` now asks the X server (`platform::cursor::x11_cursor_screen_position`: `QueryPointer` via `x11rb`'s pure-Rust connection, safe code, already in the lockfile through winit).
- **Docs:** README (Linux) and `docs/ui-parity.md` say what works where.

## Trade-offs
- Under Xwayland, fractional scaling is blurry on KDE / GNOME (fine at integer scales); `FILMCRAFT_WAYLAND=1` is the escape hatch.
- The Flatpak (`--socket=fallback-x11`) has no X11 while Wayland is available, so it stays native and still gets no drops. The follow-up PR (native Wayland drops in `crates/platform`, with a proposed ADR 0002) fixes that and makes native Wayland the default again.

## Testing
- Manually on CachyOS, KDE Plasma 6.8 Wayland: the window is an X11 client (`WM_CLASS` `ai.storyteller.filmcraft`), and a clip dragged from Dolphin was imported and placed on V2 at the drop point.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets` and `cargo xtask wasm` pass. `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: everything passes except two tests that already fail on `main` on this machine (`dev_icon::tests::desktop_file_matches_the_packaged_fields`; VA-API `bit_exact_with_the_software_decoder`, where `va…

title: Import Premiere .prfpset files and add Presets folder context menu
author: justdxvid
body:
FilmCraft currently supports hand-saved and built-in effect presets, but lacks support for importing Adobe Premiere Pro effect presets (`.prfpset`), which are widely used by editors and creators. Furthermore, the Effects panel had no direct context menu on preset folders to import, reveal, or rescan preset files on disk.

This change introduces native support for parsing, indexing, and applying Premiere Pro `.prfpset` presets as well as file-backed preset libraries:

- **Premiere `.prfpset` Parsing (`crates/engine/src/prfpset.rs`):**

  - Scans and indexes presets recursively within `<data_dir>/Effect Presets` (supporting both `.prfpset` and `.json`).

title: security: enforce HTTPS on curl downloads (SonarCloud S6506)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Enforces HTTPS on `curl` downloads flagged by SonarCloud rule **S6506** (`shell:S6506`, `docker:S6506`, `githubactions:S6506`, Security).

These `curl` calls use `-L`/`-fsSL` (follow redirects). A redirect could transparently downgrade to plaintext HTTP, exposing the download to MITM tampering. Adding `--proto '=https'` forces curl to refuse any non-HTTPS protocol, including across redirects, without changing behavior for the legitimate HTTPS endpoints already in use.

## Change
`curl <args>` → `curl --proto '=https' <args>` on each flagged line.

title: #2670: an export in progress locks its settings; Export becomes Cancel
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Fixes #2670.

While an export from Export mode ran, its settings (file name, preset, format, …) could still be changed. Clicking **Export** again started a second job writing the same file from the start, so the export looked like it restarted.

## Changes
- **Engine:** `Session::export_targets` records the file each export job writes. `spawn_export` (used by `file.exportMedia` and the Export Queue) refuses a second export to a file while a job is still writing it: "busy.wav is being exported already; wait for it to finish or cancel it". This protects agents and the CLI too, not just the button.
- **Export mode:** while the file these settings export to is being exported (`export_mode::running_export`):
  - the settings column is disabled, so nothing can change under the running export;
  - **Send to Queue** is off;
  - **Export** turns into **Cancel** and cancels that job (`jobs.cancel`).
  Once the job finishes, everything is back. Exports of other files (other names or folders) aren't affected. "Export cancelled" is translated in the full catalogs.

## Tests
- New `export_ui::an_export_in_progress_locks_its_settings_and_export_cancels_it`. A real export ends too soon to catch, so the test registers an unfinished job for the target file. Then: the button reads Cancel, a typed file name doesn't take, `file.exportMedia` to the same file is refused, Send to Queue adds nothing, clicking the button cancels the job, and once the job has finished the button reads Export again.

title: #2674: waveform peaks cover the whole clip when audio comes back short or a chunk fails
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Refs #2674 (a cause found in the code; the report's file isn't available to confirm it's this one).

The timeline places waveform peak `i` at sample `i × 256` (48 kHz). `source_peaks` built the peaks chunk by chunk from whatever the source returned, so the waveform could end early or slide:

- **A short chunk** (fewer samples than asked, e.g. a 44.1 kHz WAV resampled to 48 kHz a chunk at a time) produced fewer peaks. Everything after it moved earlier, and the waveform ended before the clip.
- **A chunk that failed to read** stopped the loop (`Err(_) => break`), and the partial peaks were cached. The waveform ended at that point for good.

## Change
`source_peaks` always returns one peak per 256 samples of the whole duration:
- each chunk is padded (or cut) to exactly the peaks it covers;
- a chunk that fails is silence, and the next chunk is still read;
- after four failures in a row the rest is silence, so a broken source isn't asked chunk by chunk to its end.

The chunk size is a multiple of 256, so every chunk starts a peak of its own, and `PEAK_SAMPLES` names the constant the drawing uses too.

## Tests
New `peaks_tests::peaks_cover_the_whole_duration_whatever_the_source_returns` (a source wrapper that returns every chunk 300 samples short, or fails for one chunk, or for all). The peak count always matches the duration, the failed chunk is silent, and the chunks after it are unchanged.

`cargo clippy -p filmcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check` and the timeline/audio UI tests pass (macOS). Not checked against the reporter's file, which wasn't attached.

title: fix: use async file I/O in async MCP handler (SonarCloud rust:S7493)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Fixes a reliability bug (SonarCloud **rust:S7493**) in the async MCP `screenshot` handler in `crates/automation/src/server.rs`.

The handler used blocking `std::fs::read` / `std::fs::remove_file` inside an `async fn` running on the Tokio runtime, which blocks the executor thread and can stall other tasks.

## Change
- `std::fs::read(&path)` → `tokio::fs::read(&path).await`
- `std::fs::remove_file(&path)` → `tokio::fs::remove_file(&path).await`
- Enable the `fs` feature on the `tokio` dependency.

Verified with `cargo check` on the `filmcraft-automation` crate.

## Note
The other `rust:S7493` findings in `apps/filmcraft-cli/src/main.rs` are in a single-shot `#[tokio::main]` CLI command path (no concurrent tasks to starve); they are intentionally left as blocking I/O and can be marked Won't Fix.

author: OliWoly
body:
Part 2 of #2714. **Stacked on #2715**, whose commit is included here (review the commits after #2715's two, starting at `d26e744e`; later ones are review fixes); after #2715 merges only these remain.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Needs a decision from the project owner:** this adds one `unsafe` call to `crates/platform` that falls outside ADR 0001 (media FFI only). It comes with a **proposed** [ADR 0002](docs/adr/0002-platform-window-system.md), which covers this and the existing Windows `GetCursorPos` call (`cursor.rs`, #171), currently without a written decision. If the ADR is rejected, #2715 alone still gives Linux working drops through Xwayland.

## Why
winit 0.30 (eframe 0.36 / 0.37) implements no drag-and-drop on Wayland. #2715 works around that by running through Xwayland, which is blurry at fractional scales and doesn't help the Flatpak (no X11 while Wayland is available). This PR receives the drops ourselves, so native Wayland is the default again.

- **`platform::wayland_dnd`** (Linux): joins the window's own libwayland connection, the way egui's clipboard (`smithay-clipboard`) does. title: Script: organize takes against screenplay lines
author: whatever-industries
body:
**ScriptSync is a fundamental tool in scripted film and television editing.** It links screenplay lines to the setups and takes that cover them, helping editors quickly find alternate line reads. This PR brings that style of script-based organization into FilmCraft through the new Script window, adding a mandatory feature used universally on top tier narrative productions. Here's a demonstration of the original (which I've improved upon): https://www.youtube.com/shorts/TWvj0ZWhlqw

The dockable Script window displays editable screenplay lines beside setup thumbnails and take candles. Editors can import a UTF-8 plain-text `.txt` script, add scene and page labels, link Project clips to rows, adjust take coverage, and place frame-specific marks. Scripts and their media references are saved with the project.

Plain text can also be pasted from another app with Cmd-V/Ctrl-V or Edit → Paste. With no script open, paste creates one; otherwise it inserts after the selected rows or appends. Inside a row editor, it replaces the character selection at the caret, with each hard line break adding a row and shifting later rows down. Existing row IDs, labels, candles, and marks remain attached. One Undo removes the paste while retaining preceding typing. Clicking outside the text box—including the next row's right margin—commits valid edits, closes the editor, and releases input even if the editor has already lost keyboard focus. An unchanged blur adds no Undo step.

Shortening candle coverage hides marks, row colors, and off-screen passages while preserving their IDs, line references, and source times. Expanding coverage restores them. Hidden marks have no canvas target and do not anchor visible-row cue interpolation. Candles extend to the exact first and last covered-row boundaries, including blank or wrapped rows; thumbnails and take numbers sit above coverage. Gray end caps remain short and equal. Repeated Scene/Page labels remain separate menu entries in script order.

title: Project thumbnails on Home's Recent Projects
author: texjer
body:
**Depends on #2547 (Home screen).** This branch is built on it, so until #2547 merges the diff here also shows its commit. The thumbnail work is the last two commits: 318ede5e and dbc322d6.

Recent Projects on Home now show a picture of each project.

**Saving** (`crates/format`, `crates/engine`): each save stores the frame the Program Monitor shows (the active sequence at its playhead, rendered straight at 320 px on its longest side) in the `.fcproj` as a base64 JPEG:


- It is written before `project`, so `filmcraft_format::read_thumbnail(path)` reads only the start of the file (at most about 0.75 MB, whatever the project's size) and never builds the project.
- Nothing in it is trusted on read. Shapes that don't match, sizes over 1024 px or 512 KB, bad base64 and wrong signatures are ignored, never a load error. Decoding uses `image::Limits`. A save with no open sequence, or one whose frame can't be rendered, keeps the previous thumbnail. The thumbnail never fails a save.
- Format: `docs/project-files.md`.

**Home** (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/home.rs`): rows are 48 px tall, with the thumbnail fitted into a 16:9 frame (vertical and square projects keep their shape) and the folder under the name. Projects without a thumbnail keep the sequence icon. Other projects' thumbnails are read once on a background thread under `catch_unwind`. title: Link Media: Offline All is saved, so reopening the project doesn't ask again
author: texjer
body:
**Problem.** Clicking **Offline All** in the Link Media dialog and saving didn't stick: the next time the project opened, Link Media asked about the same files again. In Premiere Pro, Offline All is remembered.

**Cause.** `media.offlineAll` only closed the dialog (`s.offline.prompt = false`). It never set `MediaClip::offline`, so nothing was saved, and `relink::on_open` treated those clips as newly missing.

**Fix**
- `media.offlineAll` marks every missing clip offline as one undo step, so the choice is saved with the project. Relinking still clears the mark.
- `relink::on_open` shows the dialog only for clips that are missing (`status == "missing"`), not for ones made offline on purpose. If other media goes missing later, the next open asks about just that.
- When the dialog opens on project open, it lists only the newly missing files. File ▸ Link Media… still lists every offline clip so they can be reconnected.
- The per-file **Offline** button marks its clip offline too, the same as Make Offline.
- **Cancel** (and Esc) only closes the dialog, so the files stay missing for this session and the next open asks again.

**Test:** `relink_tests::offline_all_is_saved_and_reopening_does_not_ask_again` opens a project with missing media, runs Offline All, saves and reopens, and checks Link Media isn't asked for. It then makes one clip missing again and checks the next open does ask.

title: Reuse identical embedded audio when an AAF/OMF source path repeats
author: nuclearspike
body:
# Reuse identical embedded audio when an AAF/OMF source path repeats

After #2023 made embedded-audio extraction collision-safe, importing an AAF or OMF again from the same source path creates another numbered WAV even when the earlier extraction has identical bytes. An import that wrote `a.mov (2).wav`, for example, is followed by `a.mov (3).wav` on re-import.

The host interface adds `existing_file_matches` and `list_dir_bounded`, implemented by the native and browser hosts. Their defaults allow existing hosts to compile but do not enable reuse.

Before creating a new WAV, the importer searches the bounded candidate names and reuses a regular file only after an exact byte comparison. A free earlier slot therefore does not hide a matching extraction at a later name. Different files and symlinks stay untouched; new files still use exclusive creation. The native matcher compares through an open handle and checks file metadata before and after the read. On Windows, that handle excludes write/delete sharing during comparison. Browser memory-backed paths use the same match rule when a virtual source path repeats. Selecting a file again through the browser picker registers a new source path and is outside this fix; OPFS still does not support exclusive extraction.

For each embedded WAV, the first pass attempts one bounded listing of all direct child names (up to 10,000 entries and 1,000,000 name bytes). When both the candidate filename and listing are ASCII, it skips byte comparisons for candidates absent from the case-folded name set; on a case-sensitive host, a differently cased name may still trigger a comparison of an absent path. The empty-directory regression confirms zero comparison calls for an ASCII filename, and a later exact match is still found after a gap. If listing is unsupported, fails other than a missing directory, exceeds either bound, or has a non-ASCII name—or the candidate name is non-ASCII—the importer scans up to 1,000 candidate paths, preserving…

title: #2667: Motion ▸ Interpolation offers Nearest Neighbor for hard pixel edges
author: vxMacDev
body:
Fixes #2667.

Motion always resampled a clip bilinearly, so pixel art scaled up came out blurred. This adds a per-clip **Interpolation** choice to Motion: **Bilinear** (the default, unchanged) or **Nearest Neighbor**, which takes the nearest source pixel with no filtering.

## Changes

- `crates/project/src/effect.rs`: Motion gets `ch("interpolation", "Interpolation", &["Bilinear", "Nearest Neighbor"], 0)`. A project saved before this has no such param, and `effects::choice` returns 0 for a missing one, so existing projects render exactly as before.
- `crates/render/src/image.rs`: `Image::transformed_nearest` next to `transformed`; both share one resampler that point-samples (`get_or_clear`, transparent outside) instead of `sample_bilinear`. Nearest also skips the 2× box pre-filter, so minification stays unfiltered too.
- `crates/render/src/lib.rs`: `item_layer` places the layer with `transformed_nearest` when `motion_nearest(item)`.
- `crates/render/src/plan.rs`: the GPU compositor only has bilinear placement, so a Nearest Neighbor clip skips the GPU media path and takes the existing CPU-rendered layer path, as other unsupported cases do. Preview and export therefore draw it the way the CPU render does (checked against `plan::execute_cpu`, not on a GPU). Graphic clips without standard effects are drawn as vectors straight at output resolution, so the setting doesn't change them; with effects they go through the same placement.
- `es.tsv` / `ja.tsv`: entries for "Bilinear" and "Nearest Neighbor" ("Interpolation" was already there), which the catalog-completeness tests require. Other draft catalogs fall back to English.
- `README.md`: the Motion line mentions the option.

Motion is one row taller in Effect Controls for every clip. In two UI tests (`keyframes_ui::effect_and_mask_keyframes_move_together_without_crossing_parameters` and `scripted::eyedropper_picks_a_key_color_on_a_selected_clip`) that pushed the control they click below …

title: Reject TTML offset times that have no integer digits
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/captions/src/ttml.rs:358 (parse_time, offset-time branch) and :310 (decimal_ticks)` (no existing issue): TTML time expression with no digits ("s", "ms", ".5s") is accepted as a valid time.

## Cause
The offset-time branch of `parse_time` only checked that every character of the integer part was a digit, and an empty string passes that check. `decimal_ticks` then read the empty integer part as 0, so values like `s`, `ms`, `t` or `.5s` were accepted as valid times (0 or 0.5 s) instead of being rejected.

## Fix
The offset-time branch now returns None when the integer part is empty, the same way the clock-time branch already does with its `!p.is_empty()` check. A regression test checks that bare units and values with no integer part (`s`, `ms`, `h`, `m`, `t`, `f`, `.5s`, `.5ms`, `.s`) are rejected and that `0s`, `0.5s` and `1ms` still parse.

## Verified
- Regression test `ttml::tests::offset_time_without_integer_digits_is_rejected`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-captions --lib offset_time_without_integer_digits_is_rejected`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `dev_icon::tests::desktop_file_matches_the_packaged_fields`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
`decimal_ticks` still reads an empty integer part as 0, because the frame branch relies on that when it passes "0" with a fractional part. Values with a trailing dot and no fraction digits (e.g. `1.s`) are still accepted; this change leaves them as they were.

title: #2751: report why hardware decoding declined a stream (status bar, perf.stats, log)
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Refs #2751 (tells the user why a video plays from the CPU; the reporter's codec is still to be confirmed).

A 4K OBS recording (NVENC, 24 fps, CQ 16 up to 100 Mb/s) lagged on Windows. At 24 fps, 2160p is well within FilmCraft's Media Foundation hardware decoding (about 90 fps measured in `docs/performance.md`), unless the stream isn't hardware-decoded at all. HEVC and AV1 need the Microsoft Store's *HEVC Video Extensions* / *AV1 Video Extension*. Without them the factory declines the stream and FilmCraft's software decoder takes it, which runs at about 26–28 fps for 2160p HEVC even on a 28-thread Xeon. The reason was logged only at `info`, which the default log filter doesn't write, so users saw lag with nothing explaining it.

## Changes
- `codecs::hw::note_hw_declined_because(reason)` counts the decline as before and keeps each distinct reason ("HEVC video: no HEVC decoder MFT (the HEVC Video Extensions are not installed)"): trimmed, at most 300 characters, at most 16 reasons.
- The VideoToolbox, Media Foundation and VA-API factories (and NVDEC where it counts the decline) pass their reason and log it as a **warning**, so it reaches the log file.
- `perf.stats` `decode.hardware.declinedReasons` lists them for agents and bug reports (also `filmcraft_engine::perf::hw_declined_reasons`).
- The app shows each new reason once in the status bar: "Hardware decoding isn't used for HEVC video: no HEVC decoder MFT (the HEVC Video Extensions are not installed). FilmCraft decodes it on the CPU, so 4K or high-bitrate video can play back slowly." It's translated in the full catalogs.

title: Speak the minus sign of negative currency amounts in TTS normalizer
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/tts-text/src/normalize.rs:78-97 (normalize, '-' / currency arms)` (no existing issue): TTS normalizer drops the minus sign of a negative currency amount ("-$5" is read as "five dollars").

## Cause
In `normalize`, '-' only became "minus" when a digit came right after it. In "-$5", "-€3.50" or "-£2" the '-' is followed by a currency symbol, so it was kept as unspoken punctuation and the amount was read as positive.

## Fix
Added a '-' arm for a hyphen followed by '$', '€' or '£'. It emits "minus" and then the money words. It only applies when the character before the hyphen is not a letter, digit, currency symbol or hyphen, so ranges like "$10-$20" and "€5-€8" and hyphens after words stay punctuation as before. The regression test covers leading signs as well as ranges and hyphens that follow an amount or word.

## Verified
- Regression test `normalize::tests::negative_money_keeps_its_sign`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -q -p filmcraft-tts-text negative_money_keeps_its_sign`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `dev_icon::tests::desktop_file_matches_the_packaged_fields`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
The existing '-'+digit arm and the money parser are unchanged. Spaced subtraction ("$10 - $20") also reads the same as before, because there the hyphen is followed by a space, not a currency symbol.

title: Keep file URL hosts that only start with "localhost"
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/interchange/src/common.rs:68` (no existing issue): file_url_to_path strips a 'localhost' prefix from hosts like 'localhost-nas'.

## Cause
`file_url_to_path` removed the first 9 characters after `file://` whenever they matched "localhost" (ignoring case), without checking that the host ended there. So `file://localhost-nas/share/a.mov` became `//-nas/share/a.mov`, and imported media using such hosts went offline.
