title: #2760: an export to a path naming another container says what the file is called
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Refs #2760.

An export to `a.mxf` with the DNxHR format, or to `b.avi` with MJPEG, wrote `a.mxf.mov` / `b.avi.mov` and succeeded without comment. A caller that asked for `.mxf` got a different file and had to read the result's `path` to notice.

Adding the format's extension is a deliberate, tested contract (#341: `apv.mp4` becomes `apv.mp4.mov`, and the CLI's completion message names the file written; `apps/filmcraft-cli/tests/cli.rs` checks it), so this PR keeps it and **says so**. It doesn't reject the path or switch containers on its own.

## Changes
- `export_tools::container_note`: when the path's extension names a known container or audio/video file type (mp4, mov, mxf, avi, mkv, webm, wav, m4a, flac, gif, …) other than the one the format writes, the result explains it. For example: "`a.mxf` names a .mxf file, but the Avid DNxHR format writes .mov, so the file is `a.mxf.mov`; name it .mov or pick a format that writes .mxf; for MXF use format `mxf-op1a` (or `mxf-opatom`) with mxfVideoCodec `dnxhr`".
- `file.exportMedia` and `export.queue.add` return it as `note`. No note for a matching extension, for a dotted name that isn't a container's (`Final.v2`), or where the extension is replaced anyway (image sequences, AIFF).
- `docs/agents.md` describes it.

If the maintainers would rather refuse such paths (the issue's second suggestion), it's a one-line change in `settings_from_params`, but it would break #341's documented behaviour, so I've left that decision to them.

## Tests
New `export_tests::a_path_naming_another_container_is_reported`: `a.mxf` + DNxHR and `b.avi` + MJPEG keep their paths and get a note naming the real file (and `mxf-op1a` for MXF). `export.queue.add` gets the same note. `c.mov`, `Final.v2` and `d.mxf` through `mxf-op1a` get none. `cargo test -p filmcraft-engine -p filmcraft-cli` (including #341's CLI test) and `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-engine --all-targets -D warnings` pass (macOS).

title: Audio: track effect tails ring out; edit any mixer insert's parameters (#2731)
author: texjer
body:
Fixes #2731

## What

**Diagnosis.** The mixer graph (`crates/render/src/mixer.rs`) was already correct: track, submix and Mix inserts run over silent input, and their state carries across requests. A reverb tail goes on over a gap and under the next clip, in export batches, in small playback blocks, and from a cold start inside the gap (the tests below pin this down). The audible cut came from **playback stopping at the sequence end**. That is usually the end of the clip, which is the repro in the issue. `advance_playback` stopped the audio device the moment the playhead reached `Sequence::duration()`.

Commit 1, tails:
- `render::mixer::effect_tail(seq)` estimates how long the inserts keep sounding. It takes the longest insert tail (the same per-effect estimate the fresh-graph pre-roll uses, now `Plan::tail_s`, which skips solo-muted strips) plus the graph latency, capped at `MAX_TAIL_S` = 10 s. It is zero when no insert rings on.
- `ui-egui` playback: `play()` stores this as `Playback::ring_out`. When playback reaches the end, the sound keeps running until the tail has rung out, with the playhead resting on the last frame, and then playback stops as before. This only applies when the audio clock is driving. Looping, Play In to Out (`stop_at`) and voice-over are unchanged. With no ringing insert, behaviour is exactly as before.
- `render::preview::audio_segments`: when inserts ring on and the previous segment ends within the tail, a segment's hash also covers the previous segment's hash and the gap. Before, a rendered audio preview of clip B kept clip A's old reverb tail after A was edited. The doc comment had listed this as a known limitation.
- Export is unchanged: it still ends at the sequence end, as Premiere does. Tails across gaps and into following clips were already rendered. To export the tail at the very end, set the Out point past the last clip (`export_range` allows that).

title: #2749: Export starts on Source In/Out when the sequence has In/Out marks
author: Felix-Helleckes
body:
Fixes #2749.

With In/Out marks set on the sequence, Export still exported the whole sequence: the Range in Export mode always started on **Entire Source**. Premiere starts on **Source In/Out** when the sequence has marks, which is what the reporter expected.

`export_mode::sync_sequence` sets the Range from the sequence's marks when the sequence or its marks change: **Source In/Out** with an In or Out mark set, **Entire Source** without. New `export_ui::the_export_range_follows_the_sequence_marks`: no marks gives Entire Source; marks give Source In/Out; a Range set by hand stays over several frames; moving the Out mark makes the Range follow again. title: fix(interchange): FCP7 import stops at the engine's 999 tracks of a kind
author: Wbunker
body:
Follow-up to a CodeRabbit review comment on #2255 (that PR already has reviews, so I kept this separate).

## Problem
The FCP7 XML importer made one track for every `<track>` element, so a file listing more than 999 video or audio tracks imported as a sequence the engine's own add-track rule (`sequence_tools::MAX_TRACKS` = 999) would not let a user build.

## Change
`Imp::sequence` stops at the 999th `<track>` of a kind and warns once that the rest were skipped. This is a limit, not an amplification fix: the cost is linear in the file's size, unlike a single huge `lane` value. EDL audio channels are already capped at A99, and FCPXML lanes and overlap placement are capped in #2255, so FCP7 was the remaining importer without the limit.

## Tests
New file `crates/interchange/tests/fcp7_tracks.rs` (a new file so it cannot collide with other PRs):
- 1,049 video tracks give 999 plus a warning, and the same for audio;
- exactly 999 tracks, or a normal count, say nothing.

author: melchiaaronzedek

Adds Fujifilm's log curves and gamuts to Interpret Footage ▸ Color Management, next to S-Log3, V-Log, Canon Log, LogC, Apple Log and D-Log:

- **Fujifilm F-Log / F-Gamut**

- **Fujifilm F-Log2 C / F-Gamut C**

These are the profiles Fujifilm X and GFX cameras record (X-S20, X-H2S, X-T5, GFX…). Footage shot in them can now be decoded to scene light and tone-mapped into the working space like the other camera log formats, instead of being shown as flat Rec. 709.

Fujifilm's published formulas, from the *GFX ETERNA Technical Guide* white paper v1.01 (F-Log / F-Log2 data sheet section):

- **F-Gamut** = BT.2020 primaries;
- **F-Gamut C** primaries (0.7347, 0.2653), (0.0263, 0.9737), (0.1173, −0.0224), D65 white.

No other implementation was read.

- `crates/color/src/log.rs`: `LogCurve::FLog` / `FLog2` (F-Log2 C uses the F-Log2 curve) with `fujifilm_encode` / `fujifilm_decode`, both clamped like the other curves.

title: Export: chapter markers are written into MP4 and MOV (#2747)
author: texjer
body:
## What

Chapter markers (`markers.addChapter`) are now written into exported MP4, MOV and M4A files, in both forms players read. Fixes #2747.

- **Muxer** (`crates/isobmff/src/chapters.rs`, new; `mux.rs`): `WriterOptions::chapters: Vec<Chapter>` (`Chapter { start, title }`, start in the movie timescale). `Mp4Writer` writes them twice:
  - a **QuickTime chapter track**: a disabled `text` track (`gmhd` + `text` media info, QuickTime `text` sample description + `ftab`), one sample per chapter (16-bit length, UTF-8 title, `encd` atom = UTF-8), referenced by `tref/chap` from the first video or audio track.   - a **Nero `udta/chpl`** list (version 1, 100 ns units, u8 count, u8-length titles). VLC and `ffprobe -show_chapters` read this one. There's no official spec for it; the code comments describe the publicly documented layout.
  - `normalize_chapters` sorts them, keeps the first title at each start time, drops anything at or past the movie end, swaps control characters for spaces, and caps output at 255 chapters with titles of 255 bytes, cut at a character boundary. A first chapter that starts after 0 is placed with an empty edit. `FragmentedWriter` writes only `chpl`.
- **Demuxer** (`demux.rs`): `Mp4File::chpl_chapters` (parsed from `udta/chpl`) and `Mp4File::read_chapters(src)` (the `tref/chap` text track if there is one, otherwise `chpl`). The tests use both, and they're there for a future import.

title: Dock: dividers are easy to grab beside scrollbars (#2690)
author: texjer
body:
## What
Why it was hard to grab: the visible gap between docked panels is `Tokens::gap` (4 pt), and the `ResizeHandle` band reached its default 3 pt into each panel. Panel bodies are registered after the divider, so egui's hit test gave them the overlap. On the right side of the Effect Controls | Program (or Effect Controls | Source) gap, the monitor's widgets took the band. On the left side, Effect Controls' floating `ScrollArea` bar has an invisible 10 pt hit strip that sits about 6 pt in from the panel edge and appears on hover, which is right where people aim. The result was a band about 4 to 7 pt wide that sometimes scrolled the panel instead of resizing it.

- `crates/ui-egui/src/dock.rs`
  - New `pub const DIVIDER_HIT_MARGIN: f32 = 4.0`. The divider's `ResizeHandle` now uses `.hit_margin(DIVIDER_HIT_MARGIN)`, so the grab band is 12 pt (24 physical px at 2x) along its full length.
  - `layout_inner` passes down which sides of a tab group face a vertical divider (`DividerSides`). New `inset_content()` insets `Group::content` by the same margin on those sides. Panel bodies are clipped to `content`, so nothing in a panel (scroll bars, the monitor, list rows) can overlap the band. Pressing anywhere in it resizes, and the scroll bar keeps its full width beside it.
  - The tab strip keeps its full width: its grip, tabs and menu button are registered after the divider and still win there. The inset is capped at a quarter of the content width for very narrow panels.
  - The hover highlight is a bit stronger (`gamma_multiply(0.4)` → `0.6`). The resize cursor and the drag/focus highlight are unchanged.

Insetting top/bottom too pushed rows out of view in short panels and broke `masks_ui` (the Opacity/Inverted row of Effect Controls sits at the bottom edge). title: Placement: audio streams we can't decode no longer land on A1 (#2758)
author: texjer
body:
Part of #2758. This doesn't add an APAC decoder. That part of the issue stays open.

## What
iPhone 17 Pro videos carry an Apple Positional Audio stream (`apac`) next to the AAC stream, and the APAC stream often comes first. Probe reported it as `"unknown"`. Placement gave every stream its own clip, so A1 got a silent clip and the real sound landed on A2.

- **Probe:** `AudioStreamInfo` gets a `decodable` field. Serde defaults it to true and only writes it when it's false, so project files don't change. `can_decode()` also treats the old `"unknown"` and `"… (unsupported)"` codec names as undecodable, so projects saved by older versions place the same way. MP4/MOV, Matroska, AVI and the MPEG-TS placeholder set the field from whether a decoder actually exists. MP4 now names the sample entry: `Apple Positional Audio (apac)`, or `unknown (xxxx)` for other fourccs.
- **Placement:** `audio_placement_specs` now takes per-stream decodability. Undecodable streams get no clip. Decodable streams keep file order starting at the targeted track, so the AAC stream goes on A1. Everything goes through `place_item`, so this covers drag, `timeline.place`, insert/overwrite, New Sequence From Clip and Automate to Sequence. A Modify ▸ Audio Channels map describes stream 0, so its extra clips are dropped along with stream 0 when stream 0 can't be decoded.

title: graphics: typing into a title on Linux input methods no longer stops working
author: Katacc
body:
On Linux with an X11 input method (fcitx5, ibus), typing into a title on the Program monitor did nothing, and afterwards no text field accepted keys until restart.

## Cause

Each IME on/off makes winit recreate the X11 input context. The monitor text editor requested focus every frame, so it restarted the IME ~60×/s. Turning the IME off while a key was still being handled (e.g. Esc) left the new context deaf.

## Fix

- Request focus only when the text doesn't have it, and set the IME only while it has the keyboard.
- New `ime_hold.rs`: keep the IME on until keys are released plus 0.3 s.
- Separate commit: dev desktop entry includes `MimeType=` again, fixing a test failing on `main`.

## Testing

- Regression test in `graphics_handles_ui` (fails on `main`) and `ime_hold` unit tests.
- Verified with real key input through fcitx5 on Xorg.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

This fix is very high priority for Xorg + fcitx5 Linux x86_64 users

title: fix(audio-dsp): prevent filter clamp panics on low sample rates and enforce 8 kHz sequence minimum
author: justdxvid
body:
Resolves #2791.

### Summary
When a sequence or export uses low sample rates (around 1–2 Hz), `clamp` bounds in several filter calculations crossed (`min > max`, e.g. `freq.clamp(1.0, sr * 0.49)` with `1.0 > 0.49`), triggering panics in `f64::clamp` / `f32::clamp`. Additionally, unconstrained low sample rates allowed division by zero or sub-unit values in filter warping and DC blockers.

### Changes
1. **Filter clamp robustness (`crates/audio-dsp`)**:
   - `biquad::Coeffs::design`: bounds `sr = sample_rate.max(1.0)` and clamps frequency with `(sr * 0.49).max(1.0)`.
   - `effects::util::OnePole::alpha`: safe upper bound `(sr_safe * 0.49).max(1.0)` and `sr_safe = sr.max(1.0)`.
   - `effects::util::AllPass1::coef`: safe upper bound `(sr_safe * 0.49).max(1.0)`.
   - `effects::util::DcBlock::r`: clamps feedback coefficient to `0.0..=0.9999` and guards against sub-unit sample rates.
   - `design::realize`: safe upper bound `(nyq * 0.98).max(1.0)` and `sr = sample_rate.max(1.0)`.
   - `effects::time::prepare_delay` & `read_frac_reference`: safe upper bound with `len.saturating_sub(2).max(1.0)`.
2. **SequenceSettings validation (`crates/project`)**:
   - Sets the minimum sequence audio sample rate to 8000 Hz (`8000..=384_000`), matching Premiere Pro's minimum supported rate.
3. **Regression Tests**:
   - Added unit regression tests in `biquad`, `design`, `util`, and `project` validating that sample rates `<= 2.04 Hz` (including 0 Hz and hostile inputs) do not panic and hostile sequence sample rates `< 8000 Hz` are rejected.

title: Read the a of a.m. and attached am as the letter name A
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/tts-text/src/normalize.rs:416 (parse_time am/pm suffix) and :947 (parse_wordish a.m. branch); consumed by crates/tts-text/src/phonemize.rs:398 (is_single_letter)` (no existing issue): TTS reads 'a.m.' / '9:00am' with the article 'uh' instead of the letter name 'A'.

## Cause
The normalizer emitted the 'a' of 'a.m.' and of an attached 'am' (as in '9:00am') as a lowercase "a". The phonemizer's `is_single_letter` treats a lowercase function word as an ordinary word, not a letter. The dictionary lookup then used the article entry, so the 'a' was spoken as 'uh' instead of 'ay'.

## Fix
The normalizer now emits an uppercase "A" for the 'a' in both the `a.m.` branch of `parse_wordish` and the `am` suffix in `parse_time`. The phonemizer then reads it as the letter name. I updated the existing `times` test to expect "A", and added a regression test for 'At 9:00 a.m.' and 'At 9:00am'.

## Verified
- Regression test `phonemize::tests::am_reads_the_letter_name_not_the_article`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-tts-text --lib am_reads_the_letter_name_not_the_article`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The 'p' and 'm' tokens stay lowercase because they already read as letters. `is_single_letter` in the phonemizer is unchanged.

Fixes the first two points of #2813 (the clippy failures). The other points (tts lint header / workspace lints, `deny.toml`, fuzz targets, CI coverage) are separate changes and are not touched here.

- `crates/speech/src/whisper/tokenizer.rs`: `char::from_u32(c).expect("valid")` in the GPT-2 byte table tripped the crate's own `deny(clippy::expect_used)` once feature `whisper` is on, so `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features` failed. It now uses `filter_map`; every code point in the table is below 0x200, so nothing is ever dropped.
- `crates/h264/src/picture.rs`: `Frame::row` uses `.expect` only when feature `threads` is off (the wasm build). Without threads, reference rows are decoded in order, so a row is always published before it is read, and the function has to return a `&FrameRow`. It gets `#[cfg_attr(not(feature = "threads"), allow(clippy::expect_used))]` with a comment saying why, the same way `text::fonts::face` handles its infallible `expect`.

Test: `byte_table_covers_every_byte_once` checks that the table has 256 entries, maps back to every byte exactly once, and keeps the known pairs (`'!'` -> `!`, `U+0120` -> space). The fix is for a lint, so this test also passes on the old code. It guards the `filter_map` rewrite against dropping entries. The fix itself shows up in `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` and in clippy with `-p h264 --no-default-features`.

title: #1582: NVENC drains the pictures in flight before its session is dropped
author: FernandoOliveiraESouza
body:
Fixes #1582.

## What happened

Cancelling an export that uses NVENC (or an export that stops on an error) drops the `Exporter`, and with it `NvencEncoder` and `Nvenc`, without `Nvenc::flush()` having run. `Session::drop` then destroys the input and bitstream buffers of pictures the driver is still encoding asynchronously. The driver jumps into freed memory: the app crashes (SIGSEGV in `libnvidia-encode` / `libnvcuvid`, `ip 0x2` here) and the output is left without its `moov` atom.

The backtrace matches the one in #1582:

```
#0  0x0000000000000002
#1-3 libnvcuvid.so.1
#4-8 libnvidia-encode.so.1
#9  <filmcraft_platform::nvenc::session::Session as Drop>::drop   (nvEncDestroyEncoder)
#12 drop_glue<filmcraft_platform::nvenc::export::NvencEncoder>
#14 drop_glue<filmcraft_export::job::Exporter>
#15 filmcraft_export::export
```

## The fix

`impl Drop for Nvenc`: when pictures are pending, it flushes them (end of stream, then reads each one, as `flush()` does on a normal finish) before the session frees its buffers. An error while draining is logged, not raised. This is the fix proposed in the issue.

## Proof

New regression test in `crates/platform/tests/nvenc.rs`: `an_encoder_dropped_with_pictures_in_flight_does_not_crash` drops an encoder with eight 1280×720 pictures in flight, twenty times. It skips without an NVIDIA GPU, like the other NVENC tests.

- **Without the fix:** the test aborts with SIGSEGV within a second.
- **With the fix:** it passes.

Tested on Linux, RTX 3060 Ti, NVIDIA driver 595.99.02.

In the app, 24 exports of a real project in a row, 12 of them cancelled mid-way, gave no crash, no partial file left and every finished file decoded end to end. Without the fix the first cancel crashed.

## Gates run

| Gate | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --check -p filmcraft-platform` | clean |
| `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-platform --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo nextest run -p filmcraft-platform` | 73 passed |

The full `cargo xtask ci` was not…

title: fix(packaging): declare the riscv64 packages' real glibc floor
author: benandez
body:
Fixes storytold/craft-common-actions#44 for FilmCraft. Pilot: the other 13 apps get the same change once this is reviewed. Pairs with storytold/craft-common-actions#62.

**Problem:** the riscv64 deb and rpm are cross-built on `ubuntu-24.04`, and `filmcraft` needs `GLIBC_2.39` (`pidfd_spawnp`, `pidfd_getpid`). But `nfpm.yaml` declares `libc6 (>= 2.35)` / `glibc >= 2.35`. Ubuntu 22.04 riscv64 installs the 0.10.0 deb and then can't start the app. (Moving the job to 22.04 doesn't work. storytold/craft-common-actions#62 explains why.)

**Change:**
- `nfpm.yaml`: the deb `libc6` and rpm `glibc` floors read `${GLIBC_FLOOR}`.
- `package.sh`: `export GLIBC_FLOOR="${GLIBC_FLOOR:-2.35}"`, so x86_64, aarch64 and local builds are unchanged. Without a default, nfpm would write `libc6 (>= )`.
- The shared release workflow sets `GLIBC_FLOOR=2.39` on the riscv64 job (storytold/craft-common-actions#62).
- `README.md` and `docs/releasing.md` list the riscv64 deb and rpm, which the release already ships. Both docs said tarball only.

**Order:** either PR can merge first. Without storytold/craft-common-actions#62, riscv64 keeps declaring 2.35 as it does today.

**Tested** with nfpm 2.47.0 (the version the workflow pins) on this `nfpm.yaml`:

| `GLIBC_FLOOR` | deb `Depends` | rpm `Requires` (`rpm -qpR`, Fedora 41) |
|---|---|---|
| 2.35 (default) | `libc6 (>= 2.35)` | `glibc >= 2.35` |
| 2.39 | `libc6 (>= 2.39)` | `glibc >= 2.39` |

`bash -n packaging/linux/package.sh` passes.

title: fix(interchange): bound subclip parent resolution to prevent cycle stack overflow
author: justdxvid
body:
## Summary

Addresses #2788.

Interchange export functions `item_path`, `item_media`, and `base_item` in `crates/interchange/src/common.rs`, as well as `ale::export_items` in `crates/interchange/src/ale.rs`, previously traversed subclip parents recursively without a depth bound or cycle check. When exporting a damaged project or imported timeline containing a self-referencing subclip or cyclic subclip chain (`A -> B -> A`), any interchange export (FCP7 XML, FCPXML, EDL, OTIO, AAF, OMF, ALE) caused an infinite recursion stack overflow and process crash.

## Fix Details

1. **`item_media`**: Refactored to delegate directly to `p.resolve_media(id).map(|(_, m, _)| m)`, which already implements a safe 16-step bound (`crates/project/src/lib.rs:1691`).
2. **`item_path`**: Refactored to read from `item_media(p, id)`, avoiding recursive parent traversal and properly returning `None` for cyclic or over-depth subclips.
3. **`base_item`**: Replaced recursive call with a bounded 16-step iterative loop (`for _ in 0..16`), returning the root item or the terminal item upon exhausting iterations.
4. **`ale::export_items`**: Updated row source media lookup to use `p.resolve_media(id)`, properly resolving chained subclips and safely skipping cyclic ones.

## Testing

- Added unit tests in `crates/interchange/src/common.rs` verifying bounded resolution for self-referencing subclips, mutual cycles, chained subclips, and missing parent items.
- Added unit test in `crates/interchange/src/ale.rs` verifying chained subclip resolution and cyclic subclip skipping without hanging.
- Added comprehensive integration test in `crates/interchange/tests/cyclic_subclips.rs` placing self-referencing, mutually cyclic, missing-parent, and >16-level deep subclips on timeline sequences and verifying that all interchange formats (FCP7 XML, FCPXML, EDL, EDL per-track, OTIO, AAF, OMF, ALE) export cleanly without stack overflow or abort.
- All 81 tests in `filmcraft-interchange` pass.

Closes #2788

title: CI: xtask ci in the dev profile, one test binary per crate, nextest
author: aiongg
body:
Makes `cargo xtask ci` fast enough to run on every PR, following the measurements in storytold/craft-common-actions#60. Supersedes #618.

## Measured

One run of `cargo xtask ci` on a 16-core Linux box. Dependencies were already built; every workspace crate was rebuilt, as in the study.

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `cargo xtask ci` | over 1 h (release profile, thin LTO, one codegen unit; #2563) | 6:52 |
| Integration-test targets | 217 | 54 |
| Test and bin executables in `target/debug/deps` | | 110 |
| Test run (3581 tests) | | 1:59 with nextest |
| Target dir after the gate | | 13 GB |

On GitHub (`ci.yml`, `ubuntu-24.04`, no cargo cache), the Quality gate step took 16:55 and 22:37 in two runs of this PR (39882995383 and 39892117035) and 21:20 on main with release LTO switched off (39880174751). Cold runs vary this much from runner to runner, so the GitHub comparison needs warm-cache runs after this merges.

The 6:52 breaks down as 5:45 for fmt, clippy, the test build and the nextest run, then 1:07 for doctests, layers, assets and the wasm check.

- **xtask ci builds in the dev profile.** Clippy and tests no longer use `--release`. The 15 codec and audio crates stay at opt-level 3, so their tests run at release speed.
- **Profiles.** `debug = "line-tables-only"` for workspace crates and `debug = false` for dependencies. Panics keep their file and line. Incremental builds stay on.

title: Scroll the timeline clip menu when it is taller than the screen (#2852)
author: HEOJUNFO
body:
Fixes #2852.

## What and why

The timeline clip menu (`CLIP_MENU`) has about 35 items plus separators and the Label and Multi-Camera submenus. It was drawn straight into `resp.context_menu` with no scroll area, so on a short screen it ran past the bottom and the last items (Reveal in Project, Join Through Edits, the frame-fit commands) couldn't be reached.

- The menu body now sits in a vertical `ScrollArea` capped at the window's content height − 16, the same pattern the panel menu uses (`panels/mod.rs`, `panel-menu-scroll`). The marker, edit point and gap menus that share this `context_menu` scroll the same way. They are short, so nothing changes for them in practice.

body:

title: Raise a loaded project's next_id past the ids already in it
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #2809 (covers both points of the ticket: the stale `next_id` and the `u64::MAX` overflow).

Every id in a project (items, bins, search bins, tracks, clips, links, groups, transitions, markers, captions, the `lut<id>` LUT names) comes from `next_id`, and `format::decode` kept the file's value as is. The keys of `transcripts`, `source_graphics` and `narrations` matter too: deleting an item leaves its entries there, and a new item taking that id would inherit them. A file whose `next_id` lags behind its ids (hand edit, merge, an older writer; the `v1-edit` fixture itself has a sequence marker `800000` with `next_id: 48`) then hands out an id already in use, and `add_item` silently replaces the item in the map. `validate_loaded` now raises `next_id` to one past the largest id of any kind (new `Project::max_id`), with a warning in the log, using `checked_add` as #1056 does for the Avid import. A file whose ids leave no room is refused as damaged ("project ID space exhausted") instead of panicking in debug or wrapping to 0 in release on the first new id: that covers an id of `u64::MAX` and a `next_id` above `Project::MAX_NEXT_ID` (`u64::MAX / 2`, far beyond what editing can reach, so `alloc_id` can't overflow on a loaded project). The bound is my choice; happy to switch to a different one.

The demo project (`engine::demo`) had the same problem: its transitions and markers take fixed ids (900001…, 800000…) without moving `next_id`, which is where the fixture's 800000 comes from; it now sets `next_id` past them, so `save_and_open_roundtrip` still gets back the project it saved. `v1_edit_loads_with_defaults_for_later_fields` asserted the stale `next_id` of 48; it now expects 800001. #2228 (draft) also edits `validate_loaded`, so one of the two will need a small rebase.

- `next_id_is_raised_past_every_id_in_the_file`: each id kind is pushed past the rest on its own, with `next_id = 1`; fails on main (`left: 1, right: 5000001`), passes here

title: settings: persist preferred new-sequence frame rate (#2859)
author: jnohclee-rgb
body:
New Sequence always starts at 23.976 fps, so editors repeatedly choose their usual timebase. Add **Settings → General → Preferred Sequence Frame Rate**, persisted through the existing preferences schema and exposed to automation as `general.preferredSequenceFps`.

The dialog now initializes from that preference using exact rational rates. Old preferences keep the current 23.976 default. An explicit dialog override still applies only to that sequence; existing sequences and source-matching creation retain their own rates and the default timecode mode is preserved.

Closes #2859.

Validation: all six repository gates pass (`fmt`, workspace Clippy with warnings denied, workspace tests, layers, assets, WASM). Workspace tests: 3,570 passed, 45 ignored; WASM: 49 crates. Focused tests cover preference persistence, old/corrupt preferences, invalid choices, fractional rates, dialog overrides/reopening, existing sequences, source matching and the automation control. Visually inspected the General settings dialog through the headless UI harness.

AI assistance: implemented with Antigravity and independently reviewed/validated with Codex.

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

title: codecs: walk open-GOP leading pictures back in a loop, not by recursion
author: mercuryVM
body:
Fixes #2803

## Problem

`MxfVideo::sync_before` (`crates/codecs/src/mxf.rs`) and `MpegVideo::sync_before` (`crates/codecs/src/mpeg.rs`) step back one GOP per leading picture of an open GOP by calling themselves. An index in which every GOP's leading picture is shown before its key frame recurses once per GOP: tens of thousands of levels for a small crafted file, a plausible stack overflow in dev builds (AGENTS.md §0.5: bound recursion).

## Fix

- `gop::open_gop_sync` does the same walk in a loop: take the index's sync sample for `i`; if `i` leads it, continue from the sample before that key.
- It stops when the sync sample lies past `i`. The recursion would have called itself with the same or a larger index there, forever.
- The MXF and MPEG wrappers pass their own sync lookup and "is shown before" test, reading `pts` and `keys` with `get()` (§0.4). In MPEG this also covers a track with no key flags, where `keys[k]` indexed an empty vector.

Behaviour is otherwise unchanged: the comparison per step is the one the recursion made.

## Tests

- `gop::tests::open_gop_sync_walks_a_long_chain_of_leading_pictures_without_recursing`: 200,000 chained GOPs walk back to sample 0; a picture that is not a leading one keeps its own key; a sync sample past `i` ends the walk.
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-codecs --lib`: 129 passed.
- With a working ffmpeg (`FILMCRAFT_FFMPEG`): `mxf_oracle` 9 passed, `mp4_oracle` 5, `ogg_oracle` 5, `eac3_oracle` 1, and 7 of 13 `mpeg_oracle` tests. The 6 others need `ffprobe`, which this machine doesn't have; they fail the same way on `main` without this change.

`cargo xtask ci` on Windows 11 (MSVC): fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, `layers`, `assets` and `wasm` pass. The workspace tests pass except the ffmpeg/ffprobe oracle tests, which fail here at fixture generation because of the local ffmpeg install, not at decoding. Not run on macOS or Linux.

title: CI: shared gate workflow; FreeBSD nightly and on release
author: aiongg
body:
Switches FilmCraft's CI to the suite's shared gate workflow and takes the slow platform builds off the pull-request path. **Depends on storytold/craft-common-actions#69**; merge after it. Until then this PR's CI fails, because `gate.yml` doesn't exist yet.

- `ci.yml` calls `storytold/craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/gate.yml@main`. That workflow brings the cached apt install, nextest, rust-cache saved only from main (keyed on the root `Cargo.toml`, so profile changes start a fresh cache), and a check that `Cargo.lock` is unchanged. Every push to main now runs to the end, and pushes to a PR branch cancel their older run. The apt package list, the craft-fonts pin (the same commit as `release.yml`) and the 120-minute timeout are the old file's.
- `ci.yml` keeps the old `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO` and `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS` lines, passed through the gate's `env` input: on main, `cargo xtask ci` still builds clippy and the tests with `--release`. Remove the lines and the longer timeout once #2860 merges, since that PR moves `xtask ci` to the dev profile.
- `freebsd.yml` also runs on pushes to `release` now. It already ran nightly and on PRs that change the workflow or the FreeBSD packaging.
- `windows-arm64.yml` runs nightly instead of weekly, and no longer on pushes to main or on Cargo-file and `build.rs` changes in PRs. Pushes to `release` and PRs that change the Windows packaging still run it.

The speed changes to `cargo xtask ci` are in #2860. Every craft app gets the same pair of PRs. Background: storytold/craft-common-actions#60.

File ▸ New ▸ Sequence From Clip (`file.newSequenceFromClip`) already does everything the issue asks: a sequence named after the clip, with its frame size, frame rate, pixel aspect and audio, the clip (and its audio) at the start, open in the Timeline, as one undo step. The New Item button at the bottom of the Project panel just wasn't a drop target, so this makes it one: while a Project item is dragged over it the button gets the same accent outline a bin shows, and on release it runs that command. Dragging one of several selected items brings the whole selection, back to back, as the Timeline drop does (`dragged_selection`); the sequence then takes its name and settings from the first selected item, as File ▸ New ▸ Sequence From Clip does. Only Project panel items are taken: a Source Monitor drag carries an In/Out range and a video/audio choice that only a timeline drop keeps, so the button ignores it.

This follows Premiere: "You can also create a new sequence based on a clip's properties by dragging the clip onto the New Item menu in the Project panel." ([Adobe, How to create and edit sequences](https://web.archive.org/web/20230623194814/https://helpx.adobe.com/premiere-pro/how-to/create-edit-sequence.html)). Adobe doesn't say what happens with several clips; carrying the selection, as Sequence From Clip already does, seemed the natural reading. Happy to switch if you'd rather it took only the dragged clip.

Validation:
- `dragging_clips_onto_new_item_makes_a_matching_sequence` (`crates/ui-egui/tests/project_panel_ui.rs`): fails on main (the drop makes no sequence), passes here. The clip is set to 1280x720 at 25 fps so it can't match the new-sequence defaults by chance; it also checks that the New Item menu doesn't open, and that a drop on New Bin or a Source Monitor drag makes nothing

title: Draw window decorations on Wayland compositors without server-side decorations
author: pick2510
body:
On GNOME (Wayland) the FilmCraft window has no title bar and no close / minimise / maximise buttons.

## Cause
GNOME's compositor does not offer server-side decorations, so a Wayland client has to draw its own (client-side decorations). winit only does that with its `wayland-csd-adwaita` feature. The workspace builds `eframe` with `default-features = false`, and nothing turned that feature back on, so the window got no decorations at all.

## Fix
`apps/filmcraft/Cargo.toml` enables `winit`'s `wayland-csd-adwaita` feature on Linux (Cargo unifies it with eframe's winit). winit then draws an Adwaita-style title bar when the compositor has no server-side decorations; compositors that offer them (KDE, Sway) and X11 are unchanged.

New dependencies (`Cargo.lock`): `sctk-adwaita`, `tiny-skia`, `tiny-skia-path`, `ab_glyph`, `ab_glyph_rasterizer`, `owned_ttf_parser`, `ttf-parser`, `strict-num`, `arrayref`. All pure Rust, MIT / Apache-2.0 / BSD; no C libraries.

## Verified
- Fedora 44, GNOME on Wayland: the window now has a title bar, and close, minimise and maximise work.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets` pass. `cargo xtask wasm` was not run locally (no `wasm32` std on that toolchain); this change only touches the L5 app crate.

title: Reject non-increasing AV1 film grain scaling points
author: pick2510
body:
Found by `crates/av1/tests/fuzz_hostile.rs` (`hostile_streams_never_panic`, case `av1_fz_10bit frame 0 byte 13=0xff`): the AV1 decoder panics with "attempt to divide by zero" at `crates/av1/src/grain.rs:136`.

## Cause
Film grain scaling points with equal values (two `point_y_value` / `point_cb_value` / `point_cr_value` entries the same) make `dx` zero when the scaling lookup is interpolated, and `(65536 + (dx >> 1)) / dx` divides by it. The spec requires the points to strictly increase (6.8.20), but the header parser never checked.

## Fix
- `header.rs`: `film_grain_params()` rejects luma, Cb and Cr points that do not strictly increase (`Error::Invalid`), like the existing point-count checks.
- `grain.rs`: the scaling lookup skips segments with `dx <= 0` as a second guard, so the division can never see zero even for parameters built elsewhere.

## Verified
- Regression test `grain::tests::equal_scaling_points_do_not_panic`: panics at `grain.rs:136` without the fix and passes with it.
- Unit test `header::tests::film_grain_points_must_strictly_increase`.
- All `filmcraft-av1` tests pass, including `fuzz_hostile` and the conformance tests.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets` pass. `cargo xtask wasm` was not run locally (no `wasm32` std on that toolchain).


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Film-grain processing now handles repeated or descending scaling points safely, avoiding failures when building the grain lookup table.
  * Invalid luma and chroma grain points that are not strictly increasing are now rejected during frame-header validation.
  * Added coverage for empty, single-point, increasing, repeated, and descending point sequences.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

title: platform: NVDEC on Linux for 10-bit H.264 and 4:2:2 H.264 / HEVC (draft; builds on #2431)
author: pick2510
body:
**Depends on #2301 and #2431.** This branch is stacked on #2431, which already contains #2301. Review only the last commit, c852dac5 ("G3: NVDEC on Linux for 10-bit H.264 and 4:2:2 H.264 / HEVC"). I'll rebase it once those land.

## What it does

This is the Linux follow-up to #2431, using its design unchanged: the `cuvidGetDecoderCaps` query per codec, chroma format and bit depth, the NV16 / P216 output surfaces, and the 4:2:2 biplanar conversion. It doesn't touch the software decoder or the Windows NVDEC path.

- `nvdec::NvDecoder` accepts 8- and 10-bit, 4:2:0 and 4:2:2 streams of both codecs on every platform; #2431 limited that to Windows. The GPU's capability query decides, so older GPUs still decline 4:2:2 and 10-bit H.264.
- On Linux, NVDEC stays in front of VA-API, whose drivers (Intel iHD, for example) decline these formats. Streams NVDEC declines go to VA-API and then to the software decoders: #2301 for H.264, and nothing yet for HEVC 4:2:2 (#1952). Windows keeps `nvdec_wanted`.

title: fix(captions): VTT parse decodes the writer's cue-text arrow escape (#2066)
author: rollroyces
body:
Closes #2066.

**Cause.** `crates/captions/src/vtt.rs:140` escapes a cue's `-->` as `-->` — correctly, since a bare arrow inside cue text reads as a timing line to anything scanning the block. But `parse` never undid that substitution, so `A --> B` came back as `A --> B` on every VTT sidecar and export round trip, corrupting the text a little further each time.

**Fix.** `parse` now reverses exactly that one substitution, before the voice span is split off:

```rust
/// Undo [`write`]'s cue-text escape, so `A --> B` comes back as `A --> B` and not `A --> B`.
fn unescape_text(text: &str) -> String {
    text.replace("-->", "-->")
}
```

Other entities (`&`, `<`, …) are cue markup and stay verbatim, which is what `parse` has always done — so this cannot double-decode an escaped body.

**Tests.**

- `an_arrow_in_cue_text_survives_a_round_trip`: write → parse gives the original text, and a second write is byte-identical.
- `other_entities_stay_verbatim_in_cue_text`: `&` still round-trips untouched, so the new decode is not over-eager.

**Build.** `cargo test -p filmcraft-captions` → 38 + 13 passed, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-captions --lib --no-deps --tests` clean.

title: fix(interchange): memoise a reserved <media> item before filling it (#2063)
author: rollroyces
body:
Closes #2063.

**Cause.** `Imp::media`'s comment already said *"Reserve first so recursion terminates"*, but the `media_items` insert only ran **after** `sequence()` returned — which is exactly too late to break a cycle. A `<media id="b">` whose spine contains a `<ref-clip ref="b">` therefore looped

```
media → sequence → storyline → element → media → …
```

until the process aborted with `fatal runtime error: stack overflow`. FCP7 import, OTIO export and the FCPXML *exporter* all carry cycle guards; only this import path missed one.

**Fix.** `sequence()` is split so `media()` can memoise before it recurses:

- `sequence_settings()` — read the declared format / `tcFormat` / `audioRate`.
- `fill_sequence()` — build the tracks and storyline into an item that `Builder::reserve_sequence` has already added.

`media()` now reserves the item, inserts it into `media_items`, and only then calls `fill_sequence`. The reserved item is filled in place by `put_sequence`, so a self-reference lands on the finished sequence rather than a half-built one.

**Test.** `a_self_referential_media_imports_instead_of_overflowing_the_stack` imports a document whose `<media>` spine ref-clips itself, and checks the self-referencing clip resolves to the same sequence item. Verified against the unfixed code: the test aborts with a stack overflow (SIGABRT); it passes with the fix.

**Build.** `cargo test -p filmcraft-interchange` — every suite passes. `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-interchange --lib --no-deps --tests` clean.

title: fix(captions): bound TTML nesting depth (#2065)
author: rollroyces
body:
Closes #2065.

**Cause.** `walk` (`crates/captions/src/ttml.rs:561`) and `collect` (`:439`) took no depth parameter, so a document nested a thousand levels deep was walked in full with no warning: on main, a 1000-deep TTML document emits every cue and costs a 1000-frame stack.

Every other nestable-document walker in the repo is capped — AAF read 32, AAF store 200, comp 16, render 8 — so TTML was the one exception.

**Fix.** Both walkers now carry a depth and stop at `MAX_NESTING = 64`, recording a warning so a truncated document is visible rather than silent.

```rust
/// Elements nested deeper than this are not descended into. Every other nestable-document
/// walker in the repo is capped (AAF/OMF 32, store 200, comp 16, render 8); TTML was the one
/// that walked a document of any depth. (#2065)
const MAX_NESTING: usize = 64;
```

`walk` becomes `walk_at(…, depth)` and `collect` becomes `collect_at(…, depth)`; the originals stay as the depth-0 entry points, so their two other call sites are unchanged.

**Test.** `deep_nesting_is_bounded_and_warns` checks both halves: 256 levels is truncated with a warning and no cue, while 4 levels (more nesting than real captions use) imports whole with no warning.

**Build.** `cargo test -p filmcraft-captions` → 48 + 13 + 10 + 12 passed, 0 failed. `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-captions --lib --no-deps --tests` clean.

title: Import: numbered embedded-audio names keep the path's separators on Windows
author: dotCooCoo
body:
## Problem

On Windows, `filmcraft-engine`'s `interchange::embedded_audio_tests::virtual_extraction_keeps_existing_media` fails on
`main` (`abf44fda`):

```
left: "/files\\cut Audio (2).wav"
right: "/files/cut Audio (3).wav"
```

When an AAF or OMF import finds its embedded-audio path taken, `write_embedded_audio` tries numbered names built with
`Path::with_file_name`. On Windows that call puts `\` between the folder and the new name whatever separator the path
was written with. The test's in-memory files are keyed by string, so `/files\cut Audio (2).wav` looked free next to
`/files/cut Audio (2).wav`. In the app, a document imported by a forward-slash path (`file.importAaf` with `C:/…/cut.aaf`)
whose embedded-audio name is taken stores a media path with mixed separators (`C:/…/cut Media\Audio (2).wav`).

## Fix

A numbered name now replaces only the file name: `write_embedded_audio` splits the path at its last `/` or `\`, as the
interchange crate's `file_name` does, and keeps the folder as written.

## Tests

New `numbered_names_keep_the_path_separators`: a taken `C:/files/cut Audio.wav` and a taken `C:\files\cut Audio.wav`
each give `(2)` with the same separators, and the existing file keeps its bytes. On Windows it fails without the change
and passes with it. This pull request leaves `virtual_extraction_keeps_existing_media` as it is on `main`; with the
change it passes on Windows too.

Open #2025 and #2924 change `virtual_extraction_keeps_existing_media` to build its keys with `Path`, which makes the
test pass on Windows without a code change. This branch merges cleanly with each of them, and with `main` at `3fadb8af`.

title: Only materialise kept frames when filling an H.264 frame_num gap
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #2779

## Cause
`Dpb::fill_frame_num_gap` called `make_frame` for every missing frame_num, up to `max_frame_num - 1` (65,535) per access unit. In the software decoder each call allocates a full-size picture and copies the last decoded frame into it, so a tiny stream with large frame_num jumps forces tens of thousands of full-frame copies per access unit.

## Fix
The gap fill now works out how many frames are missing and, for all but the last `max_num_ref_frames` of them, only runs the POC / frame_num bookkeeping callback. The sliding window would have evicted those earlier frames before the gap ended, so the final DPB state is the same while at most `max_num_ref_frames` pictures are built. The software decoder and the VA-API path both get this through the shared DPB.

title: #2633: the scrub playhead no longer waits for the audio device
author: XIILO
body:
## What
Opening a WASAPI output stream starts the Windows audio engine: 559 ms measured on Realtek (cpal 0.16) from a cold engine, 19-23 ms while another stream is running. A playhead drag paid that on the UI thread, twice:
- `scrub_playhead` called `app.stop()` on every press, and the press path runs twice per drag, so the first grain's stream was closed two frames later and opened again;
- `CpalOut::config` listed every supported configuration (191 ms) even when the device already ran at the rate the settings ask for;
- the remaining open still ran on the UI thread.
- 
## Fix
- stop only a transport that is running (`transport_running()`);
- skip the rate search when the device's default rate is the wanted one (`stream_config`);
- play the scrub grain on its own output (`ScrubOut` / `CpalScrubOut`): its thread owns the stream (`cpal::Stream` is `!Send`), keeps it for 5 s after the last grain and swaps in the current mixer per grain. The UI only sends over a channel, so a press or a drag does no blocking work.
A cold drag goes from ~1.5 s of frozen playhead to no blocking work in the frame. The first grain after the engine went cold is silent (~0.6 s: the stream is opening on its own thread). Playback's own start is unchanged and still opens on the UI thread, out of scope here.

## Tests
- `crates/ui-egui/tests/scrub_stream_ui.rs`: one drag asks for the scrub output once (it fails with `left: 2` before the `transport_running` guard), never touches the playback output, a second drag in the linger reuses the stream, and a press while playing still stops the transport.
- `apps/filmcraft` audio tests: `play` returns without waiting for the device.
- 199 ui-egui lib tests, 12 audio tests and 29 timeline / escape / scroll / playback integration tests pass; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --all-targets` are clean.
- Before / after numbers are in `docs/performance.md`.
Fixes #2633.

title: gpu: fall back to CPU for plans beyond the texture limit (#2996)
author: justacalico
body:
Fixes #2996.

## What was wrong

A still larger than the GPU's `max_texture_dimension_2d` (8192 on many devices, including the reporter's Asahi GPU) made `plane_texture` fail `Device::create_texture` validation. The layer then drew nothing and the export baked black frames into the output while reporting success.

## What changed

- `GpuCompositor::render_export_prepared` now declines a plan that needs a texture side beyond the device's limit, so the export pipeline renders those frames with `render_sequence` on the CPU. No invalid texture is created, no error is raised, and the device is never marked failed: the frames around the oversized still keep using the GPU.
- `GpuCompositor::render_plan` defends the same case for the display paths (`composite`/`composite_prepared`): when the output still fits a texture it composites the plan with `execute_cpu` and draws that image, so a direct call with an oversized plan can no longer produce a validation error or a black frame.
- The CPU fallback is memory-bounded: `plan_cpu_shrunk` decimates oversized layer sources per axis to the detail the placed quad can show (the same decimation rule the CPU renderer picks for `want`), converting in linear light via `to_linear_f32_decimated_with` plus a residual per-axis box, so the executor's linear images never grow to full source resolution and an axis that still needs its rows or columns keeps them. Layers carrying effects keep their frames; the working image already bounds their conversion.
- `GpuCompositor::effect_image` returns `None` for a source frame that cannot upload, mirroring the existing `FxStage::job` working-image check.

The monitor already sends oversized plans to the CPU path (`gpu_present` checks `plan_side` and hands off), so it renders correctly; this change makes the compositor itself safe wherever it is called.

## Tests

Three regression tests in `crates/gpu/src/tests.rs` run on any adapter:

- `oversized_source_composites_from_the_cpu`: a layer wider than th…

title: AMD VA-API GPU-resident export (strict, fail-closed)
author: Silvazrlq
body:
## Motivation

FilmCraft export on Linux had no path that keeps video frames on the GPU from composition to the encoder. This PR adds a strict AMD path: VA-API H.264/HEVC encoding fed by Vulkan DMA-BUF interop with NV12 surfaces, so export does not read video pixels back to the CPU.

The behaviour is intentionally strict:

- Fail-closed: if the AMD GPU-resident requirements are not met, export fails with an error instead of silently falling back to CPU rendering or FFmpeg.
- No CPU readback of video pixels on the hardware export path.
- Opt-in from the CLI: `--hardware-export`. The GUI offers a manual CPU export option; the default stays GPU.

## Scope

In scope:

- H.264 High 8-bit and HEVC Main 8-bit, strict export, on AMD RADV with VA-API on the same DRM node as Vulkan.
- Allowlisted effects and transitions only (see parity below).
- Linux packaging for the new path.

Not in scope:

- NVENC and software export (unchanged).
- HEVC Main10, HDR, P010 (not enabled), AV1 encode (not offered).
- Non-AMD GPUs.

## Design

Pipeline: MP4 sample -> VA-API decode (LINEAR) -> Vulkan DMA-BUF import -> wgpu compositor, effects and transitions per layer -> NV12 repack -> VA-API encode -> mux.

- **Transfer ledger.** Three in-flight transfer slots (`ResidentLedger` / `ResidentReservation` in `crates/export/src/lib.rs`), admitted against host RAM headroom. See the ADR.
- **Persistent decode cursors.** Up to four long-lived decode sessions (`MAX_DECODE_CURSORS` in `crates/platform/src/amd_resident.rs`). Cursors do not hold ledger slots.
- **Quarantine.** Resources that may still be used by VA-API or the GPU after a post-submission error are retained, not destroyed.
- **Fail-closed routing.** `GpuRendering::AmdRequired` and `Auto` return an error before dispatch on any unsupported route or unlisted effect or transition. `Off` is the explicit CPU reference mode.

## Profile matrix

|---|---|
| H.264 High 8-bit | Enabled, strict export |

title: render, gpu: adjustment layers composited on the GPU
author: EduardoAndradeMachado
body:
Refs #30.

## The problem

With Export ▸ GPU Rendering on (`gpuRendering: auto`), every frame with an adjustment layer at that time is rendered by the CPU: `plan::layered_at` returns false for it, `plan_frame` hands back `FramePlan::Image(render_sequence(..))`, and since #760 `Pipeline::frame` doesn't even take a pooled renderer for it. A grade on an adjustment layer over a whole edit (a common way to colour a timeline) therefore turns GPU export off for the whole edit. On a real 82 s 1080p30 edit with a Lumetri adjustment layer over 89 % of it, GPU rendering Auto exported at the CPU's speed with the GPU's 3D engine at 1–4 %.

## The change

title: engine, codecs: open an item's media source once under parallel first requests
author: EduardoAndradeMachado
body:
## Summary

An export renders each batch's frames in parallel, so a clip's first frames reach `MediaPool::resolve` at the same moment. `resolve` read the cache, opened the file on a miss and stored the source afterwards, so every worker missed and every worker opened the file: one `MediaSource`, one `GopCache` and one hardware decoder each, each walking the GOP from the sync sample to deliver a single frame. Only the last source stored survived; the others were dropped with their decoders. `perf.stats` showed it as one hardware session and one seek per renderer for every clip an export entered.

## The change

- **One open per item.** `MediaPool` holds a lock per item while that item is being opened (`MediaPool::opening`). The first worker opens; the others wait, re-check the cache under the lock and share the one source. An item already in the pool takes the read-locked lookup as before, and different items still open in parallel. The same gate covers `proxy_source`.
- **The open runs on a pool of its own** (`codecs::gop::isolated_open`, one thread per core, beside the decode pool of #480). An opener that decodes as it opens (the EXR still, `par_chunks_mut`) starts rayon work; a frame worker waiting inside that work on its own pool could pick up another frame job of the batch, which would block on the gate that worker holds. Opens do not run on the decode pool, so a slow file never holds up the caches' decoding. An open started from an open runs in place.
- **No pool, no gate.** Where the open pool cannot be made, and on the web build (no threads), the open runs on the asking thread without the gate, as before. A deferred-read mark (`media::pending`) the thread already had stays set across the open, so a frame with a layer still being fetched is still known to be incomplete.
- **A failing proxy is tried once.** A proxy that fails to open is not tried again for that item for one second (`PROXY_RETRY`), so the requests waiting on the gate fall back to the original in…

title: codecs, render, export: skip non-reference pictures no exported frame uses
author: EduardoAndradeMachado
body:
## Summary

A 30 fps export of 59.94 fps media uses every other source picture, but the GOP cache decoded every one of them (the "59.94 fps sources decoded for 30 fps output" left as a follow-up in #3046). A sample is decoded or skipped as the decoder reaches it, and only playback's catch-up hint (M4.8) let the cache skip one. That hint is a time threshold ("frames before this one are late"), which an export cannot give: its frames are rendered in parallel batches, so requests reach a cache out of order, and a sample below one request's threshold can be the next request's frame.

This PR lets an export say which instants it will ask for, and the cache leaves out the non-reference samples none of them is shown at. The output is byte-identical; no setting, as with the other bit-exact decode work (M4.8 catch-up, M4.9).

## The change

- **The export's frame step reaches the media.** `RenderOptions::frame_step` (set by `export::Pipeline` to the output frame duration) becomes the thread's frame grid (`filmcraft_media::cancel::with_frame_grid`, carried by `cancel::Context` like the other hints) around the frame request of each clip that maps output frames to media time one to one: a clip of the rendered sequence at 100 % speed, forward, with no frame hold and no enabled effect that reads other frames (`vfx::is_temporal`). Clips inside nested and multicam sequences get no grid, on the CPU and the GPU plan paths.
- **The MP4 / MOV source turns the grid into a prediction.** `mp4::grid_instant` gives, for a sample, the first grid instant at or after it is presented, rounded as `video_at` rounds a request. A sample is presented at its pts plus the edit list offset: x264 files with B-frames delay every picture by the reorder, so the raw pts would put the prediction off by that many samples (this is what the 59.94 fps test catches).
- **The GOP cache leaves out a non-reference sample** (`VideoDecoder::is_disposable`, as in M4.8: H.264 `nal_ref_idc` 0, HEVC sub-layer non-referenc…

title: export: convert H.264 pictures to 4:2:0 while rendering, with a 40 % cheaper conversion
author: Exalted5373
body:
## Summary

The built-in H.264 encoder converted every rendered RGBA8 picture to 8-bit 4:2:0 on the export's encoding thread. The conversion's rows ran on the shared rayon pool, which is busy rendering the next batch, so the encoder sat idle waiting for them (`perf.stats` `export.stages.convertMs`: about 450 ms of a 5.7 s 1080p export).

```diff
 Exporter::step
   render_batch                      (rayon, one batch ahead of the encoder)
     Pipeline::frame -> RGBA8
+    VideoEncoder::yuv420_input -> rgba_to_yuv420_8 / rgbf_to_yuv420_8 -> Yuv420
   encode_batch                      (serial)
-    H264Encoder::encode
-      rgba_to_yuv420_8              (queued behind the render on the shared pool)
-      try_encode
+    H264Encoder::encode_yuv420
+      try_encode
```

- `VideoEncoder::yuv420_input` / `encode_yuv420` (default methods): an encoder names the 4:2:0 conversion it runs, and the exporter runs that same function in the render task that drew the frame. A frame waiting to be encoded holds 1.5 bytes per pixel instead of 4 (12 for HDR). Encoders that take other pictures (NVENC's RGBA input, ProRes, DNxHR, …) are unchanged.
- `rgba_to_yuv420_8` / `rgbf_to_yuv420_8` work 64 pixels at a time with the chroma terms on the stack (no allocation per row pair), and round with `+ 0.5` and a truncating cast instead of `f32::round`, which is a libm call on the baseline x86-64 target. The rounding equals `round().clamp(1.0, 254.0)` for all 2^32 `f32` values, and the new functions give the old codes for every 8-bit RGB colour.
- A short picture no longer panics the conversion, and the H.264 encoder returns an error for a picture of the wrong size.

## Evidence

The output is byte-identical. Every A/B export below has the same MD5 (`663b0244…`). The new determinism test exports SDR, two-pass and PQ H.264 with the conversion on either side, rendering ahead or not.

title: gpu: export on the high-performance GPU, and read staging memory in bulk
author: Exalted5373
body:
## Summary

On a laptop where an Intel integrated GPU is listed before an NVIDIA GPU, Export ▸ GPU Rendering made exports **40× slower**. There were two causes:

- **Wrong GPU.** The export renderer asked wgpu for an adapter with no power preference, which takes the first one listed: the integrated GPU. The app's window asks for the high-performance one.
- **Slow read-back on that GPU.** The integrated GPU's read-back memory is uncached, and the compositor read each 1080p half-float frame from it two bytes at a time. That took 650 ms per frame, and 1.3 s with four renderers at once.

```diff
 ExportRenderer::new
-  request_adapter(RequestAdapterOptions::default())            # first listed: the iGPU
+  request_adapter(power_preference: from_env() or HighPerformance)

 GpuCompositor::map_accumulator / effect_image, GpuMask::run
   for each row of the mapped staging buffer
-    convert sample by sample from mapped memory
+    copy the row out in one go (copy_mapped), then convert from ordinary memory
```

- `WGPU_POWER_PREF` still overrides the choice, as it does for the window.
- On a single-GPU machine nothing changes.
- On cached memory the row copy stays in the CPU cache and costs next to nothing.

## Evidence

**Read-back alone** (throwaway test, a mapped 1080p RGBA16F buffer):

| GPU | read sample by sample | copy each row first |
|---|---|---|
| Intel integrated (Mesa ANV) | 650 ms | 85 ms |
| NVIDIA RTX 50 series | 2 ms | ~2 ms |

**Whole exports.** `cargo xtask bench --sections export --repeat 2 --hw auto` (GPU rendering Auto plus NVENC; ProRes has no hardware encoder), best of 2. Main and this branch were built and run back to back on the same laptop:

| scene | main | this PR | this PR, iGPU forced (`WGPU_POWER_PREF=low`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `h264` | 61.69 s | **1.42 s** | 7.97 s |
| `h264_fx` (3 layers + effects) | 65.28 s | **1.56 s** | 14.21 s |
| `prores` | 61.11 s | **4.63 s** | 7.53 s |

- CPU time per frame dropped from about 1,250–1,540 ms to 44–3…

title: export: hardware encoding on by default, falling back to the built-in encoder
author: Exalted5373
body:
## Summary

This is a proposal for the maintainers to decide on. It makes **Export ▸ Hardware encoding default to Auto**, which is how Premiere Pro and Media Encoder ship. Adobe's documentation says ["Hardware Encoding is the default"](https://helpx.adobe.com/premiere/desktop/render-and-export/export-files/video-encoding-settings.html), and Premiere switches to software automatically when the settings aren't supported. CapCut also turns hardware encoding on by default (Settings ▸ Performance).

```diff
 pub enum HardwareEncoding {
-    #[default]
     Off,
+    #[default]
     Auto,
 }
```

What doesn't change:

- **No hardware encoder, or settings it declines.** The built-in encoder runs, exactly as before. Declined settings are two-pass, CRF, HDR H.264, MXF, interlaced output, odd sizes and non-square pixels.
- **Off is still there.** It gives the built-in encoder's byte-identical output on every machine. It's one checkbox in Export ▸ Video, or `"hardwareEncoding": "off"` in `file.exportMedia` / `--settings`.

title: UI: survive a lost or starved graphics device during paint
author: admbe
body:
**Problem.** egui-wgpu panics inside its paint path when the window's device refuses a staging
buffer ("Failed to create staging buffer for index data"), which happens when GPU memory runs out
or the device is lost. A field report had it close the app three times in three minutes while
another GPU-heavy process filled video memory. The panic is in the dependency, so the UI's
`catch_unwind` only wrote the crash log; the work was lost.

**Change.**
- `gpu_health` installs wgpu's device-lost callback and uncaptured-error handler on the window's
  device, logs the reason and raises a flag. Out-of-memory and internal errors count as a loss;
  validation errors only move the preview to the CPU compositor, as before.
- A flagged device gets an empty frame (nothing to upload, nothing to panic on); playback stops,
  control requests are held, and the window closes with the session intact.
- The desktop host runs `eframe::run_native` under `catch_unwind` and reopens a window on the same
  session in software rendering (on X11, where the panic leaves winit's event loop marked as running
  and the first new window never starts, it starts that window once more), with a notice ("Graphics device lost; rendering in software. Save
  your work.") and a Help entry. The panic text also goes to the normal app log.

**Tests.** `apps/filmcraft/tests/graphics_loss.rs` launches the real binary, simulates the device-lost
callback and a failed staging buffer, and asserts the app keeps running and shows the notice (skip
with `FILMCRAFT_SKIP_WINDOW_TESTS=1`). Layering unchanged.

title: Playback plan for throughput-bound sources
author: admbe
body:
**Problem.** The playback planner assumes decode cost is sequential per source (true for long-GOP
codecs) and asks for every frame. A source that decodes each frame independently but slower than the
sequence rate (a 6K camera RAW decoder at ~25 fps under a 59.94 fps sequence, or any slow intra-frame
decoder) then delivers every frame a little late and the monitor freezes.

**Change.**
- `MediaSource::frame_delivery()` lets a source say its frames decode independently and, optionally,
  the rate it sustains; wrappers forward it; the default changes nothing for existing sources.
- `throughput_plan` keeps m of every n frames (1/1, 3/4, 2/3, 1/2, 2/5, 3/8, 1/3, 1/4, then 1/n),
  the densest the measured capacity covers (the lesser of the source's rate and workers / latency),
  with hysteresis and anchored so the set does not shift with the playhead; each frame starts its
  latency plus slack ahead; running jobs within six frames behind the playhead finish and show late.
- The plan cache evicts frames already shown before prefetched ones, and the prefetch depth is bounded
  by what the cache holds; a media-pool item opened by several workers at once opens only once.
- `FILMCRAFT_FRAME_WORKERS` and `FILMCRAFT_PLAYBACK_PATTERN=keep/of` pin the worker count and the
  pattern for measurements. No in-tree source sets `independent` yet; intra-only decoders (ProRes,
  DNx, MJPEG, APV) are candidates for a follow-up.

**Measured** with a 6K intra-frame source at half resolution: 59.94p went from a frozen picture to an
even 22.5–24 fps on screen with no cancelled jobs; 23.976p plays three of four frames; a 119.88p 4K
source plays every frame. Unit tests for the plan, the patterns, the hysteresis and the cache.

title: frame: convert full-size 8-bit Y'CbCr row by row, 28 % faster and bit-identical
author: Exalted5373
body:
## Summary

Converting a decoded 8-bit Y'CbCr picture to the compositor's linear float RGBA (`VideoFrame::convert_region`) is the largest CPU cost of rendering plain footage. In a profile of an NVENC export of a plain 1080p clip it was 37 % of all CPU time. At full size (`n == 1`, used by export and full-size playback), the general loop still did everything per pixel:

- worked out the sample's row and column through `min` and shifts;
- looked up all three planes through bounds-checked indexing;
- ran the `dy` / `dx` box loops, each of a single step.

```diff
 convert_region, PixelData::Yuv8
+  if n == 1                                  # one source pixel per output pixel
+    per output row: get() the Y, Cb, Cr (and alpha) rows once
+      per pixel: the same arithmetic as the general loop
+        ((0 + q(..) * a) * inv, in the same order)
+    a sample the planes don't hold → transparent
   else
     the general box-filter loop, unchanged
```

**Every value is the same, bit for bit.** The arithmetic and its order are the general loop's.

It also fixes a panic. A frame whose planes are shorter than its size used to panic in this loop (index out of bounds). At full size, pixels whose samples are missing now come out transparent, and a row that a plane ends in keeps the samples it has.

## Evidence

`cargo run --release -p filmcraft-render --example frame_bench`: synthetic 1080p sources, milliseconds per frame, median of 40 frames. Single thread, main and this branch run alternately, 3 rounds on a loaded machine:

| stage | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| camera frame → linear f32 image | 22.96 / 20.71 / 16.88 | **14.89 / 15.03 / 14.28** |
| camera only: render + 8-bit | 31.48 / 38.54 / 26.65 | **24.70 / 22.52 / 24.94** |
| checksum, camera only | `05d43d7b529cb76d` | `05d43d7b529cb76d` |
| checksum, camera + banner | `4265d8e33c58d09a` | `4265d8e33c58d09a` |

- **28 % less time for the conversion** (median 20.7 → 14.9 ms).
- **Identical output.**

title: export: hand frames nothing is drawn on to the encoder as decoded
author: Exalted5373
body:
## Summary

**Builds on #3051**, whose two commits come first here; review the commits from "export: hand frames nothing is drawn on to the encoder as decoded" on. GitHub can't stack a PR from a fork on another fork branch.

Plain footage was still rendered. Take a frame that is one clip at the sequence's size, with nothing drawn on it. It went through these steps:

1. Converted from its decoded 8-bit 4:2:0 to linear float RGBA (`convert_region`).
2. Flattened over black and turned into RGBA8.
3. Converted back to 4:2:0 by the encoder: on the CPU for the built-in one, on the GPU for NVENC.

That round trip was most of the CPU of a plain export. It also clipped colours outside the RGB cube.

Now such a frame goes to the encoder as its decoded planes:

```diff
 render task, frame f
+  untouched_frame(project, seq, t)           one clip, nothing drawn, Motion at rest (plan_frame's own answer)
+    && yuv420_of(frame)                       8-bit 4:2:0, BT.709, limited range, no alpha
+    && encoder.takes_yuv420()                 built-in H.264; NVENC 8-bit (H.264, H.265 Main)
+      → encode_yuv420(decoded planes)          no render, no conversion
   else
     render → RGBA8 (or 4:2:0 while rendering, #3051) → encoder, as before
```

**What still goes through the renderer:**

- Clip edits: opacity below 100 %, Motion away from rest, any effect or mask, a transition, a clip or caption above.
- Source footage: BT.601, full range, 4:2:2, or an alpha plane.
- Export settings: HDR, alpha output, the limiter, any overlay, another frame size.

`untouched_frame` checks the timeline before planning, so a composited frame is never planned twice. A source whose video stream declares frames this can't take (alpha, a matrix, range or transfer other than BT.709 limited, or another size) is not decoded to look at them. `render::plan::untouched_source` gives the clip's media item without decoding, and the renderer alone plans and decodes those frames. title: Store media paths relative to the project file
author: justacalico
body:
Closes #3067

When a project file is saved, media paths that can be expressed relative to the project file's folder are stored relative, so a project and the media beside it keep working when the folder moves to another drive, an SMB share, or a different machine/OS.

- Write side: every `.fcproj` write (`file.save`/`saveAs`/`saveCopy`, auto-save, recovery journal, templates, selection export, Project Manager) resolves each media/proxy path through the media pool's per-document tracking, then stores it relative to the file being written when that round-trips (`doc_path::project_for_document`/`store`). - Also fixes two spots that took `parent()` of stored paths (narration, extract audio) and makes the Media Browser already-imported check compare resolved files.

title: nvdec: read pictures back through a page-locked buffer on a stream of their own
author: Exalted5373
body:
## Summary

NVDEC (Linux) copied each decoded picture to the host with a synchronous `cuMemcpyDtoH` into a new, zero-filled `Vec`, and mapped the picture with the default output stream. Two costs came with that:

- **Ordinary memory.** A copy into pageable memory goes through the driver's own staging buffer and pins the destination's pages on the way. In a profile, the readback was mostly `ioctl` time plus a CPU copy.
- **The default stream.** Work on the legacy default stream waits for every blocking stream of the context, and NVDEC shares the primary context with NVENC. In an export with hardware encoding, each picture's post-processing and copy waited for the pictures being encoded: about 2 ms per 1080p picture.

```diff
 cuvid map_picture / readback
-  cuvidMapVideoFrame(proc.output_stream = 0)          default stream
-  host = vec![0; pitch × rows × 1.5]                   new, zeroed, pageable
-  cuMemcpyDtoH(host, mapped)                           synchronous, via the driver's staging
+  cuvidMapVideoFrame(proc.output_stream = stream)      the session's non-blocking stream
+  cuMemcpyDtoHAsync(pinned, mapped, stream)            page-locked buffer kept by the session
+  cuStreamSynchronize(stream)
   to_frame(...) → planar Y'CbCr, as before
```

- `cuda::Device` resolves its CUDA functions once instead of looking them up on every call. It owns:
  - the page-locked staging buffer (`cuMemAllocHost_v2`, grown when needed, zeroed once);
  - the non-blocking stream (`cuStreamCreate` with `CU_STREAM_NON_BLOCKING`).

  Both are released with the context current, before the primary context is released.
- `Device::with_host_copy(source, len, read)` replaces `copy_to_host`. Without page-locked memory or a stream from the driver, it falls back to the old copy into ordinary memory. When the stream exists, it waits for it first, because the picture's post-processing ran on it.
- **Failures.** A copy that fails may still be writing into the buffer, so that buffer is never re…

title: h264enc: code CRF and constant-QP GOPs in parallel, byte-identical
author: Exalted5373
body:
## Summary

The built-in H.264 encoder codes a picture's slices in parallel, and the B pictures of a mini-GOP together, but one picture batch after another. With **CRF and constant QP** it now also codes whole GOPs at the same time. **The output is byte-identical** to the serial encoder, for both the stream and the exported file.

This only works for these two modes, because they pick a frame's QP from its type alone, and IDRs are closed (they empty the DPB and restart `frame_num` and the POC). The bitrate modes stay serial: CBR, one-pass VBR (the export default) and both passes of two-pass VBR. In those, every picture's QP comes from the real size of the pictures before it, and per-macroblock AQ is rounded from that fractional QP, so parallel GOPs would change the bytes. CRF exports are always software-encoded (NVENC and VideoToolbox decline CRF), so this is the mode that gains.

```diff
 try_encode(picture)                       serial, as before: import, analysis, AQ,
                                           IDR / scene-cut decision, mini-GOP, DTS
-  encode_batch(...) on the calling thread
+  CRF / QP, ≥ 2 threads, two GOPs fit in 1 GiB:
+    IDR → start a GOP thread (its own DPB; idr_pic_id parity, ref numbering, SEI flag handed over)
+    batches → that GOP's thread: the same encode_batch calls, in the same order
+    packets / RC stats / reconstructions come back in decoding order
+  otherwise: encode_batch on the calling thread, unchanged
```

- **Memory.** Uncoded input pictures plus each GOP's working set stay under 1 GiB; a new GOP starts only once its working set fits. Where two GOPs of `keyint` pictures don't fit, the encoder stays serial (1080p with `keyint` 250, 4K with a 2-second keyint), as it does with one thread or `EncoderConfig::parallel_gops = false`.
- **Analysis pool.** Per-picture analysis runs on a small pool of its own. On the shared pool it queued behind the GOPs' slices and starved them.
- **Failures.** A GOP thread that panics is repor…

title: export: smart rendering of ProRes and DNxHR, copying untouched source frames
author: Exalted5373
body:
## Summary

**Builds on #3068** (which builds on #3051); review the commits from "export: smart rendering of ProRes and DNxHR" on. GitHub can't stack a PR from a fork on another fork branch.

A ProRes or DNxHR export decoded every frame, rendered it, converted it back to Y'CbCr and encoded it again, even where the timeline shows a source frame untouched. Now, when the source is ProRes or DNxHR in the flavour the export writes, such a frame is written as the source's compressed sample, unchanged (smart rendering). Every other frame is rendered and encoded as before, in the same track; the codecs are intra-only, so the two kinds of packet mix freely.

```diff
 render task, frame f
+  encoder.sample_copy() (ProRes, DNxHR adapters)
+  && Pipeline passthrough (#3068: SDR, nothing drawn on the output)
+  && render::plan::untouched_clip(f)       one clip, untouched, at the sequence's size; nothing decoded
+  && 100 % forward, no hold, source rate == output rate
+  && source.compressed_video_sample(t)     MOV/MP4, MXF: the sample video_frame would decode
+  && SampleCopy::check(sample)             flavour, size, scan, alpha, colour, aspect, frame tables
+    → packet = the sample's bytes (sync, one frame long, no composition offset)
   else
     render → encode, as before (also for any sample that can't be read or fails a check)
```

- **`MediaSource::compressed_video_sample(time, max_bytes)`**, defaulting to `Ok(None)`. A sample over `max_bytes` is refused from the file's index, before anything is read or allocated. The export passes the memory a rendered frame takes (`frame_bytes`), so copies stay within the batch budget. MOV/MP4 and MXF sources implement it for ProRes and DNx, with the same time-to-sample mapping `video_frame` uses. Sources whose decoded picture is cropped (clean aperture) or rotated return `None`.
- **`render::plan::untouched_clip`** is `untouched_frame` without decoding. It shares the timeline checks in `sole_plain_clip` with `untouched_frame` and `unt…

title: Keep WebVTT cues whose identifier is STYLE or REGION
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/captions/src/vtt.rs:86` (no existing issue): WebVTT cue whose identifier is "STYLE" or "REGION" is dropped as a style/region block.

## Cause
The WebVTT parser's STYLE/REGION block check only looked for "-->" in the first line of a block. A cue with the identifier STYLE or REGION has its timing on the second line, so the parser took it for a STYLE/REGION block and put it in `doc.blocks`. The cue was lost. This only happened before the first cue had been seen.

## Fix
The STYLE/REGION check now looks for "-->" on any line of the block, the same way the NOTE check does. A block with a timing line is parsed as a cue. A regression test covers both STYLE and REGION identifiers.

## Verified
- Regression test `vtt::tests::style_region_identifier_cue_is_kept`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-captions --lib style_region_identifier_cue_is_kept`).
