title: Lift and Extract put the removed range on the clipboard
author: EduardoAndradeMachado
body:
Fixes #3019.

## Problem

Set In/Out, Lift (`;`) or Extract (`'`), then Paste: `command 'edit.paste' is not available right now: clipboard is empty`. `sequence.lift` and `sequence.extract` removed the range but never wrote `EditorState::clipboard`. In Premiere the lifted or extracted frames go on the clipboard, and its help describes Lift followed by Edit > Paste as the way to move a range.

## Change

- `crates/engine/src/commands.rs`: before editing, `cut_range` reads the sequence and splits a copy of each targeted, unlocked track at In and Out with `edit::split_track_at`, the same split Lift and Extract use, so speed, reverse, frame hold and source In match what leaves the timeline and linked video/audio pieces stay linked. The clipboard is written only after the edit succeeds. Copy now stores through the same `set_clipboard`, which also clears the caption clipboard (it takes precedence in Paste).
- `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`: `sequence.lift` / `sequence.extract` join `edit.copy` / `edit.cut` in snapshotting stale OS media (#697) and putting the clip names on the system clipboard (#199). Without it, Ctrl+V after a Lift could paste a leftover image or files, or do nothing on Windows/Linux.
- `sequence.lift` / `sequence.extract` now return `{"copied": n}` (clips put on the clipboard, as `edit.copy` reports for captions; previously `null`). Over a range with no clips on the targeted tracks they copy nothing and leave the clipboard as it was, and the app then leaves the OS clipboard alone too, so an image or files copied since still paste (CodeRabbit review).

Choices, following Premiere and the existing Copy:
- Only targeted tracks are copied. Extract also cuts sync-locked untargeted tracks to keep them in sync; that material is not put on the clipboard (Premiere: select the track headers to lift from, Lift, then Paste).
- Pieces are placed relative to the earliest one, as Copy does for clips and captions.
- Captions are not copied; the caption clipboard takes pr…

title: Timeline: Show Duplicate Frame Markers marks media frames used more than once
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Timeline Display Settings has no Show Duplicate Frame Markers, so the Timeline cannot show where a sequence uses the same media frames twice. Premiere Pro's help describes the option under "Duplicate frame detection" (https://web.archive.org/web/20140512195956/http://helpx.adobe.com/premiere-pro/using/whats-new-7-0.html): a colored stripe runs across the bottom of a clip for each duplicated frame, each master clip that has a duplicate clip gets a color, up to ten colors are assigned and the tenth is reused, and still images and time remapping have no markers.

- Timeline Display Settings has a Show Duplicate Frame Markers check box under Show Through Edits. When it is on, a compared video clip gets a 3-point stripe along its bottom under each frame where it shows a media frame that another video clip of the same sequence also shows, in its master clip's color.
- Clips are compared by the media frame each one shows at each frame of the sequence, so a clip at 200 % is compared by the media frames it shows, which skip every other frame between its In and Out. A subclip counts as its master clip.
- Master clips with duplicate frames take their colors in the order they first appear in the sequence. The help page does not say how the colors are picked, so this order is FilmCraft's own rule.
- The help page excludes still images and time remapping. FilmCraft reads time remapping as a Time Remapping speed with keyframes, so a clip whose Time Remapping speed has no keyframes is compared. Generators, frame holds, nested sequences, graphics and adjustment layers are not compared. A sequence compares at most 1,000,000 frames: a clip whose frames would pass that count is not compared and gets no markers, and later clips that still fit are compared.
- The Timeline works the markers out again only after the project changes, draws only the stripes in view (stripes a point or less apart are drawn as one), and keeps them inside a clip while a trim drag shortens it.

title: gpu, render: composite HDR / wide-gamut sequences on the GPU
author: zsoli69
body:
Related to #965 (HEVC preview performance).

## What

A sequence whose working space is not Rec. 709 (Rec. 2100 PQ / HLG, or wide gamut) planned every frame as one CPU image: the composite, the input transforms and the working -> monitor transform all ran on the CPU, the largest cost of 4K HDR playback.

- color: OutputTransform::gpu_params() (GpuOutputParams) carries the stages after the compositor - BT.2390 tone mapping, the working -> target matrix, the gamut desaturation - in apply()'s order, leaving the SDR encode to the shader. None for a target the shader does not encode (an HDR export target), which stays on the CPU.
- gpu: the resolve pass runs those stages (display() in composite.wgsl) before its sRGB encode, from a display-transform uniform set with GpuCompositor::set_display_transform(). The default (all zeros) is the identity, so a caller that never sets one gets exactly the old output. Only the resolve pass uses it; reading the working-linear accumulator back (the export path) is unaffected.
- render: plan_frame plans an HDR / wide-gamut sequence as layers whenever the resolve pass can finish it; gpu_input no longer refuses a non-plain pipeline, so display-referred HDR / wide-gamut media (PQ, HLG, BT.2020, P3) is converted in the shader. Log media and camera gamuts still decode on the CPU and are composited as working-space float layers. is_cpu_frame (the export pool's predicate) is unchanged.
- ui: gpu_present sets the display transform of the sequence a frame belongs to.
- golden: gpu_matches_cpu_on_golden_scenes sets the scene's display transform as the app does; HDR scenes now composite on the GPU and are compared tone mapped (lumetri_hdr_pq, hdr_tone_map: max 1 code).

Known difference: burned-in captions are composited as layers in the working space, so in an HDR sequence they pass through the display transform on the GPU while the CPU draws them after it.

title: platform: read VA-API pictures through vaDeriveImage
author: zsoli69
body:
Sibling PRs of this series add rows to the same revision-history tables in `docs/`; whichever merges second has a one-line conflict there (keep both rows).

## What

Every decoded picture was copied out of the surface with vaGetImage into a second image before it was mapped - most of the readback's cost at 4K. vaDeriveImage maps the surface's own memory instead.

- The session reads through vaDeriveImage first; the first failure (a driver that cannot derive this surface) logs once and switches the session back to vaGetImage. vaDeriveImage is loaded optionally (sym_opt!, new): an older libva keeps vaGetImage.

- A failed vaDestroyImage of a derived image is an error, so the session stops deriving rather than leaking images.
- Biplanar has a chroma pitch of its own: a derived image whose planes are pitched differently is read, not refused (chroma_rows_use_their_own_pitch).
- p010_chroma_rows_use_their_own_pitch covers the 10-bit branch.

title: gpu: 10-bit video uploads as its codes, with no half-float conversion

title: codecs: no GOP re-walks in playback
author: zsoli69
body:
## What

Several frame jobs share one decoder. The job holding the decoder decoded past the pictures the others were waiting for and evicted them, so each of those seeked back and decoded its GOP again; and a decoder far behind the playhead decoded up to 48 pictures nobody asked for rather than restart at the wanted GOP.

- Requests register the pts they wait for (Waiting, removed on drop) and eviction keeps those frames (eviction_victim); lock order is state, then waiting.
- A decoder restarts at the wanted sync sample when it is more than 8 pictures behind (was 48), unless another request waits for a frame in between.
- 4K50 HEVC playback (Ryzen 7 5800X3D, RX 9070 XT, Mesa 26.2.5 VA-API): seeks 23-45 -> 1 per 8 s, picture lag 200-400 frames -> ~10 (perf.stats during development; the load average was not recorded). Unit tests cover the restart and the eviction choice.

After review:
- The catch-up skip keeps a late disposable picture another request waits for, and a test covers continuing past the threshold for such a frame (it fails without wanted_on_the_way).
- A request whose job was cancelled (a frame a scrub has left; it stays registered until it returns) no longer counts as waiting: it kept a decoder far behind the scrubbed-to frame decoding forward instead of restarting at its GOP, so the scrubbed-to picture came late (a_cancelled_request_does_not_keep_a_decoder_far_behind_going).

title: ui: playback on a slow source - short queue, newest picture
author: zsoli69
body:
Fixes #2696.

Sibling PRs of this series add rows to the same revision-history tables in `docs/`; whichever merges second has a one-line conflict there (keep both rows).

## What

A 4K50 HEVC source that takes 26-28 ms per picture can never feed every frame. The playhead ran at real time while the Program monitor froze on one picture (2 shown of ~400), with 15-28 requests queued and 0.8 s of source latency; a click on the timeline waited behind those jobs. (Observed on Ryzen 7 5800X3D, RX 9070 XT, Mesa 26.2.5 VA-API, through perf.stats; the load average was not recorded.)

- While one decoder cannot make the frame rate (source_cannot_keep_up), playback asks for the next SOURCE_BOUND_AHEAD (3) frames instead of the render-bound prefetch depth (14): the decoder is the serialized stage, so the queue is every picture's latency, and a scrub's latency too. (Asking for a sparser subset does not help: a long-GOP stream decodes the frames in between anyway.)
- The estimate is the recent frame jobs' source phase, timed by the UI (no decoder statistics needed): the cost is a low quantile, so queueing cannot feed back into it, and only the last SOURCE_WINDOW (32) jobs count, so a burst of scrubs ages out.
- The monitor shows the newest picture the source has: nearest_plan looks back by the measured picture latency (plan_lookback), bounded to one second of frames, instead of 6 frames. That also makes a scrub show the previous keyframe while the exact frame decodes.
- Unit tests cover the estimator (queueing, ageing out) and the source-bound plan.

After review:
- While source-bound, the kept span has no slack, so frames queued under the deeper render-bound prefetch are dropped at the switch; and running jobs within the look-back finish instead of being cancelled when the playhead passes them (a cancelled job's result is not cached, so the monitor would have nothing newer to show). playback_span / keeps_playback_job are unit tested.

title: gpu, color: decode log curves on the GPU from the CPU's own table
author: zsoli69
body:
Depends on #3213: this branch contains its commit. Only the last commit (1a1884fb) belongs to this PR; merge #3213 first.

## What

With HDR sequences on the GPU, a log source (S-Log3, V-Log, C-Log, LogC, Apple Log) still decoded on the CPU: InputTransform::gpu_params refused Curve::Log and the camera-gamut compression stage, so camera footage - what HDR grading is mostly done on - kept a scalar f32 decode per frame.

- color: GpuCurve::Lut, and InputTransform::gpu_lut() hands the shader the decode table the CPU interpolates (a log curve is a table on the CPU too: 8192 entries over -0.1..1.1). The effect stage draws its source through the same table (an S-Log3 clip with GPU effects would otherwise come out black).
- tests: gpu_params is checked against DecodeTable::lookup for every log space; an S-Log3 / S-Gamut3.Cine source composited into the Rec. 2100 HLG working space matches execute_cpu (p99 1 code), plain and with a GPU effect.

author: zsoli69
body:

title: Trim Mode: select and edit linked audio with picture (#3085)
author: thecyberbutler
body:
Selecting a video edit point in Trim Mode left its linked audio edge unselected. Rolling through the Trim Monitor then moved only the picture, breaking synchronization. Explicitly selecting both partners could also run regular/ripple trims twice.

Fixes #3085.

## Changes

- Explicit and nearest-edge selection include unlocked linked partner edges when Linked Selection is enabled; Shift-click toggles the group.
- Reuse the existing timeline commands to clamp and edit each linked group once. Rolling edits follow matching linked cuts at the same time, preserving split edits; regular/ripple trims follow corresponding In/Out edges.
- Add engine and UI regression coverage and document the selection behavior. The right-click edit-point menu and default-transition tests now verify both picture and linked sound.

## Validation

Three regressions failed before the fix: missing linked selection, audio left behind during a roll, and double trimming of explicitly selected linked clips. Coverage also includes Linked Selection off, untargeted audio, track locks, unequal media handles, split edits, dynamic trimming, and Undo/Redo. title: matroska: preserve PTS semantics in the lacing oracle
author: KeroZelvin
body:
`filmcraft-matroska`'s `laced_remux` fails on unchanged `main` at `bfc23840` with FFmpeg/ffprobe 9.0.2: `vorbis.mkv Xiph: nothing was laced`. The generated Vorbis fixture declares a 1,333,333 ns `DefaultDuration` while its stored packet timestamps advance by 21 or 22 ms. The pinned writer correctly preserves those timestamps by declining to lace packets whose timing that duration cannot describe; the oracle incorrectly requires a lace in this case. This is an oracle repair, with no muxer or dependency changes.

The positive matrix still requires actual Xiph/EBML lacing on AAC and FLAC, and FixedOrEbml on PCM; FLAC gains Xiph coverage. A separate Vorbis regression deliberately supplies an incompatible 1 ns declared duration, leaves every source packet timestamp and payload unchanged, and strictly requires unlaced output for both Xiph and EBML. Every remux is compared independently with ffprobe. Existing payload, packet-count and timestamp assertions remain, with added codec-header, keyframe and exact fallback timestamp checks. No assertion is conditionally skipped when lacing is absent.

This follows the timestamp-preserving fallback contract of the pinned writer and [RFC 9559 §10.3.5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9559.html#section-10.3.5). The mismatch does not establish a gap in decoded Vorbis audio.

Reproduction on a clean detached baseline:

```sh
cargo test -p filmcraft-matroska --test oracle laced_remux -- --exact --nocapture
```

Before: 0 passed, 1 failed (`vorbis.mkv Xiph: nothing was laced`). After: the complete oracle target passes 16 tests, with the existing fixture-generator test ignored.

Validation: Linux x86_64 / Rust 1.99.1 / FFmpeg 9.0.2. Format, strict workspace all-target Clippy, full native workspace (3,655 passed, 0 failed, 45 existing ignored across 112 binaries), eight doctests, layering, asset attribution (69 assets), WASM (49 crates), and native desktop build all pass. Gates were run before committing; no test or CI exclusions were add…

title: timeline: add Shift-drag ripple rate stretch
author: KeroZelvin
body:
Depends on #3225: this branch retains the separate Matroska oracle repair commit `3299fc25`. The feature originated in `214b159b`; current head `d730a02c` merges `main` at `3a5f217b` (FilmCraft 0.13.0). This resolves conflicts with upstream's Alt edge edits while preserving their link-following choice in both preview and release. Alt is captured on the press frame, before the drag threshold.

Rate Stretch changes speed by dragging an edge, but it has no visual ripple mode: shortening leaves a gap and lengthening stops at the next clip. The Speed/Duration dialog's “Ripple Edit, Shifting Trailing Clips” option applies to that dialog operation only. This PR adds an explicit gesture for the missing workflow rather than making that checkbox global.

title: ui: Lumetri Scopes computed off the UI thread
author: zsoli69
body:
Independent of the other open PRs: based on `main`, it touches neither `crates/ui-egui/src/frames.rs` nor the GPU / render code of the HDR series.

## What

With the Lumetri Scopes panel open, playback lagged hard: every new frame was turned into a scope signal and scope images inside the UI pass. For Rec. 2100 scopes of an HDR sequence that is a working-space render of the frame, sources decoded (filmcraft_engine::scopes::scope_signal), on every refresh while playing.

- ui: a scope worker (scope_worker.rs): one background thread, work keyed per slot (a panel's signal, each scope image), the newest request of a slot wins, so playback never queues scope work. Jobs run under catch_unwind; a panicking one leaves the slot's last result. The worker asks egui for a repaint when a result lands. Without threads (wasm32) a request runs at once, as before.
- ui: the Lumetri Scopes panel (and the Reference monitor's scopes) submit the signal (HDR: the working-space render; SDR: the frame server's picture, requested as before) and every scope image to the worker and show the newest finished result meanwhile. While playing, an HDR scope render starts at most every 100 ms: it decodes the frame a second time, next to the Program monitor.
- engine: scope_signal_of() renders the scope signal from a project and a source provider, without the Session; scope_signal (scopes.read) uses it.
- tests: the worker's newest-wins, panic and thread behaviour; the HDR scopes UI test waits for the worker's result.
- 4K50 HEVC Main 10 PQ clip, scopes open, UI pass per frame step (egui_kittest, release, software decode, Ryzen 7 5800X3D, load ~5, measured once): p50 24.1 -> 3.3 ms, max 968 -> 19 ms; with the scopes closed it is 3.4-3.6 ms (docs/performance.md).

title: Monitors: Transparency Grid shows the picture's transparent areas
author: dotCooCoo
body:
The Source and Program monitors have no Transparency Grid. The frames they show are flattened over black before they reach the screen (`over_black_rgba8` sets every alpha to 255), so the transparent areas of a title, graphic or clip with an alpha channel show as black, and Display Mode ▸ Alpha shows white everywhere. Premiere Pro's help describes the grid under "Transparency Grid" (https://web.archive.org/web/20230623133015/https://helpx.adobe.com/premiere-pro/how-to/intro-to-compositing.html): "Select Transparency Grid from the Source Monitor Settings menu or Program Monitor Settings menu."

- View ▸ Transparency Grid and an item in each monitor's wrench menu (`view.transparencyGrid`) paint a checkerboard behind the picture in place of the monitor background. Like the other view toggles, the command takes `{"enabled": bool}` and `{"monitor": "program"|"source"}`, and the setting is `transparency_grid` in `ui.inspect` and `ui.set`. It is off by default, and each monitor keeps its own setting. The help page names only the monitors' settings menus; FilmCraft also lists the item in the View menu with its other monitor view toggles.
- The help page does not give the square size or the colors, so FilmCraft uses 8 pt squares in white and #cccccc, starting with a white square at the picture's top-left corner. A magnified picture paints only the squares in view. In Comparison View the reference frame gets the grid too.
- The monitor frame cache keeps each pixel's alpha (`Image::over_black_with_alpha_rgba8`; the color bytes are the same as before). `texture_for` still uploads the picture opaque, so every other place that shows cached frames looks as it did. With the grid on, the monitor uploads the frame with its alpha, converted to egui's gamma-space premultiplied colors. The GPU compositor's output and the render previews are opaque, so while the grid is on the Program monitor and the Comparison View reference render the sequence live on the CPU (`Target::SequenceLive`).

title: Timeline: a transition stays within its clips after a regular trim
author: dotCooCoo
body:
A Regular trim (the Selection tool's edge drag) that shortens one of the two clips of a transition could leave the transition reaching past that clip: trimming the second clip's Out edge, or the first clip's In edge, moved the clip's edge but not the transition. A Speed/Duration change without ripple that made one of the clips shorter did the same. Only fades to or from nothing followed the trimmed edge. `transitions::set_span` refuses a span that leaves the clips, and `Sequence::check` does not catch it.

- After a Regular trim or a non-ripple speed change, each transition between the changed clip and its neighbor is shortened when the two clips are now shorter than it and moved back inside them (`transitions_stay_within_clips` in `crates/edit/src/lib.rs`). Its stored alignment follows where that leaves it on the cut, as `transitions::set_span` stores it.

Tests (each fails on `main`, where the transition still reaches past the second clip):
- `tests::a_transition_stays_within_its_clips_after_a_regular_trim_or_speed_change`: an Out trim of the second clip, an In trim of the first clip and a 1,000 % speed change of the second clip each leave the transition inside the clips, stored as centered.
- `tests::a_regular_trim_shortens_a_transition_longer_than_its_clips`: a 4-frame transition over clips that a trim leaves 3 frames long together becomes 3 frames long.

A two-clip transition whose clips no longer meet after a trim (a Regular trim that opens a gap at the cut) is left as it is here; #1623 drops such transitions.

#3115 fixes the same fault for a ripple trim of the second clip's Out edge, in `transitions_follow_cuts`. This change does not touch the lines #3115 changes, and `git merge-tree` reports no conflicts between the two branches.

title: Frame workers: a replaced frame server's workers end and release its cache and media pool
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Each time the session's media pool or preview store is replaced, for example when a project is opened (`file.open` goes through `install_project`, which makes a new `MediaPool`), `sync_pool` (`crates/ui-egui/src/lib.rs:643`) builds a new `FrameServer` with 2 to 6 worker threads. The old server's workers had no exit: `worker` (`crates/ui-egui/src/frames.rs:767`) loops forever, so they stayed parked in `cv.wait` and kept the old `Shared` (with its frame cache, which holds up to 768 MiB by default), the old `MediaPool`, the preview store and the services alive for the rest of the process. In a stack dump of one `it` test process on Windows, 3,522 of its 3,568 threads were `filmcraft-frames-N` workers, and 3,261 of those were waiting for a job at `frames.rs:785`.

Changes (`crates/ui-egui/src/frames.rs`):
- `FrameServer` stops its workers when it is dropped. Under the queue lock it sets a new `stop` flag and clears the queue. It then sets the cancel flag of every job in flight and wakes every worker.
- A worker checks `stop` under the queue lock before it looks for a job or waits, and returns when it is set. A worker in the middle of a job returns after that job, which runs cancelled.
- `run_job` checks `stop` while it holds the `in_flight` lock and cancels the job when it is set, so a job that a worker took from the queue just before the drop does not run uncancelled.
- `Drop` does not join the threads.

Tests (each fails when the check it covers is removed):
- `frames::tests::dropping_the_server_ends_its_workers`: after a server with three workers and a queued job is dropped, its `Shared` and the job's project are released within 30 s. Without the worker's `stop` check, the workers keep `Shared` alive.
- `frames::tests::a_job_started_after_the_drop_is_cancelled`: a job that starts after the drop has set `stop` runs with its cancel flag set, and its frame is not cached. It fails without the check in `run_job`.
- `perf_ui::opening_a_project_releases_the_previous_media_p…

title: Settings: Selection Follows Playhead persists across restarts
author: amoisttowe1
body:
Fixes #3089.

Sequence ▸ **Selection Follows Playhead** did not survive a restart: the toggle worked until you quit, then came back off every session. It is now a real preference — saved to `preferences.json` like every other Timeline setting and restored on launch.

## Why

The command in `crates/engine/src/sequence_tools.rs` wrote only the volatile `state.selection_follows_playhead` field (in `crates/engine/src/lib.rs`): no `TimelinePrefs` field and no settings-registry row existed for it, so nothing was ever saved and nothing was restored. Premiere persists this toggle, and editors expect the menu to remember — that is the issue's repro.

## How

Follows the existing `timeline.*` toggle precedent (`dropImportToTimeline`), with the preference as the single source of truth:

- `crates/engine/src/settings.rs` — a `selection_follows_playhead` bool on `TimelinePrefs` (default **off**, so `preferences.json` files written before this key keep today's behaviour) and a wired `timeline.selectionFollowsPlayhead` row in the settings registry, so the Settings dialog and `prefs.get`/`prefs.set` pick it up. The label already ships translated in every catalog — it is the menu item's own string.
- `crates/engine/src/sequence_tools.rs` — the command now writes through `set_prefs`, so the file, the preferences and the live session update together; toggling without `on` inverts the persisted value.
- `crates/engine/src/lib.rs` — `set_prefs` mirrors the preference into `state.selection_follows_playhead` (menu and Settings dialog cannot diverge), and `start_autosave` applies the restored value to the session at load, after `Preferences::load`.

## Tests

Six new tests in `crates/engine/src/settings_tests.rs`: persists across sessions (reload through `start_autosave`, the repo's own reload idiom); off persists and `prefs.set` drives the live session; toggling without `on`; a hostile stored value is rejected and the stored one kept; older preferences files default to off; the registry r…

title: platform: VideoToolbox export takes the RGBA pictures and converts them itself (#3030)
author: ZJHeepfixer
body:
Fixes the hardware half of #3030 ("High CPU usage and slow export on macOS (Apple Silicon)"; duplicate of #1741, and #2367 is the same report with ProRes sources). It does not change the default export path, which is the software encoder by design (see *Not in this PR*).

### Measured root cause

On macOS, Export ▸ Hardware encoding (VideoToolbox H.264 / H.265) was CPU-bound by its own colour conversion, not by compositing or encoding:

- `platform::hardware_encode` converted every RGBA frame to NV12 with `rgba_to_yuv420_8` **on the export's encode thread**, the one serial thread of an export.
- That conversion is `par_chunks_mut` on the global rayon pool, and the pool is busy rendering the next batch while the encode thread runs (the overlap `crates/export/src/job.rs` describes). Injected from a non-pool thread it waited behind the frame tasks: **20–27 ms a 1080p frame** on an idle-pool cost of ~5 ms.
- The hardware encode itself takes well under 1 ms of the encode thread per frame. So with hardware encoding on, `perf.stats` `export.stages` of a 60 s 1080p export read `convertMs` 29.6 s of `encodeMs` 30.3 s against `renderMs` 30.6 s and `waitMs` 0.1 s: the media engine idled while one CPU thread converted colour, at 570 % CPU and 1 % GPU.

This is the same defect #486 fixed for NVENC ("the conversion used to run on the encode thread, where it competed with the render of the next frames for the thread pool and held NVENC back", `crates/platform/README.md`); the VideoToolbox path never got that change.

### The fix

`VtEncoder::with_rgba_input` creates the compression session with `32BGRA` source buffers. `encode_rgba` copies the export's straight RGBA8 picture into a pooled buffer (R and B swapped, BT.709 primaries and transfer attached so VideoToolbox applies no transfer conversion, only the session's BT.709 matrix to limited-range 4:2:0) and submits it; VideoToolbox converts. The encode thread's work per 1080p frame drops from 20–27 ms to 0.3–0.4 ms (the copy), wh…

title: aac: memoise the encoder's per-band work across rate-loop iterations (2.4x faster, output identical)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3259

## What

The CBR rate loop runs `quantise_channel` 5-9 times per frame. Each run redid the scalefactor bisection per band (about 8 distortion passes), re-quantised every band and recounted the Huffman bits for up to 12 codebooks, although all of it depends only on (band, scalefactor), not on lambda.

- New `QuantCache` per channel: distortion per (band, scalefactor), quantised values, largest magnitude and codebook cost row of each band at its last scalefactor, plus the cost row of an all-zero band. The final spectral bit count is read from the cost row instead of a second pass.
- The cache is owned by the frame next to its channel and passed as `&mut` (`par_iter_mut` with the `rayon` feature), so there is no `RefCell` and no sharing between workers.
- Distortion loop as its own out-of-line function with a hoisted `x^(4/3)` table (the accumulator no longer spills to the stack).
- `count_bits_pair`: codebooks 1/2, 3/4, ... 9/10 share dimension, modulus and signedness, so the index is computed once.

Not changed: the lambda search itself (a warm start would change the bitstream and needs a quality sweep).

## Proof

Encoded 60 s of a synthetic music-like signal (tones, chirp, clicks, noise), FNV hash over the whole output stream, upstream/main vs this branch, default features and `--features rayon`: identical in all five configurations.

| config | bytes | hash |
|---|---|---|
| stereo 128k | 980203 | 32a31b435d770f1c |
| stereo 64k | 499954 | 7a7862cc0a665b65 |
| stereo 256k | 1940419 | 58e97e2e8a0bbc42 |
| mono 64k | 499942 | d91b6f5b1d4620bf |
| 5.1 320k (20 s) | 807853 | 249f9c32d25f52b7 |

## Measurement

| config | instructions before -> after | cycles before -> afte…

title: aac: faster decoder (Huffman lookup table, FFT twiddles and stage fusion, scratch buffers; PCM identical)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3260

Three commits, each bit-identical in output and independently revertable.

## What

1. Table-driven Huffman decoding, per-stage FFT twiddles, hoisted dequantisation tables.
   - Huffman: two-level lookup (9-bit first level plus sub-tables) decoded from one 32-bit window, read with a single 8-byte load when possible. The codebooks are complete prefix codes, so a codeword cut off by the end of the data still fails with `Eof`.
   - FFT: contiguous twiddles per stage, butterflies over split halves, a separate length-2 stage. Same arithmetic.
   - Dequantisation: `x^(4/3)` table fetched once per spectrum; `sf_gain` reads a 256-entry table built with the same expression.
2. Scratch buffers: quantised values, the 2048-sample block, the inverse-transform output and the MDCT re/im/u buffers live in the decoder instead of being allocated per channel/window.
3. FFT: two radix-2 stages are fused into one pass over the data (radix-4 style traversal). Every element goes through the same butterflies with the same twiddles in the same order, so the result is bit-identical. A true radix-4 with different twiddle arithmetic was not needed, so there is no rounding change and no oracle drift to check.

`tables.rs` carries the same `pow43_table` change as #3264 (identical hunk).

## Proof

- PCM FNV hash over every decoded f32, upstream/main vs this branch: identical for stereo 128k, stereo 256k, 5.1 320k, mono 64k (60 s / 20 s synthetic music-like streams). The encoder output (which shares the FFT) is also unchanged (stereo 128k hash identical).
- Differential fuzz: 9000 cases (truncated, bit-flipped and randomised access units across three streams, six units per decoder), result of every call (PCM hash or error text) compared between upstream/main and this branch: all identical, so Eof/invalid-code behaviour is unchanged.
- New unit tests: every codeword of every codebook plus the scalefactor code decodes to its own symbol and length; truncated codewords give `Eof` at all …

title: Opus decoder: build the PVQ V(n,k) table once
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3266

`decode_pulses` in `crates/opus/src/celt/bands.rs` rebuilt a full V(n,k) table of saturating u64 adds for every coded partition (about 25 % of CELT decode). The table is now built once (`OnceLock`, n <= 176, k <= 128, u32 saturated, 91 KB) and decoding reads only the O(n+k) entries it needs. Every coded (n,k) has V(n,k) < 2^32 and every entry read is <= V(n,k), so the integer maths is unchanged. The unused `pvq_v` scratch in `BandCtx` is removed.

Bit-identical: `cmp` of the f32 PCM old vs new is identical on 9 ffmpeg/libopus streams (CELT, hybrid, SILK, mono/stereo, low delay) and 7 streams from the in-tree encoder. A new test checks the table against `rate::pvq_v` for all n, k.

Speed (`perf stat`, one thread pinned, median of 5, base and branch alternating):

| input | instructions | cycles |
|---|---|---|
| music stereo 128k CELT | 5.603G -> 4.306G (0.77x) | 1.599G -> 1.222G (0.77x) |
| music mono 64k CELT | 2.846G -> 2.197G (0.77x) | 0.805G -> 0.621G (0.77x) |
| music stereo 32k (hybrid/CELT) | 3.890G -> 3.623G (0.93x) | 0.980G -> 0.905G (0.92x) |

title: mxf writer: write pictures directly, sound read cursor instead of front drain
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3262

## What
`MxfWriter::emit` (OP1a):
- copied every picture into a content-package `Vec` that grew from empty (realloc and page faults for each frame). Now the picture key/length goes into a small header and the picture is written straight from its buffer; the sound KLVs follow. Slice offsets are shifted by the picture length.

title: mxf: faster decode_pcm, AES3 read_pcm no longer decodes the whole element per call
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #3261 (the open window and the caller side follow as separate PRs)

## What
- `decode_pcm` (PCM): one pass per channel with the sample width as a const generic, and outputs allocated with exact capacity (`vec![Vec::with_capacity(n); ch]` clones empty vectors, so all but the first channel reallocated). Output is bit identical.
- `MxfFile::read_pcm` for AES3 (ST 331, D-10) elements: it used to read and decode the whole element on every call and keep the tail. For a clip-wrapped or hostile single element every 1920-frame read allocated and decoded the full element (O(n^2), allocation up to the file size). No limit is weakened: the allocation per call is now bounded by the request and by 65535 frames. The more-than-8-channels error is kept.

- `aes3_read_rejects_more_than_eight_channels`.

title: mxf: adaptive read window while walking KLVs at open (reads 8x less for intra files)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #3261 (decode_pcm/AES3 is #3276, the caller side follows)

## What
`walk()` refilled its `Window` with 64 KiB on every miss. With big elements (intra pictures, clip-wrapped sound) the next KLV header lies behind a long jump, so each header cost a 64 KiB read that was mostly thrown away.

Now the refill is 4 KiB for the next four KLVs after a value of 64 KiB or more, and 64 KiB otherwise. Files with small frames keep exactly the old read pattern. The 25 header bytes are copied into an array instead of a `Vec` per KLV. The design option of opening from the RIP/index is not part of this.

## Proof
- Parse result identical: FNV hash of the Debug dump of `tracks`, `partitions`, `index_segments`, `timecode`, `warnings` is the same before and after on four ffmpeg-made fixtures (DNxHD 36M 1080p + PCM24, ProRes 720p + PCM16, MPEG-2 long GOP 320x240, AVC long GOP with B frames).
- New test `open_does_not_read_through_big_pictures` (fails on the old code: 2.7 MB of 8.3 MB read).
- `cargo test --release -p filmcraft-mxf` 31 passed, `-p filmcraft-codecs mxf` (incl. the ffmpeg oracle) passed, clippy `-D warnings`, `fmt --check`.

## Measurement
File-backed `ByteSource` (pread) with read counter, 20 s fixtures:

| file | before reads / bytes | after reads / bytes | warm open |
|---|---|---|---|
| DNxHD 98 MB | 534 / 32.8 MB (34%) | 1034 / 4.2 MB (4%) | 3.5 ms -> 1.0 ms |
| ProRes 101 MB | 537 / 32.9 MB (32%) | 1039 / 4.3 MB (4%) | 2.2-3.3 ms -> 0.9-1.1 ms |
| MPEG-2 40 MB (small frames) | 619 / 37.0 MB | unchanged | unchanged |
| AVC 7 MB (small frames) | 141 / 6.9 MB | unchanged | unchanged |

Bytes read drop about 8x for intra files, but the number of reads doubles (one 4 KiB read for each of the two elements of a frame instead of one 64 KiB read per frame). On cold local storage, NAS or blob sources the byte volume dominates; on a very high-latency source with no read-ahead the doubled request count could matter.

title: Opus decoder: cap concealment and FEC length at 120 ms
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #3269

`StreamDecoder::conceal(n)` and `decode_fec(.., n, ..)` (`crates/opus/src/decoder.rs`) did `out.resize(n * channels)` for any caller-supplied `n` that was a multiple of 2.5 ms, so a huge `n` (for example from a corrupt container timestamp) allocated without limit. Both now return `InvalidArgument` for `n` above 120 ms (the longest Opus packet) before any output is reserved. The internal callers (concealment of the last packet's duration, `multistream.rs`) never exceed that, so `multistream.rs` needs no change.

Choice: reject rather than loop in 120 ms pieces, because a loop still produces `n` samples of output and a corrupt `n` would only become a slow OOM. Callers that really want longer concealment can call `conceal` repeatedly.

Test: `concealment_length_is_capped` in `tests/it/robustness.rs` (120 ms accepted; 120 ms plus one 2.5 ms step, 10 s and a near-`usize::MAX` value rejected for both calls, no output reserved). No speed claim.

`cargo test --release -p filmcraft-opus` (including the ffmpeg oracle tests), clippy and fmt are clean.

title: codecs: read 2 KiB instead of 16 KiB of each picture for AVC reordering at open
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #3261 (the mxf crate parts are #3276 and #3279)

## What
`MxfSource::open_reader` derives the presentation order of AVC long GOP without temporal offsets from the slice headers (POC). It read `min(size, 16 KiB)` of every picture for that, up to 240 MB for 15k frames, although only the slice header is needed.

Now it reads 2 KiB of every picture first. If the order cannot be derived from those heads (a slice header or parameter set cut by the short read), it falls back to the previous 16 KiB heads, so the outcome is the same as before. Token loop micro-work in `tile/recon.rs` and `boolcoder.rs`:

- `tokens` dispatches to `tokens_impl::<COUNTING>`, so the non-counting path has no per-symbol branch.
- The `more_coefs` / `token` count tables are indexed by `[tx][ptype][rtype]` once per call, not per symbol.
- `sc`, `nb` and `bands` are re-sliced to `seg_eob`, so the loop has no bounds checks on them.
- The sign bit uses `BoolDecoder::read_bool_half`: `read_bool(128)` with `split = (range + 1) >> 1`, which equals `1 + (((range - 1) * 128) >> 8)`.

## Proof of identical output
`framemd5` equal to ffmpeg's md5 on 11 streams with 1 and 4 threads (libvpx-vp9 1080p crf 20 / crf 32 with 4 tile columns / crf 45 realtime / 10-bit crf 30, 4K crf 32 with 8 tile columns, libvpx 1366x770 and 332x196 with 4 tile columns, EffectCraft 1080p Q50 / Q80 / Q80 with 4 tile columns and 333x197). `cargo test --release -p filmcraft-vp9`, `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-vp9 --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check` pass.

## Measurement
One thread, pinned to one core, `perf stat`, upstream/main and this branch alternating, 5 rounds, medians (shared machine; cycles are noisy and the cycle gain is smaller than the instruction gain at 1080p crf 32):

| stream | instr before | instr after | cycles before | cycles after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1080p crf 20, 1 tile col | 45.94 G | 43.24 G (-5.9 %) | 14.76 G | 14.22 G |
| 1080p crf 32, 4 tile cols | 22.03 G | 21.57 G (-2.1 %) | 6.63 G | 6.59 G |
| 4K crf 32 | 77.12 G | 75.36 G (-2.3 %) | 26.51 G | 26.37 G |
| EffectCraft 1080p Q80 | 33.71 G | 33.01 G (-2.1 %) | 8.95 G | 8.55 G |

## Overlap with open PRs
None: no open PR touches `tile/recon.rs` or `boolcoder.rs`. Independent of #3294 and #3295.

title: Alt-drag of a clip edge trims only that side of a link
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3300

## Cause
`timeline.trim` and `timeline.rateStretch` always added the clip's linked partners through `with_links`, which only looks at the global Linked Selection setting. The Timeline edge drag never passed the Alt state on, so the live preview, the edge clamp and the edit on release all moved the linked audio/video partner too.

## Fix
`timeline.trim` and `timeline.rateStretch` now take an optional `"linked": bool` parameter (default true, so existing callers behave as before), and a new `trim_delta_linked` clamps the drag preview the same way. `Drag::Trim` and `Drag::Stretch` record `linked: !alt` when the drag starts and use it for the preview, the clamp and the command sent on release.

## Verified

- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `hevc_probe::register_answers_the_hevc_probe_in_the_background`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

Rolling edits (`timeline.roll` / `Drag::Roll`) still follow linked cuts whether or not Alt is held. The global Linked Selection toggle is not changed by an Alt-drag.

title: Apply background mask tracking in headless sessions
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #3302

## Cause
Tracked mask paths only become Mask Path keyframes in `masks::poll`, and outside tests only `Session::poll_persistence` calls it, once per UI frame. Headless sessions (MCP, `filmcraft-cli run`/`exec`) have no UI frame loop. So a `masks.track` job run without `wait` would finish but never write keyframes, and its stale `PendingTrack` stayed in `mask_jobs` and blocked re-tracking with "this mask is already being tracked".

## Fix
`Session::execute` now calls `masks::poll` before each top-level command while mask jobs are pending. The next command (`jobs.list`, `masks.list`, `file.save`, …) applies the finished tracking and clears the job. The local CLI backend also makes `masks.track` wait by default, as it already does for exports, because that process exits right after the command.

## Verified
- Regression test `masks_tests::background_tracking_is_applied_without_a_ui_frame_loop`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-engine --lib masks_tests::background_tracking_is_applied_without_a_ui_frame_loop`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `hevc_probe::register_answers_the_hevc_probe_in_the_background`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
`file.newProject`/`file.open` still don't clear `mask_jobs`. A job that is still running when the project is replaced is dropped with an error toast on the next poll, the same as in the UI. The MCP `LONG_COMMANDS` list (export-only progress reporting) is unchanged, and no CLI-level test was added.

body:
Part of #2633 — split out of #3000 as asked. This does not close the issue: moving the scrub
output off the UI thread stays in #3000.

| step | warm | cold |
|---|---|---|
| `supported_output_configs` | 191.3 ms | - |

Tests: a press that only moves the playhead closes no output (2 stops before the guard), a press while playing still stops the transport, and the rate rule is unit-tested.

title: Interface fonts: read installed fallback faces when text needs them, and hold each once (−158 MB at idle on macOS)
author: ZJHeepfixer
body:
### Problem

FilmCraft holds 158 MB of font data it almost never uses, from the first frame, in every session, English interface included.

The interface falls back to installed faces for scripts its fonts lack: Hangul in every build, plus Chinese, Arabic and Hebrew in builds without craft-fonts. `theme::install` reads them on the first frame, and each file ends up in memory three times:

1. the font database's copy, which `Face::data()` reads and keeps in the face;
2. the copy `Face::data()` returns, owned by our `FontData` (`cjk::find_system_font`, `rtl::system_fonts`);
3. egui 0.36's copy: `FontsImpl::new` deep-copies owned font data each time it builds its fonts (`blob_from_font_data`, `epaint-0.36.2/src/text/fonts.rs:391-396, :982`).

On macOS the Hangul face is Apple SD Gothic Neo, a 52.8 MB collection. In a release build (with craft-fonts), malloc stacks at idle with no project show it three times:
- 52.8 MB from `std::fs::read` under the face cache;
- 52.8 MB from `cjk::find_system_font`;
- 53.3 MB from `FontsImpl::new` (with SF Hebrew).

`footprint` shows the same 158 MB as MALLOC_LARGE.

In release builds Hangul doesn't even come from that face: craft-fonts' Noto Sans CJK SC covers every Hangul syllable and comes ahead of it in every family. Beyond what the earlier faces draw, Apple SD Gothic Neo adds about 65 arrows and math symbols (↲ ⇢ ⤶ ≀ ⊀ …).

### Change

**1. One copy (`fe46da3e`).** egui is given the font database's bytes, borrowed. `Face::bytes` is public, and `fallback_fonts::SystemFace` keeps the face it found in a `static`, so those bytes live as long as the process. egui wraps borrowed data without copying it. `cjk`, `rtl` and the system Japanese face use it, and this also replaces the `Box::leak` copy in `i18n`. Which face is chosen, and when, is unchanged.

**2. Read when needed (`05e38afa`).** `fallback_fonts::Watch`, an egui plugin, reads the faces when painted text needs them. After each pass, `output_hook` looks at the text the pass pain…

Clip ▸ Modify ▸ Interpret Footage… now opens a Modify Clip dialog with an **Interpret Footage** tab and a **Color** tab, as in Premiere.

- **Frame Rate:** "Use Frame Rate from File" or "Assume this frame rate". The rate can be typed (`25`, `23.976`, `24000/1001`) or picked from the common rates, and the tab shows how long the footage plays at that rate.

  - Stills and audio-only items ignore `frameRate`.
- **Field Order:** shows the file's field order. "Conform to" is disabled with a tooltip, because FilmCraft decodes woven frames and has no field-aware decoding or deinterlacing yet. This is recorded in `docs/gaps.md`.

title: color: tone-map iPhone HLG footage consistently to SDR
author: justacalico
body:
## Problem and result

iPhone HLG footage looked noticeably too bright when converted to SDR in FilmCraft (#3305: mean luma 153 vs Apple's 112, 1.5–10% of pixels clipped at >= 245). The shared conversion now uses ITU-R BT.2446-1 Method A (1000-nit HDR to 100-nit SDR), including its perceptual chroma correction in BT.2020 before gamut conversion. Source, Program and SDR exports use the same conversion; the GPU layer path remains available.

HLG 50% and 75% signals now map to approximately 39% and 67% sRGB, respectively, instead of the previous brighter mapping. Existing projects with automatic HLG-to-SDR conversion adopt the new appearance without a schema migration. Auto Tone Map Off, HDR working values and HDR export retain their existing behavior; PQ continues to use BT.2390. This processes the HLG base layer; HDR/EDR display and Dolby Vision dynamic metadata remain outside this change.

This carries #1273 forward onto current main (it had gone stale and conflicted); the fix is unchanged, only the merge was redone. Fixes #3305.

- Add the Method A CPU transform and an explicit GPU tone-map method, with matching shader stage order.

- Add procedural 10-bit patch coverage through Source, Program, layer plans, PNG and H.264/ProRes SDR exports; strengthen HDR export coverage for preserved working light.

title: tests: stabilize Opus timing and VP9 draft fixtures
author: JSuttHoops
body:
## Summary

The Opus timing and VP9 draft tests now use fixtures that satisfy the properties those tests assume. This removes two baseline failures without changing decoder behavior or lowering the existing accuracy and draft-coverage requirements.

The old VoIP fixture, generated with FFmpeg 5.1, has a 312-sample OpusHead pre-skip but a 104-sample Matroska CodecDelay. Those fields must agree at the 48 kHz clock ([Matroska Opus mapping](https://www.matroska.org/technical/codec_specs.html#a_opus)). Explicitly setting the encoder clock to 48 kHz keeps the 16 kHz source and 16 kbps VoIP case while producing consistent metadata. A fresh cache name avoids the old malformed file, and a metadata assertion makes future inconsistencies explicit.

The temporal-layer request produced only one eligible draft frame, below the test's required six. The new key/inter-pair fixture explicitly clears each inter frame's refresh mask; the following key frame resets references. FFmpeg decodes the rewritten stream as the oracle. The original count, changed-pixel and exact-unflagged-picture assertions still run with one and three decoder threads.

## Validation

- All four Opus container tests passed with FFmpeg 5.1.9. The repaired VoIP case measured 48.9 dB sequentially and 46.7 dB at both seek positions against the unchanged 40 dB requirement. Packet inspection confirmed hybrid coding in all 151 packets.
- The VP9 draft test passed with both FFmpeg 5.1.9 and 8.1, including a fresh fixture root for the older encoder.

The Timeline's wheel differs from Premiere Pro in three places:

- **Timeline Mouse Scrolling default.** Adobe's Timeline preferences page says: "By default, mouse scrolling is Horizontal for Windows and Vertical for macOS. Press the Ctrl key to switch to Vertical scrolling on Windows." FilmCraft defaulted to Vertical everywhere.

title: fix(platform): notice pictures Microsoft's VP9 decoder drops without an error
author: sarayunova
body:
## Problem

On Windows, the VP9 Video Extensions decoder MFT occasionally accepts a sample and never returns its picture, with no error, while other work keeps the GPU busy. In the app, hardware VP9 playback or export silently loses that frame. In CI-like runs of `cargo test -p filmcraft-platform --test it` (Intel Iris Xe, ffmpeg oracles required), roughly one run in three or four failed on a VP9 parity test (`vp9_profile_0_is_bit_exact`, `vp9_profile_2_10bit_is_bit_exact` or `bit_exact_with_the_software_decoders`) with one pts missing. It happens on `main` as well.

A trace of a failing run showed it plainly: the MFT accepted pts 21504, returned nothing for it, then returned 22016, 22528, … as usual.

## Fix

- **Detect it** (`media_foundation/mod.rs`): VP9 / AV1 pictures come out in the order they go in, so a picture that overtakes one still in flight means the earlier one was dropped. `MfDecoder` now returns an error there, and `HybridDecoder` replays the run in software, which recovers the picture in presentation order. A drained decoder that still has pictures in flight logs and counts them too. `media_foundation::dropped_pictures()` counts drops per process.
- **No false alarms** (`vp9`, `codecs::hw_frame`): `filmcraft_vp9::shows_picture` reads `show_existing_frame` / `show_frame` from the start of each frame header, so a sample holding only a hidden frame is not waited for. `FrameStreamInfo::shows_picture` uses it (an AV1 temporal unit always shows one).
- **Tests:** the Media Foundation parity check retries an attempt (up to 3) only when the drop counter rose during it; every other failure fails at once. New unit tests cover the overtaking check and the VP9 header bits.

## Testing

- 10 consecutive runs of `cargo test -p filmcraft-platform --test it` with `FILMCRAFT_REQUIRE_ORACLES=1`: all passed. The decoder dropped a picture in 5 of them (8-bit VP9 at 360p and 1080p, 10-bit VP9 at 360p); each was detected and the retried attempt passed.

title: fix(interchange): bound OMF traversal and reject cyclic segments
author: thecyberbutler
body:
A tiny OMF file with a cyclic master-source sequence currently aborts with a stack overflow; a shared sequence graph can also expand exponentially. This change returns an actionable OMF parse error for cycles or excessive traversal, while preserving the order and multiplicity of legitimate repeated segments and source clips.

Addresses the OMF reference-traversal portion of #2795. The separate Bento value and AAF/CFB amplification concerns remain outside this PR, so this does not close the umbrella issue.

- Detect cycles on the active segment path, including effect inputs and master/file-source clip lookups. Enforce the existing 32-edge segment limit with an error instead of silently substituting a gap; discovery retains a 64-edge limit.
- Share the existing 65,536-visit allowance across discovery, compositions, tracks, segment expansion and source lookups. Count repeated references, materialised early-exit lookup lists, effect slots and gain points; a visited set alone must not erase valid edits or permit repeated empty expansions.
- Propagate traversal errors through the importer so no partial document is returned. Document the limits and add 14 synthetic regression tests, including truncation and bit-flip mutations under `catch_unwind`.

title: Text tool: the IME preedit and its active clause show on the video, through craft-ui's composer
author: aiongg
body:
Japanese (and other) input on the Program monitor's Text tool: the text being composed and the selected clause show on the video until it is committed.

**Cause.** The on-video editor only recorded which layer a composition belonged to. It never stored the preedit text, so nothing was drawn until the commit.

## Changes
- The editor's text and IME events go through craft-ui's shared composer (`craft_ui::ime::Composer`), the IME path the craft apps share (DesignCraft's canvas text uses it too).
- The preedit is drawn at the caret, underlined, on a dark plate so it reads on any picture. The active clause gets a heavier underline; an empty active range draws a caret. Automation ids: `program.textEdit.preedit` and `program.textEdit.preedit.clause`.
- FilmCraft's reset fences and stale-target checks stay.
- With the composer, keys pressed while composing (Home, Cmd+A) go to the input method, and a click during a composition keeps the marked text.
- craft-libs is pinned to craft-libs main `b926b5c`, which has the composer (craft-libs#338) and per-window IME publishing for native floating windows (craft-libs#355).

## Floating viewer windows
In a floating Program monitor, the text editor's composer records its IME descriptor in that window's own pass, and craft-ui docking (craft-libs#355) publishes it after the window's last body. FilmCraft's `DockContent::window_drawn` runs the editor's end-of-pass check and the reset fence for that window, binding the fence to the descriptor the window published in its previous pass. Test: `native_windows_ui::a_floating_program_monitor_composes_and_rearms_its_ime_fence`.

## What the composer's descriptor doesn't carry
The composer is the only publisher of the IME descriptor, so these earlier FilmCraft details go:
- the committed-text snapshot (surrounding text, caret and anchor);
- the `ImeChangeCause::InputMethod` / `Other` labels;
- the text-bounds rect (the descriptor rect is the caret only).

Adds a host bridge to the FilmCraft web build, with both transports: `?host=parent` (a same-origin iframe, `postMessage`, the same protocol as GridCraft, PdfCraft, WordCraft and CADCraft) and `data-host="page"` on the canvas (the page's own document, non-bubbling `CustomEvent`s on the canvas, as proposed in storytold/gridcraft#2593 and siblings). Messages: `filmcraft:ready`, `filmcraft:open`, `filmcraft:save` (`name`, `saveAs`, `bytes`), `filmcraft:dirty`, `filmcraft:failed`.

**Design.** `apps/filmcraft-web/src/host.rs` holds a `Bridge` with a `Transport` (`Parent` or `Page`) and one `send`; open, save, dirty, ready and failure handling are shared. `?host=parent` is checked first; there is no bridge for an unframed page or a cross-origin parent. Only the exact attribute value `page` opts in. Host mode starts without the demo project and without OPFS recovery, since the host owns the document. A `.fcproj` the host sends takes File › Open's route; media takes the drop route (register, prewarm, `file.import`). Opens over 512 MiB are refused before any byte is copied. In host mode the write hook queues each written file for the bridge instead of calling `fs::download`, and `WebApp::logic` flushes the queue after the frame's commands and jobs, so an export goes out in the frame that wrote it. Dirty is `Session::is_dirty()`, sent on change. The crate is wasm32-only, so the pure rules are tested natively through `tests/it/hostmode.rs`. The pure rules (opt-in, names, the `saveAs` decision, the open size limit) live in `hostmode.rs`. `packaging/web/README.md` documents both modes with a host-page example. The commit before it adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

**`saveAs`.** `true` when the written file is the session's project path after the frame (the write was adopted: Save As, or the first Save of an untitled project) and the host did not already have that file as the document. `false` for a Save of the document under its own name, Save a Copy, …

title: Reject non-PCM WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE files in parse_wav
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/interchange/src/wav.rs:50` (no existing issue): parse_wav accepts WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE float files as integer PCM.

## Cause
parse_wav accepted format tag 0xFFFE (WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE) without reading the sub-format GUID. A 32-bit IEEE-float extensible WAV was returned as integer PCM, and AAF/OMF import then embedded the float bytes as integer samples.

## Fix
For tag 0xFFFE, parse_wav now reads the format code at the start of the sub-format GUID (body[24..26]) and returns None unless it is 1 (PCM). An extensible fmt chunk too short to hold the GUID is also rejected without panicking.

Regression tests in crates/interchange/tests/it/wav_extensible.rs:
- wav_extensible::extensible_float_is_rejected: fails on main without the fix, passes with it.
- wav_extensible::extensible_pcm_is_accepted: guards PCM extensible files; passes on main and with the fix.
- wav_extensible::extensible_truncated_does_not_panic: guards against panics on truncated fmt chunks; passes on main and with the fix.

Verified with `cargo test -p filmcraft-interchange --test it wav_extensible`.

## Verified
- Regression tests `wav_extensible::extensible_float_is_rejected`, `wav_extensible::extensible_pcm_is_accepted`, `wav_extensible::extensible_truncated_does_not_panic`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-interchange --test it wav_extensible`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `hevc_probe::register_answers_the_hevc_probe_in_the_background`, `menus::tests::hovering_another_title_switches_the_open_menu`, which also fail on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
Not changed: I did not add float-to-integer conversion. Other sub-formats, such as A-law or µ-law, are now rejected the same way as plain non-PCM tags. The AAF/OMF callers are unchanged.

title: speech: a pause inside a word's span ends the word (#3346)
author: tdog37
body:
Fixes #3346.

## Problem

Whisper's alignment makes words contiguous and places a start that follows a pause late, so the previous word's span holds the pause and the next word's beginning. `vad::tighten_words` only trimmed silence at a word's edges, and the edge in that case is voiced, so the pause stayed inside the word: on a 48-minute interview, 336 of 530 pauses ≥ 0.3 s sat inside one word's span, and `transcript.removePauses` and extract / lift cuts never saw them.

## Change

`tighten_words` gets a first pass before the edge trim (`split_at_pauses`): a run of at least 200 ms of frames below the threshold inside a word's span, with voice on both sides, is a pause between two words. The word ends at it and the next word, when it was contiguous, starts at the voice after the pause. When the voice before the pause is too short to be the word (under half of 50 ms per letter, i.e. the previous word's tail that the alignment handed to this word), the word starts after the pause instead and a contiguous previous word takes the scrap. A span that holds several pauses is cut at the first; the following words are measured in turn, so a late run cascades back into place. The edge trim then runs as before. The threshold and frame grid are the ones `vad.rs` already uses.

The side a word takes is decided from its length, not its content. The alternative, the frame where the token's cross-attention peaks, was measured and rejected: on a 60 s probe 13 of 158 peaks fall on silent frames.

## Measured

Same probe (60 s, whisper-small), measured against 10 ms frame levels with the `vad.rs` threshold:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| pauses ≥ 0.3 s inside one word's span | 4 of 8 | 0 of 8 |
| start of the word after a pause vs the voiced onset, max | 0.53 s | 0.00 s |
| words with ≥ 100 ms of silence at an edge | 1 | 0 |
| longest word | 1.94 s | 1.76 s |

48-minute interview (7,228 words before from the app, 7,230 after from the `transcribe` example on the same audio):

title: test: wait for the condition in two timing-sensitive tests
author: sarayunova
body:
## Problem

Two tests fail intermittently on a slow Linux machine. I hit them running the CI gate (`cargo xtask ci` under nextest, all tests in parallel) inside an Ubuntu 24.04 container, where frames render with software rendering at roughly 12–17 fps:

- **`filmcraft-automation` `server::tests::export_progress_and_cancel`**: after sending `notifications/cancelled`, the test waited until the partial file was gone *and* 500 ms had passed, then read `jobs.list` once. The partial file did not exist yet, so the wait ended after 500 ms while the export was still at frame 12 of 480 (`"finished": false`, `result: null`), and `assert_eq!(last["result"]["error"], "cancelled")` failed.
- **`filmcraft-ui-egui` `frame_worker_survives_a_panicking_job_and_keeps_rendering`**: it injects `workers + 2` frame-job panics and then sets ten fixed playhead positions, assuming they make more jobs than that. When requests merged or hit the cache, they made exactly `workers + 2` jobs, all of which panicked, so `jobs` did not grow and `workers still finish jobs after the panics` failed (2 of 3 container runs).

## Fix

The assertions are unchanged; only the waiting changes:

- **Export cancel:** polls `jobs.list` until the export job reports `finished` (30 s limit), checks it ended as `cancelled`, waits (same limit) for the partial file to be gone, and still checks that the cancelled request never gets a response.
- **Frame worker:** steps the playhead in 0.25 s increments within the same 1–10 s range until the injected panics are used up and a job completes, up to 40 positions. If the workers really died, it still fails.

**Follow-up (3756ea13, from the CodeRabbit review):** `settle()` waits for the queue, not for running jobs, so a job started before the panics could finish after them. The frame-worker test now records the finished-job count once the last injected panic has happened and requires more than `workers` jobs to finish after it (at most one per worker was already running), step…

title: security(render): bound nested sequence renders per frame
author: Silvertree2010
body:
## Problem

`MAX_NEST_DEPTH` limits how deep nested sequences go, but not how often one sequence is drawn for a frame. A sequence that holds the next one on `k` video tracks, eight levels deep, asks for `k^8` nested renders per frame, while the project file only grows linearly (about `k × 8` clips).

Measured on `main` with a 16×16 matte at the bottom:

- `k = 4`: 65,536 nested renders, 7.8 s for one frame
- `k = 8`: 16.7M renders, roughly half an hour per frame

The Program monitor, thumbnails, playback and export all render the active sequence, so a small `.fcproj` sent to someone pins their CPU as soon as it is opened.

#2942 bounded the GPU frame plan for the same shape, but a plan over budget falls back to the CPU compositor, which had no bound.

## Fix

The CPU path counts nested sequence pictures per frame of the outermost sequence (all levels together) and draws nothing past `MAX_NEST_RENDERS` (4096), the same way a nest past `MAX_NEST_DEPTH` is empty. A single clip rendered on its own (`render_clip`, Apply Match) starts its own budget.

## Test

`nest_tests::a_nest_fanned_out_on_every_level_stops_at_the_render_budget`:

- `k = 2` (256 nested pictures) is still drawn in full
- `k = 4` stops at the budget instead of reading 65,536 sources; it fails on `main`

`cargo xtask ci` passes except two tests that also fail on unmodified `main` on my machine (`menus::tests::hovering_another_title_switches_the_open_menu`, missing "⇧" glyph; `hevc_probe::register_answers_the_hevc_probe_in_the_background`, only in the full suite run).

## Not covered

Nested sequence audio (`audio.rs` `nested_mix`) recurses the same way and probably has the same fan-out. I have not measured it, so it is left for a follow-up.

title: perf(codecs): SIMD kernels and hot-loop work for AV1, H.264, HEVC, VP8 and VP9 (ADR 0002)
author: ArintonAkos
body:
This speeds up all five software decoders. Most of it comes from NEON/SSE2 kernels in `filmcraft-simd`; the rest is rework of the hot loops (entropy decoding, prediction, transforms, loop filters). Output doesn't change: it's still bit-exact with dav1d/ffmpeg.

On a single thread we were at 27–66% of ffmpeg's speed; now we're at 68–105%. With threading on, H.264 and HEVC (1080p and 4K) and VP9 1080p now beat ffmpeg.

`filmcraft-simd` needs `unsafe`, so I've added ADR 0002 (marked proposed) along with the AGENTS.md and architecture.md updates that go with it. If you'd rather draw the line somewhere else, I'm happy to change it.

## Numbers

All runs are on an M4 Pro. Each number is the best of 9 alternating runs, timed on the wall clock for the whole process. The comparison is ffmpeg 8.1.1 with its native decoders, and libdav1d for AV1.

author: evillollive

title: timeline: Track Select Forward/Backward selects and moves the captions with the clips (#3388)
author: x-labb
body:
Fixes #3388

## What changed

The Track Select Forward / Backward tool selected only clips, and a drag with it moved only clips. Every caption after the pointer stayed where it was, so the subtitles ended up out of sync with their audio.

- **Selection** (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs`): a click with the tool now also selects the captions on its side of the pointer (Forward: those that end after it; Backward: those that start before it). - **Move** (`crates/engine/src/commands.rs`): `timeline.move` takes an optional `captions: [id]`. The call is all or nothing: if the captions cannot go as far as the clips (they would overlap a caption that stays, or sit on a locked track) it fails and nothing moves, so captions never drift off their dialogue. `captions` cannot be combined with `copy`.
- The timeline sends `captions` only when the drag was made with a Track Select tool, and not for an Option-drag copy. Other drags behave as before.
- `docs/control-protocol.md` documents the new parameter.

Not changed, to keep this on the issue: Option-drag copies still copy only clips, and a Selection-tool drag after a Track Select click still moves only clips (the captions stay selected but do not follow).

title: engine: effects.addKeyframe keeps an explicit time at the out point and says what it did (#3386)
author: x-labb
body:
Fixes #3386

## What was wrong

`effects.addKeyframe` pinned even an explicit `time` to the clip's last tick (`out - 1 tick`). Asking for a keyframe at the out point put it one tick earlier, so a script that then looked for it at the out point (`effects.setKeyframe`, `effects.deleteKeyframe`, `mediaTime` = the out point) found nothing. `effects.deleteKeyframe` also answered `null` whether or not it removed anything.

`effects.setParam` already behaves differently: since #1055 an explicit `time` keeps its place, outside the clip too, and only the playhead fallback is pinned to the clip. The keyframe commands now follow the same rule.

## What changed

- `keyframe_op` (`crates/engine/src/commands.rs`): an explicit `time` is no longer clamped; with no `time`, the playhead is still pinned to the clip's last tick, as before. This covers `effects.addKeyframe` and the default time of the interpolation command.
- `effects.addKeyframe` (a toggle) replies `{"added": bool, "mediaTime": t}`: whether it added the keyframe or removed the one that was there, and the media time of that keyframe.
- `effects.deleteKeyframe` replies `{"removed": bool}` instead of `null`: whether a keyframe sat exactly at `mediaTime`. It still returns an error when `mediaTime` is missing, and it is still not an error when nothing is there (the reply says so), so existing callers are not broken.
- `docs/agents.md` describes the replies next to the `effects.setParam` ones.

This follows the issue's suggestion to make `effects.deleteKeyframe` report what it did. Of its other suggestion (clamp or reject a time at or beyond the out point), neither fits: clamping is the bug, and rejecting would break `effects.setParam`'s #1055 rule that a keyframe can sit outside the clip (for example, a ramp that spans a cut).

## Tests

Reproduced first: the old code puts the keyframe at media tick `1504430927999` for an out point of `1504430928000`.

title: Shorten atomic_write temp names so long project names still save
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/format/src/atomic.rs:12-17 (temp_path)` (no existing issue): atomic_write fails to save a project whose file name is close to the 255-byte limit.

## Cause
atomic_write stages data in a temp file named `.{name}.{pid}-{n}.tmp`, which is longer than the target's file name. When the target name is close to the 255-byte limit, the temp name goes over it and creating it fails with ENAMETOOLONG. The save then fails even though the target path is valid.

## Fix
temp_path now keeps at most 200 bytes of the target's file name, cut at a UTF-8 character boundary, before adding the dot, pid, counter and `.tmp`. The temp name always fits the limit. The regression test covers a 245-character name and a multibyte name.

## Verified
- Regression test `atomic::tests::long_file_name_still_saves`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-format --lib long_file_name`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `hevc_probe::register_answers_the_hevc_probe_in_the_background`, `menus::tests::hovering_another_title_switches_the_open_menu`, which also fail on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
The final target path is unchanged, and only the temp file name is shortened. Names that were already short produce the same temp names as before.

title: Refuse non-finite colour components in effects.setParam
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/engine/src/commands.rs:3817 (json_to_param, Color array branch); load failure in crates/format/src/lib.rs decode` (no existing issue): effects.setParam accepts a huge colour component; it becomes f32 infinity and the saved project can no longer be opened.

## Cause
json_to_param cast each colour component with `as f64 ... as f32`. A finite JSON number such as 1e300 saturates to an infinite f32, and nothing checked the result. The project then held an infinite colour. It was saved as `null`, and decoding it back failed with `expected f32`.

## Fix
json_to_param now returns None when any colour component is not finite after the f32 cast, so effects.setParam returns an error for that value. The regression test checks that the call is refused and that the project still encodes and decodes.

## Verified
- Regression test `clip_ops_tests::set_param_rejects_colour_component_that_overflows_f32`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-engine set_param_rejects_colour`).

title: Strip UTF-8 byte order mark when parsing .cube LUT files
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/lut.rs:213 (Lut::parse_cube, first line handling)` (no existing issue): A .cube LUT file saved with a UTF-8 byte order mark fails to parse.

## Cause
Lut::parse_cube never removed a leading U+FEFF. The BOM is not whitespace, so the first token became "\u{feff}TITLE" (or "\u{feff}LUT_3D_SIZE"). It failed the keyword check and was parsed as a data row, and the whole LUT was rejected with 'not a finite number'. A BOM followed by a `#` comment failed the same way.

## Fix
parse_cube now strips a leading U+FEFF from the input before it reads any lines. A regression test covers a BOM followed by TITLE and a BOM followed by a comment.

## Verified
- Regression test `lut::tests::parse_cube_strips_utf8_bom`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-color --lib parse_cube_strips_utf8_bom`).

## Not changed
Nothing else changed. Other parsers and the `to_cube` writer are as before.

Graphic text could be underlined but not struck through. This adds strikethrough, per layer and per character.

title: Use default interpolation for keyframes added before the first
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/project/src/keyframe.rs:222 (Param::set_at)` (no existing issue): Keyframe added before the first keyframe inherits the interpolation of the following keyframe.

## Cause
`Param::set_at` copied the interpolation of the previous keyframe using `keyframes.get(i.saturating_sub(1))`. When the new time is before every keyframe, `i` is 0 and `saturating_sub` gives index 0, which is the next keyframe. The new keyframe therefore inherited the first keyframe's mode, for example Hold.

## Fix
The previous-keyframe index now uses `i.checked_sub(1).and_then(|j| self.keyframes.get(j))`. With no previous keyframe, the new one gets the default interpolation (Linear). Inserting after an existing keyframe still inherits that keyframe's interpolation.

## Verified
- Regression test `keyframe::tests::set_at_before_first_keyframe_uses_default_interp`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-project set_at_before_first_keyframe_uses_default_interp`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `hevc_probe::register_answers_the_hevc_probe_in_the_background`, `menus::tests::hovering_another_title_switches_the_open_menu`, which also fail on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
`add_keyframe` and `set_at_force` are unchanged. They already create keyframes with the default interpolation.

title: Fix trim_caption moving edges of captions shorter than one frame
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/edit/src/captions.rs:~170 (trim_caption, Edge::In branch)` (no existing issue): trim_caption on a caption shorter than one frame moves its In edge backwards into the previous caption.

## Cause
trim_caption clamped the delta with bounds like `c.duration - min_duration`. For a caption shorter than the minimum duration that bound is negative, and `Tick::clamp` (max(lo).min(hi)) lets the negative upper bound win. A forward trim of the In edge then returned a large negative delta, which moved the start into the previous caption and before time zero.

## Fix
The clamp bounds in trim_caption are now limited so the lower bound is at most zero and the upper bound is at least zero, for both the In and Out edges. A caption shorter than the minimum can no longer shrink or jump. Trimming it that way returns `Nothing`, and trimming outward within neighbour limits still works. The regression test covers both edges.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::trim_caption_shorter_than_min_duration_does_not_cross_bounds`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p filmcraft-edit trim_caption_shorter`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `hevc_probe::register_answers_the_hevc_probe_in_the_background`, `menus::tests::hovering_another_title_switches_the_open_menu`, which also fail on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
I did not change `Tick::clamp` or the other callers. `move_captions` already guards its bounds. `set_caption_times` already rejects spans shorter than the minimum.

title: fix(codecs): frame lookup inside a frame with one timestamp unit per frame
author: alexanderalber
body:
## Frame lookup inside a frame with one timestamp unit per frame

**What was wrong.** MP4 and Matroska find the frame shown at a time by rounding the requested time to the nearest timestamp unit. When a file's unit is one frame (an MP4 whose timescale equals its frame rate, or a Matroska `TimestampScale` of one frame duration), half a unit is half a frame. From the middle of each frame on, the lookup returned the next frame: the first frame was never shown and the last was shown twice. Callers asking for frame starts never saw it; any caller asking for a time inside a frame did. Found with recordings muxed at timescale = fps by another app that uses `filmcraft-codecs`; ffmpeg decodes those files correctly.

**Why round-to-nearest stays.** It is the fix for #73: muxers round frame times to their unit (Matroska usually 1 ms), so a stamp can sit up to half a unit after the true frame start, and flooring missed every frame stamped late. That is still right for fine units: at 1 ms or 90 kHz, half a unit is a tiny fraction of a frame.

**New bound.** The new `gop::lookup_time` is used by both containers. If a unit is shorter than half a frame, it rounds to the nearest unit as before. If a unit is half a frame or longer, it first moves the requested time back to the start of its frame (nominal rate), then rounds. That start rounds onto the frame's own stamp. This also works when the unit is slightly shorter or longer than a frame (Matroska 33 333 333 or 33 333 334 ns at 30 fps), where plain flooring would miss frame starts. AVI, MXF, MPEG, APV and Y4M look frames up by index and were not affected.

**Tests** (`rounded_pts_tests.rs`, same Motion-JPEG index pictures):
- MP4 at 24/25/30/60 fps with 1 and 2 units per frame
- Matroska with a one-frame `TimestampScale` (rounded down and up where a frame is not a whole number of ns)
- every frame asked at its start, middle and 9/10; both tests fail before the fix, and #73's tests still pass

author: Silvertree2010
body:
## Summary

Exporting to H.264 + AAC on the CPU takes about 22 % less wall time (1080p benchmark: median 7.86 s -> 6.14 s), and the exported file is byte for byte the same. Most of the time went to the software H.264 encoder and to colour conversion on the encoding thread; both now do less work or do it where threads are idle, without changing a single coding decision or output value.

## What changed

**Benchmark** (`crates/engine/examples/bench_export.rs`, listed in `docs/testing.md`): exports a 1080p23.976 H.264 + AAC clip (made once in `target/fixtures/export-bench/`: with ffmpeg when installed, otherwise a demo scene written by FilmCraft's own encoders) to H.264 + AAC MP4 through `file.exportMedia`, CPU only, and prints each run, median, minimum and the export stage times. `--keep out.mp4` keeps the file for comparison.

**H.264 encoder** (`crates/h264enc`), every decision unchanged:
- The adaptive 4x4/8x8 transform trial keeps the winning trial instead of coding the winner a third time.
- Motion search no longer costs a point again that it already costed in the same search (such a point can never become the best).
- Without RD, an inter candidate's residual is only coded once the candidate can still be chosen (P 16x16 against intra, B 16x8/8x16 partitions).
- SATD of 8- and 4-wide blocks is computed lane by lane (the 16-wide path was already fast). The two lookahead analyses run side by side. The transform trial's bit estimate reads log2 from a table of the same values.

title: captions: reject unparseable MCC timecode fields
author: SevenxDev
body:
MCC timecode parsing used `filter_map`, silently dropping empty, nonnumeric or overflowing fields. A malformed timestamp such as `bad:00:00:01:20` could therefore become a valid four-field timestamp.

Collect every field into `Option<Vec<i64>>` and return the existing line-numbered syntax error if any field fails. No change to valid timecodes or caption decoding.

The regression fails on main, then passes with the fix. It covers empty, nonnumeric, overflowing and extra numeric fields, plus a valid caption round trip.

Tested on macOS:
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-captions` — 59 unit tests + 36 integration tests passed.
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-captions --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `git diff --check`

Full workspace CI was not run.

title: interchange: reject overflowing EDL fields without leaking event metadata
author: SevenxDev
body:
An EDL timecode field larger than `i64::MAX` was silently replaced with zero. Return `None` instead, so the existing parser skips the malformed event and reports it.

Keep a rejected numbered event as a boundary: its clip names, source files, markers, M2 and AUD lines must not modify the preceding valid event. A following valid event starts cleanly, including when it reuses an earlier event number.

Tests cover overflow in each timecode field, a valid timecode, and valid/rejected/valid event sequences with distinct and reused numbers. The metadata isolation and reused-number cases were reproduced failing before their fixes.

Tested on macOS:
- `cargo test -p filmcraft-interchange` — 31 unit tests + 62 integration tests passed.
- `cargo clippy -p filmcraft-interchange --all-targets -- -D warnings`
